Split the $2^L$ samples into halves and write $A,B\in[0,1]^N$ for their empirical means. Return the rational score

$$Y=f(Z)+\frac{f((A+B)/2)-(f(A)+f(B))/2}{w_L}.$$ 

This is a finite effective algorithm on each finite branch $L$, with only finitely described rational coins, counts, arithmetic and score calibration. It never queries the real $p$. $L$ is finite almost surely. A truncation $L\le L_{\max}$ is a different source with a calculable bias.

**Proof of exactness and variance.**

Let $B_m f(p)=\mathbb{E}f(\text{mean of } m \text{ i.i.d. Bernoulli vectors})$. For $\Delta_{l}$ equal to the numerator above,

$$\mathbb E\Delta_l=B_{2^l}f(p)-B_{2^{l-1}}f(p).$$ 

The baseline mean is $B_1 f(p)$. Uniform continuity and the elementary mean-square bound $\mathbb{E}\lVert\text{mean}-p\rVert^2\le N/(4m)$ give $B_m f(p)\to f(p)$ uniformly.

For a scalar component with Hessian operator norm $\le H$, Taylor's theorem about $(A+B)/2$ yields

$$|\Delta_l|\le(H/8)\|A-B\|^2.$$ 

For $m=2^{l-1}$, each coordinate of $A-B$ is the mean of $m$ independent centered differences of two Bernoulli variables, each bounded by 1. Independence and expansion of the fourth moment give $\mathbb{E}(A_j-B_j)^4\le C/m^2$. Since $(\sum_j x_j^2)^2\le N\sum_j x_j^4$,

$$\mathbb E\|A-B\|^4\le CN^2/m^2.$$ 

Therefore $\mathbb{E}|\Delta_l|\le CHN\,2^{-l}$ and $\mathbb{E}|\Delta_l|^2\le CH^2N^2\,4^{-l}$, uniformly over every real $p$ in the cube. Absolute summability justifies the telescoping expectation:

$$\mathbb EY=B_1f+\sum_{l\ge1}\mathbb E\Delta_l=f(p).$$ 

Also $\mathbb{E}|\Delta_L/w_L|^2=\sum_l\mathbb{E}|\Delta_l|^2/w_l<\infty$ because $4r>1$. The vector version follows by summing component estimates. This gives a uniform finite second-moment bound $V_{f}$ with computable constants. Averaging $M$ independent complete runs yields $\mathbb{E}\lVert\operatorname{mean}(Y)-f(p)\rVert^2\le V_f/M$. Markov's inequality gives confidence $\le V_f/(M\epsilon^2)$ for Euclidean error $>\epsilon$. A tangent bank independent of the entire source gives the same exact all-real bilinear derivative response as in Theorem Q.0.3i; its bounded score factor preserves finite variance.

**Expected budget and the essential schedule.**

For $r=3/8$, $\mathbb{E}[2^L]=5$, $\mathbb{E}[L]=8/5$, and the mean raw selector consumption is $24/5$ fair bits. The bank and independent baseline together consume mean $6N$ Bernoulli input qubits (plus $N$ for a tangent bank when used). Also $\sum_l 4^{-l}/w_l=6/5$. Expected input consumption is finite because $\sum_l w_l 2^l<\infty$ when $2r<1$. Finite expected input consumption leaves the expected complete tariff open: serially retaining $2^l$ bits for $2^l$ slots would charge order $4^l$ bit-time and diverge at $r=3/8$.

Use instead a callable finite-stage factory that, after $L$ is selected, delivers the specified finite bank and a parallel finite circuit. Read the bank in one scheduled parallel slot (full support and summed generator norm charged). Count by a balanced adder tree, then use finite rational arithmetic and archive collection. The retained selector bits, their preparation/record pulses and their pre-bank holding intervals add at most $\operatorname{polynomial}(l)$ support and work, including $O(l^2)$ pre-bank selector bit-time. The circuit has $\operatorname{polynomial}(l)$ depth and $O(2^l\operatorname{polynomial}(l))$ support/bit-time/gate costs for fixed $N,f$. Fresh records and arithmetic workspace are retained without resets. Full simultaneous Hamiltonian norm is bounded by the corresponding sum over active primitive supports, $O(2^l\operatorname{polynomial}(l))$. Include local supplier commissioning, coefficient ROM, input-bank delivery, qualification, clock distribution and all retained intervals. Under a callable-source tariff bounded by $C_f\,2^l\operatorname{polynomial}(l)$, the total expected tariff is finite since $2r<1$.

This is a sufficient source contract. If the factory's commissioning or stock-delivery costs exceed that bound, the exact expectation theorem remains true and the finiteness of the expected total tariff must be rechecked. The rational encoded score labels have $O(l)$ bit length for fixed $f$; they are digital signed scores, and an analog force actuator or action reserve proportional to the score magnitude has its own magnitude-dependent source cost. Each realization has finite support and finite duration, while the source family has no fixed maximum support, peak strength or worst-case latency. The input supplier owns the requested independent samples and their preparation costs.

Every conditional-L processing map is normalized and CP on all input/reference extensions; the direct sum over the normalized stopping law is normalized. No failing branches are discarded. The response is a signed score with an unbounded range across L. Robustness under perturbations in total variation or diamond distance requires in addition the weighted-score moment or tail control appropriate to this unbounded readout.

**Boundary.**

The construction extends the mean-response source from polynomial ledgers to rational-function responses with certified denominators. The positive-mixture argument of Theorem Q.0.3i, section 6, applies on every fully supported finite raw branch and on their countable positive sum, so a nonconstant coherent relative-phase channel with unitary $\operatorname{diag}(1,\exp(i\kappa_A f_j(p)/\hbar))$ is excluded for this interface as well; the obstruction of section 7 to uniform continuum force recovery is unchanged.

<a id="theorem-q03k-exact-mean-logarithmic-likelihood-ledger-and-accessible-generator-derivative"></a>**Theorem Q.0.3k (Exact Mean Logarithmic Likelihood Ledger and Accessible Generator Derivative).** For a repeatable instrument source with success probability $p(u)>0$, the harmonic score of the geometric waiting time has mean $-\log p(u)$; on a source whose nominated control gate has a two-eigenvalue generator, paired shifted invocations give a bounded score with mean $p'(u)$ and a logarithmic-force score with mean $\frac{d}{du}[-\log p(u)]$. Repeatable preparation and the shifted interventions are premises of the source contract.

**1. Log ledger from repeated events.**

Fix a normalized source instrument with success probability $p(u)>0$ at its all-real externally supplied control $u$. Each invocation prepares a fresh instance through the registered supplier and retains both success/failure outcomes. Invoke it independently until the first success. Let $N\ge 1$ count all invocations and output the rational signed-score label $H_{N-1}=\sum_{j=1}^{N-1}1/j$, with $H_{0}=0$. Retain every source invocation, all FAIL records, the SUCCESS/STOP record, controller, arithmetic and archive state. No trial is postselected away from the invoice.

Then $P(N>j)=(1-p)^j$ and, by summing nonnegative terms,

$$\mathbb EH_{N-1}=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{\mathbb P(N>j)}j=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{(1-p)^j}j=-\log p.$$ 

The power series identity follows by integrating the geometric series from $0$ to $1-p$. Hence this is an exact all-real mean likelihood ledger. $\mathbb{E}N=1/p$ and $\mathbb{E}N^2=(2-p)/p^2$. Since $H_{N-1}\le N$, its second moment is finite. At $p=1$ the ledger is identically zero. At $p=0$ the protocol never stops, and that point is excluded from the finite-a.s. source contract.

A uniform $p\ge p_{\min}>0$ gives uniform bounds on invocation count, second moment and expected serial archive bit-time. Without it, finiteness is pointwise and the source budget is not uniform. Under a specified polynomial-in-$N$ total-source tariff, geometric tails give finite expected total tariff at each $p>0$, uniformly when $p\ge p_{\min}$. The preparation/control/maintenance tariff of the supplier must be included and tested against the polynomial bound.

The rational $H_{N-1}$ has a finite exact description. Its numerator/denominator bit lengths are at most polynomial in N (the common denominator N! suffices); finite arithmetic and retained intermediates therefore admit polynomial-in-N source bounds. The value is an encoded score, and $F_{\mathrm{out}}$ below is an encoded signed response calibrated in derivative units. An actuator of strength $H_{N-1}$ or $F_{\mathrm{out}}$ must own its generator, dynamic range, energy/current reserves and interactions, with their magnitude-dependent costs.

**2. The value port carries no derivative.**

The instrument of section 1 determines $p(u)$ at the control value in use only: two families can agree in $p$ at one control and differ in derivative. A force response therefore requires a separately admitted derivative-source intervention. The following one is explicit and finite.

**3. Finite-generator derivative service.**

Suppose a source word contains a nominated control gate $U(u)=\exp(-iuG)$, with fixed known finite Hermitian $G$ having precisely two eigenvalues $+r$ and $-r$, $r>0$. Preparation and all other gates/instruments in that invocation are independent of this occurrence's $u$. The source manifest explicitly admits repeating the same fresh preparation and shifting this gate control by $+s$ or $-s$, $s=\pi/(4r)$, while retaining the corresponding source costs. This is physical intervention access to the gate control; the Bernoulli-state inputs of Theorem Q.0.3i need not admit these shifts.

For any retained event, its probability is $p(u)=A+B\cos(2ru)+C\sin(2ru)$: expand $U(u)$ by its two spectral projections and take the event expectation. Thus exactly

$$p'(u)=r[p(u+s)-p(u-s)].$$ 

Use independent shifted invocations to obtain event bits $B_+,B_-$ and the bounded signed response $Y=r(B_+-B_-)$. Then $\mathbb{E}Y=p'(u)$, $|Y|\le r$. Irrational shift angles/generator constants require their admitted finite descriptions and calibrated physical service, exactly as the source gate does.

If a common control occurs in finitely many gates, differentiate the finite product: the derivative is the sum of the partial derivatives obtained by shifting one occurrence at a time while holding all other occurrences at $u$. This requires separately addressing those occurrences in the source interface. Performing all such paired calls supplies a signed $Y$ with $\mathbb{E}Y=p'(u)$ and $|Y|\le\sum_a r_a$. The identity holds with arbitrary finite intermediate instruments after classical outcome branches are retained/summed, since composition remains linear in each nominated unitary channel. The two-eigenvalue hypothesis concerns the total generator on the full gate support. It cannot be checked only on an active block: a coherently controlled $\exp(-iuG)$ generally has total-generator spectrum $\{0,+r,-r\}$, so the displayed two-shift formula is not justified for that gate. Such a coherent-control service is excluded here unless its full response independently has the stated single-frequency form; a general finite-spectrum shift rule requires its own derivation and additional admitted interventions. Classical branch conditioning does not authorize coherent-control substitution. Parameter-dependent preparations, readout effects or hidden controls have additional derivative terms and cannot be omitted.

**4. Logarithmic force.**

Independently of the shifted calls, run the unshifted geometric stopping experiment from Section 1 and form

$$F_{\mathrm{out}}=-YN.$$ 

By independence, $\mathbb{E}F_{\mathrm{out}}=-p'(u)/p(u)=d[-\log p(u)]/du$. If $|Y|\le C$, then $\mathbb{E}F_{\mathrm{out}}^2\le C^2(2-p)/p^2$. Hence the exact logarithmic force has finite variance and pointwise finite expected source cost under the stated supplier tariff; $p_{\min}$ makes the bounds uniform. No finite trial determines the exact real derivative, but the complete physical response has the exact required mean.

For several control coordinates repeat the separately registered derivative service for each. An unknown real tangent v needs its own input representation and independent response source. If bounded tangent coordinates are supplied as independent Bernoulli qubits with mean scores $v_{j}$, the product construction gives an exact mean directional derivative, with the input-bank promise and source charges retained.

For an additive finite likelihood ledger $\sum_i[-\log p_i(u)]$, independent invocations and summation give exact mean value and derivative. Multiplying the readout scores by the independently calibrated $\kappa_{A}$ gives action units for the mean scores.

**5. Reference and cost boundary.**

Each invocation is its normalized finite instrument tensored with identity on an external spectator. Composing all STOP histories gives a trace-preserving countable instrument on the admitted product-preparation family because N is finite a.s. All failures, input preparations, clocks, shifts, supplier stocks and growing records remain owned. The on-demand repetition contract is stronger than receiving one unknown state; no cloning operation is used. If the source is correlated between trials, its waiting law need not be geometric and the identities above need not hold. Errors in such a source require explicit waiting-time/moment control: a small per-call trace distance bounds the error of the unbounded score uniformly only together with a success floor or another tail certificate.

The construction gives exact mean value and derivative responses for stochastic-rate ledgers $-\log p(u)$ whose parameter derivatives are accessible through the shift interventions of section 3. Structural and thermodynamic ledgers of Definition Q.0.1 are outside this class.

<a id="theorem-q03l-canonical-field-observable-source-for-the-all-dimensional-quasilinear-ledger"></a>**Theorem Q.0.3l (Canonical Field-Observable Source for the All-Dimensional Quasilinear Ledger).** The complete finite-source family below supplies qualified-PU action and tangent-response instruments for the all-dimensional quasilinear ledger of Theorem Q.0.3e, including its degenerate stationary and recovery cases. It joins the same raw marked likelihood ledger to an independently calibrated positive action coupling, exact finite kick instruments, and a controlled canonical-field limit with normal inputs. Finite devices, ideal identities and supplied approximation/tail errors remain distinct. Together with Theorem Q.0.3e and Corollary Q.0.3e.1 it is the calibrated realization of that higher-dimensional, non-semilinear family and of its degenerate stationary field.

*Proof and complete source record.*

**Ledger and source family.**

The construction uses the family of Theorem Q.0.3e and the coefficient sequences of Corollary Q.0.3e.1. It supplies their field-observable action and first-variation response as coherent instruments on the primitive-service branch of Definition C.6c.4a.

Fix spatial dimension $d$, FE level $n$, $N=2^{nd}$, and rational $a\in[0,A]$, where $A\ge 0$ is one supplied rational bound for the entire coefficient sequence. Let $\phi_{j}$ be the periodic nodal basis of Theorem Q.0.3e. Define the scalar polynomial

$$
E(q)=\int\bigl[|\sum q_{j}\nabla\phi_j|^4+|\sum q_{j}\nabla\phi_j|^2+(\sum q_j\phi_j)^4+(\sum q_j\phi_j)^3+a\sum q_j\phi_j\bigr]\,dx.
$$

Every coefficient is an explicitly computable rational from the simplex formula (Q.0.3h.2). Put $C_A=7+A+A^2$ and $L(q)=\ln(2)[C_A+E(q)]$. The elementary inequalities $|t|^3\le t^4/4+27/4$ and $A|t|\le t^4/4+3A^{4/3}/4$, together with $A^{4/3}\le A+A^2$, prove $E(q)\ge -27/4-3(A+A^2)/4$. Thus $C_A+E(q)>0$ uniformly over this whole source family. $C_{A}$ is fixed before the level or input; its physical phase/action is retained. The source owns this constant offset; the offset-one source of Construction Q.0.3h is a separate source. The partial derivatives of $L$ are exactly the nodal residuals $B_j(q)$ of (Q.0.3h.3), multiplied by $\ln(2)$, and the mixed and all higher derivatives are derivatives of this same polynomial.

**Ideal canonical input and action.**

The ideal field-coordinate Hilbert carrier is $K=L^2(\mathbb{R}^N,dq)$. $Q_j$ is multiplication by $q_{j}$, and $P_j=-i\hbar\,\partial_j$ on its standard self-adjoint domain. The field-input domain is normal states, including states entangled with any external reference. No delta-position eigenvector is a supplied input. Schwartz vectors form the specified common core for all polynomial multiplication and momentum expressions below.

$L(Q)$ is the nonnegative self-adjoint maximal multiplication operator, with domain $\{\psi:L\psi\in L^2\}$. It is defined by its spectral measure. Fix the source clock and physical $\hbar$ independently of the polynomial coefficients. For this explicitly nominated source choose and independently calibrate the action unit $\kappa_A=2\pi\hbar/\ln(2)$, once for every level and field input. This value is fixed before the field, mesh, coefficient or tangent inputs. It is a calibration choice of this source: by Convention Q.0.2x the action scale is independent input, and Construction Q.0.3h uses the scale $\hbar$. It makes the finite phase $\exp[-i\kappa_A L(q_z)/\hbar]=\exp[-2\pi i(C_A+E(q_z))]$ a root of unity, while the real, unwrapped splitting integral $\kappa_A L(q_z)$ remains a separately retained physical response. Different rational ledger values may yield the same root-of-unity phase; the installed generator, its unwrapped energy splitting, raw comparison probabilities and retained coefficient record distinguish them. Action and ledger equality refer to these unwrapped data. The canonical identities below hold for every positive $\kappa_{A}$; the exact algebraic spectral compiler uses this one registered value. Choose the pulse duration $\tau>0$ independently as well. Let $g\ge 0$ be a registered $C^1$ pulse, supported on $[0,\tau]$, with $\int g\,dt=1$. $C^1$ regularity suffices for the exact commuting propagator and retained switching integral, and the raised-cosine profile used below is $C^1$. On a real two-state phase probe with projector $\Pi=|0\rangle\langle 0|$ supply the physical coupling

$$
H(t)=\kappa_A g(t) L(Q) \otimes \Pi.
$$

For $g(t)>0$ its self-adjoint domain is $D(L)$ on the active probe summand and all $K$ on the inactive summand; at $g(t)=0$ the operator is zero on all $K\otimes\mathbb{C}^2$. The common Schwartz core suffices for every differentiated identity below. This ideal multiplication Hamiltonian is the limit of the finite zero-idle matrix sources below and contains no kinetic term. Its exact propagator is

$$
U=\exp[-i \kappa_A L(Q) \otimes \Pi / \hbar].
$$

This is a controlled action on the input field. Its two probe branches retain the real splitting integral $\kappa_A L(Q)$, including the fixed offset, and a calibrated measurement of the generator fixes this lift of the phase.

Every derivative of exp[-i $\kappa_{A}$ L(q)/hbar] is a polynomial times that unit-modulus function. Therefore U and U* preserve Schwartz space. On that common invariant core, direct differentiation proves

$$
U^{*} (P_j \otimes I) U = P_j \otimes I - \kappa_A (\partial_j L)(Q) \otimes \Pi.
$$

This is a Heisenberg momentum-kick identity. For every real FE tangent $v=\sum v_j\phi_j$, the corresponding linear combination of physical momenta satisfies

$$
U^{*} P_v U - P_v = -\kappa_A \ln(2)\, DE_a(q)[v],
$$

as a multiplication operator on the active probe branch. Thus the force observable is exactly the first variation of the finite-dimensional ledger whose continuum and stationary properties Theorem Q.0.3e proves. On a normal field wavepacket it is the operator-valued, distribution-sensitive response; its variance and field/probe correlations are retained.

Further commutators with $P_{k}$ give the mixed derivatives on Schwartz space. This supplies a common differentiable physical tangent response. The joint action channel of the source on field, probe and arbitrary external reference is $\operatorname{Ad}(U)\otimes\mathrm{Id}$, without field copying or postselection.

**Finite sources.**

The ideal source is the explicit limit of the following finite physical cabinets. At grade $m$ take a rational box $[-R_m,R_m)^N$ with $R_m=2^m$ and a uniform rational grid step $h_m=2^{-m}$, subdividing the box exactly. Let $D_m=(2R_m/h_m)^N$ and $b_m=N(2m+1)$, so $D_m=2^{b_m}$ exactly. Every $b_m$-bit word labels one cube and its center $q_{z}$. The finite source exactly supplies rational $a_{n}$ within its fixed rational bound $A$. The family includes $a_{n}=0$ and the rational degeneracy and recovery sequences of Corollary Q.0.3e.1; coefficients enter as rational inputs. If computable real coefficients are requested, use certified rational approximants: on a box with $|q_j|\le R$, coefficient error $\delta$ changes $E$ by at most $\delta R$ and each directional derivative by $\delta|\int v|$, since only the linear $a\int u$ term changes. These errors are retained separately, and a nonzero coefficient error leaves the exact zero pattern of the sequence undetermined. The source supplies the finite diagonal matrix

$$
L_m = \sum_z L(q_z)|z\rangle\langle z|,
$$

with its entire all-input coefficient table installed before the unknown input. Polynomial evaluation gives rational $E(q_z)$, so $L_{m}$ has rational-times-$\ln 2$ eigenvalues, finite descriptors and a nonnegative bound. The physical Hamiltonian is $H_m(t)=\kappa_A g(t)L_m\otimes\Pi$; it is supplied as a finite matrix coupling on the whole register, a primitive pulse of Definition C.6c.4a. Its maximum energy is $\kappa_{A}\lVert g\rVert_\infty\max_z L(q_z)$, action norm is $\kappa_A\max_z L(q_z)$, and switching variation is $\kappa_A\max_z L(q_z)\int|g'|\,dt$. Each is finite and fully charged, and each grows without bound in $m$ and in $n$.

Use $b_{m}$ payload factors $w$ of $c_m=\max(2,b_m)$ otherwise unchanged 75-bit cells of Theorem C.6c.P17a. Their original core gates never touch $w$. Accept the unknown finite field register by paid basis SWAPs into these payloads at a declared ready cut, then transfer it by a second paid basis-SWAP bank to a separate $b_m$-bit field appliance. Each SWAP is three explicit basis CNOTs. Only these admitted basis gates touch $w$; all general finite phase, reflection, spectral-readout and preparation matrices below act on the separate appliance. The field is transported and never copied to classical records. The source supplies one complete qualification prefix on the original zero-ready cells, using the original fresh fair-source circuit, exact ROM gates, feedback and forecast instruments. Additional requested copies of that task use fresh full ready cores, their complete 75-bit stock, ROM writes and source/record calls with a new invoice; evolved cores are not reused. The coherent action port accepts its input after the complete prefix on every source history. The source-message bit $e$ gates the raw comparison instrument only, and readiness involves no test or postselection of the field. These are completed local field macros on the primitive-service branch of Definition C.6c.4a; the heat-endpoint access manifest and its passive-payload convention are unchanged. The qualification instruments retain gain $1/16$ and null gain zero because they act as the identity on every $w$ factor, also for unknown $w$ states entangled with an external reference. The paid transfer macros act on $w$, and the ready-state complexity certificate of Theorem C.6c.P17a refers to the initial ready state.

Install the physical diagonal action coupling on the separate field appliance and phase probe. The transported field is the same input state, including its external-reference correlations; $w$ now holds the former ready zero state of the appliance. For a classical basis-field calibration run, the comparator circuit of Construction Q.0.3h has reverse probability $2^{-[C_A+E(q_z)]}$ and forward probability one, on the same enabled event. Its unconditioned log-likelihood ratio is $L(q_z)$, with the qualification weights cancelling as in (Q.0.3h.4). This is a separate declared raw calibration run. In coherent field-input action mode, the comparator is not applied to that input: otherwise its records would dephase the field. Mode choice, dummy factors and both complete histories are retained. The shared coefficient table and same physical splitting link the raw scalar ledger and the coherent action; the two modes run on separately supplied inputs.

For momentum readout the cabinet supplies the cyclic shift $S_{j}$ of its field-grid basis and the Hermitian central-difference momentum matrix

$$
P_{j,m} = \hbar(S_j-S_j^{*})/(2 i h_m).
$$

Choose the orientation $S_j\psi(q)=\psi(q+h_m e_j)$. The source may measure this matrix by its discrete Fourier instrument. For a tangent-response measurement, supply instead the finite Hermitian matrix $K_{v,m}=U_m^*P_{v,m}U_m-P_{v,m}$, where $P_{v,m}=\sum_j v_jP_{j,m}$ for the declared real tangent $v$. To measure this input-picture kick after the action pulse, the terminal observable is $K_{\mathrm{out}}=U_mK_{v,m}U_m^*$, with projectors $U_mE_\lambda U_m^*$ whenever $E_{\lambda}$ resolves $K_{v,m}$. Pullback through the action gives exactly the $E_{\lambda}$ law on the original input. The terminal basis unitary is $V_KU_m^*$, where $V_{K}$ diagonalizes $K_{v,m}$; its full matrix and its unitarity certificate are supplied and charged as one complete local service. Its spectral resolution is a supplied full finite local projective instrument: its matrix entries are explicitly determined by the already installed phase and shift matrices, and the retained spectral certificate states orthogonal projectors summing to $I$ and $K_{v,m}=\sum_\lambda\lambda E_\lambda$. For rational tangents $v$, the registered calibration makes every entry of $K_{v,m}/\hbar$ algebraic: $L(q_z)/\ln 2$ is rational, $U_{m}$ has root-of-unity entries and $P_{j,m}/\hbar$ has rational imaginary shift entries. Exact algebraic root isolation, nullspace solving and Gram–Schmidt within each eigenspace therefore give a terminating finite spectral certificate, with repeated eigenvalues grouped and no division by a presumed nonzero eigenvalue gap. Every algebraic number is retained by its finite defining polynomial and isolating data. All individual coordinate tangent instruments $v=e_j$ are included. An arbitrary real finite-dimensional tangent is their mathematical linear combination; a requested effective nonrational tangent is implemented with certified rational approximants and retained error bounded by $\sum_j|v_j-\hat{v}_j|\,\lVert K_{j,m}\rVert$ at finite grade, or by the supplied polynomial moment bound in the ideal limit. The diagonalizing finite local unitary and complete basis records are charged on the whole field-appliance/probe support. These exact algebraic source matrices use the ideal primitive-service boundary of Definition C.6c.4a, whose principal-logarithm construction supplies their pulse generators. A numerical implementation retains its operator/instrument error in addition to the grid error. A sequence of projective momentum measurements before and after the pulse on one unknown state disturbs the input and measures a different observable; the source can estimate separate momentum expectations on independently supplied copies, with that protocol and its costs recorded. The diagonal residual matrix is a further readable observable, distinct from $K_{v,m}$. The finite matrices satisfy no exact canonical commutation relation.

**Explicit finite cabinet and resource compiler.**

One fixed-stock implementation is specified completely as follows. Set $b=b_m$, $c=\max(2,b)$, $D=2^b$. At one local port allocate: $c$ complete 75-bit cells; an external $b$-bit field input bank and its one-bit phase probe; a separate $b$-bit field appliance; a $b$-bit dummy field and one dummy probe; the eight qualification source/work bits A1,B1,A2,B2,F1,F2,X2,e; four comparator bits B,C,D,E; four immutable records for the fair-source measurements; one comparator record; and $b+1$ terminal field/probe records. All cell $w$ bits used as the field register are already in the $75c$ count. Thus the data/input/readout allocation before programme and controller stock is

$$
B_{\mathrm{data}} = 75c + 4b + 20.
$$

Inputs are not included among fresh pure preparations. All other data bits start at the specified basis zero, except declared preloaded programme descriptors. The dummy field is a separate physical register. A raw-comparison run applies its table-controlled reflection to the field and the phase pulse to the dummy. A coherent-action run applies the reflection to the dummy and its phase pulse to the field. Mode is a fixed supplied classical programme bit, set before input; controlled-routing blocks are explicitly completed on both settings and their full support is charged. Neither mode reuses the other mode's state or records.

Serialize the following finite list of logical service calls, each of duration $\tau_*$: one commissioning preparation of all pure noninput stock; $16c$ cell-ROM X writes; 4 Hadamards on fair-source bits; 2 Toffoli source ANDs; 4 CNOT source XORs (two to form X2, two to form e); $6c$ core CNOTs and $6c$ cursor X updates in the exact forecast-before-outcome order of Theorem C.6c.P17a; $6b$ basis CNOTs implementing the input-to-$w$ and $w$-to-appliance SWAP banks; one full table-controlled comparator reflection and 3 comparator copies; one positive action pulse; one complete finite basis unitary $V_KU_m^*$ for the requested $K_{v,m}$ on field plus phase probe, and its inverse $U_mV_K^*$ after the complete terminal basis records; alternatively the registered diagnostic mode uses a field Fourier basis and phase-probe basis before its records. In raw-comparison mode both reserved terminal basis calls are identities, so the $b$ field records are exactly the coordinate-grid labels $z$ and their active comparator probabilities are $\mu_m(z)$, $p_z\mu_m(z)$, and $(1-p_z)\mu_m(z)$; the marked $e=1$ weights include the common $1/4$ and the separate $e=0$ weight $3/4$ as stated below, and the Radon–Nikodym law of this mode is read in the coordinate basis. The mode is fixed before input, with identical reserved full support and slot counts. The reflection uses the delivered-message XOR $e$ in raw mode; the coherent phase pulse does not. Four fair-source record services occur only at their designated consumption times; one comparator record and $b+1$ terminal field/probe records complete the word. The force mode records the complete spectral outcome and its full conditional state using the transported $K_{\mathrm{out}}$ spectral certificate just defined. Its input-picture response is exactly $K_{v,m}$. Its $b+1$ basis records distinguish every output eigenvector even within a degenerate eigenspace. After those records, the charged inverse-basis call $U_mV_K^*$ returns the field/probe to its original physical basis. Thus its conditional poststate is the fine-grained projector state on that basis. Coarse-graining produces the spectral value law, and the retained eigenvector records refine degeneracies: on a degenerate eigenspace the instrument is the fine-grained projective measurement in the retained eigenbasis and differs from the Lüders instrument of the coarse spectral projector. The diagnostic field Fourier matrix on one grid coordinate diagonalizes its shift and hence $P_{j,m}$; the phase basis is a supplied two-by-two matrix.

Consequently the logical unitary/preparation count and record-service count are exactly

$$
u = 28c + 6b + 18,\quad j = b + 6,\quad L_{\mathrm{calls}} = u+j.
$$

The 16c ROM writes, 6c core gates and 6c cursor updates give 28c; the remaining 18 are commissioning 1, fair Hadamards 4, source Toffolis 2, source CNOTs 4, comparator reflection and copies 4, action 1, and terminal bases 2. Each operation has a full matrix/instrument descriptor and its owned support. Initial/source wires and measured records persist, and no register is reset or reused.

To make programme progression explicit, allocate $r=\lceil\log_2(L_{\mathrm{calls}}+1)\rceil$ controller bits, initialized zero, and $r$ fresh trace bits per logical call. After each logical call append a finite cyclic increment of the controller (on all $2^r$ states), followed by a finite XOR-into-fresh copy of its $r$-bit value to the next trace bank. These are two charged finite unitary calls. Their source clock reserves the same duration $\tau_*$. Programme ROM contains an explicit prefix-coded serialization of this complete matrix/record word, the fixed rational FE coefficients, algebraic comparator entries, pulse parameters, input-domain bounds and its support table. Let $R$ be the exact bit length of that serialization, computed by concatenating the stated finite encodings before input. This logical serialization refers to named data supports and logical calls only, so its length is defined without self-reference. After its length is computed, the separate finite installation descriptor assigns the ROM/controller/trace addresses and the compiler supplies their physical supports. The source uses the preloaded pure-ROM service boundary of Construction Q.0.3h. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
B &= B_{\mathrm{data}} + R + r(1+L_{\mathrm{calls}}), \\
G &= u+2L_{\mathrm{calls}},\quad J=j,\quad K=3L_{\mathrm{calls}},\quad I=BK
\end{aligned}
$$

when all stock, including the external input reserve, is charged for the full $K$-slot horizon. This conservative full-horizon retention convention is the nominated allocation, so $I=BK$ holds with equality. The external field waits in its input bank until the SWAP cut; its original supplied state and any outside reference remain owned by their input supplier. All ancillary stock commissioning is one admitted finite pure-register service with its declared full support and preparation pulse. A different manufacturing boundary adds its own costs.

For each nonphase finite unitary choose a Hermitian logarithm $A$ with spectrum in $[0,2\pi]$, supplying its full spectral/matrix certificate; $H_A(t)=\hbar g_*(t)A$, with $g_*=(1-\cos(2\pi t/\tau_*))/\tau_*$, is positive and has peak at most $4\pi\hbar/\tau_*$, action at most $2\pi\hbar$ and switching variation at most $8\pi\hbar/\tau_*$. The phase call uses $H_{\mathrm{phase}}=\kappa_A g_*L_{m}\otimes\Pi$, with peak $2\kappa_A\ell_{\max}/\tau_*$, action $\kappa_A\ell_{\max}$ and variation $4\kappa_A\ell_{\max}/\tau_*$, where $\ell_{\max}=\max_z L(q_z)$. Record and pure-stock preparation services carry their explicitly supplied finite primitive profiles and peak/action records in the same word; if their peaks exceed these bounds, use their recorded maximum as well. Zero baseline Hamiltonians apply outside these registered pulses. The profile integrals determine the total action and switching records.

There are no interport lanes or links. With $\Omega$ the maximum of every installed service's full-support peak and $A_{\mathrm{word}}$ the sum of its norm-action integrals, the full nominated tariff is exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}
V/u_{*} &= \alpha_B B + \alpha_I I + \alpha_G G + \alpha_J J \\
&\quad+ \alpha_K K + \alpha_\Omega (\tau_{*}/\hbar)\, \Omega.
\end{aligned}
$$

All $\alpha$ values are independently fixed positive source prices. $A_{\mathrm{word}}$ and the sum of switching variations are separate retained responses. This exhausts acquisition/representation via full stock and ROM, processing via calls, maintenance via I, controller/update via explicit counter and trace calls, and readout/custody via record services and retained factors. Ready pure-register energy, clock preparation and any external work/holding buffers are separately described service stock: their carrier, occupied intervals and preparation/control calls are concatenated into this same compiler before B,G,J,K,I and $\Omega$ are evaluated. The displayed formula describes the nominated externally driven primitive boundary; stock of a microscopic manufacturer or an external buffer inside the declared boundary extends these counts by its serialized calls and bit-time. The source-resource total, the selected raw ledger and heat are distinct quantities.

**Normal-state raw-ledger owner.**

Normal field states have an ideal raw instrument. Put $p(Q)=\exp[-L(Q)]$, a bounded multiplication effect with $0<p\le 1$, and supply the bounded controlled reflection $R_p$ on the comparator bit, with entries $\sqrt{p}$, $\sqrt{1-p}$ as in Construction Q.0.3h. Its finite cabinets are the table-controlled reflections of that construction. In a forward comparison run the success flag is certain; in a reverse run its success effect is $p(Q)$, and failure effect is $I-p(Q)$. If the incoming normal field state has position law $\mu$, joint measurement of the field position spectral measure and the success flag gives forward measure $\mu(dq)$, reverse success measure $p(q)\mu(dq)$, and retained reverse failure measure $(1-p(q))\mu(dq)$. Since $p>0$, the Radon–Nikodym log ratio is exactly $L(q)$, $\mu$-almost everywhere. The preceding display describes the active comparator law. In the qualified source the marked event includes $e=1$, whose input-independent probability is $1/4$. Its complete marked measures are $P_F(dq,e=1,\text{success})=\mu(dq)/4$, $P_R(dq,e=1,\text{success})=p(q)\mu(dq)/4$ and $P_R(dq,e=1,\text{failure})=(1-p(q))\mu(dq)/4$. The disabled $e=0$ branch has measure $3\mu(dq)/4$ and remains separately recorded. Thus the common factor cancels on the marked success event exactly as in (Q.0.3h.4). The log ratio $L$ belongs to the marked success event pointwise in $q$; the unmarked success probability includes disabled outcomes, and the integrated ratio $-\log\int p\,d\mu$ is a different quantity.

Position spectral measures here are ideal limiting response observables. Each finite cabinet has the corresponding active laws $\mu_m(z)$, $p(q_z)\mu_m(z)$, $[1-p(q_z)]\mu_m(z)$. Its marked weights are $P_F(z,e=1,\text{success})=\mu_m(z)/4$, $P_R(z,e=1,\text{success})=p(q_z)\mu_m(z)/4$ and $P_R(z,e=1,\text{failure})=[1-p(q_z)]\mu_m(z)/4$; the disabled weight $3\mu_m(z)/4$ is retained. The marked successful log ratio is exactly $L(q_z)$ wherever $\mu_m(z)>0$. Binned ideal continuous outputs have the log ratio $-\log\mathbb{E}_\mu[p(Q)\mid\text{bin}]$; on a bin where $|L-L(q_z)|\le\varepsilon$ this differs from $L(q_z)$ by at most $\varepsilon$, directly from $\exp(-\varepsilon)\le p(q)/p(q_z)\le\exp(\varepsilon)$. Input and spatial tails are retained separately. A normal external-reference correlation does not alter these marginal probabilities. The bounded comparator instrument itself has normal poststates from the Kraus operators $\sqrt{p(Q)}$ and $\sqrt{1-p(Q)}$. Finite-bin and finite-cabinet records retain their complete postinstrument states. Coherent action and raw-ledger comparison are separate modes run on separately supplied inputs. The same explicit function $L$ controls the reflection and the positive phase coupling, so their action-ledger link is physical and testable.

**Declared input preparation and access.**

Unknown-input mode accepts one finite field register from the user of the cabinet, together with a registered state-domain/tail certificate. A source-prepared calibration mode supplies a finite rational-complex normalized amplitude vector (with its algebraic normalization), a complete unitary taking a fresh standard basis state to that vector, and its positive finite-matrix pulse under Definition C.6c.4a. Finite linear algebra completes the first column to a unitary. Its Hermitian logarithm, full matrix stock, precision, peak and duration are charged. Smooth compact-support continuum test vectors can be approximated by these vectors with supplied integration/quadrature bounds.

For physical continuum convergence use the explicit input domain consisting of a normal state together with a decomposition/approximation certificate by compact smooth vectors, bounds on the requisite derivatives and weighted moments, and certified remainder tails. Pure states may supply a $C_c^3$ vector with bounding box and explicit derivative bounds; finite mixtures and purified finite sums follow by linearity, with all preparation/reference costs. Schwartz vectors with effective norm, momentum and polynomial-weighted tails are another admitted class. For these inputs choose the truncation radius and grid grade before input arrival using their certificates; report the finite error. These operational domains are nonempty. The strong extension to all normal states is an analytic limit without a uniform rate.

**Strong canonical limit and physical force convergence.**

Embed the valid finite field space isometrically into $K$ by sending $|z\rangle$ to $h_m^{-N/2}$ times the indicator of its cube. Let $J_{m}$ be this embedding, $P_m=J_mJ_m^*$, the cube-average projection extended by zero outside the box. As $R_{m}$ tends to infinity and $h_{m}$ tends to zero, $P_{m}$ tends strongly to $I$: prove it first for continuous compactly supported functions by uniform continuity and then use density and $\lVert P_m\rVert\le 1$.

Let $L_m(q)$ denote the piecewise-constant center value. For compactly supported smooth $\psi$, eventually its support lies strictly inside the box, and the mean-value theorem gives $\sup_{\mathrm{support}}|L_m-L|\le\sqrt{N}h_m\sup|\nabla L|/2$ on an enlarged compact set. Hence the embedded phase matrices converge strongly to $U$ on that dense class, and thus on all $L^2$ by their norm-one bound. The same proof works jointly with the probe and every external reference, first on finite sums of simple tensors and then by density. $J_{m}$ and $J_m^*$ are analytic comparison embeddings. At finite $m$ the embedded map $T_m=J_mU_mJ_m^*$ is a contraction; $T_m\rho T_m^*$ has trace $\operatorname{Tr}(P_m\rho)$, and the missing weight $\operatorname{Tr}((I-P_m)\rho)$ remains an explicit cutoff deficit. For every trace-class normal state this positive embedded output converges in trace norm to $U\rho U^*$; prove it first for finite-rank states by strong convergence, then use contraction bounds and trace-norm approximation. The deficit tends to zero and is retained at every finite $m$. The devices accept supplied normalized finite states with their approximation certificates. The convergence is strong, state by state, and is not uniform over inputs of unbounded energy.

For $\psi$ smooth compactly supported in the interior, central differences converge in $L^2$ to $\partial_j\psi$, with error bounded by $h_m^2\lVert\partial_j^3\psi\rVert_2/6$ for the continuous translation expression. Cube averaging commutes with translations by integer grid steps away from the boundary. Therefore

$$
J_m P_{j,m} J_m^{*} \psi \to P_j \psi,
$$

and, using the direct conjugated-shift expression below,

$$
\begin{aligned}
J_m [U_m^{*} P_{j,m} U_m-P_{j,m}] J_m^{*} \psi \\
&\to -\kappa_A (\partial_j L)(Q) \otimes \Pi \psi.
\end{aligned}
$$

Strong convergence of the unitaries leaves this limit of unbounded observables open; a quantitative direct proof follows. Write $f_{z}$ for the cube average of $\psi$, and $\Delta_\pm=L(q_z\pm he_j)-L(q_z)$. On a fixed enlarged compact let $M_1$ bound $|\partial_j L|$ and $M_2$ bound the Euclidean norm of $\nabla(\partial_j L)$. Then $|\Delta_\pm|\le hM_1$ and $|\exp(ix)-1-ix|\le x^2/2$. The exact conjugated-shift expression has leading term $-\kappa_A[(D_+L)f_{z+}+(D_-L)f_{z-}]/2$, with $D_+L=[L(q_z+h)-L(q_z)]/h$ and $D_-L=[L(q_z)-L(q_z-h)]/h$. The exponential remainder has $L^2$ norm at most $\kappa_{A}^{2}hM_1^2\lVert\psi\rVert_2/(2\hbar)$. Taylor's theorem bounds the difference of either $D_\pm L$ from $\partial_j L(q)$ anywhere in its center cube by $h(1+\sqrt{N})M_2/2$. Translations obey $\lVert\psi(\cdot\pm he_j)-\psi\rVert_2\le h\lVert\partial_j\psi\rVert_2$, and cube averaging obeys $\lVert P_m\psi-\psi\rVert_2\le\sqrt{N}h\lVert\nabla\psi\rVert_2$ by the cube Poincaré estimate. Consequently a conservative explicit total error bound is

$$
h\{[\kappa_A^2M_1^2/(2\hbar)+\kappa_A(1+\sqrt{N})M_2]\lVert\psi\rVert_2+\kappa_{A}M_1(1+\sqrt{N})\lVert\nabla\psi\rVert_2\}.
$$

Projection contractions and the triangle inequality prove this bound componentwise on each probe branch. All constants are finite polynomial derivative bounds on the supplied compact box. Boundary wraparound terms vanish once the support and its two-cell enlargement lie inside the source box. The extension to supplied Schwartz inputs also needs a uniform tail bound; the estimate $\lVert K_{j,m}\rVert=O(1/h)$ alone would not suffice. Let $C_{L}$ be the sum of the absolute coefficients of $\partial_j L$, increased if necessary so $|\partial_j L(q)|\le C_L(1+|q|^3)$ globally. On an interior neighbor edge, $|\exp(ix)-1|\le|x|$ bounds the kick coefficient by $\kappa_A C_L(1+\sup_{\mathrm{segment}}|q|^3)/2$. On a wraparound edge the trivial bound gives $\hbar/h=\hbar R_m$, but both endpoint cubes have a coordinate of modulus at least $R_m-h$ and hence their weight $1+|q|^3$ dominates $R_{m}$ uniformly. Neighbor weights, including wraparound neighbors, are comparable by a constant depending only on $N$; cube averaging is a contraction and Jensen's inequality bounds its weighted norm by the corresponding continuum weighted norm with a fixed dimension factor. These explicit estimates give, for example, the conservative uniform bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert J_m K_{j,m} J_m^{*} \psi\rVert_2 \\
&\le C_{\mathrm{tail}} \lVert(1+|Q|^{3})\psi\rVert_2, \\
C_{\mathrm{tail}}&=128(1+\sqrt{N})^{6}(\kappa_A C_L+\hbar),\quad m\ge 1.
\end{aligned}
$$

The same weighted bound holds for the limiting multiplication kick, with a smaller constant. To verify the displayed choice, use $|q_z-q|\le\sqrt{N}/2$, $(1+x+y)^3\le 4[(1+x)^3+y^3]$, the two neighboring shift contractions, and $R_m\ge 2$; each conversion costs less than the displayed dimension factor. A tangent combination multiplies the bound by $\sum_j|v_j|$ and uses the corresponding maximum $C_{L}$. Thus split $\psi=\chi_R\psi+(1-\chi_R)\psi$ with a fixed smooth compact cutoff: the two tail contributions are at most the uniform constant times the supplied weighted tail, independently of $m$. The compact part has the direct $O(h)$ estimate. Choose $R$ first and $m$ second. This proves the Schwartz kick extension without a tail times $1/h$ error. The response certificate is the sum of these weighted tails and the finite compact derivative estimate, and it depends on the supplied weighted norm of the input. The momentum convergence above is needed on compact smooth test vectors only, where it was proved directly.

The ideal kick identity is exact; a finite cabinet has its exact finite momentum matrix and a nonzero controlled error relative to that ideal. Finite-shot readout errors are separately bounded and charged.

**Degenerate solutions and continuum spatial limit.**

Use any supplied rational coefficient sequence of Corollary Q.0.3e.1 with the fixed bound $A$, retaining the exact zero/nonzero pattern as source data. At every spatial level, the polynomial generating the physical action/kick is the exact $E_{a_n}$ whose complete real stationary set Theorem Q.0.3e classifies. The physical kick vanishes as a multiplication response precisely at the polynomial zero set, which normal states approach by concentration. For an explicit concentration family choose one fixed normalized $C_c^\infty$ bump $\eta$ supported in $[-1,1]^N$ with supplied derivative/integration bounds, and $\psi_{\hat{q},\delta}(q)=\delta^{-N/2}\eta((q-\hat{q})/\delta)$, where $\hat{q}$ is a supplied rational center and $\delta>0$ rational. This is a normal state. On its support $|q-\hat{q}|\le\delta\sqrt{N}$. If $M_2$ bounds $\lVert\nabla(\partial_j L)\rVert$ there, then

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\langle\partial_j L(Q)\rangle-\partial_j L(\hat{q})|&\le\delta \sqrt{N}\, M_2, \\
\langle|\partial_j L(Q)-\partial_j L(\hat{q})|^{2}\rangle&\le\delta^{2} N M_2^{2}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The second inequality bounds the variance as well. For a tangent combination use the analogous gradient bound for $\sum_j v_j\partial_j L$. Rational $\hat{q}$ approaching a chosen real FE field adds the corresponding center-approximation error by the same mean-value bound. If that field is stationary, its exact derivative vanishes, so both force bias and variance tend to zero under these explicit bounds. Finite cabinets approximate these bump states by supplied normalized rational-complex vectors with controlled quadrature/norm and weighted errors. The state-preparation unitary and its full descriptor/pulse are additional registered service calls. The stationary solutions and their full-tail and subsequence recovery criteria are those of Theorem Q.0.3e and Corollary Q.0.3e.1, including loss of the degenerate zero field when $a_{n}>0$.

The scalar source ledgers have the following spatial recovery schedule. At spatial mesh size $h_{\mathrm{FE}}=2^{-n}$, take $m(n)\ge 2n$, so the source coordinate grid step is at most $h_{\mathrm{FE}}^{2}$ and its amplitude box tends to infinity. Rounding each smooth interpolant nodal coefficient to a cube center changes the field by at most $h_m/2$ and its gradient by at most $C_dh_m/h_{\mathrm{FE}}$; both vanish. Smooth approximation and diagonal recovery therefore give the same Mosco limit $\ln(2)[C_A+E_a]$ for the finite-grid ledger functions, with the coercive lower bound inherited from $E_{a}$. Every finite grid attains its minimum; its minimizers converge to the unique continuum minimizer by equicoercivity and recovery. This is the rational-rounding argument of Construction Q.0.3h, with the present fixed offset and grid boxes. The grid need not contain an exact stationary coordinate; the stationary classification is that of the real space $V_{n}$.

The effective source family includes $a_n=1/(n+1)$, which approaches zero but never recovers the degenerate stationary zero field; a sequence that is identically zero beyond a supplied cutoff, which recovers it on the full tail; and $a_{n}=0$ for even $n$ and $1/(n+1)$ for odd $n$, which recovers it on a subsequence but not the full tail. These are explicit rational descriptors within $A=1$; by Corollary Q.0.3e.1 no total algorithm decides the eventual-zero property of uniformly supplied sequences. All source wavepacket localization and finite-grid force errors remain separately controlled.

Spatial FE convergence and source-digitization convergence are separate limits. Given a particular bounded spatial field/tangent sequence and a requested error $\epsilon_{n}$, choose the physical grid grade $m(n)$ using the above finite polynomial/tail bounds so its force/action error is $\le\epsilon_n$. Strong $W^{1,4}$ first-variation convergence in Theorem Q.0.3e then gives the same limiting continuum variation. The grade $m(n)$ depends on the input and tail domain, and the two limits are taken in this order.

**Summary.**

The construction gives a calibrated PU field-observable realization of an all-dimensional, non-semilinear family with an exactly classified degenerate stationary field and explicit recovery criteria. It adds a coherent field action and a momentum-response interface to the finite-label source of Construction Q.0.3h. The compact stationary spectra of Theorem Q.0.3f and the functionals of Theorem Q.0.3g have no source realization here. ∎

<a id="theorem-q01r-full-state-dependent-singular-entrance-and-accessibility-coercivity-classification"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1r (Full State-Dependent Singular-Entrance and Accessibility-Coercivity Classification).**

#### 1. Exact claim and comparison with the previous work

This is a new, proved source class. It is not a claim that every degenerate generator has an integrated local-conjugate rate. It extends the previous everywhere-available rare-edge/DAG construction in two directions that matter: hazards can vanish on arbitrary closed state-dependent sets, and positive-cost directed cycles are allowed. Zero-toll edges are allowed, subject to the exact no-zero-toll-cycle condition below. Boundary accessibility is computed from the support of the actual joint history density, not from the graph alone or the limiting generator. No diffusion or uniformly positive jump theorem is reproved.

The theorem has no unpopulated LDP or accessibility certificate among its premises. Its effective rational piecewise-affine subclass has a finite exact accessibility and constrained-recovery algorithm at every action bound. The source construction in Theorem Q.0.1s gives the same law to superexponential precision on an actual finite ND–RID carrier.

#### 2. Source class

Fix a finite directed graph $G=(V,E)$, a starting vertex $i_0$, a horizon $T>0$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^p$. Multiple labelled edges are permitted. In vertex $i$ the continuous coordinate solves $x'=b_i(t,x)$, where the finitely many drifts are uniformly bounded by $B$ and jointly Lipschitz on the compact finite-horizon reachable set $K$. They may be extended with the same bounds to a surrounding compact set. An edge changes the vertex and leaves $x$ continuous. For each edge $e:i\to j$ fix:

* a constant dimensionless toll $a_{e}\ge 0$;
* a bounded nonnegative Lipschitz function $k_e(t,x)$, with $0\le k_e\le K_e$.

The rate at refinement $n$ is $r_e^n(t,x)=k_e(t,x)\exp(-na_e)$. Zero means exactly zero. Let $E_+=\{e:a_e>0\}$, $E_0=\{e:a_e=0\}$. Assume the graph $(V,E_0)$ is acyclic. If $E_+$ is empty, the entire graph is acyclic and all statements reduce to a finite set of words. Otherwise let $a_*=\min_{E_+}a_e>0$. Set $d=|V|$. Let $\Lambda$ be any certified uniform upper bound on the total outgoing rate before exponential suppression; $\sum_e K_e$ is always sufficient. Likewise choose $\Lambda_+$ bounding the total outgoing prefactor on $E_+$; $\sum_{E_+}K_e$ is sufficient. Tighter maximum-outgoing-row bounds are permitted and are used in the witness.

The process exists nonexplosively by thinning a Poisson process of rate $\Lambda$, integrating the current drift between proposals and selecting the actual outgoing edges with their rates. Thus this definition supplies a law, rather than presupposing one. The retained state set V times K is compact. The generator, on differentiable f, is

$$
G_n f(i,x,t)=\partial_t f+b_i(t,x)\cdot\nabla_x f+\sum_{e:i\to j} k_e(t,x)e^{-na_e}[f(j,x,t)-f(i,x,t)].
$$

It is a genuinely state-dependent jump generator with deterministic (fully degenerate) within-sector transport. For positive tolls its ordinary limiting generator loses entrance information.

#### 3. The actual common carrier and accessible histories

A word $w=(e_1,\dots,e_m)$ is any directed word from $i_0$. Let $\Delta_w=\{0\le t_1\le\dots\le t_m\le T\}$. Include the empty word as a point. Given $t\in\Delta_w$, concatenate the drift flows with switches at $t_1,\dots,t_m$; denote the resulting continuous path $x_w(t;\cdot)$ and sector word by $i_0,\dots,i_m$. Zero-duration intermediate sectors are kept in the word. Continuous dependence of ODE solutions and Gronwall give continuity of $(t,s)\mapsto x_w(t;s)$, with the evident one-sided interpretation at a switch; $x$ itself is continuous there.

Let

$$
\begin{gathered}
O_w=\{t:0<t_1<\dots<t_m<T\text{ and }k_{e_l}(t_l,x_w(t;t_l))>0\text{ for every }l\}, \\
S_w=\operatorname{closure}_{\Delta_w}(O_w),\quad A(w)=\sum_l a_{e_l}.
\end{gathered}
$$

The closure is joint. Replacing it by separate closures of the edge-positive sets is generally wrong. If $O_{w}$ is empty, $S_{w}$ is empty even if every edge of $w$ is individually present in the graph. The empty word has $S_{\emptyset}=\{\emptyset\}$, $A=0$.

Use $H=\bigsqcup_w\Delta_w$, with distance 1 between distinct words and $\min(1,\max_l|t_l-s_l|)$ within a word. This is a countable disjoint union of compact metric spaces, hence a complete separable metric space. Its compact subsets meet only finitely many words. This is the marked-history topology. It is not the discrete-sector Skorokhod $J_1$ topology. In particular collapsed entrance clusters are represented without discarding their order or cost.

Define $I(w,t)=A(w)$ for $t\in S_{w}$ and $\infty$ otherwise.

#### 4. Exact density identity

On a nonempty word with strictly ordered times the law has Lebesgue density

$$
f_{n,w}(t)=\exp(-n A(w)) [\prod_l k_{e_l}(t_l,x_w(t;t_l))] \exp(- \int_0^T R_n(i_w(s),x_w(t;s),s)\, ds),
$$

where $R_{n}$ is the total outgoing rate. The empty-word probability is its survival factor. This follows directly by multiplying successive survival probabilities and hazard densities; deterministic inter-event flows introduce no Jacobian in the jump-time coordinates. The survival factor lies between exp(-Lambda T) and 1, uniformly in n,w,t.

Let $\mu_{w}$ be the finite measure on $\Delta_{w}$ with density $\prod_l k_{e_l}$ on strictly ordered times and zero on the faces. Then $\operatorname{support}(\mu_w)=S_w$. Indeed the product is continuous and positive on $O_{w}$. Every neighborhood of a point in its closure contains a positive-volume ball in $O_{w}$. Off that closure it vanishes in a neighborhood. Consequently, for every measurable $F$ in $\Delta_{w}$,

$$
\exp(-\Lambda T) \exp(-n A(w)) \mu_w(F) \le P_n(\{w\} \times F) \le \exp(-n A(w)) \mu_w(F).
\tag{1}
$$

This comparison is the entire finite-word LDP proof. It also makes clear why an exactly absent gate and a gate approached through positive histories are different.

#### 5. Count tail and good full LDP

A word with $r$ positive-toll edges has at most $d-1$ consecutive zero-toll edges before, between, and after them. Thus $m\le d(r+1)-1$, so $r\ge\lfloor m/d\rfloor$. The number $N_+$ of positive-toll jumps is stochastically dominated by a Poisson variable with mean $\Lambda_+T\exp(-na_{*})$, by a separate thinning of the positive-edge proposal clock. Therefore, for $q\ge 1$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_n(N\ge dq) &\le P(\mathrm{Pois}(\Lambda_+ T e^{-na^*})\ge q) \\
&\le \exp(\Lambda_+ T e^{-na^*}) (\Lambda_+ T)^q e^{-n a^*q}/q! .
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$

The last bound follows by $\mathbb{E}[(1+z)^P]=\exp(\lambda z)$, or directly by factoring the Poisson tail; the slightly looser $\exp(\lambda)\lambda^q/q!$ bound suffices. In particular $\limsup_n n^{-1}\log P_n(N\ge dq)\le -a_*q$.

The sets $K_m=\bigcup_{|w|\le m}\Delta_w$ are compact. Equation (2) proves exponential tightness at every prescribed speed-$n$ level by choosing $m$ large. If $E_+$ is empty, $H$ itself is a finite union and is compact.

For an open $O$ in $H$ and any $h=(w,t)$ in $O$ with finite $I$, the relative-open set $O_w'=O\cap\Delta_{w}$ has $\mu_w(O_w')>0$. Equation (1) gives $\liminf n^{-1}\log P_n(O)\ge -A(w)$; taking the infimum proves the lower bound.

For a closed $F$, split $F$ into $F\cap K_{m}$ and $K_m^c$. The first part has finitely many words. A component disjoint from $S_{w}$ has $\mu_{w}$ mass zero. Every remaining component is bounded using (1) by a finite constant times $\exp[-n\inf_{F\cap K_m}I]$. The tail has exponent at most $-a_*\lfloor(m+1)/d\rfloor$. The inequality $\limsup n^{-1}\log(u_n+v_n)\le\max(\limsup n^{-1}\log u_n,\limsup n^{-1}\log v_n)$, followed by $m\to\infty$, proves the closed-set upper bound.

Finally $\{I\le L\}$ is a finite union of the closed $S_{w}$: the word-length bound gives $|w|\le d(\lfloor L/a_*\rfloor+1)-1$. It is compact. Hence $I$ is a good rate function and $P_{n}$ satisfies a full good speed-$n$ LDP on $H$.

This proves the theorem for every bounded Lipschitz gate in the declared class, including nonalgebraic zero sets. The proof covers arbitrary entrance times, repeated positive-cost cycles, zero-toll acyclic cascades, limiting endpoint entrances, and simultaneous limiting cascades. No inaccessible path receives a finite rate merely because a local conjugate happens to be finite.

#### 6. A fully computed hard-gate witness

Take $T=1$, $x_0=0$, vertices $\{0,1,2,3\}$, and $b_1=1$, $b_0=b_2=b_3=0$. The five labelled edges are

$$
\begin{aligned}
01&:\ a=2,\ k=(t-1/4)_+; \\
12&:\ a=0,\ k=(x-1/4)_+; \\
02&:\ a=5,\ k=1; \\
10&:\ a=1,\ k=1; \\
13&:\ a=0,\ k=(1/4-t)_+.
\end{aligned}
$$

Only the reachable range $0\le x\le 1$ is needed. $\Lambda=3$ is a valid total-rate upper bound. The zero-toll graph contains 12 and 13 and is acyclic. The cycle 01,10 costs 3.

For $w=(01,12)$, $x(t_2)=t_2-t_1$, so

$$
\begin{aligned}
O_w&=\{1/4<t_1,\ t_1+1/4<t_2<1\}, \\
S_w&=\{1/4\le t_1,\ t_1+1/4\le t_2\le 1\},\quad I=2.
\end{aligned}
$$

At $h=(t_1,t_2)=(1/4,1/2)$, BOTH hazards are exactly zero. Nevertheless $I(h)=2$ because the joint positive set approaches $h$. This is a concrete singular boundary entrance, not a positive-rate special case. For example $(1/4+\epsilon,1/2+3\epsilon)$ lies in $O_{w}$ for sufficiently small $\epsilon$.

For $w=(01,13)$, positivity would require $t_1>1/4$ and $t_2<1/4$ with $t_1<t_2$, an impossibility. $S_{w}$ is empty. The same argument after any number of 10 cycles shows that state 3 is unreachable. Individual graph reachability would give the wrong answer.

With $a=t_1-1/4$, $b=t_2-t_1-1/4$, the gate product is $ab$ on $a,b>0$, $a+b<1/2$. Its integral is $(1/2)^4/24=1/384$. Equation (1) gives the rigorous all-$n$ bounds

$$
e^{-3}e^{-2n}/384 \le P_n(\text{word}=01,12) \le e^{-2n}/384.
$$

The direct word 02 has toll 5. Every word ending in 2 either has toll $\ge 5$ through 02 or at least 2 through 01,12; cycles only add 3. The terminal-2 event is a union of clopen word components. Both its interior and closure are itself, and its rate infimum is exactly 2. Thus

$$
\lim_n -n^{-1}\log P_n(\text{final sector}=2)=2.
$$

The same equality holds for the finite source constructed below, by superexponential equivalence. State 3 has probability exactly zero in both sources.

#### 7. Necessary scope distinction

An integral depending only on the ordinary limiting local generator cannot encode these costs. Change $a_{01}$ from 2 to 4, leaving all positive-toll edges positive. The limiting generator, drift, all exact gate zero sets, and the accessible support are unchanged, but the terminal-2 exponent changes from 2 to 4 (the competing direct cost remains 5). Therefore no function of those limiting data alone determines the transition rate.

Nor is the rate a universal absolutely-continuous path integral on the discrete sector coordinate: a finite-cost retained history has sector jumps and explicit entrance tolls. It is a singular-boundary extension of the original local-action branch, with its own stated carrier. This extension is mathematically complete; it is not a silent redefinition of Definition Q.0.1a.

#### 8. Exact accessibility classification when zero-toll cycles are allowed

The acyclic-zero-edge hypothesis above is a convenient finite graph certificate. The density argument yields the following sharper necessary-and-sufficient result for EVERY finite graph with the same bounded Lipschitz gates and constant nonnegative tolls, including zero-toll cycles. This states an intrinsic mathematical classification; it does not postulate an LDP and it does not claim an algorithm for arbitrary noncomputable gate functions.

For $q\ge 0$ let $W_{q}$ be the set of words w such that $O_{w}$ is nonempty and w contains at most q positive-toll edges. Call the source accessibility-coercive if $W_{q}$ is finite for every q. When E+ is empty this means the complete accessible word language is finite. Then:

**Classification theorem.** The laws admit a good speed-$n$ LDP in the declared marked-history topology if and only if the source is accessibility-coercive. In the affirmative case its rate is exactly $I(w,t)=A(w)$ on $S_{w}$ and $\infty$ otherwise. If accessibility-coercivity fails, no alternative good rate on this same topology can repair the claim.

Proof of sufficiency. The finite-word density identity (1) never used the no-zero-cycle hypothesis. For each $q$ take the compact set $K_q=\bigcup_{w\in W_q}\Delta_w$. A realized history outside $K_{q}$ has at least $q+1$ positive-toll edges, almost surely. The positive-edge Poisson domination remains valid on arbitrary finite graphs, because its total rate is at most $\Lambda_+e^{-na_*}$. Thus $P(K_q^c)$ has speed-$n$ upper exponent at most $-(q+1)a_*$. If $E_+$ is empty, all probability lies in the finite compact language. The previous finite-component upper/lower proof now applies with $K_{q}$ in place of the word-length truncation. $A(w)\le L$ implies at most $\lfloor L/a_*\rfloor$ positive edges, so rate sublevels meet finitely many words and are compact. This proves the full good LDP.

Proof of necessity and uniqueness of the local rate. Suppose some $W_{q}$ is infinite. Since $a_{\max}=\max_{E_+}a_e$ is finite, infinitely many nonempty support components have $A(w)\le q\,a_{\max}$ (use zero when $E_+$ is empty). Their union contains one point per component with pairwise distance 1, so the claimed sublevel cannot be compact.

It remains to exclude a different good rate $J$. Every point outside $S_{w}$ has an open neighborhood in its word component of zero probability; the LDP lower bound forces $J=\infty$ there. For $h\in S_{w}$, every sufficiently small relatively open neighborhood $O$ of $h$ has exact exponent $-A(w)$ by (1). Its LDP lower bound forces $\inf_O J\ge A(w)$. In particular $J(h)\ge A(w)$. On the other hand every closed component-ball $F_{r}$ around $h$ has positive $\mu_{w}$ mass, so its probability has exact exponent $-A(w)$. The closed-set upper bound forces $\inf_{F_r}J\le A(w)$. Choose points $h_r\in F_r$ with $J(h_r)\le A(w)+r$. Since $h_r\to h$, lower semicontinuity gives $J(h)\le A(w)$. Hence $J(h)=A(w)$ at every supported point. Every candidate rate is therefore $I$, whose bounded-action sublevel above is noncompact. A good rate is impossible. QED.

This also gives an exact failure of exponential tightness: for any compact $K$ only finitely many word components meet $K$, so choose $w\in W_{q}$ outside them. Equation (1) gives $\limsup n^{-1}\log P(K^c)\ge -A(w)\ge -q\,a_{\max}$. No compact family achieves levels above $q\,a_{\max}$. A zero-toll cycle that can actually be repeated arbitrarily often in $[0,T]$ is an immediate failure witness; a graph-theoretic zero cycle that gates render impossible is not. Thus the classification explicitly distinguishes graph cycles from actual accessible boundary dynamics.

**Nonempty examples on both sides.** An everywhere-open zero-toll two-state cycle has positive density for every alternating word and fails the criterion already at $q=0$. Its n-independent law may have the trivial nongood rate zero on support, but it has no good marked-history rate. Conversely a graph may contain a zero-toll return edge whose gate closes permanently before the outward edge first opens. Its return words have empty $O_{w}$; if all remaining accessible cycles have positive toll, the accessible language meets the criterion despite the graph-theoretic zero cycle. The hard-gate witness already demonstrates the basic chronological exclusion mechanism.

This theorem completes the good-versus-nongood classification for the entire declared finite-graph, constant-toll, deterministic-transport class on its actual marked carrier. It does not classify density-dependent small jumps, infinitely many sectors, singular jump sizes, or an unannounced replacement topology.

<a id="theorem-q01s-finite-same-history-nd-rid-source-and-exact-constrained-recovery"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1s (Finite Same-History ND-RID Source and Exact Constrained Recovery).**

#### 1. Effective source family, formally declared here

For the finite construction specialize the theorem to rational T,x0, constant rational drift vectors $b_{i}$, rational nonnegative tolls $a_{e}$, and rational bounded continuous piecewise-affine gates $k_{e}$ supplied as finite min/max expressions of affine functions. A global rational Lipschitz bound L and drift bound B on the reachable box are obtained directly from their coefficients. This is an effective, genuinely state-dependent subfamily of the proved theorem. It contains the hard-gate witness verbatim.

Theorem Q.0.1s declares a mathematical finite driven-register source family. The source consists of the explicitly prescribed finite pulse list, supplied ready registers and maximally mixed coin registers below. Its actuator is the prescribed external Hamiltonian; it is not asserted to be an autonomous finite clock/battery. No bounded-power, bounded-stock, or refinement-uniform efficiency claim is made. All ideal source resources within this declared externally driven model are populated below, without symbolic unspecified cost functions.

Choose a nonnegative integer $c$ with $T\Lambda 2^{-(1+c)}\le 1/2$. Let

$$
\begin{aligned}
M_n&=n!\, 2^{n^2+c},\quad \delta_n=T/M_n, \\
b_n&=4\lceil \log_2 M_n\rceil+n+\lceil \log_2(2|E|+2)\rceil+4.
\end{aligned}
$$

The factorial is important: it permits exact rational fixed-boundary recovery, which a purely dyadic clock can obstruct. The physical observation horizon is T at every n. There is no rescaling to a second unpaid clock.

At a tick beginning at t and coordinate x define

$$
k_e^{\mathrm{safe}}(t,x)=[k_e(t,x)-L(1+B)\delta_n]_+.
$$

Compute a rational $p_{e,n}$ with $0\le p_{e,n}\le\exp(-na_e)$ and error $\le 2^{-b_n}$; set $p_{e,n}=1$ exactly if $a_{e}=0$. Define the dyadic row

$$
\begin{aligned}
q_e(t,x) &= 2^{-b_n} \lfloor 2^{b_n}\delta_n k_e^{\mathrm{safe}}(t,x)\,p_{e,n}\rfloor, \\
q_0(i,t,x) &= 1-\sum_{e\ \text{leaving}\ i}q_e(t,x).
\end{aligned}
$$

On the final tick $k=M_n-1$ set every event probability to zero and $q_{0}=1$. This harmless terminal guard ensures all recorded events occur strictly before $T$, which is used by the exact constrained-recovery theorem. Its total comparison error is at most $\Lambda\delta_n$. All other $q$ are exact rational numbers with denominator $2^{b_n}$. The total event probability is at most $\Lambda\delta_n\le 1/2$. Exactly zero gates stay exactly zero. A $b_n$-bit uniformly random integer, partitioned by the cumulative integer row, generates precisely this law. After the outcome, advance $x$ by $\delta_nb_i$ using the old sector $i$, advance $t$ by $\delta_{n}$, and replace $i$ by the edge head (or retain it on outcome 0). Record the event at the tick's right endpoint. There is at most one event per tick.

The safety subtraction ensures that every event in the digital source is allowed at its recorded endpoint in the exact continuous concatenated flow: $k_e(t+\delta,x+\delta b_i)\ge k_e(t,x)-L(1+B)\delta>0$ whenever $q_{e}>0$. Thus every digital word/time point belongs to the actual $O_{w}$. This prevents small discretization errors from inventing inaccessible boundary words.

#### 2. A terminating certified exponential computation

No exact transcendental floor oracle is used. For $a_{e}>0$ put $z=na_e$, $m=\max(1,\lceil z\rceil)$, $u=z/m\in(0,1]$. Choose odd $J\ge b_n+\lceil\log_2 m\rceil+4$. The alternating Taylor partial sum

$$
s_J=\sum_{j=0}^J(-u)^j/j!
$$

satisfies $0<s_J\le e^{-u}$ and $0\le e^{-u}-s_J\le 1/(J+1)!\le 2^{-J}$. Therefore $p_{e,n}=s_J^m$ is rational, below $e^{-z}$, and

$$
0\le e^{-z}-p_{e,n}\le m 2^{-J}\le 2^{-b_n}.
$$

All floors defining $q$ now concern rational numbers and terminate exactly. To make arithmetic size explicit, write $u=A/D$ in lowest terms and use the common denominator $D^J\,J!$. Numerator and denominator of $s_{J}$ require at most

$$
Q_0=\lceil \log_2(J+1)\rceil+J \lceil \log_2 \max(2,D)\rceil+J \lceil \log_2 \max(2,J)\rceil+3
$$

bits. The unreduced rational power $s_{J}^{m}$ needs at most $mQ_0+1$ bits in each part. Factoring, summing and multiplying these explicit integers gives a finite construction using, conservatively, $O((J^2+m)(mQ_0+1)^2)$ bit operations with school arithmetic. This is an algorithmic size bound, not a claimed hardware clock rate. No numerical approximation is silently exponentiated without its error ledger.

For each edge on a nonterminal tick,

$$
0\le \delta k_e^{\mathrm{safe}} e^{-na_e}-q_e\le (1+\delta K_e)2^{-b_n}\le 2 \times 2^{-b_n}
$$

after enlarging $c$ if necessary so $\delta\max K_{e}\le 1$. Hence a whole row's total-variation error is at most $2|E|2^{-b_n}$.

#### 3. Superexponential same-history comparison

Let $X_{n}$ be the continuous process of the theorem and $Y_{n}$ this digital source. Couple both through a common rate-$\Lambda$ marked proposal clock, then couple its first-order tick transition to the dyadic row. A tick with at least two proposals has probability $\le(\Lambda\delta)^2/2$; summed over $M$ ticks its contribution is $\le\Lambda^2T\delta/2$.

Before any mismatch, corresponding accepted jumps have the same labels and times differing by at most $\delta$. With constant drifts, after $N$ proposals the continuous coordinates differ by at most $2BN\delta$. Inside a tick add $B\delta$ for elapsed flow. The gates are Lipschitz, their exponential factors are $\le 1$, and $\mathbb{E}N\le\Lambda T$. Thus the expected integrated rate discrepancy is bounded by

$$
\lvert E\rvert LT[1+B+2B\Lambda T]\delta.
$$

The safety subtraction contributes at most $|E|L(1+B)T\delta$. The at-most-one-proposal law and its first-order row differ by at most another $2\Lambda^2T\delta$. The terminal guard contributes at most $\Lambda\delta$. Maximal row coupling and the rounding estimate therefore give the explicit safe bound

$$
\begin{aligned}
P(\text{coupling failure})&\le C \delta+2|E|M 2^{-b_n}, \\
C&=\Lambda+3\Lambda^2T+|E|LT[2(1+B)+2B \Lambda T].
\end{aligned}
\tag{S1}
$$

$L$ may be enlarged to a common bound including all time and state arguments; this only makes $C$ conservative. On success the word is identical and every time differs by $\le\delta$, hence $d_H(X_n,Y_n)\le\delta$. Since $\log M_n/n\to\infty$,

$$
\limsup_n n^{-1}\log P(d_H(X_n,Y_n)>\epsilon)=-\infty
$$

for every $\epsilon>0$. Consequently the good LDP, exact accessible support rate, and all proved tube exponents transfer to this actual finite source. Superexponential absolute error also implies vanishing relative error against every fixed finite-action tube having probability exp[-n(A+o(1))]. This is stronger than weak approximation.

#### 4. Exact ND–RID realization and predictive update

Represent the digital state by the current sector $i$, tick $k$, and occupation counts $c_1,\dots,c_d$; each $c_{j}$ counts elapsed ticks spent in sector $j$ and $\sum c_j=k$. Then

$$
t=k\delta,\quad x=x_0+\delta \sum_j b_j c_j.
$$

Also retain the previous outcome. All entries have finite ranges. Let $X_{n}$ be this finite state set, $Y=\{\text{the fixed source program at }n\}$, and $O=\{0\}\cup E$. Define

$$
\begin{gathered}
V_{\mathrm{prob}}(x,y)(\alpha)=q_\alpha(x), \\
T_{\mathrm{prob}}(x,y,\alpha)=\text{point mass at }F_\alpha(x),
\end{gathered}
$$

where F advances the old-sector occupation count, tick, outcome, and vertex as just specified. Define arbitrary normalized updates on zero-probability outcomes. These are exactly the two kernels of Definition 6, not a simulation of unspecified kernels. The outcome changes the next state and hence its next forecast row. The source-to-marked-history map records nonzero outcomes and their physical tick endpoints; its continuous-coordinate readout is the exact affine concatenation. The diagram between the finite register, this ND–RID tuple, and the digital history law commutes exactly.

A predictor can read the finite row $q$ before verification. The realized one-hot outcome supplies the Brier discrepancy; its conditional mean is $1-\lVert q\rVert_2^2$. The row for the updated state is the next prediction. This populates predict/verify/update. No PCE global-optimality or minimal-MPU irreducibility theorem is inferred from this elementary source.

#### 5. Completely finite driven implementation and stock ledger

Put $l=\lceil\log_2(M+1)\rceil$, $r=\lceil\log_2\max(2,d)\rceil$, $o=\lceil\log_2(|E|+1)\rceil$. A state snapshot fits in

$$
s=(d+1)l+r+o
$$

bits. Every tick is a deterministic function $F$ of the current $s$-bit snapshot and $b=b_n$ fair bits, with $s$-bit output. Its complete truth table has at most $D=s\,2^{s+b}$ output bits; values on invalid input strings are fixed arbitrarily. This truth table is computed from the exact rational program above, before the run. It is the finite control description, not an unknown implementation constant.

Use a fresh zero $s$-bit output register at each tick. The reversible map $|z\rangle|v\rangle\to|z\rangle|v\oplus F(z)\rangle$ retains the complete old input and therefore needs no erasure. One explicit circuit applies, for each input pattern and every output bit equal to 1, a multi-controlled NOT with complements for zero controls. With $c_{\mathrm{in}}=s+b$ controls, the standard clean-ancilla AND/uncompute construction uses at most $2c_{\mathrm{in}}-3$ Toffolis, plus at most $2c_{\mathrm{in}}$ input complements. Thus

$$
R=s\, 2^{s+b}(4(s+b)+1)
$$

is a conservative finite upper bound on primitive gates per tick; s+b-2 clean reusable AND ancillas suffice. Pad unused gate slots by identity. All old snapshots and all coin bits remain owned by the source after the run. The archive is lossless without a hidden reset.

At idle take $H_0=0$ on every register and fix a bath inverse temperature $\beta$. Supply $Mb$ maximally mixed independent coin bits, exactly thermal for $H_0$. Supply all snapshots, reusable work ancillas, and the $D$-bit control description as ready pure stock. A conservative ready-bit count is

$$
B_{\mathrm{ready}}=D+(M+1)s+(s+b)+1.
$$

The last bit is the action readout below. The total Hilbert carrier uses $B_{\mathrm{total}}=B_{\mathrm{ready}}+Mb$ qubits. The exact initial nonequilibrium free-energy excess is $\beta^{-1}B_{\mathrm{ready}}\ln 2$. Coins contribute zero. This is supplied stock, not an assertion that a finite-time reset attains the Landauer lower bound. There is no reset during the experiment; repeating it requires new stock or a separately paid reset. Neither the archive nor seeds are discarded.

Every classical primitive is a Hermitian involution U. In a slot of length $\tau$ implement

$$
G_U=(\pi \hbar/(2\tau))(I-U).
$$

Then $\exp(-iG_U\tau/\hbar)=U$ exactly and $\lVert G_U\rVert\le\pi\hbar/\tau$. Include one additional controlled phase slot per tick as described next, so $\tau=T/[M(R+1)]$. The gate list, pulse widths, finite stock, and control description completely specify this ideal driven source. At a pulse beginning and ending with idle Hamiltonian zero, the two switching-work expectations are $\operatorname{tr}(G\rho_{\mathrm{in}})$ and $-\operatorname{tr}(G\rho_{\mathrm{out}})$; they cancel exactly because the pulse unitary commutes with $G$. Their absolute sum is bounded by $2\lVert G\rVert$. Thus there is no unaccounted net ideal quench work, but the large peak-energy and gross-throughput bounds below are retained. This finite prescribed-drive convention does not include a claim about the cost of an autonomous controller or about uniform physical resources in the continuum limit.

#### 6. Independent action calibration on the SAME source carrier

Independently fix energy and time standards $E_{\mathrm{ref}}>0$, $\tau_{\mathrm{ref}}>0$ and $\kappa_0=E_{\mathrm{ref}}\tau_{\mathrm{ref}}$. Add a Ramsey bit initially $|+\rangle$. After outcome $e$ in a tick, apply for one slot

$$
G_e=-(\kappa_0 a_e/\tau)|1\rangle\langle 1|,
$$

controlled by that tick's outcome; for no event apply zero. The gate is an actual independently energy/time-calibrated Hamiltonian. It is not a relabelling of log probability. The reference pulse $-E_{\mathrm{ref}}|1\rangle\langle 1|$ for $\tau_{\mathrm{ref}}$ has phase $\kappa_0/\hbar$, fixing the action conversion on the same readout standard.

For a digital history h with edge word w, the conditional Ramsey state is

$$
(|0\rangle+\exp[i \kappa_0 A(w)/\hbar]|1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}.
$$

The relative dynamical action of this specified retained readout is exactly $S_{\mathrm{phase}}(h)=\kappa_0A(w)$.
