Thus $S_{\mathrm{phase}}/\kappa_0=I$ on every supported finite history, and on all finite-rate limit histories by continuity within each word. Both normalized X/Y Ramsey quadratures are specified, so this is a response-level, historywise equality. Choosing $\kappa_0=\hbar$ is an explicit independent calibration choice; it is not derived from $\ln 2$ or from the stochastic law.

This identifies the action of the retained Ramsey response. It does NOT identify A with the total actuator action, bath heat, or the Appendix-U field action. Those quantities have separately specified carriers and ledgers. Removing the Ramsey gates leaves the entire stochastic law unchanged; their addition is explicit source data. The construction supplies a real calibrated source action, while also showing why it cannot be inferred from stochastic probabilities alone.

Let $a_{\max}=\max_e a_e$ and $C_G=\max(\pi\hbar,\kappa_0a_{\max})$. Every pulse obeys $\lVert G\rVert\le C_G/\tau$. There are $M(R+1)$ slots, so the actual registered worst-case bounds are

peak control norm $\le C_GM(R+1)/T$,
gross switching-work throughput $\le 2C_G[M(R+1)]^2/T$,
maximum retained relative action $\le\kappa_0a_{\max}M$.

These are explicit finite quantities determined by the source inputs and $n$. The exact per-history action is the smaller sum $\kappa_0A(w)$. No finite source resource is equated with that rare-history rate.

#### 7. What has and has not been realized

The new family has an exact finite ND–RID source, a complete finite driven implementation, a populated stock/clock/energy description, certified LDP-scale precision, exact state-dependent gates, and an independently calibrated same-carrier action response. These are completed constructions, not proposed certificate slots.

This bare zero-idle driven-register family is not asserted to be the qualified P17/native Appendix-B MPU source used in other source joins, nor does it establish MPU minimality. It does not identify the Ramsey response with the original U Euclidean bounce/Hessian/contour or with Y's electroweak/APS/transport observables. Renaming an edge U or Y, or setting its toll numerically to 284 or 77/4+ln2/3, would not establish those maps. A separate original-domain source map is required for those identifications.

#### Exact constrained recovery on the same source
#### 1. Rational polyhedral histories and constraints

With rational constant drifts, $x_w(t;s)$ is piecewise affine in the switch times. Suppose gate-positive regions are finite unions of rational open polyhedra in $(t,x)$, as holds for the supplied rational piecewise-affine gates. At a fixed word, its positive-history set $O_{w}$ is therefore a finite union of relatively open rational polyhedral cells in the ordered time simplex. A fixed endpoint $x(T)=y$ with rational $y$ gives rational affine equalities in the switch times. A rational convex polyhedral obstacle $x(s)\in P$ for all $s$ is equivalent to membership of $x$ at the endpoints of each affine segment, hence a finite list of rational linear inequalities. Finite intersections and finite unions of such declared constraints are allowed. Call the resulting closed history constraint $C_{w}$.

For a given word the exact necessary and sufficient inward-recovery restriction is

$$
S_{w}\cap C_w=\operatorname{closure}(O_w\cap C_w).
\tag{R}
$$

The closure is relative to $\Delta_{w}$. The right side is always contained in the left. Equality can fail when the exact constraint pins a gate to its zero boundary.

#### 2. A finite exact checker for (R) below every action bound

Fix a finite rational action bound L0. The positive-cycle argument bounds word length by d(floor(L0/a*)+1)-1, or by d-1 if there are no positive edges. Enumerate those finitely many words. Decompose $O_{w}$ into its supplied rational polyhedral gate cells; intersect each with each polyhedral constraint component.

For a cell with strict inequalities $a_j\cdot t>b_j$ and weak/equality constraints, solve the bounded rational linear program maximizing $\rho$ subject to $0\le\rho\le 1$, $a_j\cdot t\ge b_j+\rho$, and all weak/equality constraints. Its optimum is positive exactly when the strict cell is nonempty. If positive, the closure of that cell is exactly the polyhedron formed by replacing all its strict inequalities by weak ones: for any point $z$ in that polyhedron and one strict feasible point $y$, $(1-\epsilon)z+\epsilon y$ is strict feasible and converges to $z$. If the optimum is zero or infeasible, the cell contributes nothing.

Apply this construction once without $C_{w}$ to compute $S_{w}$ and once with $C_{w}$ to compute $\operatorname{closure}(O_w\cap C_w)$. Their equality after intersection is a finite equality of rational polyhedral unions. It can be decided by enumerating sign cells of all boundary hyperplanes and rational feasibility, or ordinary exact polyhedral set-difference checks. This terminates for every supplied bound and input. There is no claim of deciding arbitrary noncomputable real zero sets.

#### 3. Source-supported exact discrete recovery

Let $H_{n}$ be the actual positive-probability digital histories, at times $jT/M_n$. Every $h_{n}\in H_{n}$ lies in $O_{w}$, by the safety-margin proof. Define the finite digital variational ledger $I_n(h)=A(w)$ on $H_{n}$ and $\infty$ elsewhere. This is a rate-labelled support functional; it is not $-n^{-1}\log$ of an individual clock cell. A clock cell contains discretization entropy and must not be mistaken for a tube probability.

Assume (R) for the declared constraint on every finite-action word. Then $I_n+\mathrm{indicator}_C$ $\Gamma$-converges to $I+\mathrm{indicator}_C$ on $H$.

Liminf: if $h_n\to h$ in $H$ and $\liminf I_n(h_n)<\infty$, convergence eventually fixes the same word $w$. Each $h_{n}$ lies in $O_{w}\cap C_{w}$; closedness of $C_{w}$ and the definition of $S_{w}$ give $h\in S_{w}\cap C_{w}$. Since the toll is constant on the word, the liminf is $A(w)=I(h)$.

Recovery: fix $h\in S_{w}\cap C_{w}$. By (R), find points of $O_{w}\cap C_{w}$ approaching $h$. A nonempty rational relatively open polyhedral cell has rational points dense in it, so choose such points $h^{(j)}$ with rational time coordinates $t_l/T$. Let $D_{j}$ be a common positive integer denominator. Because $M_{n}$ contains $n!$, every coordinate of $h^{(j)}$ is on the actual source clock for all $n\ge D_j$. At each fixed $h^{(j)}$, all strict order and gate margins are positive. As $\delta_n\to 0$ the safety margin is smaller than these margins; and because $b_{n}$ grows like $4\log_2 M_n$ while $-\log(\delta_n e^{-na_e})=\log M_n+O(n)$, every required rounded probability $q_{e}$ is positive for all sufficiently large $n$. The no-event probability is $\ge 1/2$. Therefore that exact constrained history has positive probability in $H_{n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. Choose an increasing diagonal schedule $j(n)\to\infty$ slowly enough to meet the denominator, margin, and precision conditions. Then $h_n=h^{(j(n))}$ is exactly endpoint/obstacle admissible, converges to $h$, and $I_n(h_n)=A(w)=I(h)$.

This proves the claim. It is actual source-supported recovery on the same clock and carrier, with exact endpoints and obstacles, not a generic fixed-start approximation.

Necessity: if $h$ is in $S_{w}\cap C_{w}$ but outside $\operatorname{closure}(O_w\cap C_w)$, no sequence from $H_{n}\cap C$ can converge to $h$ because $H_{n}$ is a subset of $O_{w}$. Hence no recovery theorem for these source ledgers is possible there. Condition (R) is exact, not an arbitrary stronger gate.

#### 4. Two explicit tests

1. In the hard-gate witness, for word (01,12), impose endpoint $x(1)=1/3$. Once sector 2 is reached, $x$ is constant, so this means $t_2-t_1=1/3$. The positive set has $1/4<t_1<2/3$ and $t_2=t_1+1/3$. Its closure includes the endpoint times $(t_1,t_2)=(1/4,7/12)$. Thus (R) holds for the full constrained support. Taking $t_1=1/4+1/j$ and $t_2=t_1+1/3$ gives exact rational constrained recovery for $j$ large. A purely dyadic grid could never represent $t_2-t_1=1/3$; $n!\,2^{n^2+c}$ does so for every $n\ge 3$.

2. Instead impose endpoint $x(1)=1/4$. This forces $t_2-t_1=1/4$, so $k_{12}=0$ at every such exact history. The constrained support $S_{w}\cap C_{w}$ is nonempty, but $O_{w}\cap C_{w}$ is empty. Recovery fails, exactly as (R) predicts. The ambient LDP rate at that boundary remains 2; conditioning on an exact measure-zero endpoint is a different problem. Neither the ambient LDP nor the source construction claims a positive probability for that exact endpoint event.

The finite witness/checker implements both tests using exact rational arithmetic, along with the graph, accessibility, source normalization, and calibrated action checks. It does not treat finite testing as proof of the all-input theorem.

<a id="theorem-q01t-common-clock-native-jump-limit-and-complete-whole-cell-compiler"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1t (Common-Clock Native Jump Limit and Complete Whole-Cell Compiler).**

#### 1. Exact sequence

Use the full original matrix $N=72I+16A+5J$ on the 276 pairs of a 24-set. Let

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_0&=J/276,\quad P_1=(6A+12I-J)/132,\quad P_2=(460I-23A+2J)/506, \\
\lambda&=(2156,392,40),\quad d_s=1/\lambda_s,\quad v_{sj}=P_s e_j.
\end{aligned}
$$

These are rational mutually orthogonal projectors of ranks 1,23,252, and $N=\sum\lambda_sP_s$. Every original cross term is retained. For integer $r\ge 1$, on time [0,1] take independent signed Poisson channels of rates $r^3d_s/2$ and jumps $\pm v_{sj}/r^2$. This is $m_r=r^2$ in the requested moderate-deviation sequence. There are $K=1656$ marked signed channels. Drift is zero, covariance per unit time is exactly $N^{-1}/r$, and total event rate is

$$
\Lambda_r=r^3 D,\quad D=276(1/2156+1/392+1/40).
$$

All rates and increments are rational. Endpoint $e_{p}$ is attainable for every $r$: take exactly $r^{2}$ positive jumps in each of channels $(s,p)$, $s=0,1,2$, and no others. The observed physical horizon is always one; $r$ is the LDP speed, not a clock conversion.

The speed-r Hamiltonian is

$$
H_r(p)=r^2 \sum_{sj} d_s[\cosh(p\cdot v_{sj}/r)-1].
$$

Put $H_0(p)=p^TN^{-1}p/2$. The Taylor series with nonnegative even terms gives

$$
0\le H_r(p)-H_0(p)\le [\sum_{sj} d_s(p\cdot v_{sj})^4 \cosh(|p\cdot v_{sj}|/r)]/(24r^2).
\tag{1}
$$

Since $\lVert v_{sj}\rVert\le1$ and $\sum_{sj}d_s=D$, on $\lVert p\rVert\le R$ this is at most $DR^{4}\cosh(R)/(24r^{2})$. Thus convergence is uniform on compact dual sets with a populated remainder. Also $H_r(p)\le H_1(p)$ for all $r\ge1$, by the same series.

#### 2. Path LDP on the common unit clock

We give the argument, including the compactness step. For a partition $0=t_0<\dots<t_k=1$, independence and the Poisson exponential formula give exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}
r^{-1}\log \mathbb{E} \exp[r \sum_i p_i\cdot (X_r(t_i)-X_r(t_{i-1}))] \\
&=\sum_i (t_i-t_{i-1}) H_r(p_i).
\end{aligned}
$$

By (1) its limit is the everywhere finite differentiable strictly convex quadratic sum. Exponential tilting proves the finite-dimensional upper/lower bounds: at a prescribed increment $a$ over duration $h$, tilt by $p=Na/h$; under this tilt its mean tends to $a$ and its covariance tends to zero, and the log likelihood has limit $p\cdot a-hH_0(p)=a^TNa/(2h)$. Exponential Markov bounds and compact covering give the upper bound. Gaussian coercivity makes the finite-dimensional rate good.

For path compactness, apply the exponential martingale separately to each signed coordinate on a time window of length h. For each fixed $a>0$ its maximal-increment bound is at most

$$
\begin{aligned}
&2\cdot 276 \exp[-r(a \epsilon/\sqrt{276}-h C_a)], \\
C_a &= \max_{j,\text{sign}} H_1(\text{sign}\, a e_j)<\infty.
\end{aligned}
$$

Cover $[0,1]$ by at most $2/h$ overlapping windows; oscillation over any interval of length at most $h$ is controlled by one of the windows of length at most $2h$, with a harmless factor two in $\epsilon$. Therefore for fixed $\epsilon$, sending $h$ to zero and then $a$ to infinity gives arbitrarily negative exponential rates for the modulus violation. The same bound with $h=1$ controls the supremum norm. The deterministic jump bound is $\max\lVert v_{sj}\rVert/r^2\le 1/r^2$ and tends to zero.

To state the uniform-topology conclusion on continuous paths without asserting that discontinuous paths belong to $C$, replace $X_{r}$ by the polygonal interpolation of its values on the deterministic grid of size at most $r^{-4}$. The preceding martingale bound and a polynomial union bound show that its uniform distance from $X_{r}$ is superexponentially small: for every $\epsilon>0$ the $\limsup$ of $r^{-1}\log$ of that probability is $-\infty$, since $a$ is arbitrary. The interpolated process is exponentially tight in $C([0,1],\mathbb{R}^{276})$. Finite-dimensional bounds, compact covering, and this exponential tightness give the full good path LDP; the original cadlag process has the corresponding LDP in the usual Skorokhod topology and the same continuous finite-rate paths.

Its rate is the supremum over partitions of

$\sum_i(x(t_i)-x(t_{i-1}))^TN(x(t_i)-x(t_{i-1}))/(2(t_i-t_{i-1}))$.

This equals $I_0[x]=(1/2)\int\dot{x}^{T}N\dot{x}$ when $x(0)=0$ and $x$ is $H^1$, and $\infty$ otherwise. Proof: Cauchy-Schwarz bounds each partition energy by the integral for $H^1$ paths; conditional averages of the derivative on refining partitions converge in $L^2$. Conversely, bounded partition energies give weakly compact piecewise-constant derivatives whose integrals converge to $x$, so $x$ is $H^1$ and the same lower bound holds. This identifies precisely the original native Definition-T.13 action, not just its endpoint number.

#### 3. Equicoercive action Gamma-limit and exact boundary recovery

Let $L_r=H_r^*$ and $F_r[x]=\int L_r(\dot{x})$ for absolutely continuous $x$ starting at 0, $\infty$ otherwise. These are the deterministic local actions of the $r$-dependent jump shapes; the actual speed-$r$ triangular-array LDP has limit $I_0$ as proved above.

For every $a>0$ and every $v$, choose $p=av/\lVert v\rVert$ (or $p=0$ if $v=0$). Since $H_r\le H_1$,

$$
L_r(v)\ge a\lVert v\rVert-C(a),\quad C(a)=\max_{\lVert p\rVert=a}H_1(p)<\infty.
$$

The supremum of these lower bounds over $a$ is a nonnegative superlinear function $\Psi(\lVert v\rVert)$. Thus bounded $F_{r}$ implies uniform integrability of derivatives, uniform boundedness of paths and uniform equicontinuity, hence relative compactness in the uniform topology. This proves equicoercivity, including on the closed fixed-endpoint class $x(1)=e_p$.

For uniform $x_r\to x$ and any $C^1$ dual test $p(t)$, integration by parts and (1) yield

$$
\liminf F_r[x_r]\ge \int p\, dx-\int H_0(p)\,dt.
$$

Taking the supremum over such $p$ gives $I_0[x]$, including $\infty$ when the distributional derivative is not $L^2$. This proves $\Gamma$-liminf without assuming convergence of velocities. Since $H_r\ge H_0$, one has $L_r\le L_0$. Local uniform convergence of $H_r$ and Gaussian coercivity of $H_0$ imply $L_r(v)\to L_0(v)$ for each $v$: maximizers stay bounded because $H_r\ge H_0$, and (1) controls that compact dual set. Therefore the constant recovery sequence $x_r=x$ works for every finite-energy path by dominated convergence, as $0\le L_r(\dot{x})\le L_0(\dot{x})$. It preserves both endpoints EXACTLY. Infinite-energy points impose no recovery upper-bound obligation. Hence $F_{r}$ $\Gamma$-converges equicoercively to $I_0$ on the full starting-point class and on the original fixed-endpoint class.

For endpoint $e_{p}$, Jensen gives $\min F_r=L_r(e_p)$, with the linear witness $te_{p}$. The limiting minimum is $e_{p}^{T}Ne_p/2=77/2$. There is also an explicit bound, using $p=Ne_p$ in the dual formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}
77/2-E_r &\le L_r(e_p)\le 77/2, \\
E_r&=[\sum_{sj} d_s u_{sj}^4 \cosh(|u_{sj}|/r)]/(24r^2),\quad u_{sj}=v_{sj}^{\mathsf T} N e_p.
\end{aligned}
$$

Put $U_4=\sum_{sj}d_su_{sj}^4$, an exact rational number computed by the checker. Since $|u_{sj}|\le\lambda_s\le 2156$, for $r\ge 2156$, $\cosh(|u|/r)<2$ and $E_r\le U_4/(12r^2)$. The half-history on $[0,1/2]$ has action $L_r(e_p)/2$, converging to $77/4$ without any clock renormalization.

#### Exact endpoint and linear-witness recovery in the actual laws

An integer-count argument proves the stronger local result here, rather than inferring it from the LDP. Set $u_{sj}=v_{sj}^TNe_{p}$ and prescribe signed count means

$$
\mu_{sj,\pm}(r)=(r^3 d_s/2)[\sqrt{1+(u_{sj}/r)^2} \pm u_{sj}/r].
$$

Their endpoint mean is exactly $e_{p}$, because their signed differences are $r^2d_su_{sj}$. Round each mean to an integer. Multiply all rational $v$ by a fixed common denominator, giving a fixed integer lattice $G$. The rounded endpoint-count discrepancy from $r^2e_p$, in these integer units, lies in $G$ and remains in a fixed bounded set. Membership follows from the exact three-channel endpoint representation. For each possible discrepancy choose once an integer channel correction. There are only finitely many such discrepancies; the maximum correction is $O(1)$, independent of $r$. All means grow proportionally to $r^{3}$, so corrected counts are nonnegative for large $r$ and give endpoint EXACTLY $e_{p}$.

The independent Poisson probability of this count vector has log probability equal to minus its count-relative entropy plus $O(\log r)$ per channel, by Stirling. Bounded count corrections change entropy by $o(r)$. The unrounded entropy divided by $r$ is

$$
r^2 \sum_{sj} d_s\, \ell(u_{sj}/r),\quad \ell(z)=z \operatorname{asinh}(z)-\sqrt{1+z^2}+1,
$$

which tends to $(1/2)\sum d_su_{sj}^2=77/2$. Thus $\liminf r^{-1}\log P(X_r(1)=e_p)\ge -77/2$. The endpoint closed-ball LDP upper bound, followed by ball radius tending to zero, gives the matching limsup. Therefore the exact-point exponent is $77/2$.

Conditionally on these count vectors, each channel's event times are independent uniform points. Centered bridge fluctuations after multiplication by $v/r^2$ have uniformly vanishing size in probability: the expected squared maximal empirical-count deviation is bounded by a constant times its count $O(r^3)$, hence the scaled bound is $O(1/r)$; the finite channel sum preserves convergence. The mean path differs from $te_{p}$ only by the bounded count correction divided by $r^{2}$. Hence every fixed uniform tube around $te_{p}$ together with the exact endpoint has the same limiting exponent. The dyadic compilation couples the exact channel word, so (S1)'s superexponential total-variation bound transfers this exact-endpoint result, as well as the witness-tube lower bound, without subtracting a conditioning normalization. Exact digital fixed-boundary recovery is therefore proved for this original native endpoint. Arbitrary obstacles or U/Y boundary data are not inferred.

#### 4. What action transport is now actually proved

Take the limiting source response class to be $H^1$ paths from 0 to $e_{p}$, with identity quotient (distinct paths are distinct registered native responses), source action $I_0$, map $\Phi(x)=x$, and observable $\rho(x)=B\dot{x}$. Then every native T.13a-type mathematical diagram commutes: endpoints and unit clock are unchanged, domination is equality historywise, $x^*=te_p$ is saturating, and $B^TB=N>0$ makes $\rho$ separate paths with fixed start. All this is derived as the rate/action limit of the explicit source sequence and its finite implementation, rather than by assigning a Ramsey action toll or declaring a desired exponent.

The qualifier “native” is essential. Identity quotient is the specified coordinate-source quotient; it has not been proved equal to the original electroweak gauge quotient. B dot x is its original incidence readout, not an independently derived physical electroweak observable. No CP-odd nonzero midpoint readout, Berry/APS operator family, chiral transport, or S3 single-budget allocation is supplied by a symmetric Poisson law. In particular an odd observable of an invariant unconditioned symmetric ensemble has zero mean; adding a physical CP source needs its original certificate. This supplies the common-sequence jump/native-action component; the sector-action realization is supplied separately below.

#### Exact same-sequence whole-cell digital supplier
#### 1. Finite digital law and comparison

Use the exact rational projector channels of Theorem Q.0.1s, $K=1656$, $D=276\sum_s 1/\lambda_s$. At stage $r$ set

$$
l=r^2+20,\quad M=2^l,\quad \delta=1/M,\quad b=4l+r+20.
$$

At each of the first M-1 ticks give signed channel (s,j,sign) the probability

$$
q_{sj,\mathrm{sign}}=2^{-b} \lfloor 2^b \delta r^3/(2 \lambda_s)\rfloor.
$$

The remaining probability is “no event.” At the last tick set every event probability to zero. This preserves the prior no-terminal-event convention. Record an event at its tick's right endpoint, adding sign $v_{sj}/r^2$. Each row is an exact integer partition of $b$ fair bits; no transcendental or real oracle is used. All $q$ are strictly positive, and the event sum is below $1/2$. Indeed $D<8$ and $8r^3/2^{r^2+20}<1/2$ for integer $r\ge 1$. The last tick's guard does not affect endpoint accessibility: $M-1>3r^2$ and every needed channel has positive $q$.

Couple the original independent Poisson source and this law by total marked proposals at rate $\Lambda_r=r^3D$. The probability of any tick with two proposals is at most $\Lambda_r^2/(2M)$. The difference between an at-most-one Poisson row and its first-order row is bounded conservatively by $2\Lambda_r^2/M$ after summing ticks. Rounding costs at most $KM2^{-b}$; suppressing the last tick costs $\Lambda_r/M$. Thus

$$
P(\text{any channel-word mismatch})\le 3 \Lambda_r^2/M+K M 2^{-b}+\Lambda_r/M.
\tag{S1}
$$

The logarithm of its right side divided by $r$ tends to $-\infty$. On successful coupling events have the same marks and times differ by at most $\delta$. Their uniform coordinate-path difference is at most $1/r^2$, because there is at most one proposal per tick. Polygonal interpolation of the digital grid values changes the step path by at most $1/r^2$. Therefore the implemented digital response is exponentially equivalent at speed $r$ to the source of Theorem Q.0.1s, and has the SAME full path LDP and native action. No absolute-probability error is mistaken for relative rare-event control; (S1) is superexponential and hence is negligible against every fixed finite-action open tube with a finite exponent.

All events stay on the same unit observation clock. There is no state-dependent gate in this specific constant-rate source; the old state-dependent gated source and its support guards are retained unchanged as a separate construction. This compiler does not claim to transfer arbitrary U/Y boundary constraints.

#### 2. Explicit finite reversible construction

Store each channel's count, the tick, and last outcome. A snapshot fits in

$$
s=(K+1)(l+1)+\lceil \log_2(K+1)\rceil
$$

bits. (The l+1 count bits cover M.) The next snapshot is the deterministic function F of the old snapshot and a b-bit seed that selects a channel from the integer probability row. The update increments that channel's count and the tick. The endpoint and path coordinates are exact rational functions of the count record. Invalid snapshots receive a fixed default update, making F a total finite Boolean function.

A complete truth table has at most $D_F=s\,2^{s+b}$ output bits. A truth-table XOR circuit using fresh output bits, multi-controlled NOTs and clean AND/uncompute ancillas computes $F$ without erasure. A conservative primitive X/CNOT/Toffoli count is

$$
R=s\, 2^{s+b}[4(s+b)+1],
$$

with at most s+b clean workspace bits. Each input pattern is tested by complementing zero-controls, computing its conjunction, toggling the requested outputs, and uncomputing. Every old snapshot and seed is retained. Nothing is reset or discarded. Generate each seed by b Hadamards on fresh zero payloads; because seeds remain orthogonal recorded labels, the final computational response has exactly the same law as independent fair bits even if the full state remains coherent. Its ordinary computational instrument, with fresh owned pointer payloads, is the one already specified by the source leaves.

Let $o=\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil$ and $S=M(b+R+o+1)$. This bounds the raw payload computation, seed generation, outcome-pointer copying and padding slots. ROM, a one-hot cursor and readout records are retained. A controlled execution slot (ROM enable and cursor enable), including clean-control conjunctions, a controlled primitive and cursor advance, uses at most 64 of the already admitted X, H, CNOT, Toffoli and controlled-H pulses. Controlled-Toffoli is synthesized by clean AND/uncompute; no new arbitrary-matrix gate leaf is needed. Write $Q=64S$ for a padded pulse count during observation.

For an explicit noncircular upper bound on all storage, put

$$
Z=s+b+S+D_F+M+K+100,\quad N_{\mathrm{cells}}=2^{Z^2}.
$$

This enormously conservative value exceeds snapshots $(M+1)s$, seed bits $Mb$, workspace, $D_{F}$ truth-table bits, $S$ cursor bits, pointer and record bits, and a full gate-address ROM of at most $S[6\lceil\log_2 N_{\mathrm{cells}}\rceil+100]$ bits, plus a finite binary description of the integers and formulas above. Unused cells are padding and remain owned and charged. This is a terminating constructive family, not a practical or uniform resource estimate. Enumerating $F$, outputting its circuit, assigning consecutive payload addresses and writing the padded ROM is a concrete finite constructor at every $r$; all integer arithmetic is exact.

#### 3. Join to the admitted small-cell source leaves

The independently supplied Theorem C.6c.Q02a declares C8 modules with two predictive-core qubits and one independently addressable payload, the ready core and zero payload, admitted finite X/H/CNOT/Toffoli/controlled-H pulses on named supports, computational instruments, owned ROM/cursors and finitely driven control. The compilation above uses only those leaves. Allocate EVERY seed, snapshot, work, ROM, cursor and pointer bit to the payload of a distinct such cell; count its full three-qubit carrier and its baseline, not just the payload. The core is untouched by payload computation. The cell's demonstrated qualifying two-CNOT core protocol remains available on its independent core; it need not be rerun during every payload tick. Programme-loaded/runtime cells are evolved admitted cells, as expressly allowed in that source record.

Thus the compiler uses assemblies of the declared C8 primitive family. It is not the old numerical packing experiment, nor a recovery of the original structural universal presentation; its source-relative domain is the displayed finite supplier grammar, and the global comparison with the original MPU is a separate question. Geometry is an ordinary finite cabinet assembly with one cubic-centimetre cell volume, not a source-derived electroweak geometry or a new emergent-manifold theorem. No unlisted current sheet or spatial sensor is used here.

#### 4. Clock, energy, stock and retention

Use $\tau_0=1$ second for the native baseline $e_b=\hbar/\tau_0$ per whole cell. At the observation stage pad the prescribed pulse list to $Q$ slots and set $\tau=1\,\text{second}/Q$. Every involution pulse has the admitted generator $\pi\hbar(I-U)/(2\tau)$, norm at most $\pi\hbar/\tau$. All core and payload idles carry the declared baseline. No bounded-power claim is made.

The owned carrier is $3N_{\mathrm{cells}}$ qubits, baseline energy $N_{\mathrm{cells}}e_b$ and cabinet volume $N_{\mathrm{cells}}$ cubic centimetres. The ready source has two pure bits per cell (core-high and payload) and one degenerate maximally mixed core-low bit. Its supplied excess ready-stock free energy is $2N_{\mathrm{cells}}\ln 2/\beta$. This is supplied preparation stock, not a claim of finite-time exact thermal reset. The baseline and its native cost are separate from this entropy excess.

Installation of ROM and initial cursor needs at most $N_{\mathrm{cells}}$ X pulses of duration $\tau_0$ each, leaving all records owned; denote the actual count $W\le N_{\mathrm{cells}}$. It is preparatory time, explicitly outside the fixed one-second observed history. Total owned duration is $W\tau_0+1$ second, with full carrier qubit-time $3N_{\mathrm{cells}}(W\tau_0+1\,\text{second})$. A constructor producing the finite ready assembly and its ROM uses the admitted delivery/installation service; no microscopic manufacturing efficiency or autonomous battery is inferred.

Observation peak control norm is at most $\pi\hbar Q/(1\,\text{second})$. The sum of absolute on/off switching-work expectations is bounded by $2\pi\hbar Q^2/(1\,\text{second})$. Installation contributes at most $2\pi\hbar W/\tau_0$. Each ideal pulse begins and ends at idle; its two switching expectations cancel because its propagator commutes with its generator, so no net ideal quench work is hidden by this gross-throughput bound. Ready stock, baseline, programme, clock and archive remain charged even when this ideal net work is zero. If an autonomous waveform supplier or finite-power refinement limit is required, that is not supplied by this finitely driven branch and is not claimed here.

The physical unit clock is therefore paid with stage-dependent pulse strength and very large retained stock. There is no second unpaid continuum clock, silent seed disposal, cyclic reset, dropped purifier, or partial-cell resource count. These resources establish a finite implementation of the native stochastic response. They do not establish an original electroweak action/observable, APS family or baryon transport interpretation.

<a id="theorem-q01u-spatial-su2-interval-index-gauge-faithful-coordinate-and-scalar-contraction"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1u (Spatial SU2 Interval Index, Gauge-Faithful Coordinate and Scalar Contraction).**

#### 1 Geometry and operator with no connection collars

Fix $R>0$ and $X=[0,1]\times SU(2)$, oriented by $dt$ followed by the standard left-invariant spatial volume. The metric is $dt^2+R^2\,ds_{\mathrm{unit}}^2$. For the degree-one identity map $g:SU(2)\to SU(2)$, write

$$
\begin{aligned}
\theta&=g^{-1}dg=(i/2) \tau_a e_L^a, \\
ds_{\mathrm{unit}}^2&=(1/4) \sum_a(e_L^a)^2, \\
\int \operatorname{tr}(\theta^3)&=24 \pi^2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The Pauli matrices $\tau$ act on the fundamental rank-two isospin bundle and $\operatorname{tr}((\tau_a/2)(\tau_b/2))=\delta_{ab}/2$. Let

$$
a_f=f(t)\theta,\qquad a_f(\partial_t)=0,
\tag{1}
$$

where $f$ is smooth on the closed unit interval, $0\le f\le 1$, $f(0)=0$ and $f(1)=1$. There is no collar-flat requirement. The distinguished history is $f_*(t)=t$. In particular its normal curvature component is nonzero at each endpoint, so it cannot be turned into a product connection near the boundary by a smooth gauge change.

The curvature and its primitive topological number are

$$
\begin{aligned}
F_f&=f'\, dt \wedge \theta+(f^2-f)\theta^2, \\
Q_W&=-(1/(8\pi^2)) \int_X \operatorname{tr}(F_f \wedge F_f) \\
&=[3f^2-2f^3]_0^1=1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
$$

The gravitational degree-four form is zero for the fixed product metric. This computation is a direct curvature calculation; no collar-dependent geometric index formula is used here.

Let $J_a=-iE_a^L$, where $E_a^L$ is dual to $e_{L}^{a}$, and let $\sigma$ act on the two spatial spin components. The actual spatial operator in the fixed left frame is

$$
\begin{aligned}

A_f&=-H_f.
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
$$

The standard fixed-left-frame spatial normalization is given by Gibbons and Steif (1994), equations (4.10), (4.12) and (4.13).

Here is the exact four-dimensional identification, which does not require f' to vanish. In the product frame take skew Clifford matrices

c(dt)&=\begin{bmatrix}0&-I\\ I&0\end{bmatrix}, \\
c(e^a)&=\begin{bmatrix}0&i \sigma_a\\ i \sigma_a&0\end{bmatrix}, \\
-c(dt)c(e^1)c(e^2)c(e^3)&=\operatorname{diag}(I,-I).
\end{aligned}
$$

The upper two spinor components are positive chirality. Product temporal spin transport, temporal gauge in (1), and a time-independent volume density identify both chiral L2 spaces with L2([0,1],H), where

$$
H=L^2(S^3_R,\mathbb{C}^2_{\mathrm{spin}} \otimes \mathbb{C}^2_{\mathrm{iso}}).
$$

The identifications are unitary; no time reparametrization, density multiplier depending on t, omitted temporal gauge term or normalization change occurs. The lower-left block of the covariant Dirac expression is exactly

U_- D_X^+ U_+^{-1}=\partial_t+A_f=\partial_t-H_f.
\tag{4}
$$

The derivative of f enters curvature but not an additional term in this first-order minimally coupled Dirac expression. Equation (4) holds on smooth sections and then on the closed boundary realization described next.

#### 2 Boundary projectors and the interval index theorem

Write $B_f=H_f$ for the intrinsic spatial operator with the final-boundary convention $c_{\mathrm{boundary}}(v)=c(dt)c(v)$. On the positive chiral bundle $c_{\mathrm{boundary}}(e^a)=-i\sigma_a$, whereas the spatial coefficient in (4) uses $+i\sigma_{a}$. Consequently

$$
B_f=-A_f.
\tag{5}
$$

This is a derived Clifford sign, not a relabeling of an abstract matrix path. With the initial and final endpoints still named 0 and 1, impose

$$
u(0) \in H_{\ge 0}(B_0),\qquad u(1) \in H_{<0}(B_1).
\tag{6}
$$

The free spectrum has smallest absolute eigenvalue 3/(2R), and $B_{1}$ is gauge-unitarily equivalent to $B_{0}$. Thus both endpoint kernels vanish. Under (5), (6) is precisely

$$
u(0) \in H_{<0}(A_0),\qquad u(1) \in H_{\ge 0}(A_1).
\tag{7}
$$

The inequalities in (6) reproduce original Y.4.3a's written trace projectors on this invertible-endpoint example. The absence of product connection collars is still a real change of analytic branch, so this index is denoted $I_{\mathrm{lin}}$ rather than claimed as a witness to that original definition.

Let

$$
\begin{aligned}
W&=\{u: \sum_j(1+j)^2 \lVert u_j\rVert^2<\infty\}, \\
E&=H^1([0,1];H) \cap L^2([0,1];W), \\
E_{\mathrm{APS}}&=\{u \in E \text{ satisfying (7)}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
$$

The endpoint traces in (8) retain their natural half-Sobolev regularity; (7) does not replace it by an arbitrary $L^2$ trace domain. Finite spatial harmonic sums form a core. The eigenvalues of $A_{0}$ grow linearly in $j$, so its graph norm is equivalent to the $W$ norm. Projection to $j\le J$ is finite rank and its tail $H$ norm is at most $(1+J)^{-1}$ times the $W$ norm. Therefore $W$ embeds compactly in $H$. Moreover

$$
\lVert A_f-A_h\rVert_{B(H)}\le 3\lvert f-h\rvert/R.
$$

Bounded self-adjoint perturbation gives self-adjointness on the same $W$ and equivalent graph norms. Hence $t\mapsto A_{f(t)}$ is norm-continuous in $B(W,H)$. These statements apply in particular to $f=t$ and require no endpoint flattening.

The needed analytic theorem states that a norm-continuous family of self-adjoint operators on a common compactly embedded graph domain has a Fredholm interval realization of $\partial_t+A$ with initial-negative and final-nonnegative spectral traces, whose index is the spectral flow. Its closed domain is (8), and its adjoint has complementary traces. No constant endpoint collar is among those assumptions. See van den Dungen and Ronge (2021, Assumption 4.1, Definition 4.2, Proposition 4.3 and Theorem 4.9).

Applying this theorem to the literal operator in (4) proves a closed Fredholm geometric boundary problem. The smooth product spinor maps U_+,U_- preserve (8) and carry (6) to (7); equality on the smooth core therefore extends to equality of the closed realizations. In particular this is an actual domain-and-codomain unitary identification, with both endpoint projectors transported.

The paper's constant extension of A outside the interval is an auxiliary analytic proof construction. This result neither extends the physical clock nor claims that such exterior intervals are resource-free physical collars.

#### 3 Full spatial spectral flow and gauge endpoints

For completeness the spatial decomposition, including all noncrossing modes, is as follows. Scalar Peter-Weyl spin $j$ has right multiplicity $2j+1$. Coupling $J$ with $S=\sigma/2$ and $T=\tau/2$ gives grand-spin branches:

gives $A_1=U^{-1}A_0U$ on $W$. Multiplication by $g$ changes a scalar harmonic $j$ only to $j\pm 1/2$, so $U$ and $U^{-1}$ preserve $W$. This is continuum endpoint gauge equivalence. **Finite-cutoff endpoint defect and full-CAR realization.** Retain every scalar Peter–Weyl shell $j=0,1/2,\dots,J$, with $L=2J$, including the right multiplicity $2j+1$. #### 4 A field-defined quotient coordinate rather than a free scalar label

There is a precise gauge-invariant way to recover f on this limited spatial branch. Fix the trivialization used above and let

For a smooth gauge map $k:[0,1]\times S^3\to SU(2)$, the change of CS on each slice is the same integer: its degree is constant along $t$. The spatial exact-form term integrates to zero on $S^3$. Because $h$ is strictly increasing on $[0,1]$, with $h(0)=0$ and $h(1)=1$, the entire function $f=h^{-1}(q_f)$ is recovered from the field history modulo gauge. Let $\Gamma_{\mathrm{hom}}$ be the gauge saturation of all histories (1) in Section 1. The quotient $\Gamma_{\mathrm{hom}}/\text{gauge}$ is exactly the set of those functions $f$: gauge-equivalent histories have the same $q$ and hence $f$, and histories with the same $f$ are gauge equivalent by the definition of saturation. This statement includes the topology of a full based history. \rho_{\mathrm{hom}}([a])(t)&=Be\, f'(t).

It preserves the original endpoints and unit clock, is gauge invariant, and its response separates this homogeneous quotient: equality of $\rho$ gives equality of f' because Be is nonzero, and the common initial value fixes f. In particular it is not merely an arbitrary matrix coordinate called a gauge field. The inverse of h has a singular derivative at 0 and 1; no uniformly Lipschitz extension to unrestricted field histories is claimed. #### 6 A stronger homogeneous Yang Mills action obstruction

Let $C=12\pi^2/g_{\mathrm{YM}}^2>0$ with the physical coupling fixed independently, and retain the actual Euclidean action on this spatial connection:

$$
\begin{aligned}
S_{\mathrm{YM}}[f]&=C \int_0^1 [R(f')^2+(4/R)V(f)]\,dt, \\
V(f)&=f^2(1-f)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{13}
$$

This follows from the electric and magnetic field strengths in (2), the fundamental trace and volume $2\pi^2R^3$. The second term is the magnetic action; it is nonzero for $f=t$. In particular

$$
S_{\mathrm{YM}}[t]=C(R+2/(15R)).
\tag{14}
$$

There is a stronger failure than the existence of an extra term. Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
f_\epsilon(t)&=t-\epsilon V'(t), \\
V'(t)&=2t(1-t)(1-2t),\qquad 0<\epsilon<1/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{15}
$$

Since $-1\le V''(t)\le2$ on $[0,1]$, $f_\epsilon'>0$; it has the same endpoints, stays in $[0,1]$, and obeys

$$
f_\epsilon(1-t)=1-f_\epsilon(t),\qquad f_\epsilon(1/2)=1/2.
$$

Hence (15) remains in the smooth monotone complement-symmetric history class, has the same spatial boundary data and the same unique Dirac crossing at the original midpoint. Direct differentiation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
d/d\epsilon\, S_{\mathrm{YM}}[f_\epsilon] \text{ at } 0 \\
&=-(4C/R) \int_0^1(V')^2\,dt \\
&=-8C/(105R)<0.
\end{aligned}
\tag{16}
$$

The electric first variation is zero because the perturbation vanishes at both endpoints. Exact polynomial integrals give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int(V')^2&=2/105,\qquad \int(V'')^2=4/5, \\
I_{\mathrm{St}}[\Phi_{\mathrm{hom}}(a_{f_\epsilon})]&=77/2+(154/5)\epsilon^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{17}
$$

This also yields a constructive strict decrease, without an unspecified small-o remainder. Taylor's theorem and $V''\le 2$ on the full admissible range give

$$
\begin{aligned}
S_{\mathrm{YM}}[f_\epsilon]-S_{\mathrm{YM}}[t] \\
&\le C/(105R)[-8\epsilon+(84R^2+8)\epsilon^2].
\end{aligned}
\tag{18}
$$

For example $\epsilon=1/(21R^2+4)$ lies in $(0,1/2)$ and makes the right side strictly negative for every $R>0$.

Therefore the following precise no-go holds. On any proposed physical class containing $t$ and the deformations (15), with proposed response map (11) and physical action exactly (13), no positive coupling and finite radius can satisfy both T.13a's witness equation at the field $t\theta$ and its all-path domination. If (14) is not 77/2, the witness fails. If it is 77/2, (18) gives $S_{\mathrm{YM}}[f_\epsilon]<77/2$ while (17) gives $I_{\mathrm{St}}[\Phi_{\mathrm{hom}}(a_{f_\epsilon})]>77/2$, contradicting domination. Even adjusting the overall coefficient after the fact cannot fix this functional failure.

This is a no-go for the stated homogeneous Yang-Mills map and neighborhood, not for every original electroweak action or transport. Higgs and other physical terms might change the first variation; another physically registered response map might send a different minimizer to te; an independently justified class could exclude these deformations. None of those repairs is supplied or ruled out here. Restricting to the singleton linear history after discovering the descending direction would not establish the original physical class or its source law.

#### 1 Exact finite-source observable and its current pullback

#### 2 Full path contraction with the exact coefficient

The established full native LDP has good rate

$$
I[x]=(1/2) \int x'^{\mathsf T} N x',
$$

on absolutely continuous fixed-start paths, and $\infty$ otherwise. Its path topology is uniform. The linear map $x\mapsto\ell^Tx$ is continuous. For an admissible scalar $y$, every lift has the unique decomposition

$$
x=ye+z,\quad \ell^{\mathsf T} z=0,\quad z(0)=0.
$$

Because $e^{T}Nz'=77\ell^Tz'=0$ almost everywhere,

$$
I[x]=(77/2) \int (y')^2+(1/2) \int z'^{\mathsf T} N z'.
\tag{3}
$$

$N$ is positive definite. Therefore the infimum over all lifts is attained uniquely at $z=0$. If a finite-rate lift exists then $y$ is $H^1$; conversely $x=ye$ is a finite-rate lift for every fixed-start $H^1$ $y$. The contraction principle gives the full good scalar path LDP

$$
J[y]=(77/2) \int (y')^2,\qquad y(0)=0,
\tag{4}
$$

with value $\infty$ off that class. Equivalently $\ell^TN^{-1}\ell=1/77$. There is no conditioning on a line and no use of an empty-interior event.

The same coefficient follows from the actual source's connected current functional. Substituting $J_{\mathrm{full}}=bj/77$ into the established full-current generating functional $W(J_{\mathrm{full}})=(1/2)\int J_{\mathrm{full}}^TPJ_{\mathrm{full}}$ gives

$$
W_{\mathrm{scalar}}(j)=1/(2\cdot 77) \int j^2.

Its Legendre transform is (4). This checks the normalization by both path contraction and the original measured-current source map.

For endpoint $y(1)=1$, (4) has unique minimizer $y=t$ and value $77/2$. The full native minimizing lift is exactly $X=te$. The exact finite-source scalar endpoint subprobability also has this rate: its upper bound follows from the closed scalar endpoint fiber, while its lower bound follows from the already proved exact native $X_r(1)=e$ subprobability and its pinned LDP, which is a subset of $Y_r(1)=1$. The lower argument works for every relative open scalar-path neighborhood by lifting $y$ to $ye$. It does not require all microscopic paths to equal their minimizing lift.

<a id="theorem-q01v-same-word-full-car-checkpoint-channel-with-admitted-pulse-compilation"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1v (Same-Word Full-CAR Checkpoint Channel with Admitted Pulse Compilation).**

<a id="theorem-q01w-owned-coefficient-input-yang-mills-selector-and-full-normalized-boundary-law"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1w (Owned Coefficient-Input Yang-Mills Selector and Full Normalized Boundary Law).**

\nu_r(D)&=\sum_\omega p_r(\omega) q_r(\omega) 1_E(\omega) 1_D(f_\omega) \\
&\quad+ (1-Q_r) 1_D(0), \\
Q_r&=\sum_\omega p_r(\omega) q_r(\omega) 1_E(\omega).
\end{aligned}
$$

This is a normalized probability measure. The complementary term includes both selector rejection and endpoint rejection. There is no q-dependent state reset and no denominator.

Let $C_0=C([0,1],[0,1])$ with initial value 0 and uniform topology. Define the closed admitted history domain

$$
\Gamma=\{\text{the constant vacuum path } 0\} \cup E.
$$

This is a source protocol boundary restriction fixed before any asymptotics. The two components are separated by uniform distance at least 1. The same definition applies at every finite stage. The full good LDP on the ordinary ambient C0 has rate

$$
K[f]=\begin{cases} 0, & f \text{ identically } 0; \\ J_a[f]+\beta \int V(f), & f \in E \cap H^{1}; \\ +\infty, & \text{otherwise}. \end{cases}
$$

**Proof.** The known exact-endpoint subprobability has its relative good LDP with rate $J_a$. $H(f)=\beta\int V(f)$ is bounded and uniformly continuous. Local upper/lower LDP bounds multiplied by $\exp(-rH)$, followed by finite compact covers and exponential tightness, give the weighted subprobability rate $J_a+H$ on $E$. The uniform multiplicative comparator bound preserves it. In particular $Q_{r}$ has exponent $-m$, where $m=\inf_E(J_a+H)\ge a>0$. Hence $1-Q_r$ tends to 1 and has rate zero. Adding its atom at 0 gives the stated LDP by the finite union bound for closed sets and by considering whichever component meets a given open set. $E$ is closed in $C_0$, so its relative closed subsets are ambient closed; exponential tightness is inherited from the proposal because weights are at most 1, together with the one added compact atom. The rate is good because $J_{a}$ is good and $H$ is nonnegative continuous. The rate is infinity at every other path because a sufficiently small uniform neighborhood separates it from both support components; $\Gamma$ is closed. This proves the total normalized law, not a law conditioned on $A_{r}=1$. QED.

On $\Gamma$ this is exactly the local homogeneous action: $K[f]=\int[a|f'|^{2}+\beta V(f)]$, including the vacuum where it vanishes. Its extension outside the **declared** admissible boundary domain is infinity. This is not a claim that the scalar observation is an unconstrained Markov diffusion whose finite local Lagrangian assigns this rate to every scalar path. The latent finite ROM/cursor update is the actual finite ND-RID dynamics; the retained field is the specified output. The prescribed boundary-domain restriction must be retained in every Q.0.1c use.

#### 5 Minimum, exact endpoint tube, and symmetry

The direct method gives an attained minimum $m(a,\beta)$ on $E$: bounded action gives an $H^1$ bound, uniform compactness, weak $H^1$ lower semicontinuity of kinetic energy, and uniform continuity of the bounded potential. Every admissible path joins 0 to 1.

A quantitative strict gap is elementary. Write $f(t)=t+g(t)$, $s^{2}=\int|g'|^{2}$, with $g(0)=g(1)=0$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\int |f'|^{2}&=1+s^{2}, \\
|g(t)|&\le\sqrt{t(1-t)}\, s\le s/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

On $[0,1]$, $V$ has Lipschitz constant $L=1/(3\sqrt{3})$, and $\int_0^1 V(t)\,dt=1/30$. Thus $\int V(f)\ge 1/30-Ls/2$. If $s^{2}\le 3/100=1/(900L^{2})$, the potential integral is at least $1/60$. Otherwise the kinetic excess is at least $3a/100$. Therefore

$$
m(a,\beta)\ge a+\min(\beta/60,3a/100)>a.
$$

There is also a complete global characterization, without numerical shooting. There is a unique $E_0>0$ solving

$$
\sqrt{a} \int_0^1 [E_0+\beta V(u)]^{-1/2}\,du=1.
$$

The left side decreases strictly from infinity to zero, using $V(u)\sim u^{2}$ at the endpoint. Define $f_{*}$ implicitly by

$$
t=\sqrt{a} \int_0^{f_{*}(t)} [E_0+\beta V(u)]^{-1/2}\,du.
$$

It is smooth, strictly increasing, and has exact endpoints. For any absolutely continuous competitor,

$$
\begin{aligned}
a f'^{2}+\beta V(f) \\
&=a \left(|f'|-\sqrt{(E_0+\beta V(f))/a}\right)^{2} \\
&\quad+2 \sqrt{a} \sqrt{E_0+\beta V(f)}\, |f'|-E_0.
\end{aligned}
$$

The integrated weighted total variation is at least its endpoint integral. Equality holds precisely on this increasing solution, proving uniqueness and

$$
m=2 \sqrt{a} \int_0^1 \sqrt{E_0+\beta V(u)}\,du-E_0.
$$

The potential symmetry proves $f_{*}(1-t)=1-f_{*}(t)$, hence $f_{*}(1/2)=1/2$ and equal half-actions $m/2$. The latter is an action symmetry, not a physical CP or exact baryon prefactor theorem. The minimizer has nonzero endpoint velocities $\sqrt{E_0/a}$, so it does not acquire forbidden connection collars. The linear path is not stationary when $\beta>0$; the previously displayed deformation lowers its action, giving $m<a+\beta/30$.

An actual **ambient** transition tube is, for example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
T_\delta&=\{f \in C_0: \lVert f-f_{*}\rVert_\infty<\delta \text{ and } f(1)>1/2\}, \\
&0<\delta<1/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

It is open in C0. Its closure excludes the vacuum. Every finite-stage output in this tube has endpoint exactly 1, because all non-vacuum outputs come from the endpoint-success branch. Every finite-rate path in its closure belongs to E and has action at least m; f_* lies in its interior and attains m. For the closed initial basin {0} and closed terminal basin [1/2,1],

$$
\begin{aligned}
\inf_{T_\delta^{\mathrm{interior}}} K &= \inf_{\operatorname{closure}(T_\delta)} K \\
&= \inf_{f(0)=0,\, f(1) \in [1/2,1]} K = m, \\
\lim_r (1/r) \log \nu_r(T_\delta)&=-m.
\end{aligned}
$$

This is exactly the interior/closure/minimum condition, while successful physical gauge endpoints remain 0 and 1. We do not claim that E itself has ambient interior. The larger tube contains off-support intermediate-endpoint paths, but those have infinite source rate and zero finite-stage probability. This is why the explicit vacuum-fallback source change matters.

#### 6 Normalization, repeat attempts, and what the source law does not say

There are three distinct normalizations:

- Filter alone: $Z_r=\mathbb{E}[q_r(\omega)]$ has rate 0, since $\inf(J_a+H)=0$ at the unpinned vacuum path. Its normalized unpinned selected law has the same rate $J_a+H$, although its exact finite normalization is not generally 1.
- Filter plus endpoint: $Q_{r}$ has rate $m$. Its normalized successful bridge has rate $I_{\beta}-m$. That subtraction is never called the absolute Yang–Mills action.
- Full output with vacuum fallback: $\nu_{r}$ is already normalized and its transition probability has absolute rate $m$, as proved above. The failure probability has rate 0.

If one demands a successful transition on demand, independent fresh attempts require mean attempt count $Q_r^{-1}=\exp[rm+o(r)]$. A finite $L$-attempt bank fails with probability $(1-Q_r)^L$. It cannot guarantee success. To make this at most $\delta$, take $L\ge\log(\delta)/\log(1-Q_r)$, rounded up, using the exactly computable finite dyadic $Q_{r}$. Parallel attempts multiply the owned carrier, pure stock, installation and record budget; serial attempts multiply preparatory time and use fresh owned banks unless a separately supplied reset protocol is admitted. Retain the all-failed output. Amplification changes the unconditional transition probability and therefore cannot preserve the old rare-transition exponent while claiming near-certain delivery. No repetition or reset is used in the present one-shot construction.

#### 7 Same field and finite Dirac supplier, with all resources paid

For each actual accepted word use its own $f_{\omega}$ in the existing no-collar connection and operator:

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_f&=-R^{-1}(2 \sigma \cdot J+3/2+f\, \sigma \cdot \tau), \\
D_X^{+} &\text{ identified with } \partial_t+A_f, \\
&\text{initial trace in } H_{<0}(A_0),\ \text{final trace in } H_{\ge 0}(A_1).
\end{aligned}
$$

These are precisely the previously proved transported projectors and Clifford sign; they are not replaced by the intrinsic $B$ family. Successful endpoints are the same gauge-equivalent $A_0,A_1$, and the entire endpoint fiber has primitive interval index $+1$ and Chern–Weil number 1. The vacuum fallback has constant $A_{0}$ and index 0. At finite CAR cutoff $J$ use the same full $m_J$-mode CAR target, filled negative $A_{0}$ sea, and physical C8 checkpoint compiler. The programme is now controlled by the single complete record $(\omega,u,A_r)$; its target coefficient is $f_{\omega}$ or 0 as specified in Section 4. No independently prepared word is used for the action, index or driver.

For every registered finite transcript choose the existing uniform per-word channel error $\epsilon_r=\exp(-r^{2})$, accounting for the full Fock norm and all readout dilations. The classical pointer law and $F_{r}$ readout remain exact. The uniform conditional quantum bound survives rare selection without division by $Q_{r}$. The old autonomous Fourier-clock supplier may also be used only with its actual enlarged-support, positive-baseline and clock-stock ledger; it is not needed for this finite driven construction. Neither compiler makes its instantaneous microscopic Hamiltonian or switching work equal to Yang–Mills action.

The new selector uses only fresh Hadamard bits, exact Boolean comparisons built from $X$/CNOT/Toffoli, AND, pointer copies, and the admitted computational instrument. For a completely explicit terminating implementation, tabulate $k_r(\omega)$ and $E_{r}$ over the finite original seed words. A truth-table XOR circuit for the total Boolean function $(\omega,u)\to A_r$ uses at most $2^d(4d+1)$ elementary comparison/uncompute slots before controlled-slot padding, with $d$ the finite input bit count, and $O(d)$ clean workspace. No unknown real gate is required. A more efficient arithmetic circuit is optional. Failed inputs and invalid states receive specified total default updates.

Let $B_{\mathrm{log}}$ count every original seed, snapshot, outcome and raw counter, the $n_{r}$ selector seeds, selector and endpoint pointers, old and new ROM tables, every arithmetic/workspace bit, all matter occupations and driver labels. Let $Q_{\mathrm{pre}}$ and $Q_{\mathrm{obs}}$ be the complete finite padded preparation and observation gate counts, and $L_{\mathrm{cat}}$ the total programme catalogue length before physical addresses. Put

$$
Z=B_{\mathrm{log}}+Q_{\mathrm{pre}}+Q_{\mathrm{obs}}+L_{\mathrm{cat}}+100,\quad N_{\mathrm{cells}}=2^{Z^{2}}.
$$

The earlier whole-cell address bound applies after these additions, not with the old numerical cell count. All $d$-bit truth tables, gate addresses, one-hot cursors, clean scratch, failed-seed archives, pointers and padding fit in this conservative finite bound. Each bit uses the payload of one whole three-qubit C8 cell. The two qualifying core bits remain intact. The physical inventory is $3N_{\mathrm{cells}}$ qubits and $N_{\mathrm{cells}}$ cubic-centimetre cabinet volumes, with $N_{\mathrm{cells}}\,\hbar/(\text{one second})$ baseline throughout.

Installation has $W\le N_{\mathrm{cells}}$ $X$ pulses. Give every installation and preparation pulse one second, so $T_{\mathrm{pre}}=(W+Q_{\mathrm{pre}})$ seconds, followed by the unchanged one-second observation. Retain the entire carrier for $T_{\mathrm{pre}}+1$; its qubit-time is $3N_{\mathrm{cells}}(T_{\mathrm{pre}}+1)$. Ready stock is two pure bits per cell and one maximally mixed zero-Hamiltonian core bit, with the admitted $2N_{\mathrm{cells}}\ln 2/\beta_{\mathrm{thermal}}$ supplied free-energy inventory. This is fresh initial stock, not a finite-bath exact reset theorem. Nothing is erased or cyclically reused.

For observation slots $\tau_{j}>0$ summing to one second, admitted pulse norms are bounded by $\pi\hbar/\tau_j$ and gross switching work by $2\pi\hbar\sum_j(1/\tau_j)$. Equal padding gives peak $\pi\hbar Q_{\mathrm{obs}}$ and gross $2\pi\hbar Q_{\mathrm{obs}}^{2}$ in the chosen second units. Installation/preparation add their actual pulses and gross work, bounded by $2\pi\hbar(W+Q_{\mathrm{pre}})$ in those units. Catalogue fabrication and drive service are the explicit original ideal source leaves, not free manufacturing. Growing power, stock, geometry, preparation time and archive are stated rather than claimed bounded.

<a id="theorem-q01ac-one-finite-coherent-source-for-rare-entry-histories-and-no-jump-response"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1ac (One Finite Coherent Source for Rare-Entry Histories and No-Jump Response).** Fix a finite directed acyclic graph $(V,E)$, initial vertex $v_0$, horizon $T>0$, nonnegative dimensionless tolls $a_e$, positive attempt rates $k_e$ in inverse seconds, a diagonal phase generator $H=\operatorname{diag}(E_i)$, and $\hbar>0$. These data are chosen before the requested response. Put
$$
r_e(n)=k_ee^{-na_e},\qquad R_i(n)=\sum_{e:i\to j}r_e(n),\qquad
\Lambda=\max_i\sum_{e:i\to j}k_e.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.1}
$$
Every missing edge has rate zero at every refinement. The finite instrument below has the same diagonal rare-entry history law, its coherent no-jump extension and a quantitative reduced-system GKSL limit. It supplies an explicit finite driven realization for each $n$, with its outcome stocks and control scales counted. It does not impose a bounded-resource continuum realization.

*Proof and construction.*

##### I. One clock, exact instrument and superexponential digital approximation

Choose a time unit $t_{\rm ref}>0$, let $M_n=\lceil(T/t_{\rm ref})e^{n^2}\rceil$, increasing it if necessary so $\delta_n=T/M_n$ and $\Lambda\delta_n\le1/2$. On $\mathbb C^{|V|}$ use
$$
K_0=\operatorname{diag}\left(e^{-iE_i\delta_n/\hbar}\sqrt{1-\delta_nR_i}\right),\qquad
K_e=\sqrt{\delta_nr_e}\,|j\rangle\langle i|\quad(e:i\to j).
\tag{Q.0.1ac.2}
$$
Their squared Kraus sum is exactly $I$. Each tick has a fresh outcome register with alphabet $\{0\}\cup E$. For history $h=(\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_{M_n})$, put $C_h=K_{\alpha_{M_n}}\cdots K_{\alpha_1}$ and $p_n(h)=\operatorname{Tr}(C_h\rho C_h^*)$. Classical rare-entry statements take $\rho=|v_0\rangle\langle v_0|$; coherent statements allow every density matrix and arbitrary spectators.

Fix $b_0\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ and choose $b_n=\lceil6n^2/\log2\rceil+b_0$. Round each $\delta_nr_e$ downward to a multiple $q_e$ of $2^{-b_n}$ and set $q_0(i)=1-\sum_{e:i\to j}q_e$. The rounded instrument has Kraus factors $\sqrt{q_e}|j\rangle\langle i|$ and diagonal $e^{-iE_i\delta_n/\hbar}\sqrt{q_0(i)}$. It is exactly complete. Its coherent isometry is
$$
V_q|i\rangle=e^{-iE_i\delta_n/\hbar}\sqrt{q_0(i)}|i,0\rangle
+\sum_{e:i\to j}\sqrt{q_e}|j,e\rangle.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.3}
$$
Distinct columns are orthonormal: the common no-jump label retains distinct vertex states, and each edge label has one fixed initial vertex. Thus the isometry has a finite unitary completion. A $b_n$-bit uniform integer and the row's cumulative dyadic table implement exactly the same population/outcome transition on diagonal inputs. The measured random seed implements this classical restriction; the coherent isometry supplies the quantum channel without replacing an unknown quantum input by a sampled classical label.

Couple the continuous-time chain of rates (Q.0.1ac.1) and the rounded tick chain using one rate-$\Lambda$ proposal clock and maximal coupling on each tick. Two or more proposals in a tick have probability at most $(\Lambda\delta_n)^2/2$. The first-order table differs from the exact one-tick transition by at most $C\Lambda^2\delta_n^2$, uniformly in states and $n$, and rounding adds at most $|E|2^{-b_n}$. Therefore
$$
\Pr(\text{coupling fails on }[0,T])
\le C\Lambda^2T\delta_n+M_n|E|2^{-b_n}.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.4}
$$
On success the complete ordered edge word agrees and every jump time moves by at most $\delta_n$. Consequently, in the marked-history topology of Theorem Q.0.1r,
$$
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log\Pr(d_{\mathcal H}(X_n,Y_n)>\varepsilon)=-\infty
\quad(\varepsilon>0).
\tag{Q.0.1ac.5}
$$
For this DAG, words have length at most $|V|-1$, so its marked carrier is a finite union of closed time simplices. The exact continuous density is
$$
f_{n,w}(t)=\left(\prod_{e\in w}k_e\right)e^{-nA(w)}
\exp\left[-\sum_{\ell=0}^{m}R_{i_\ell}(n)(t_{\ell+1}-t_\ell)\right],
\quad A(w)=\sum_{e\in w}a_e.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.6}
$$
Here $t_0=0,t_{m+1}=T$, and the empty-word probability is its survival factor. This factor is between $e^{-\Lambda T}$ and one. Theorem Q.0.1r, or its direct finite-word upper/lower proof applied to this density, gives rate $A(w)$ on each simplex, including limiting simultaneous cascades. Equation (Q.0.1ac.5) transfers it to the actual finite digital source. No independent microscopic-action normalization is inferred.

##### II. Reduced-system quantum approximation on the same clock

The continuous comparison generator is
$$
\mathcal L_n(\rho)=-\frac i\hbar[H,\rho]
+\sum_e\left(L_e\rho L_e^*-\frac12\{L_e^*L_e,\rho\}\right),\qquad
L_e=\sqrt{r_e}|j\rangle\langle i|.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.7}
$$
Scalar Taylor expansion of $\sqrt{1-x}$ for $0\le x\le1/2$ and of the phase in (Q.0.1ac.2), including spectators, gives one-step diamond expansion $\Phi_\delta=I+\delta\mathcal L_n+O(\delta^2)$ with a constant depending only on the fixed finite menu, $\Lambda$ and $\|H\|/\hbar$. Telescoping CPTP contractions yields
$$
\|\Phi_{\delta_n}^{M_n}-e^{T\mathcal L_n}\|_\diamond\le CT\delta_n.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.8}
$$
For rounding, each jump-amplitude change is at most $\sqrt{2^{-b_n}}$, and the no-jump change is at most $C|E|2^{-b_n}$ because its survival is at least $1/2$. Thus the isometries differ in norm by at most $C\sqrt{|E|2^{-b_n}}$; their reduced channels differ in diamond norm by at most twice this. The conservative accumulated bound is
$$
C M_n\sqrt{|E|2^{-b_n}}=O(e^{-2n^2}).
\tag{Q.0.1ac.9}
$$
Hence the same finite source supplies classical marked-record approximation and reduced-system quantum convergence. A joint coherent continuous-record limit would additionally require a common record-Hilbert embedding; it is not asserted by these two estimates. Finite-history traces remain exact as in Proposition X.1c.

##### III. Selective no-jump conditioning and off-diagonal response

For the continuum instrument the no-jump operator and probability are
$$
K_\varnothing(t)=\operatorname{diag}(e^{-iE_it/\hbar-R_it/2}),\qquad
s_t(\rho)=\sum_i\rho_{ii}e^{-R_it}.
$$
Its conditional state is $K_\varnothing\rho K_\varnothing^*/s_t(\rho)$. On a diagonal law $p$,
$$
\mathscr F_t(p)_i=\frac{p_ie^{-R_it}}{\sum_jp_je^{-R_jt}},
$$
$$
\mathscr F_t(\lambda p+(1-\lambda)q)
=\frac{\lambda s_t(p)\mathscr F_t(p)+(1-\lambda)s_t(q)\mathscr F_t(q)}
{\lambda s_t(p)+(1-\lambda)s_t(q)}.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.10}
$$
The normalized selection is generally nonlinear, while its unnormalized instrument and full unconditional evolution are affine and spectator compatible. Every jump gain $L_e\rho L_e^*$ is diagonal, so the generator gives exactly
$$
\rho_{ij}(t)=e^{-i(E_i-E_j)t/\hbar-(R_i+R_j)t/2}\rho_{ij}(0),\qquad i\ne j.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.11}
$$
On edges $01,12,02$ with tolls $a>0,0,b>0$ and prefactors $u,v,w>0$, the terminal-two exponent is $\min(a,b)$ by (Q.0.1ac.6). In contrast, as $n\to\infty$, $R_0\to0$, $R_1=v$, $R_2=0$. Thus the $01$ and $12$ coherences decay at limiting rate $v/2$, while $02$ has finite-$n$ decay rate $(ue^{-na}+we^{-nb})/2$ tending to zero. Its phase remains unless $E_0=E_2$. The zero-toll downstream edge can destroy coherence while adding no rare entrance toll. The two jump operators on $01,12$ do not commute: only $L_{12}L_{01}$ is nonzero.

The marked compactification cannot be replaced by a good discrete-sector $J_1$ principle. In this three-state example every compact $J_1$ set of paths starting at zero has a uniform positive initial interval $\varepsilon_K$ on which its paths stay zero. Otherwise a convergent subsequence with departure times tending to zero would violate right continuity at zero after time changes tending uniformly to the identity. A direct $02$ jump before $\varepsilon_K$ lies outside the compact set and has probability
$$
r_{02}\frac{1-e^{-R_0\varepsilon_K}}{R_0},\qquad
-\frac1n\log\left[r_{02}\frac{1-e^{-R_0\varepsilon_K}}{R_0}\right]\longrightarrow b.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.12}
$$
No compact family achieves exponential-tightness levels greater than $b$ on that $J_1$ space. The good marked-history result therefore has substantive topology and endpoint data.

##### IV. Exact finite driven source and normalized operational maps

Complete the columns of (Q.0.1ac.3) to a unitary $U_n$ by lexicographic Gram–Schmidt on the remaining computational basis vectors, skipping zero residuals. The finite construction depends only on its declared table, phases and clock. On the joint system and fresh outcome register choose
$$
G_n=\frac{i\hbar}{\delta_n}\operatorname{Log}U_n,\qquad
\|G_n\|\le\frac{\pi\hbar}{\delta_n},\qquad
 e^{-i\delta_nG_n/\hbar}=U_n,
\tag{Q.0.1ac.13}
$$
with unitary-log eigenphases in $(-\pi,\pi]$. This is a finite self-adjoint controlled Hamiltonian with the actual phase response. Padding to eight-level tensor factors is a Hilbert-carrier encoding, not an MPU minimality or functional-qualification proof. If a gate list is required, finite two-level elimination supplies its actual length $L_n$; subwindows $\delta_n/L_n$ have individual norm bound $\pi\hbar L_n/\delta_n$. No nearest-neighbor geometry is supplied by this factorization.

For the classical operational map, let the retained state be current vertex, tick and previous outcome, with fixed context containing the table, $\delta_n$ and tick arming. Verification probabilities are $q_\alpha(i)$, and the normalized update sends it to $(j(\alpha,i),k+1,\alpha)$. Define a fixed normalized update on zero-probability outcomes. For the quantum map use probabilities $\operatorname{Tr}\mathcal I_\alpha(\rho)$ and normalized state $\mathcal I_\alpha(\rho)/\operatorname{Tr}\mathcal I_\alpha(\rho)$ on nonzero branches, with tick advance, fixed perspective kernel $\delta_{s_0}$, and supplied arming at every tick. These populate the normalized verification/update and registered instrument interfaces of Definition 6 and Definition 27 on this source.

On the diagonal branch a predictive register may write the known row $q(i)$ before verification and update to $q(j(\alpha,i))$ after the outcome. Its Brier discrepancy is $\|q(i)-\operatorname{onehot}(\alpha)\|^2$, of mean $1-\|q(i)\|^2$. Relative to the uniform row on $r=|E|+1$ outcomes, the improvement is $\|q(i)-\operatorname{uniform}\|^2$, strictly positive for a nonuniform row. This is a concrete forecast/verify/update response. Coherent inputs are acted on by the instrument without copying an unknown state into that classical predictor.

##### V. Finite-horizon stocks, clock and control account

For this driven realization take idle Hamiltonian zero on the entire pulsed carrier, including system, work, records and ancillas. The $H$ in (Q.0.1ac.2) is an externally pulsed phase generator included in $U_n$, rather than a nonzero idle Hamiltonian. At inverse temperature $\beta$, each pure supplied ready register of dimension $D$ has excess free energy $\beta^{-1}\log D$ relative to its zero-Hamiltonian Gibbs state. Each fair Gibbs bit has zero excess. The coherent realization supplies $M_n$ pure outcome registers of dimension $r$, costing ready-stock free energy $M_n\beta^{-1}\log r$, together with the system preparation and every declared work/control/prediction register. Each additional pure dimension-$D_j$ factor contributes $\beta^{-1}\log D_j$; a supplied mixed input has its actual zero-idle excess free energy. All outcome registers and garbage are retained throughout the finite horizon; no reset is invoked.

A raw classical realization can use $M_n\lceil\log_2r\rceil$ archive bits, $b_n$ random-work bits, $\lceil\log_2|V|\rceil$ state bits, $\lceil\log_2(M_n+1)\rceil$ tick bits and a table of at most $|V|rb_n$ bits. Store the dyadic jump numerators and infer $q_0$ by the row remainder. Optional prediction/scoring workspace is additional and must be counted for that extension. The $M_nb_n$ independent fair-bit draws are preparation data; if retained rather than consumed, their full seed storage is counted separately. Lossless DAG compression can retain at most $|V|-1$ edge labels and tick indices plus length, with its actual compression/control cost.

Each constant gate Hamiltonian $G$ on a subwindow $\tau$ has two separately owned quench works $\operatorname{Tr}(G\rho_{\rm in})$ and $-\operatorname{Tr}(G\rho_{\rm out})$. Its expectation is conserved during its isolated pulse, so they cancel in net, while the absolute sum is at most $2\|G\|$. For $M_nL_n$ gates of duration $\delta_n/L_n$, a gross throughput bound is
$$
\mathcal W_{\rm gross}\le2\pi\hbar M_nL_n^2/\delta_n.
\tag{Q.0.1ac.14}
$$
This does not price construction or maintenance of the external clock/controller at zero. If a nonzero idle $H_0$ is retained instead, net switching work is $\operatorname{Tr}[H_0(\rho_{\rm out}-\rho_{\rm in})]$ and stock free energy uses $F(\rho,H_0)-F(\gamma_\beta,H_0)$; the zero-idle formulas no longer apply.

For a repeated cycle, any reset is charged by actual conditional entropy given the retained side information. Erasing all independent uniform seeds with no side copy has ideal heat lower bound $k_BT_{\rm bath}M_nb_n\log2$. Saturation requires a separate quasistatic realization; quantum ready-stock renewal has its own reset protocol. Source preparation, gate execution, clock, archive/compression, reset and calibration remain disjoint ledger entries. The explicit finite counts and norm bounds do not provide their physical prices or a bounded-power refinement.

Finally the toll ledger has reference-measure dependence. In dimensionless times $t/t_{\rm ref}$,
$$
-\log f^s_{n,w}=nA(w)-\sum_{e\in w}\log(k_et_{\rm ref})+\int_0^TR_{i(t)}dt.
$$
An individual digital jump-cell surprise contains $-\log\delta_n\asymp n^2$; integration over its time cells or use of this density reference removes that discretization entropy. The LDP uses tube probabilities. An independent factor $\kappa_A$ can give $\kappa_AA(w)$ action units, but neither the source nor its record dual identifies it with $\hbar$ or a mechanical action. This is a specified finite ordinary quantum instrument and controlled source, with the topology, resources and response limits stated above. $\square$

<a id="theorem-q01l-full-stopped-birth-path-ldp-with-an-entrance-correction"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1l (Full Stopped Birth Path LDP with an Entrance Correction).** Fix $a,T>0$. Let $\lambda:[0,a]\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous and nondecreasing, with

$$
\lambda(0)=0,\quad \lambda(x)>0\ (x>0),\qquad
\int_0^a|\log\lambda(x)|dx<\infty,\qquad
\int_0^a\frac{dx}{\lambda(x)}=\infty.
\tag{Q.0.1l.1}
$$

Let $m_n\ge1$ be positive integers, $a_n=m_n/n\le a$, $a_n\to a$, and $\delta_n>0\to0$ with $-n^{-1}\log\delta_n\to\kappa\in[0,\infty]$. The chain $X_n(0)=0$ jumps from $k/n$ to $(k+1)/n$ at rate $n[\lambda(k/n)+\delta_n]$ for $k<m_n$, and is absorbed at $a_n$.

On $D([0,T],[0,a])$ with the Skorokhod $J_1$ topology, its laws satisfy a good LDP of speed $n$. Define

$$
\tau_a(x)=\inf\{t\in[0,T]:x(t)=a\},\qquad \inf\varnothing=+\infty,
\tag{Q.0.1l.2}
$$

and let $\mathcal A_a$ be the nondecreasing absolutely continuous paths $x:[0,T]\to[0,a]$ with $x(0)=0$. For $\kappa<\infty$, the rate is

$$
I^a_\kappa(x)=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle \kappa\mathbf1_{\{x(T)>0\}}+
\int_0^{T\wedge\tau_a(x)} L(x(t),\dot x(t))dt,&x\in\mathcal A_a,\\
+\infty,&\text{otherwise},
\end{cases}
\tag{Q.0.1l.3}
$$

where for $0<x\le a$ and $v\ge0$,

$$
L(x,v)=v\log\frac v{\lambda(x)}-v+\lambda(x),\qquad
L(0,0)=0,
\tag{Q.0.1l.4}
$$

and $L=+\infty$ for other velocities (using $0\log0=0$). The value at the single first hitting time does not affect the integral. In particular $I^a_\kappa(0)=0$. For $\kappa=\infty$, the rate is zero at the identically zero path and $+\infty$ elsewhere. All finite sublevels are compact in the uniform topology as well as in $J_1$.

The same good LDP and rate hold on $C([0,T],[0,a])$ with uniform topology for the following continuous interpolation: join $(0,0)$ and every actual jump vertex $(t_j,j/n)$ by line segments, then hold the last value through $T$. Equally, any measurable continuous interpolation staying within $o(1)$, deterministically, of $X_n$ has this conclusion.

The entrance charge occurs once whenever the limiting path is nonzero. Waiting at zero before departure costs zero; holding still at a positive interior state costs $\lambda(x)$ per unit time; holding at the absorbing endpoint costs zero. The theorem does not charge the interior value $L(a,0)=\lambda(a)$ after absorption.

**Proof.**

**A. A constant-rate Poisson path reference, with its hypotheses checked.**

Let $Q_n$ be the law of $Y_n(t)=N(nt)/n$, where $N$ is a rate-one Poisson process, on $D([0,T],[0,\infty))$ with $J_1$. Its good rate is

$$
J(x)=\int_0^T\ell(\dot x(t))dt,\qquad \ell(v)=v\log v-v+1,
\tag{Q.0.1l.5}
$$

for nondecreasing absolutely continuous $x$ starting at zero, and $+\infty$ otherwise. Here is a direct proof of this reference assertion, so a theorem about a weaker Skorokhod topology is not being substituted.

For a finite time partition, increments are independent Poisson random variables with means $n\Delta t_i$. The normalized vector has log-mgf

$$
\frac1n\log E\exp\{n\sum_i\theta_i\Delta Y_{n,i}\}
=\sum_i\Delta t_i(e^{\theta_i}-1).
\tag{Q.0.1l.6}
$$

Its finite-dimensional LDP has rate $\sum_i\Delta t_i\ell(u_i/\Delta t_i)$ on nonnegative increment vectors. This follows directly from Stirling's formula for lattice probabilities, including the exact probability $e^{-n\Delta t_i}$ of zero increments, and exponential Chernoff tails; finite products preserve these bounds. Thus no boundary steepness claim at a zero increment is needed.

Take nested uniform dyadic partitions of mesh $h=T/2^r$. Let $P_hY_n$ linearly join their sampled values. Its finite-dimensional image LDP is good and its rate is

$$
J_h(z)=\sum_i h\ell\!\left(\frac{z((i+1)h)-z(ih)}h\right)
\tag{Q.0.1l.7}
$$

on the corresponding nondecreasing polygons, infinity otherwise. Monotonicity gives

$$
\|Y_n-P_hY_n\|_\infty\le\max_i\{Y_n((i+1)h)-Y_n(ih)\}.
\tag{Q.0.1l.8}
$$

For $\varepsilon>h$, the union bound and the Poisson Chernoff bound give

$$
\limsup_n\frac1n\log Q_n\{\|Y_n-P_hY_n\|_\infty>\varepsilon\}
\le-\varepsilon\log(\varepsilon/h)+\varepsilon-h,
\tag{Q.0.1l.9}
$$

which tends to $-\infty$ as $h\downarrow0$. The finite partition count contributes zero on the speed-$n$ scale. Uniform distance bounds $J_1$ distance, so (Q.0.1l.9) applies to that topology too.

For completeness the needed limiting-rate compactness is elementary. If $J_h(z)\le R$, its nonnegative slope $v_h$ has $\int\ell(v_h)\le R$. Superlinear growth of $\ell$ makes the slopes uniformly integrable with bounded total mass, hence the polygons are uniformly bounded and equicontinuous. Every sequence with $h\downarrow0$ and bounded cost therefore has a uniformly convergent subsequence with absolutely continuous limit $x$. Weak lower semicontinuity of the convex integral gives $J(x)\le\liminf J_h(z_h)$. This lower semicontinuity can also be read directly from

$$
\int\ell(v)dt=\sup_{f\in C([0,T])}\left\{\int fv\,dt-\int(e^f-1)dt\right\}.
\tag{Q.0.1l.10}
$$

Conversely, if $J(x)<\infty$, then $P_hx\to x$ uniformly and Jensen gives $J_h(P_hx)\le J(x)$. These compactness, lower-bound and recovery statements identify the limiting rate exactly as (Q.0.1l.5); they also prove it is good, with uniformly compact sublevels.

Here is explicitly how they give the path LDP. For an open neighborhood of a finite-cost $x$, choose $h$ so that $P_hx$ lies well inside it and the error exponent in (Q.0.1l.9) is more negative than $-J(x)-1$. The finite-dimensional lower bound, minus the error probability, gives the lower bound $-J(x)$. For a closed $F$,

$$
Q_n(F)\le Q_n(P_hY_n\in F^{\varepsilon})+
Q_n(d_{J_1}(Y_n,P_hY_n)>\varepsilon),
\tag{Q.0.1l.11}
$$

where $F^{\varepsilon}$ denotes the closed metric enlargement. Apply the polygon upper bound. If the resulting infima of $J_h$ stay bounded along $h\downarrow0,\varepsilon\downarrow0$, the preceding equicoercivity produces a limit in $F$ with no greater cost. If they do not stay bounded, their exponent tends to $-\infty$. Taking first suitably small $h$ for each fixed $\varepsilon$, then $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, proves the closed upper bound. This proves the full good $J_1$ reference LDP, including exponential control beyond compact sets.

**B. Bounded extension and the exact finite-(n) likelihood.**

Extend the rate by $b(x)=\lambda(x)$ on $[0,a]$ and $b(x)=\lambda(a)$ for $x>a$. Then $b$ is bounded, continuous, nondecreasing, zero only at zero, and log-integrable on every bounded interval. Write $M=\lambda(a)>0$. Let $Z_n$ be the unstopped pure-birth chain with rates $n[b(k/n)+\delta_n]$ for every $k\ge0$. For large $n$, all rates are bounded by $n(M+1)$, which proves nonexplosion by Poisson domination.

On a count history $z$ with $j=nz(T)$ jumps, multiplication of the successive holding-time densities, including survival from the last jump through $T$, gives the exact likelihood

$$
\frac1n\log\frac{dP_n}{dQ_n}(z)
=\frac1n\sum_{k=0}^{j-1}\log(b(k/n)+\delta_n)
-\int_0^T[b(z(t))+\delta_n-1]dt.
\tag{Q.0.1l.12}
$$

Jump-time values and left limits have the same time integral. Formula (Q.0.1l.12) is a true density, not an unnormalized tilt: both sides come from nonexplosive birth-process path densities, the rates are positive at every finite $n$, and these densities integrate to one. The $j=0$ case is included, with empty sum. No separately chosen normalizing constant is allowed.

For $j\ge1$, separate the $k=0$ term and define

$$
\kappa_n=-\frac1n\log\delta_n,\quad
B(y)=\int_0^y\log b(u)du,\quad
\Phi(z)=B(z(T)) -\int_0^T[b(z(t))-1]dt.
\tag{Q.0.1l.13}
$$

The primitive $B$ is finite and continuous, including at zero.

**C. Uniform singular Riemann convergence.**

For every finite $K$,

$$
\sup_{1\le j\le nK}\left|
\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{j-1}\log(b(k/n)+\delta_n)-B(j/n)
\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{Q.0.1l.14}
$$

An explicit justification handles arbitrary decay schedules $\delta_n$. On $[\epsilon,K+1]$, positivity and continuity imply uniform convergence of $\log(b+\delta_n)$ to $\log b$, and ordinary Riemann sums converge uniformly in their partial endpoint. Near zero choose $\epsilon$ so that $b(2\epsilon)<1$. For large $n$,

$$
|\log(b(k/n)+\delta_n)|
\le |\log b(k/n)|+\log(M+1)^{+}.
\tag{Q.0.1l.15}
$$

The function $-\log b$ is nonnegative and nonincreasing on $(0,2\epsilon]$. Thus for $l\le n\epsilon$,

$$
\frac1n\sum_{k=1}^{l}|\log b(k/n)|
\le\int_0^{l/n}|\log b(u)|du\le\int_0^\epsilon|\log b(u)|du.
\tag{Q.0.1l.16}
$$

The latter tends to zero with $\epsilon$. A possible final cell and the omission of the endpoint cell are controlled by absolute continuity of the integral of $|\log b|$, uniformly in their positions on a compact interval. This proves (Q.0.1l.14), not only convergence at one fixed terminal point. In particular no hidden uniform lower bound on $b(1/n)$ or polynomial floor assumption is used.

Consequently, on $1\le nz(T)\le nK$, (Q.0.1l.12) equals

$$
-\kappa_n+\Phi(z)+r_{n,K}(z),\qquad
\sup|r_{n,K}|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{Q.0.1l.17}
$$

Let $E$ be the closed subspace of nonnegative nondecreasing càdlàg paths starting at zero. The map $\Phi:E\to\mathbb R$ is continuous in $J_1$: endpoints converge in $J_1$, $B$ is continuous, and $z_n(t)\to z(t)$ at every continuity point of $z$. A càdlàg path has at most countably many discontinuities, so boundedness and continuity of $b$ give convergence of its time integral by dominated convergence. On $\{z(T)\le K\}$, $\Phi$ is bounded above and below.

**D. The unstopped good LDP and the exceptional zero path.**

Suppose first $\kappa<\infty$. The candidate unstopped rate on $E$ is

$$
I_\kappa(z)=J(z)-\Phi(z)+\kappa\mathbf1_{\{z(T)>0\}},
\tag{Q.0.1l.18}
$$

and it is infinity outside $E$. Since $J(0)=T$ and $\Phi(0)=T$, the zero path has rate zero.
