H_n&=P_n^{2}/(2m),\quad B_n=\max_j p_j^{2}/(2m).
\end{aligned}
$$

On padding assign $P_{n}=0$ and $H_{n}=0$. The installed kinetic Hamiltonian is the quadratic expression in this momentum matrix. A supplied finite position comparison matrix is the cyclic central difference

$$
X_n=i\hbar(S_n-S_n^{*})/(2h_n),
$$

where $(S_n v)_j=v_{j+1}$ on the active cyclic index. It is zero on padding. It is a finite comparison observable: $X_{n}$ and $P_{n}$ satisfy no exact canonical commutation relation, and their canonical limit on a common core is proved in part 5. Its measurement, if requested, has a separately supplied finite Fourier-basis instrument.

The field/probe carrier has exactly zero idle Hamiltonian outside the two explicitly installed mechanical pulses. All preparation, transport, controller gaps and readout schedules retain this zero-idle convention.

The apparatus uses the primitive services of Definition C.6c.4a, the finite local driven matrix and record service boundary of the cabinet of Theorem Q.0.3l, with its own matrices, word and invoice supplied in part 8. All entries used here have finite algebraic, logarithmic or elementary-computable descriptors. At the ideal native boundary their calibrated finite coefficients and waveforms are supplied as couplings. A numerical realization carries the operator and instrument errors of part 9.

The kinetic path-action comparison starts at the appliance entrance after the paid transfers; transfer/preparation/control actions remain separate in the complete source invoice. The kinetic, raw-comparison and readout services share this one installed $P_{n}$ spectrum, the independently fixed $m,t,\hbar$ and one finite descriptor. Raw comparison, coherent unknown-input, and prepared diagnostic modes are separately registered before input. The raw mode measures its own prepared states; the coherent mode acts on the unknown input without measuring it.

#### 2. Two complete normalized raw Gaussian sources

Define

$$
\begin{aligned}
\alpha_j&=a p_j^{2}=\ln(2)\, \delta_n^{2} j^{2}, \\
Z_{F,n}&=\sum_j \exp(-\alpha_j),\quad Z_{R,n}=\sum_j \exp(-2\alpha_j), \\
f_n(j)&=\exp(-\alpha_j)/Z_{F,n}, \\
r_n(j)&=\exp(-2\alpha_j)/Z_{R,n}, \\
c_n&=\ln(Z_{F,n}/Z_{R,n})\ge 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

Supply two pure normal finite preparations

$$
\begin{aligned}
|F_n\rangle&=\sum_j \sqrt{f_n(j)}\, |j\rangle, \\
|R_n\rangle&=\sum_j \sqrt{r_n(j)}\, |j\rangle.
\end{aligned}
$$

Every amplitude is algebraic: $\exp(-\alpha_j)=2^{-j^{2}/4^{n}}$. Finite algebraic normalization and a full algebraic unitary completion give a concrete preparation matrix from a fresh basis state. A Householder preparation may be used when its denominator is nonzero, with the identity used for an already equal target; finite Gram–Schmidt is another terminating construction. The matrix, complete support, positive-duration implementation and source stock are paid. These are coherent Gaussian preparations of pure finite states.

The raw experiment measures the momentum basis with all $d_{n}$ outcomes retained. Both laws are normalized exactly. Their registered full-output likelihood ratio is

$$
L_n(j)=\ln[f_n(j)/r_n(j)]=\alpha_j-c_n.
\tag{Q.0.2g.1}
$$

This ledger can be negative. It is a raw comparison ledger in the sense of Definition Q.0.1, supplied by this stochastic implementation record; its values are log-likelihood ratios of either sign. The constant $c_{n}$ is retained as part of the ledger.

Each preparation follows one complete unchanged qualification prefix of the cells of Theorem C.6c.P17a, transported through payload SWAPs as specified in part 8 of this proof. If $h$ denotes any positive-probability complete qualification history, its law $q(h)$ is identical in the two experiments and independent of the fresh Gaussian preparation. The complete paired raw law on the declared comparison carrier is

$$
P_F(h,j)=q(h) f_n(j),\quad P_R(h,j)=q(h) r_n(j).
$$

Thus (Q.0.2g.1) holds also with every qualification history retained. Preparation choice and apparatus descriptor are retained; the registered comparison maps the F experimental choice to the R choice. All supplier services in the declared driven boundary are deterministic conditional on their predeclared choice, or have the same retained independent law; a stochastic arm-dependent supplier requires a new full law. The finite Gaussian preparations and basis instruments are trace-preserving native services on their declared fresh-state domain, so both laws contain every outcome.

For a registered finite sequence of independently supplied raw trials the product likelihood has additive sum of these $L_{n}$ values. Each repetition needs a fresh full preparation/record word and invoice.

#### 3. Positive kinetic, reference and echo Hamiltonians

Set the physical reference-arm energy

$$
E_{\mathrm{ref},n}=\hbar c_n/t.
$$

It is registered from the normalized source probabilities and the fixed energy and time units before any coherent response is requested; it is a normalization calibration chosen for this source. Its finite logarithmic coefficient is supplied and priced as a native coupling.

Let $\Pi_0=|0\rangle\langle0|$ and $\Pi_1=|1\rangle\langle1|$ on the probe. The first positive-duration pulse is

$$
\begin{aligned}
H_{\mathrm{first},n}(s)&=g(s)[H_n\otimes\Pi_0+E_{\mathrm{ref},n} I\otimes\Pi_1], \\
g(s)&=1-\cos(2\pi s/t),\quad 0\le s\le t.
\end{aligned}
$$

It is positive, continuous and zero at endpoints, and $\int g\,ds=t$. Its exact endpoint is

$$
W_n=\operatorname{diag}(\exp(-itH_n/\hbar),\ \exp(-ic_n)I).
\tag{Q.0.2g.2}
$$

The physically retained common free factor is field-dependent:

$$
\begin{aligned}
W_n&=(\exp(-itH_n/\hbar)\otimes I)\, R_n, \\
R_n&=\operatorname{diag}(I,\exp[i(\alpha(P_n)-c_n)]).
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.3}
$$

The common factor in (Q.0.2g.3) is an operator on the field and stays in the channel. The un-echoed $W_{n}$ is one separately nominated transport menu.

For the primary channel comparison supply a second positive-duration pulse, acting on the field and identically on both probe arms:

$$
H_{\mathrm{echo},n}(s)=g(s)[B_n I-H_n]\otimes I.
$$

Because the finite spectrum of $H_{n}$ lies in $[0,B_n]$, this Hamiltonian is positive: the inverse-free operation is implemented with its positive baseline. Its endpoint is $\exp(-itB_n/\hbar)\exp(+itH_n/\hbar)\otimes I$. The complete two-pulse endpoint is

$$
V_n=\exp(-itB_n/\hbar)\, R_n.
\tag{Q.0.2g.4}
$$

The scalar $\exp(-itB_n/\hbar)$, the baseline action $tB_n$, every intermediate kinetic motion and the Hamiltonians are retained in the path and source records. Only this scalar factor cancels from the channel. The baseline $B_{n}$ grows without bound as $n\to\infty$.

Consequently, for every admitted field/probe/reference state $\rho$,

$$
(\operatorname{Ad}(V_n)\otimes \mathrm{Id}_R)(\rho)=(\operatorname{Ad}(R_n)\otimes \mathrm{Id}_R)(\rho).
\tag{Q.0.2g.5}
$$

Equation (Q.0.2g.5) holds without selection or postselection. The external accepted-input cut and the canonical mechanical comparison cut are distinct. At the latter, both paid payload SWAP banks as well as all qualification/readiness operations have ended. Their exact action is $|\psi\rangle_{\mathrm{in}}|0\rangle_w|0\rangle_{\mathrm{app}}\to|0\rangle_{\mathrm{in}}|0\rangle_w|\psi\rangle_{\mathrm{app}}$, extended linearly to every mixed input and spectator. The input and payload factors are then fixed and independent of the unknown state. Thus the canonical appliance input is exactly the external logical input under the registered basis identification. From this mechanical cut every remaining supplier service before the end of the echo acts as identity on the unknown field/probe/reference except for the two displayed deterministic Hamiltonians; its retained histories therefore factor as the fixed channel (Q.0.2g.5) tensored with that supplier's instrument. This is a direct tensor-generator property of this declared driven source boundary; a physical driver that exports momentum or arm information requires its own proof.

The independently specified reference $R_{n}$ is the spectral/direct-sum extension of the phase reference of Theorem Q.0.2e: on each finite $|j\rangle$ sector it is exactly $\operatorname{diag}(1,\exp[iL_n(j)])$, using (Q.0.2g.1), and on superpositions it is its fixed linear coherent extension on the same $P_{n}$ spectral decomposition, a unitary channel. Equations (Q.0.2g.2)–(Q.0.2g.5) prove that the mechanical source implements that complete extension, including all off-diagonal field coherence and all reference entanglement. Because of the echo, the equality holds for the physical channel in the laboratory frame.

#### 4. Exact identifying scalar records inside the broader family

At $n=0$ the three momenta are $-p_*,0,p_*$. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
&Z_{F,0}=2,\quad Z_{R,0}=3/2,\quad c_0=\ln(4/3), \\
&L_0(0)=\ln(3/4),\quad L_0(1)=L_0(-1)=\ln(3/2).
\end{aligned}
$$

Both scalar sectors are ordinary admissible finite physical states. Their two nonzero ledger values have irrational ratio. Indeed if a rational relation exists, clearing denominators gives an integer relation between $\ln 3-2\ln 2$ and $\ln 3-\ln 2$; unique prime factorization forces both coefficients to vanish. Hence Proposition Q.0.2f identifies $\kappa_A=\hbar$ uniquely among positive action scales compatible with both scalar channel records.

Equation (Q.0.2g.5) holds for every field/probe/reference input and every grade; these two records provide the independent finite identifiability check. The higher grades, canonical dynamics and geometric records follow in parts 5 to 7.

Prepare $|j\rangle\otimes|+x\rangle$ by the paid source word, apply both pulses, and use independently specified finite $x$/$y$ projective probe detectors. Their complete outcome pairs are

$$
\begin{aligned}
p_{x,\pm}(j)&=[1\pm\cos L_n(j)]/2, \\
p_{y,\pm}(j)&=[1\pm\sin L_n(j)]/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.6}
$$

Both outcomes are retained and sum to one. The registered spectral controls of Theorem Q.0.2e are obtained on these finite sectors.

#### 5. Canonical normal limit, quadratic dynamics and errors

Use the momentum representation $K=L^{2}(\mathbb{R},dp)$, $P\psi(p)=p\psi(p)$, $X\psi(p)=i\hbar\psi'(p)$. The ideal kinetic energy $H=P^{2}/(2m)$ has its usual maximal multiplication domain. $C_c^{\infty}(\mathbb{R})$ is a common core for the polynomial expressions and is preserved by all phase multipliers below. Embed the finite active register by

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iota_n|j\rangle&=h_n^{-1/2}\, 1_{[p_j-h_n/2,\,p_j+h_n/2)}, \\
Q_n&=\iota_n \iota_n^{*}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Here $Q_{n}$ denotes this projection; the position observable is $X$. Its retained box has radius $R_n^{\mathrm{box}}=(J_n+1/2)h_n\to\infty$. Cell-average projections $Q_{n}$ tend strongly to $I$: uniform continuity proves the assertion on compact continuous functions, then density and contractivity prove it on $L^{2}$. These embeddings are analytic comparison maps.

##### Normalization and raw-law convergence

For $s=1,2$ put $I_s=\int\exp(-sa p^{2})\,dp=\sqrt{\pi/(sa)}$ and $A_{s,n}=h_n\sum_j\exp(-sa p_j^{2})$. Elementary cellwise variation and the Gaussian tail bound give

$$
\begin{aligned}
|A_{s,n}-I_s| &\le \varepsilon_{s,n}, \\
\varepsilon_{s,n}&=2h_n+\exp[-sa(R_n^{\mathrm{box}})^{2}]/(sa R_n^{\mathrm{box}}).
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.7}
$$

Indeed the total variation integral of $\exp(-sa p^{2})$ is 2, and its two outside tails are at most $\exp(-saR^{2})/(saR)$. Thus $c_n=\ln(A_{1,n}/A_{2,n})\to c=(\ln 2)/2$. Whenever $\varepsilon_{s,n}\le I_s/2$,

$$
|c_n-c| \le 2\varepsilon_{1,n}/I_1+2\varepsilon_{2,n}/I_2.
\tag{Q.0.2g.8}
$$

The embedded pure preparations converge in norm to the normal Gaussian wavepackets

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Phi_F(p)&=(a/\pi)^{1/4} \exp(-a p^{2}/2), \\
\Phi_R(p)&=(2a/\pi)^{1/4} \exp(-a p^{2}).
\end{aligned}
$$

For $u_s(p)=\exp(-sa p^{2}/2)$, piecewise sampling has $L^{2}$ error bounded by

$$
h_n \lVert u_s'\rVert_2 + \lVert 1_{|p|>R_n^{\mathrm{box}}}\, u_s\rVert_2.
$$

This follows by the fundamental theorem of calculus on each cell and Cauchy–Schwarz, with a conservative constant one. Normalization increases the bound by at most the factor $2/\lVert u_s\rVert_2$. It gives explicit preparation-state errors in norm. Their momentum measurements have densities

$$
\begin{aligned}
f(p)&=\sqrt{a/\pi}\, \exp(-a p^{2}), \\
r(p)&=\sqrt{2a/\pi}\, \exp(-2a p^{2}), \\
L(p)&=\ln[f(p)/r(p)]=a p^{2}-(\ln 2)/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.9}
$$

These are complete normalized spectral response laws on Lebesgue momentum measure, and the Radon–Nikodym identity holds almost everywhere for these normal-state measurements. Complete normalized poststates for individual momentum outcomes exist for the finite cabinets only.

##### Full coherent channel convergence

Define the ideal reference/action channel by the explicit unitary

$$
R=\operatorname{diag}(I,\exp[i(aP^{2}-c)]),\quad c=(\ln 2)/2.
\tag{Q.0.2g.10}
$$

The finite physical endpoint is $V_{n}$ from (Q.0.2g.4); its common scalar cancels only at channel level. Thus it suffices to compare $T_n=\iota_n R_n\iota_n^*$ with $R$. For a normalized field/probe/reference vector $\psi$ with momentum derivative and moment in $L^{2}$, set

$$
\begin{aligned}
e_n(\psi)&=h_n \lVert\partial_p\psi\rVert_2/\pi \\
&\quad+\lVert 1_{|p|>R_n^{\mathrm{box}}}\psi\rVert_2 \\
&\quad+a[h_n \lVert P\psi\rVert_2+h_n^{2}/4] \\
&\quad+|c_n-c|.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.11}
$$

Then $\lVert(T_n-R)\psi\rVert_2\le e_n(\psi)$. To see this, the cell Poincaré inequality bounds $\lVert Q_n\psi-\psi\rVert$ by the first two terms. On a cell, $|p_j^{2}-p^{2}|\le h_n|p|+h_n^{2}/4$ and $|\exp(iu)-\exp(iv)|\le|u-v|$. Extend the approximate phase outside the box by the exact phase for this proof only; projection still removes that outside component. This proves (Q.0.2g.11), including Hilbert-valued spectator vectors. The phase bound and projection strong convergence also prove strong convergence on every normal vector by compact approximation, without assuming its unbounded moments are finite.

For a normal joint density $\rho$, the positive embedded output $T_n\rho T_n^*$ has trace $\operatorname{Tr}(Q_n\rho)$; its missing weight is explicitly $\operatorname{Tr}((I-Q_n)\rho)$. It is retained without renormalization. Strong convergence and finite-rank approximation give trace-norm convergence to $R\rho R^*$. Quantitatively,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert T_n\rho T_n^{*}-R\rho R^{*}\rVert_1 \\
&\le 2 [\operatorname{Tr}((T_n-R)\rho(T_n-R)^{*})]^{1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.12}
$$

The factorization proof uses Hilbert–Schmidt Cauchy–Schwarz and $\lVert T_n\rVert\le 1$, $\lVert R\rVert=1$. Apply (Q.0.2g.11) to a purification or a supplied pure-state decomposition to obtain an explicit bound. The finite devices accept supplied normalized finite states, with their own approximation error added. The convergence is strong, state by state; it is not uniform in diamond norm over inputs of unbounded energy.

##### Canonical observables and motion

On $\psi\in C_c^{\infty}$ strictly inside the growing boxes, cube averaging commutes with integer-cell translations. Hence

$$
\begin{aligned}
\iota_n P_n \iota_n^{*} \psi &\to P\psi, \\
\iota_n X_n \iota_n^{*} \psi &\to X\psi.
\end{aligned}
$$

The central-difference derivative error is at most $\hbar h_n^{2}\lVert\psi'''\rVert_2/6$, plus the cell projection error for $i\hbar\psi'$. Wraparound is absent once the support and two-cell margin lie inside the box. Thus these finite matrices have the canonical limit on the common core.

The ideal echo channel obeys the exact common-core Heisenberg identity

$$
\begin{aligned}
R^{*} (X\otimes I) R &= X\otimes I -(t/m)P\otimes\Pi_1, \\
R^{*} (P\otimes I) R &= P\otimes I.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.13}
$$

This gives the backward-free shear on arm 1 and the identity on arm 0. Strong convergence of the unitaries leaves the limit of the finite unbounded responses open; it is proved from the exact conjugated-shift expression. If $\alpha(p)=ap^{2}$, $\Delta_{+}=\alpha(p_j+h_n)-\alpha(p_j)$, $\Delta_{-}=\alpha(p_j)-\alpha(p_j-h_n)$, its active-arm position change is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&(i\hbar/(2h_n))[(\exp(i\Delta_{+})-1)S_n \\
&\qquad-(\exp(-i\Delta_{-})-1)S_n^{*}].
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.14}
$$

On a fixed compact enlargement let $M_1=\max|\alpha'|$ and $M_2=\max|\alpha''|=2a$. The exponential remainder $|\exp(iu)-1-iu|\le u^{2}/2$, the mean-value theorem and translation/Poincaré bounds give the conservative direct error

$$
h_n \hbar\{(M_1^{2}/2+2M_2)\lVert\psi\rVert_2+2M_1\lVert\psi'\rVert_2\}
\tag{Q.0.2g.15}
$$

against $-(t/m)P\psi$ on that compact domain. The calculation is the explicit centered-shift expansion: the leading term is $-\hbar[(D_+\alpha)\psi_{j+1}+(D_-\alpha)\psi_{j-1}]/2$; each difference quotient differs from $\alpha'(p)$ by at most $h_{n}M_2$ on its cell, and each shift/average differs from $\psi$ by at most a conservative $2h_n\lVert\psi'\rVert$.

There is also a uniform weighted-tail bound. Every interior coefficient in (Q.0.2g.14) has magnitude at most $\hbar a(|p_j|+h_n/2)$. On the sole cyclic wrap edge the endpoint energies are equal, so its phase difference and position-change coefficient vanish exactly. Shift, cell-average and triangle inequalities therefore give, for example,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lVert\iota_n(R_n^{*}X_n R_n-X_n)\iota_n^{*}\psi\rVert_2 \\
&\le 4\hbar a\, \lVert(|P|+2p_{*})\psi\rVert_2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.16}
$$

This extends (Q.0.2g.13) from compact tests to supplied Gaussian/Schwartz inputs by choosing a compact cutoff first and then $n$. The bound (Q.0.2g.16) contains no factor $1/h_n$. The finite measurement of $X_{n}$, its conjugate or their difference, if requested, uses its supplied finite spectral instrument and its own precision record on separately prepared trials.

Equations (Q.0.2g.11)–(Q.0.2g.16) separate bounded-channel convergence, common-core canonical geometry and unbounded-observable response. Gaussian tails, derivatives and moments are explicit and finite. The baseline $B_{n}$ grows with n and remains in every finite invoice.

#### 6. Path records, endpoint polarization, Maslov and Berry typing

The physical finite sources have their exact matrices and channel records; their canonical phase-space comparison is supplied by the common-core and normal limits of part 5. Register the canonical coordinates $(x,p)$, the momentum wavefunction convention $\exp(+ipx/\hbar)$ in the inverse Fourier transform, and the Hamilton-principal spatial action $S_x=\int(p\,dx-H\,ds)$. Momentum-polarized action is

$$
S_p=S_x-[px]_{\mathrm{initial}}^{\mathrm{final}}.
\tag{Q.0.2g.17}
$$

This endpoint correction is explicit and is kept separate from $\kappa_{A}$.

During a raised-cosine pulse the mechanical flow parameter is $u(s)=\int_0^s g(v)\,dv$, with $u(t)=t$. The physical laboratory duration remains $t$; $u$ is the flow parameter of the time-dependent Hamiltonian. Momentum is constant. In the first pulse arm 0 has $x=x_0+p\,u(s)/m$, while arm 1 stays at $x_0$. During the echo both arms move by $-p\,u(s)/m$. Write $E=p^{2}/(2m)$, and retain the grade's $B_n,c_n$. The complete two-pulse path ledger is:

| arm | spatial displacement | $S_x$ | $[px]$ | $S_p$ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 0: free, then inverse-free | 0 | $-tB_n$ | 0 | $-tB_n$ |
| 1: constant reference, then inverse-free | $-pt/m$ | $-\hbar c_n-Et-tB_n$ | $-2Et$ | $Et-\hbar c_n-tB_n$ |

These values follow by integration. On the free segment, $p\,dx=2E\,du$ and $H\,ds=E\,du$, so $S_x=Et$. On the inverse segment $H\,ds=(B_n-E)\,du$ and $p\,dx=-2E\,du$, so $S_x=-Et-tB_n$. The constant first segment on arm 1 contributes $-\hbar c_n$. Equation (Q.0.2g.17) yields the last column.

The relative momentum-polarized action is therefore

$$
S_{p,1}-S_{p,0}=Et-\hbar c_n=\hbar L_n(p).
\tag{Q.0.2g.18}
$$

In the spatial-polarized record it is instead

$$
\begin{aligned}
S_{x,1}-S_{x,0}&=-Et-\hbar c_n, \\
-\Delta[px]&=+2Et,
\end{aligned}
$$

whose sum is (Q.0.2g.18). Both records are retained; the term $Et$ enters the momentum-polarized and the spatial relative action with opposite signs. The common $-tB_n$ is present in both absolute actions; it cancels in their difference and in the scalar channel quotient of (Q.0.2g.4), and it remains in the apparatus invoice.

##### Geometric contributions and domains

The probe projectors and the momentum frame are fixed. The construction transports no Hamiltonian eigenline and contains no adiabatic parameter loop, so the registered fixed-frame connection contribution, the Berry term of this family, is zero.

The classical transformations are free symplectic shears. The echo path of arm 0 retraces the shear and is a closed path with identity metaplectic endpoint; its oriented Maslov index is zero in $\exp(-i\pi\mu/2)$ convention. Arm 1 is an open negative shear. It has no interior focal crossing in the stated free coordinate-kernel chart; its interior Maslov index is zero. The kernel's initial endpoint polarization and square-root branch are fixed separately below. Thus the closed-branch specialization applies to arm 0 only, and exact open-path formulas govern arm 1.

For $u>0$ the exact free and inverse-free coordinate kernels, in the declared Fourier convention, are

$$
\begin{aligned}
K_u(x,y)&=\sqrt{m/(2\pi\hbar u)}\, \exp(-i\pi/4) \\
&\quad\exp[i m(x-y)^{2}/(2\hbar u)], \\
K_{-u}(x,y)&=\sqrt{m/(2\pi\hbar u)}\, \exp(+i\pi/4) \\
&\quad\exp[-i m(x-y)^{2}/(2\hbar u)].
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.19}
$$

These distributional kernels are comparison formulas. Their normalization and endpoint square-root phases follow by completing the Fourier Gaussian integral, with the branch continuous from positive real Gaussian regularization. Convolution $K_{-u}K_{u}$ is the identity as an operator on normal states. Thus the endpoint phases of the retraced echo cancel. The $\pm\pi/4$ Fourier endpoint factors are retained in the boundary/determinant convention and are distinct from an interior integer Maslov crossing.

Every propagation and shear above is exactly quadratic. The commuting time profile only reparametrizes u, so the finite-speed and higher semiclassical phase corrections vanish identically. The nonzero finite-grade errors are the separately bounded canonical discretization, state-preparation and service-precision errors.

#### 7. Normal Gaussian paths and complete observable records

Take the normal spatial packet

$$
\begin{aligned}
\psi_0(x)&=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/4} \\
&\quad\exp[-(x-x_0)^{2}/(4\sigma^{2})+ip_0(x-x_0)/\hbar],
\end{aligned}
$$

with $\sigma>0$ and finite $x_0,p_0$. Its momentum variance is $v=\hbar^{2}/(4\sigma^{2})$. Let $E_0=p_0^{2}/(2m)$, $\eta=\hbar t/(2m\sigma^{2})$, $b=\eta/2$. The packet and its finite approximants are supplied preparations with errors and costs.

Before the echo, the free arm's exact spatial packet is

$$
\begin{aligned}
\psi_t(x)&=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/4}(1+i\eta)^{-1/2} \\
&\quad\exp[-(x-x_0-p_0t/m)^{2}/(4\sigma^{2}(1+i\eta)) \\
&\qquad+ip_0(x-x_0)/\hbar-iE_0t/\hbar].
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.20}
$$

The square root is continuous from $t=0$ and equals one there. Its phase is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&p_0(x-x_0)/\hbar-E_0t/\hbar \\
&\quad+\eta(x-x_0-p_0t/m)^{2}/[4\sigma^{2}(1+\eta^{2})] \\
&\quad-(1/2) \arctan \eta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.21}
$$

At the moving center it is $+E_0t/\hbar-(1/2)\arctan\eta$. The first term there is the spatial principal action, the Gouy/determinant boundary phase is $-(1/2)\arctan\eta$, and the momentum-polarized phase is $-E_0t/\hbar$.

The following formulas are the canonical comparison wavepackets associated with a grade’s retained scalar baseline; the finite-grid wavefunctions approximate them with the errors of parts 5 and 9 of this proof. On the full real-line canonical space the operator $B_n-H$ is not positive, so the positive inverse-free pulse exists at finite grade only. After the full canonical comparison echo, arm 0 is $\exp(-itB_n/\hbar)\psi_0$. Arm 1 is $\exp[-i(tB_n/\hbar+c_n)]\psi_{-t}$, with

$$
\begin{aligned}
\psi_{-t}(x)&=(2\pi\sigma^{2})^{-1/4}(1-i\eta)^{-1/2} \\
&\quad\exp[-(x-x_0+p_0t/m)^{2}/(4\sigma^{2}(1-i\eta)) \\
&\qquad+ip_0(x-x_0)/\hbar+iE_0t/\hbar].
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.22}
$$

Its phase, excluding the retained constant $-tB_n/\hbar-c_n$, is

$$
\begin{aligned}
&p_0(x-x_0)/\hbar+E_0t/\hbar \\
&\quad-\eta(x-x_0+p_0t/m)^{2}/[4\sigma^{2}(1+\eta^{2})] \\
&\quad+(1/2) \arctan \eta.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.23}
$$

At its moving center $x=x_0-p_0t/m$ this is $-E_0t/\hbar+(1/2)\arctan\eta$, agreeing with the spatial-action row in part 6 of this proof and its exact boundary determinant. The phase-front term in (Q.0.2g.23) is retained away from that center.

The full Gaussian boundary correction is explicit. Its Gouy part has $|\Theta_G|<\pi/4$ for finite $t>0$; on a nominated $|x-x_{\mathrm{center}}|\le A\sigma\sqrt{1+\eta^{2}}$ window, the extra wavefront term has magnitude at most $\eta A^{2}/4$. Outside that window the exact formula still holds, and the wavefront term is unbounded in $x$. The probability of the excluded window is the known Gaussian tail, bounded for example by $2\exp(-A^{2}/2)$ for $A>0$. The Fourier endpoint convention in (Q.0.2g.19) and the complex Gaussian determinant in (Q.0.2g.20)/(Q.0.2g.22) are two descriptions of the same convolution calculation and are counted once.

##### Probe readout: normalized, possibly reduced-visibility, and correctly typed

With prepared probe $|+x\rangle$, the full ideal echo state, apart from the retained common scalar, is

$$
(\psi_0\otimes|0\rangle + \exp(-ic) \exp(+itH/\hbar)\psi_0\otimes|1\rangle)/\sqrt{2}.
$$

Put $\chi=\langle\psi_0|\exp(-ic)\exp(+itH/\hbar)|\psi_0\rangle$. Direct integration of its normalized momentum Gaussian gives

$$
\begin{aligned}
\chi&=\exp(-ic)(1-ib)^{-1/2} \\
&\quad\exp[i(E_0t/\hbar)/(1-ib)],\quad c=(\ln 2)/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.24}
$$

The root is continuous from $b=0$. The independent x/y detector records are exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}
p_{x,\pm}&=(1\pm\operatorname{Re} \chi)/2, \\
p_{y,\pm}&=(1\pm\operatorname{Im} \chi)/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.25}
$$

The sign agrees with Theorem Q.0.2e: on a scalar reference $\exp(i\ell)$, $\chi=\exp(i\ell)$ and $p_{y,+}=(1+\sin\ell)/2$. These two full normalized response pairs include the field/probe overlap. Explicitly,

$$
\begin{aligned}
|\chi|&=(1+b^{2})^{-1/4} \\
&\quad\exp[-(E_0t/\hbar)b/(1+b^{2})], \\
\arg\chi&=-c+(1/2)\arctan b+(E_0t/\hbar)/(1+b^{2}) \bmod 2\pi.
\end{aligned}
$$

In particular $|\chi|<1$ for a finite-width packet and $t>0$, so the reduced probe map is not a unitary phase channel: the probe is entangled with the momentum. The unitary equality (Q.0.2g.5)/(Q.0.2g.10) holds on the full field and probe carrier with every spectator. The exact scalar-control unitary responses are those of finite $|j\rangle$ inputs in (Q.0.2g.6).

At finite grade the exact diagnostic record is

$$
\chi_n=\sum_j |\psi_n(j)|^{2} \exp[iL_n(j)],
$$

and the same normalized formulas (Q.0.2g.25) hold with $\chi_{n}$. A joint terminal momentum/probe readout has probabilities

$$
\begin{aligned}
p(j,\pm|x)&=|\psi_n(j)|^{2}[1\pm\cos L_n(j)]/2, \\
p(j,\pm|y)&=|\psi_n(j)|^{2}[1\pm\sin L_n(j)]/2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.2g.26}
$$

All outcomes and poststates are retained. Summing j yields the reduced response; conditioning on a recorded j is a separately typed postmeasurement diagnostic.

#### 8. Complete qualified-source word, full stock and independent invoice

This part supplies the physical cabinet. Let $b=b_n$, $k=b+1$ (field plus probe bits), and $c_{\mathrm{cells}}=\max(2,k)$.
