### Q.0.5 Conditional Stationarity Transfer

<a id="definition-q02a-registered-phase-sector"></a>**Definition Q.0.2a (Registered Phase Sector).** A phase sector is an equivalence class of admissible paths on which the independently registered differential-character/connection data and boundary data are fixed. The integer $k$ in Theorem Q.0.4 is the lift of an exact trivial-phase condition; it is a topological winding number only when a separate integral homotopy or cohomology certificate identifies it as such. Variations within a sector preserve the registered data.

<a id="corollary-q03-conditional-stationarity-transfer"></a>**Corollary Q.0.3 (Conditional Stationarity Transfer).** On a fixed calibrated sector with constant $\kappa_A>0$ and $\mathcal S=\kappa_A\mathcal L$,
$$
\delta\mathcal S=0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\delta\mathcal L=0.
$$
This equivalence is a scalar-rescaling identity; it neither selects $\kappa_A$ nor proves the existence of a continuum action. ∎

**Physical Interpretation:** Principle Q.0.3a and Theorem Q.0.3a make the continuum Euler–Lagrange equation the stationarity condition of the $\Gamma$-limit of the finite predictive ledger on the declared prescribed-boundary and prescribed-holonomy class. Every sequence of discrete PCE minimizers has a convergent subsequence, every cluster point minimizes the continuum ledger, and differentiability on the admissible tangent domain then gives $\delta\mathcal S=0$. The independent constant $\kappa_A$ calibrates ledger units to action units. Nonminimizing saddles remain governed by the separately stated first-variation gate.

### Q.0.6 Connection to the Path Integral

On a branch carrying an independently defined quantum path amplitude and a historywise action--ledger calibration, its phase factor can be rewritten in ledger variables.

<a id="proposition-q02-conditional-ledger-representation-of-a-path-amplitude"></a>**Proposition Q.0.2 (Conditional Ledger Representation of a Path Amplitude).** Suppose an independently defined quantum path amplitude has phase $e^{i\mathcal S[\phi]/\hbar}$ and a certified branch identifies
$$
\mathcal S[\phi]=\kappa_A\mathcal L[\phi].
$$
Then
$$
e^{i\mathcal S[\phi]/\hbar}
=e^{i(\kappa_A/\hbar)\mathcal L[\phi]}.
$$
Only on the additional calibration $\kappa_A=\hbar$ does this reduce to $e^{i\mathcal L[\phi]}$. This algebraic substitution neither derives the Feynman measure nor identifies thermodynamic entropy with quantum phase. ∎

<a id="proposition-q02c-finite-entropy-transform-duality"></a>**Proposition Q.0.2c (Finite Entropy Transform Duality).** Let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be a finite cutoff set of admissible histories and define
$$
E[\phi]:=\sum_{i\in\phi}\varepsilon_i,
\qquad
Z_\Lambda(z):=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}w_\phi e^{-zE[\phi]},
$$
where $w_\phi\ge0$ are branch weights independent of $z$. Assume in addition that the accepted calibration certificate gives $E[\phi]=\mathcal S[\phi]/\hbar$ for every history in $\mathcal H_\Lambda$. Then $Z_\Lambda(z)$ is an entire function of $z$, and its two distinguished finite-cutoff evaluations are
$$
Z_\Lambda(1)=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}w_\phi e^{-E[\phi]},
$$
the finite Gibbs/Laplace weight of the registered additive event ledger, and
$$
Z_\Lambda(-i)=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}w_\phi e^{iE[\phi]}
=
\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}w_\phi e^{i\mathcal S[\phi]/\hbar},
$$
the finite path-amplitude weight of Proposition Q.0.2. For a countable history set $\mathcal H$, assume the same certificate gives $E[\phi]=\mathcal S[\phi]/\hbar$ for every $\phi\in\mathcal H$. The same analytic statement then holds on any domain on which
$$
Z(z)=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal H}w_\phi e^{-zE[\phi]}
$$
converges normally on compact subsets. In particular, the Gibbs value at $z=1$ is defined whenever $1$ lies in such a domain, and the phase value at $z=-i$ is defined either when $-i$ lies in such a domain or as the limit of finite-cutoff oscillatory amplitudes whenever that limit exists.

*Proof.* For finite $\mathcal H_\Lambda$, each term $w_\phi e^{-zE[\phi]}$ is entire in $z$, and a finite sum of entire functions is entire. Substituting $z=1$ gives the Gibbs/Laplace weight. Substituting $z=-i$ gives $e^{iE[\phi]}$, and by the historywise calibration hypothesis of Proposition Q.0.2c,
$$
E[\phi]=\mathcal S[\phi]/\hbar\qquad\text{on the calibrated branch}.
$$
This gives the path-amplitude form. For countable $\mathcal H$, normal convergence on compact subsets gives analyticity by the Weierstrass theorem on the stated domain. Boundary or off-domain phase evaluations are not automatic; they are exactly the finite-cutoff oscillatory limits stated in the hypothesis. ∎

<a id="corollary-q02d-single-entropy-transform-ledger"></a>**Corollary Q.0.2d (Single Entropy-Transform Ledger).** Under Proposition Q.0.2c, including its historywise calibration $E[\phi]=\mathcal S[\phi]/\hbar$, the finite Gibbs/Laplace weight and the finite path-amplitude weight are two evaluations of the same finite entropy transform:
$$
Z_\Lambda(z)=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}w_\phi e^{-zE[\phi]},
\qquad
E[\phi]=\sum_{i\in\phi}\varepsilon_i.
$$
In particular,
$$
Z_\Lambda(1)=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}w_\phi e^{-E[\phi]},
\qquad
Z_\Lambda(-i)=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}w_\phi e^{iE[\phi]}
=\sum_{\phi\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}w_\phi e^{i\mathcal S[\phi]/\hbar}.
$$
Thus, at finite cutoff, the two displayed weights are evaluations at $z=1$ and $z=-i$ of the same registered transform. This analytic-continuation identity does not identify a physical Gibbs ensemble with a quantum path integral or derive either ledger from SPAP; those interpretations require the independent weight, action-calibration, and quantum-phase hypotheses. For a countable history set, the statement holds only on domains of normal convergence or through the explicitly stated finite-cutoff oscillatory limit.

*Proof.* Proposition Q.0.2c defines the finite transform $Z_\Lambda(z)$ and proves it is entire. Evaluation at $z=1$ gives the Gibbs/Laplace weight. Evaluation at $z=-i$ gives $e^{iE[\phi]}$, and the historywise calibration hypothesis of Proposition Q.0.2c gives $E[\phi]=\mathcal S[\phi]/\hbar$. The countable case inherits exactly the normal-convergence and finite-cutoff-limit qualifications already stated in Proposition Q.0.2c. ∎

<a id="corollary-q04-conditional-ledger-phase-matching"></a>**Corollary Q.0.4 (Conditional Ledger Phase Matching).** Under Proposition Q.0.2 and the calibration $\kappa_A=\hbar$, relative phases are differences of the certified dimensionless ledger modulo $2\pi$. Without that bridge, equal structural or thermodynamic costs do not imply constructive quantum interference. ∎

### Q.0.6.1 Selected Update-Count Character Duality

<a id="convention-q06a0-character-status"></a>**Convention Q.0.6a.0 (Character Status).** The character $N\mapsto e^{iN\ln2}$ is a mathematically selected character of the update-count group. It is a physical phase only after the independent action and quantum-phase calibrations above. Density of this character in $U(1)$ does not derive a gauge symmetry or select a gauge dynamics.

<a id="definition-q06a1-update-count-group-completion"></a>**Definition Q.0.6a.1 (Update-Count Group Completion).** Let $\mathbb N$ be the monoid of registered event counts under addition. Its Grothendieck group completion is $\mathbb Z$. A character of $\mathbb Z$ is a homomorphism
$$
\chi:\mathbb Z\to U(1).
$$
The Landauer character is
$$
\chi_L(N)=e^{iN\ln 2}.
\tag{Q.0.6a}
$$

<a id="theorem-q06a2-pontryagin-dual-of-update-count"></a>**Theorem Q.0.6a.2 (Pontryagin Dual of Update Count).** The character group of the update-count completion is
$$
\widehat{\mathbb Z}\cong U(1),
\tag{Q.0.6b}
$$
with isomorphism determined by
$$
\theta\in\mathbb R/2\pi\mathbb Z
\quad\longmapsto\quad
\chi_\theta(N)=e^{iN\theta}.
$$
Under this identification, the Landauer character is the point $\theta=\ln2\pmod{2\pi}$, and its image
$$
G_L=\{\chi_L(N):N\in\mathbb Z\}
$$
is dense in $U(1)$.

*Proof.* A homomorphism $\chi:\mathbb Z\to U(1)$ is determined by $\chi(1)$. Conversely, every $z\in U(1)$ defines a homomorphism by $\chi_z(N)=z^N$. Thus $\widehat{\mathbb Z}\cong U(1)$. Writing $z=e^{i\theta}$ gives the displayed parameterization. The Landauer character has $z=e^{i\ln2}$. Density of its image is Theorem Q.0.7d, equivalently irrationality of $\ln2/(2\pi)$ from Lemma Q.0.7b. ∎

<a id="theorem-q06a3-selected-character-fourier-sums-of-update-histories"></a>**Theorem Q.0.6a.3 (Selected-Character Fourier Sums of Update Histories).** Let $\mathcal H_\Lambda$ be a finite cutoff set of histories, with update count $N[\gamma]\in\mathbb Z$ and weights $w_\gamma\ge0$. Define the finite update-count measure
$$
\mu_\Lambda
=
\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}
w_\gamma\,\delta_{N[\gamma]}.
\tag{Q.0.6c}
$$
Its Fourier transform at the selected Landauer character is the exact finite sum
$$
\widehat\mu_\Lambda(\chi_L)
=
\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}
w_\gamma\,\chi_L(N[\gamma])
=
\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}
w_\gamma e^{iN[\gamma]\ln2}.
\tag{Q.0.6d}
$$
Equation (Q.0.6d) is a selected-character Fourier sum. It is a physical path amplitude only on a branch satisfying Convention Q.0.6a.0's independent action and quantum-phase calibrations. If, in addition, every retained history has a certified equality
$$
\frac{\mathcal S[\gamma]}{\hbar}
=N[\gamma]\ln2+\Delta[\gamma],
$$
then its calibrated finite amplitude is
$$
\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal H_\Lambda}
w_\gamma e^{i\Delta[\gamma]}\chi_L(N[\gamma]).
\tag{Q.0.6e}
$$

*Proof.* The Fourier transform of a finite measure on $\mathbb Z$ at a character $\chi$ is
$$
\widehat\mu(\chi)=\sum_N\mu(N)\chi(N).
$$
Substitution of (Q.0.6c) and $\chi=\chi_L$ gives (Q.0.6d). Under the separately certified historywise action equality, multiplication by $e^{i\Delta[\gamma]}$ gives (Q.0.6e). No physical-amplitude statement follows from the Fourier identity without those calibrations. ∎

<a id="corollary-q06a4-finite-cyclic-character-orthogonality"></a>**Corollary Q.0.6a.4 (Finite Cyclic-Character Orthogonality).** On the cyclic quotient $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$, the characters
$$
\chi_j(n)=e^{2\pi ijn/q},
\qquad j=0,\ldots,q-1,
$$
satisfy
$$
\frac1q\sum_{n=0}^{q-1}
\chi_j(n)\overline{\chi_k(n)}
=
\delta_{jk}.
\tag{Q.0.6f}
$$

*Proof.* If $j=k$, every summand is $1$. If $j\ne k$, the sum is a geometric series with ratio $e^{2\pi i(j-k)/q}\ne1$ and therefore vanishes. Because $q\ln2\notin2\pi\mathbb Z$ for every $q\ge1$, $\chi_L$ does not descend to a nontrivial character of $\mathbb Z/q\mathbb Z$. Thus (Q.0.6f) is generic finite Fourier orthogonality; a physical interference rule additionally requires a separately realized coherent phase branch. ∎

<a id="theorem-q01aa-rounded-diffusion-path-laws-and-a-finite-exact-fair-bit-source"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1aa (Rounded Diffusion Path Laws and a Finite Exact-Fair-Bit Source).** Fix integers $d,m\ge1$, $T>0$, and the unit torus $\mathbb R^d/\mathbb Z^d$. Let $b:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ and $\sigma:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^{d\times m}$ be bounded, $\mathbb Z^d$-periodic, globally Lipschitz coefficients. Set $a=\sigma\sigma^{\mathsf T}$. Rank changes and zeros are allowed. Start at 0. The zero start is deliberate: it belongs to every grid and needs no computable-real rounding decision. A fixed other start can be handled by supplied grid approximants converging to it, with their initial error included below.

For $n\ge1$ put

$$
\begin{gathered}
\eta_n=h_n=\delta_n=1/n,\qquad r_n=1/n^2,\\
K_n=\lceil Tn\rceil,\quad t_k=\min(k/n,T),\quad \Delta_k=t_{k+1}-t_k,\\
G_n=(r_n\mathbb Z^d)/\mathbb Z^d,\qquad N_n=|G_n|=n^{2d}.
\end{gathered}
$$

There are at most two distinct positive $\Delta_k$. Let $R_n$ be coordinatewise nearest-grid rounding on $\mathbb R^d$, using $R_n(y)_i=r_n\lfloor y_i/r_n+1/2\rfloor$. This Borel convention satisfies $R_n(y+\ell)=R_n(y)+\ell$ for $\ell\in\mathbb Z^d$ and $|R_n(y)-y|\le c_dr_n$, $c_d=\sqrt d/2$.

Define a reference lifted chain with independent standard Gaussian vectors $\xi_k\in\mathbb R^m$ and $\zeta_k\in\mathbb R^d$ by

$$
Z_0=0,\qquad Z_{k+1}=R_n\!\left(Z_k+\Delta_k b(Z_k)+\sqrt{2\eta_n\Delta_k}\,[\sigma(Z_k)\xi_k+\sqrt{\delta_n}\,\zeta_k]\right).\tag{Q.0.1aa.1}
$$

The projected nodes form a genuine finite-state time-inhomogeneous Markov chain on $G_n$. Its transition probabilities $p_{k,n}(x,y)$ integrate the fully normalized Gaussian with mean $x+\Delta_kb(x)$ and covariance

$$
C_{k,n}(x)=2\eta_n\Delta_k[a(x)+\delta_n I_d].\tag{Q.0.1aa.2}
$$

over all lattice translates of the half-open rounding cell centered at y. The positive $\delta_n$ makes boundaries probability zero. The infinite sum is part of the mathematical definition, not an online Gaussian sampling requirement.

Define $J_n$ to interpolate any node sequence in $G_n$ by the straight torus geodesic with coordinate displacement in $[-1/2,1/2)$, resolving antipodal ties by that convention. This defines a continuous path from each finite node sequence; continuity of $J_n$ as a map between varying spaces is neither asserted nor needed.

Put

$$
B_n=n^2+\lceil\log_2(K_nN_n)\rceil,\qquad M_n=2^{B_n}.\tag{Q.0.1aa.3}
$$

For each distinct pair $(\Delta,x)$ at fixed n choose one stochastic row q of denominator $M_n$ with row total variation at most $N_n/M_n$, and reuse it at every time step with that $\Delta$ and state x. A constructive choice appears in Part III. Let $Q_n$ be the finite-state Markov law with these q rows, start 0, and path output $J_n$.

**Path-law and finite-source conclusion.** The laws $Q_n$ obey a good LDP on $C([0,T],\mathbb{R}^d/\mathbb{Z}^d)$, in the uniform topology, at speed $n$. The rate is

$$
I_0(\gamma)=\frac14\int_0^T[\dot z-b(z)]^T a(z)^+[\dot z-b(z)]\,dt.\tag{Q.0.1aa.4}
$$

if $\gamma$ starts at 0, its lift z from 0 is absolutely continuous, and $\dot z-b(z)\in\operatorname{ran}a(z)$ almost everywhere; otherwise the rate is infinity. The integral is extended-valued: its finiteness remains a separate condition. This theorem gives the full path LDP, not an arbitrary closed-event lower bound or singleton-endpoint exponent.

Each n has an exact sampler of its node sequence using $K_nB_n$ independent fair bits, finite integer registers, and a finite transition table. A finite rational description of the path clock and effective generation of the tables are asserted under the effective hypotheses below. It does not use real-coordinate Gaussian sampling online. Effective compilation is asserted only when T is a supplied positive rational and $b,\sigma$ have computable evaluation procedures with supplied effective magnitude and Lipschitz bounds. Arbitrary abstract Lipschitz coefficients are not automatically computable. No uniform polynomial preprocessing bound follows merely from these inputs.

**Proof.**

#### I. Rounded lifted polygons and the full path rate

The following proof controls the rounded Brownian functional itself, including multiplicative noise and the short final time cell.

Work on canonical Wiener space for the independent Brownian coordinates (W,B), with their usual completed, augmented natural filtration. All controls in the variational formula are progressively measurable with respect to this filtration; anticipating controls are excluded. Let $u=(q,v)$ be such a control with $\int_0^T|u|^2\le A$ almost surely. Insert its cell integrals into the Brownian-shifted recurrence. At every step perform the same rounding after adding the controlled increment. If $e_{k+1}$ is that rounding error, then $|e_{k+1}|\le c_dr_n$ for every realization and every control, without a continuity assumption on rounding.

Use the auxiliary adapted càdlàg frozen process Y, which evolves during each open cell by frozen drift, controlled drift, and Brownian noise and jumps by $e_{k+1}$ at its right endpoint. Its node values are the rounded nodes. Let $\bar Y_s$ be the most recent node value, and $R_t=\sum_{t_{k+1}\le t}e_{k+1}$. Then exactly

$$
\begin{aligned}
Y_t&=\int_0^t b(\bar Y_s)\,ds+\sqrt2\int_0^t[\sigma(\bar Y_s)q_s+\sqrt{\delta_n}\,v_s]\,ds+M_t+R_t,\\
M_t&=\sqrt{2\eta_n}\int_0^t[\sigma(\bar Y_s)\,dW_s+\sqrt{\delta_n}\,dB_s].
\end{aligned}\tag{Q.0.1aa.5}
$$

Endpoint choices for integrands do not matter. The rounding errors can depend on the current Brownian increment; R is adapted, and its deterministic variation bound, rather than any martingale property, is used:

$$
\sup_t|R_t|\le\operatorname{Var}(R)\le c_dK_nr_n\le c_d(T+h_n)\frac{r_n}{h_n}=O(r_n/h_n)=O(1/n).\tag{Q.0.1aa.6}
$$

This is the precise $O(r/h)$ rounding perturbation: the accumulated forcing in the integral equation. It is not a pathwise bound on the difference of two arbitrary multiplicative-noise trajectories under a common Gaussian coupling.

Write $B_0=\sup|b|$, $S=\sup\|\sigma\|_{\rm op}$ and $S_F=\sup\|\sigma\|_F$. Doob's inequality and Itô isometry give

$$
\mathbb E\sup_t|M_t|^2\le8\eta_nT(S_F^2+d\delta_n).\tag{Q.0.1aa.7}
$$

For every within-cell time and also its pre-rounding right limit, the increment from the left node is bounded by

$$
D_n=B_0h_n+\sqrt2(S+1)\sqrt{Ah_n}+2\sup_t|M_t|+c_dr_n.
$$

Thus $\sup|Y-\bar Y|\le D_n$ (with the appropriate left-cell interpretation at a node); if $P_n^u$ is the continuous Euclidean polygon through the rounded nodes, then $\sup|P_n^u-Y|\le2D_n$. The latter follows by comparing both to the same left node within a cell. The jump at a right node has already been included in $D_n$.

Let $\Phi(u)=z$ solve $\dot z=b(z)+\sqrt2\sigma(z)q,\ z(0)=0$. Put $L_A=L_bT+\sqrt2L_\sigma\sqrt{TA}$. Subtract its integral equation from (Q.0.1aa.5). Gronwall with integrable coefficient $L_b+\sqrt2L_\sigma|q_s|$ yields

$$
\|Y-\Phi(u)\|_\infty\le e^{L_A}\left[L_AD_n+\sqrt{2\delta_nTA}+\|M\|_\infty+c_dK_nr_n\right].\tag{Q.0.1aa.8}
$$

Consequently, uniformly over these adapted bounded-energy controls,

$$
\mathbb E\|P_n^u-\Phi(u)\|_\infty^2\le C_A[h_n+\eta_n+\delta_n+(K_nr_n)^2]\longrightarrow0.\tag{Q.0.1aa.9}
$$

The harmless $r_n^2$ term is absorbed in $(K_nr_n)^2$, and $h_n^2$ in $h_n$. This proof includes the possibly short last cell using its actual $\Delta_k$. A supplied initial grid error adds its squared magnitude to (Q.0.1aa.9).

For completeness, the remaining probability argument is stated explicitly on this canonical Brownian space. Weak $L^2$ control balls are compact metrizable. $\Phi$ is continuous from their weak topology into uniform paths: bounded-energy solutions have a common 1/2-Hölder modulus; in any uniformly convergent subsequence, Lipschitz coefficient convergence and weak testing against $\sigma(z)$ identify the integral equation and its unique solution. Thus random controls $u_n\Rightarrow u$ on a weak ball satisfy $(u_n,P_n^{u_n})\Rightarrow(u,\Phi(u))$ by (Q.0.1aa.9).

The finite rounded recurrence is a Borel Brownian functional, despite its discontinuities. The Boué--Dupuis bounded-measurable Brownian variational identity applies (Chiarini and Fischer 2014, Appendix A (A.1)). For bounded continuous F,

$$
-\eta_n\log\mathbb E e^{-F(P_n)/\eta_n}=\inf_u\mathbb E\left[\frac12\|u\|_2^2+F(P_n^u)\right].\tag{Q.0.1aa.10}
$$

Deterministic controls and (Q.0.1aa.9) give the upper Laplace bound. For the lower bound, with $L=\|F\|_\infty$ choose nearly minimizing controls whose expected squared energies are $\le4L+2$. Stop each when its energy reaches A. Stopping decreases energy, changes the output only on an event of probability $\le(4L+2)/A$, and so incurs at most $2L(4L+2)/A$ in the expected F term. On the weakly compact ball, (Q.0.1aa.9), weak lower semicontinuity of energy and Portmanteau give the lower bound by $\inf_u\{\tfrac12\|u\|_2^2+F(\Phi(u))\}$, less that stopping error. Send $A\to\infty$. This proves the Laplace principle.

Its control rate is good because $\Phi$ maps weak energy balls compactly and a minimizing sequence has a weak limit realizing the minimum. The least-norm solution of $\sqrt2\sigma(z)q=\dot z-b(z)$ is $q=\sigma(z)^+(\dot z-b(z))/\sqrt2$. The pseudoinverse is Borel even at rank changes; its squared norm is half the integrand quadratic in (Q.0.1aa.4). The unused v is optimally zero. This identifies the rate. Projection onto the torus is continuous, and each full continuous projected path has a unique lift anchored at 0, so contraction gives exactly (Q.0.1aa.4) for the projected lifted polygon.

#### II. Shortest-coordinate decoding

The lifted reference polygon uses potentially unbounded winding increments and is not itself a finite-register source. The finite node chain with $J_n$ discards that information. We now prove that this loss does not change its LDP under the stated schedules.

If every rounded lifted increment has all its coordinate magnitudes strictly below 1/2, projection of the lifted polygon equals $J_n$ of its projected nodes. For n sufficiently large, $B_0/n+r_n/2\le1/4$. A failure therefore entails a Gaussian noise coordinate with magnitude at least 1/4 in at least one cell. Conditionally on the past each such coordinate is centered Gaussian of variance at most

$$
V_n=\frac{2(S^2+1)}{n^2}.
$$

Its two-sided tail is at most $2\exp[-1/(32V_n)]$. A union bound, requiring no independence of these state-dependent increments, yields

$$
\mathbb P\{\text{projected lifted polygon differs from }J_n\}\le2dK_n\exp\!\left[-\frac{n^2}{64(S^2+1)}\right].\tag{Q.0.1aa.11}
$$

The logarithm divided by n tends to minus infinity. Hence the two coupled path laws are exponentially equivalent at speed n, for every positive uniform-distance tolerance, and have the same good LDP. Possible exact antipodal ties do not need a zero-probability argument: any tie belongs to the same long-increment event and is covered by (Q.0.1aa.11). Nearest-grid rounding ties have probability zero in the uncontrolled positive-floor reference law; under controls they may occur, but (Q.0.1aa.6) is valid under the fixed convention anyway.

This argument is schedule-specific. It does not assert that shortest-geodesic interpolation is harmless for arbitrary mesh/noise schedules or arbitrary winding processes.

#### III. Certified dyadic rows and complete path-law transfer

Use the convention $\operatorname{TV}(p,q)=\tfrac12\sum_j|p_j-q_j|$. Here $N=N_n,\ B=B_n,\ M=2^B$. Since $K\ge1\text{ and }n\ge1,\ M\ge2N$. Given any probability row p, obtain rational numbers $v_j$ with $|v_j-p_j|\le1/(4M)$. Set $z_j=\max(v_j,0),\ s=\sum_jz_j\text{ and }w_j=z_j/s$. Because $\|z-p\|_1\le N/(4M)<1,\ s>0$, and

$$
\|w-p\|_1\le\|w-z\|_1+\|z-p\|_1=|1-s|+\|z-p\|_1\le\frac{N}{2M}.
$$

Compute integer floors $a_j=\lfloor Mw_j\rfloor$. Distribute the remaining $M-\sum_ja_j$ units to entries with largest fractional remainders, breaking ties by index. All calculations here are on rational numbers, so no undecidable equality test on true probabilities occurs. Each resulting integer $c_j$ differs from $Mw_j$ by at most 1, $c_j\ge0,\text{ and }\sum_jc_j=M$. For $q_j=c_j/M$,

$$
\operatorname{TV}(q,p)\le\frac12\left[\frac NM+\frac{N}{2M}\right]=\frac{3N}{4M}\le\frac NM.\tag{Q.0.1aa.12}
$$

This proves mathematical existence for any row; its effective version requires the certified $v_j$ and thus the computability hypotheses of Part IV. The q law is exactly dyadic; it is deliberately an approximation to p, not a claim of exact finite-bit Gaussian-cell sampling.

By sequential maximal coupling, two chains whose rows differ by at most $\varepsilon$ can be coupled to keep all K transitions equal with failure probability $\le K\epsilon$. Alternatively the same bound follows by telescoping products of Markov kernels in total variation. Deterministic interpolation cannot increase TV. Therefore

$$
\begin{gathered}
\operatorname{TV}\bigl(\operatorname{law}(J_n\text{ under }p),Q_n\bigr)\le\frac{K_nN_n}{2^{B_n}}\le2^{-n^2},\\
\limsup_{n\to\infty}\frac1n\log\operatorname{TV}=-\infty.
\end{gathered}\tag{Q.0.1aa.13}
$$

This gives exponential equivalence via maximal path coupling, hence transfers the good path LDP to $Q_n$. It also follows directly from probability inequalities with a superexponential additive error. Arbitrarily small entries may become zero after dyadic approximation; (Q.0.1aa.13), rather than unsupported pointwise relative-error claims, is the reason the LDP survives.

#### IV. Effective compilation and finite resources

For an effective uniform compiler assume positive rational T, computable coefficient evaluations on rational points with supplied finite magnitude and Lipschitz bounds, and fixed finite d,m. Then $K_n$, all $\Delta_k$ and grid coordinates are exact rational data. At a grid state, the mean and covariance (Q.0.1aa.2) are computable; covariance has the supplied strictly positive lower bound

$$
\lambda_{\min}(C_{k,n})\ge2\eta_n\Delta_k\delta_n>0.
$$

Upper covariance bounds are supplied as well. Gaussian mass outside a sufficiently large rational box can therefore be bounded effectively by coordinate tail bounds. Intersect the wrapped rounding cells with that box, leaving finitely many rational rectangles. On the box the positive-definite Gaussian density is a computable smooth function with effective bounds/moduli obtained from covariance lower/upper bounds. Certified quadrature, with a density approximation error and a separate tail budget, computes all required probabilities to any absolute rational accuracy. Cell boundaries have zero Gaussian measure. No equality comparison between a true probability and a dyadic threshold is required: approximate rational values feed Part III.

The covariance may be very ill-conditioned as n grows, and an exceptionally short last cell can increase integration difficulty; this does not invalidate termination at a fixed positive rational $\Delta$. It does invalidate inferring a practical or polynomial compilation-time bound from table size alone. A general computable T without a partition/comparison promise could also make ceiling/equality decisions problematic, which is why the effective theorem states rational T. The abstract mathematical LDP does not need rational T.

Only two distinct step lengths need tables. Let $L_n\le2$ be their number. Store each row as $N_n$ nonnegative integer counts $c_j$, each in $[0,2^{B_n}]$, so $B_n+1$ bits per count suffice. Then:

- Grid states: $N_n=n^{2d}$; a packed state label uses $\lceil\log_2N_n\rceil$ bits (coordinatewise encoding uses $d\lceil\log_2(n^2)\rceil$ bits).
- Transition-count tables: at most $L_nN_n^2(B_n+1)$ bits, bounded by $2n^{4d}(B_n+1)$.
- Per-step fair randomness: exactly $B_n$ bits, forming U uniform on $\{0,\ldots,2^{B_n}-1\}$.
- Sampling rule: select the first j with $U<\sum_{i\le j}c_i$. Each destination j has exactly $c_j$ preimages and hence probability $q_j$, with no rejection and no Gaussian primitive.
- Total randomness: exactly $K_nB_n$ bits; $B_n=n^2+O(\log n)$, hence $K_nB_n=O(n^3)$ at fixed T,d.
- Online workspace apart from stored tables: current/next state labels, a step counter, a $B_n$-bit draw, and a ($B_n+1$)-bit cumulative count suffice, with $O(B_n+\log N_n+\log K_n)$ bits. A linear scan is a valid finite sampler; compiled cumulative tables permit binary search. These algorithmic choices are not a physical binary structural-operation identity.
- A full sampled node record requires $(K_n+1)\lceil\log_2N_n\rceil$ bits, $O(n\log n)$; its piecewise-geodesic path is specified exactly by these rational nodes, the rational time partition, and the fixed interpolation rule. An actual continuous-time display or physical trajectory generator is not included.
- The number of distinct output paths is at most $N_n^{K_n}$, and the fair-bit input space has exactly $2^{K_nB_n}$ elements. Unused random bits are allowed; there is no entropy-optimality assertion.

These are finite-description and online-randomness bounds after table compilation. The table compiler uses only finite work for each n under the stated effective hypotheses, but its required time and temporary memory are separate resources and have not been bounded above by the listed storage counts. Arbitrary computable coefficient evaluation procedures can themselves be slow. No claim of a uniform fixed-size machine independent of n is made.

∎

#### Explicit computable changing-rank source

On the unit two-torus take $m=1$,

$$
b(x,y)=(1,0),\qquad\sigma(x,y)=(0,\sin(2\pi x))^T,\qquad x_0=(0,0),\quad T=1.
$$

All coefficient evaluations are computable; $|b|=1,\ \|\sigma\|\le1,\ L_b=0,\text{ and }L_\sigma\le2\pi<7$ are supplied bounds. The limiting controlled path

$$
\gamma(t)=\left(t,\frac{1-\cos(2\pi t)}{2\pi}\right)\bmod\mathbb Z^2.
$$

has residual $(0,\sin(2\pi t))$, lies in the instantaneous covariance range, and has $I_0(\gamma)=1/4$. The noise rank is zero at $t=0,1/2,1$ and one between them. The least control $q=1/\sqrt2$ gives that action; values at the zero-rank times do not affect the integral. In contrast $\gamma_{\rm bad}(t)=(t,t)$ has infinite rate because its residual second component is 1 and $\int_0^\epsilon\csc^2(2\pi t)\,dt$ diverges, despite almost-everywhere range membership.

For this example $K_n=n,\ N_n=n^4,\ B_n=n^2+\lceil5\log_2n\rceil$, and the two-step-length bound improves to one table of $n^8(B_n+1)$ bits. The exact fair-bit count is $nB_n$. These large explicit bounds demonstrate finiteness, not an efficient implementation or thermodynamic cost. The positive floor remains in every finite-n reference kernel even where $\sigma$ vanishes.

These are complete finite mathematical path sources with their stated algorithmic records. A physical clock, preparation, memory, transport, lookup, erasure or bath realization requires its own source contract and cost accounting. The rate action and bit counts supply no reset-heat or mechanical-action identity.

<a id="theorem-q01ab-slowly-diverging-fair-bit-depth-for-multiplicative-diffusion-paths"></a>**Theorem Q.0.1ab (Slowly Diverging Fair-Bit Depth for Multiplicative Diffusion Paths).** Fix the dimensions, zero start, torus, bounded periodic globally Lipschitz $b,\sigma$, and time partition of Theorem Q.0.1aa. Thus $h_n=\eta_n=\delta_n=1/n$, grid spacing $r_n=n^{-2}$, $K_n=\lceil Tn\rceil$, and the actual positive cell lengths are $\Delta_k=t_{k+1}-t_k$. Put $p=m+d$. Let $\ell_n\ge1$ be any integer sequence tending to infinity. No lower divergence rate or upper growth rate is assumed.

#### I. The exact finite source

Write $\Phi$ for the standard normal CDF, and define
$$
q_{\ell,j}=\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\frac{j+1/2}{2^\ell}\right),\quad 0\le j<2^\ell,
\qquad a_n=\lceil\log_2(8n^3)\rceil.
\tag{Q.0.1ab.1}
$$
Choose dyadic rationals $\widehat q_{n,j}$ of denominator $2^{a_n}$ with error at most $n^{-3}$. For each of the at most two distinct positive step lengths and every grid state, likewise approximate every entry of
$$
D_{n,\Delta}(x)=\Delta b(x),\qquad
H_{n,\Delta}(x)=\sqrt{2\Delta/n}\,[\sigma(x),n^{-1/2}I_d]
\tag{Q.0.1ab.2}
$$
by $\widehat D,\widehat H$ of the same dyadic denominator with entry error at most $n^{-3}$. Reuse these fixed arrays whenever the same pair $(\Delta,x)$ occurs and extend them periodically. A reproducible effective selection is given in Part V. Different allowed arrays need not define the same finite-$n$ source.

At each step draw $p$ independent uniform $\ell_n$-bit words $V_{k,i}$ and set $\widehat Q_k=(\widehat q_{n,V_{k,1}},\ldots,\widehat q_{n,V_{k,p}})$. The actual source is
$$
\begin{aligned}
X_0&=0,\\
X_{k+1}&=R_n\bigl(X_k+\widehat D_{n,\Delta_k}(X_k)
+\widehat H_{n,\Delta_k}(X_k)\widehat Q_k\bigr)\pmod{\mathbb Z^d},\\
q_n(\Delta,x,y)&=2^{-p\ell_n}\#\{v\in\{0,\ldots,2^{\ell_n}-1\}^p:
\text{the displayed update sends }(x,v)\text{ to }y\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.1ab.3}
$$
All online arithmetic, rounding ties and reduction modulo one are rational operations. Word collisions are allowed. Literal counting proves that $q_n$ is stochastic and that independent words give exactly its product Markov law. Output the shortest-coordinate polygon $J_n(X_0,\ldots,X_{K_n})$ defined in Theorem Q.0.1aa.

These actual finite output laws have a good full-path LDP at speed $n$ in the uniform topology, with exactly the constrained action (Q.0.1aa.4), including changing rank and zeros of $\sigma$. Fresh randomness is exactly $pK_n\ell_n$ fair bits. In particular $\ell_n=\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil$ gives $O(n\log n)$ bits per path, and $\ell_n=\lceil\log_2\log_2(n+4)\rceil$ gives $O(n\log\log n)$. Arbitrarily slower divergence still gives this qualitative LDP; no effective convergence rate or entropy optimality is asserted.

#### II. Quantile coupling with all exponential moments

*Proof.* Let $U$ be uniform on $(0,1)$, $Z=\Phi^{-1}(U)$ and
$$
Q_\ell=\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\frac{\lfloor2^\ell U\rfloor+1/2}{2^\ell}\right).
\tag{Q.0.1ab.4}
$$
Then $Q_\ell\to Z$ almost surely. For every $a\ge0$,
$$
\mathbb E e^{a|Q_\ell|}\le2\mathbb E e^{a|Z|},\qquad \ell\ge1.
\tag{Q.0.1ab.5}
$$
Indeed $e^{a|\Phi^{-1}(u)|}$ is monotone on each side of $1/2$, a dyadic-cell boundary. On the upper side its midpoint value times cell length is at most twice the integral on the upper half; the lower side uses the lower half. Sum, using monotone integration at the unbounded end cells.

For any $\theta>0$ and $s>1$, Cauchy--Schwarz and (Q.0.1ab.5) imply
$$
\mathbb E e^{s\theta|Z-Q_\ell|}
\le[\mathbb E e^{2s\theta|Z|}\mathbb E e^{2s\theta|Q_\ell|}]^{1/2}
\le\sqrt2\,\mathbb E e^{2s\theta|Z|}<\infty.
\tag{Q.0.1ab.6}
$$
Thus $e^{\theta|Z-Q_\ell|}$ is uniformly integrable and its expectation tends to one. The rational reconstruction changes the scalar coupling error by at most $n^{-3}$. For independent coordinates $G\sim N(0,I_p)$ coupled to $\widehat Q_n$, Euclidean norm is bounded by the sum of coordinate absolute errors. Hence independence gives
$$
M_n(\theta):=\mathbb E e^{\theta|G-\widehat Q_n|}\longrightarrow1
\quad\text{for every fixed }\theta>0.
\tag{Q.0.1ab.7}
$$
No pointwise domination by the coupled Gaussian or quantitative inverse-CDF error rate is used.

#### III. Multiplicative-noise propagation with actual rounding

Take independent copies $(G_k,\widehat Q_k)$ and put
$$
A_n=\frac1n\sum_{k<K_n}|G_k|,\qquad
\overline E_n=\frac1n\sum_{k<K_n}|G_k-\widehat Q_k|.
\tag{Q.0.1ab.8}
$$
For every $\epsilon,\theta>0$, Chernoff gives
$$
\Pr(\overline E_n>\epsilon)\le e^{-\theta n\epsilon}M_n(\theta)^{K_n},
\qquad
\limsup_n\frac1n\log\Pr(\overline E_n>\epsilon)=-\infty.
\tag{Q.0.1ab.9}
$$
For the limit take $n\to\infty$ first, using $K_n/n\to T$ and (Q.0.1ab.7), and then $\theta\to\infty$. Writing $\Lambda(\lambda)=\log\mathbb E e^{\lambda|G|}$, for each $\lambda>0$,
$$
\limsup_n\frac1n\log\Pr(A_n>R)\le-\lambda R+T\Lambda(\lambda).
\tag{Q.0.1ab.10}
$$
This tends to $-\infty$ as $R\to\infty$ even at $\lambda=1$. It is an exponential-tightness localization; $A_n$ is not claimed to have superexponential tails at fixed $R$.

Couple the lifted Gaussian reference chain of Theorem Q.0.1aa to a lifted rational chain retaining the full rounding increments before projection. This lift is a proof variable, not an online unbounded register. Let $d_k$ be their Euclidean node distance. Boundedness and Lipschitz continuity give, uniformly in the cell lengths $\Delta\le1/n$,
$$
\|H(x)\|_{\rm op}\le C/n,\qquad
\|H(x)-H(y)\|_{\rm op}\le\frac{\sqrt2L_\sigma}{n}|x-y|,
\qquad |D(x)-D(y)|\le\frac{L_b}{n}|x-y|.
\tag{Q.0.1ab.11}
$$
Each nearest-grid rounding residual is at most $c_dn^{-2}$, so their difference is at most $2c_dn^{-2}$. Rounding is not assumed Lipschitz. Split
$$
H(Z_k)G_k-H(\widetilde X_k)\widehat Q_k
=[H(Z_k)-H(\widetilde X_k)]G_k
+H(\widetilde X_k)(G_k-\widehat Q_k).
\tag{Q.0.1ab.12}
$$
Adding the entrywise rational coefficient errors, with the fixed-dimensional operator-norm factors absorbed in $C$, gives
$$
\begin{aligned}
d_{k+1}\le{}&[1+C/n+C|G_k|/n]d_k
+(C/n)|G_k-\widehat Q_k|\\
&+Cn^{-3}(1+|\widehat Q_k|)+2c_dn^{-2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{Q.0.1ab.13}
$$
No Lipschitz property of the rational approximants is required. Using $|\widehat Q_k|\le|G_k|+|G_k-\widehat Q_k|$ and discrete Gronwall yields
$$
\max_{k\le K_n}d_k
\le e^{CK_n/n+CA_n}
\left[C\overline E_n+Cn^{-2}(K_n/n+A_n+\overline E_n)
+2c_dK_n/n^2\right].
\tag{Q.0.1ab.14}
$$
For fixed $R$ and $\epsilon>0$, choose $\epsilon_R>0$ so the right side is at most $\epsilon$ for large $n$ on $\{A_n\le R,\overline E_n\le\epsilon_R\}$. Equations (Q.0.1ab.9)--(Q.0.1ab.10) then imply
$$
\limsup_n\frac1n\log\Pr(\max_kd_k>\epsilon)
\le-R+T\Lambda(1).
\tag{Q.0.1ab.15}
$$
Let $R\to\infty$. The lifted polygons are exponentially equivalent at speed $n$: interpolation on their identical actual time partition, including its short last cell, does not increase maximum node discrepancy. Torus projection contracts the distance.

#### IV. Finite-register path decoding and the inherited action

The finite source stores no winding increments, so one further comparison is required. Let $L_n^G$ be the event that some coordinate of some rounded Gaussian lifted increment has magnitude at least $1/4$. Conditional Gaussian variance is at most $2(S^2+1)/n^2$, where $S=\sup\|\sigma\|_{\rm op}$. Drift plus rounding is at most $1/8$ for large $n$. Gaussian coordinate tails and a union bound, without independence of state-dependent increments, give
$$
\Pr(L_n^G)\le2dK_n\exp[-c n^2],\qquad
c=\frac1{256(S^2+1)}.
\tag{Q.0.1ab.16}
$$
On $\{\max_kd_k<1/16\}\cap(L_n^G)^c$, each rational lifted coordinate increment has magnitude at most $1/4+2(1/16)=3/8<1/2$. It therefore equals the shortest-coordinate displacement, and the projected lifted polygon equals the actual output $J_n$. Decoder failure is superexponential by (Q.0.1ab.15)--(Q.0.1ab.16). This proof allows every diverging $\ell_n$, with no upper growth restriction. For the logarithmic and double-logarithmic choices one may instead use the deterministic bound $O(\sqrt{\ell_n}/n)+O(n^{-2})$ on rational increments.

The complete rounded reference LDP is proved in Theorem Q.0.1aa. Exponential equivalence transfers its good constrained rate (Q.0.1aa.4) to these actual finite fair-bit laws. This is path-distance coupling, not total-variation approximation of every Gaussian transition or of the entire Gaussian path law. The continuously varying non-Lipschitz coefficient class is outside the propagation proof (Q.0.1ab.13). Fixed bit depth also cannot replace divergence: with constant scalar nonzero dispersion and bounded fixed reconstructed increments, lifted velocities remain uniformly bounded up to vanishing rounding error, excluding some finite-rate Brownian skeletons. This counterexample concerns this construction, not a universal lower bound on finite-source bit budgets.

#### V. Effective coefficient construction and complete finite resources

A uniformly effective compiler requires positive rational $T$, computable coefficient evaluation with supplied effective magnitude and Lipschitz bounds, and a computable sequence $\ell_n$. The grid, $K_n$ and actual positive $\Delta$ values are then decidable rational data. Equation (Q.0.1ab.2) is computable at every grid state. Each normal quantile is computable: its CDF argument is rational in $(0,1)$, the CDF is computable and strictly increasing with positive density, and tail bounds give a finite root bracket. Certified bisection refines any straddling interval until a sufficiently short bracket is certified; it need not decide equality to an unknown real threshold.

To select dyadic approximants without a real equality test, first find a rational $v$ with certified error at most $n^{-3}/4$, then round $v$ exactly to the nearest multiple of $2^{-a_n}$. Since $2^{-a_n}\le n^{-3}/8$, total error is less than $n^{-3}$. Fix this algorithm and its rational tie rules before random sampling. It defines an actual reproducible table, not a future-dependent existential choice.

For fixed coefficient bounds, each entry of $\widehat D,\widehat H$ has $O(\log(n+1))$ bits. Gaussian tails give
$$
\max_j|q_{\ell,j}|\le\sqrt{2(\ell+1)\log2},
\tag{Q.0.1ab.17}
$$
since the endpoint tail probability is $2^{-\ell-1}$ and the Gaussian upper tail is at most $e^{-x^2/2}$. Thus each $\widehat q$ needs $O(\log(n+1)+\log(\ell_n+1))$ bits; the common denominator is stored once. With $N_n=n^{2d}$ and $L_n\le2$ distinct lengths, an arithmetic-table implementation has:

- $2^{\ell_n}$ scalar quantile entries, requiring $O(2^{\ell_n}[\log(n+1)+\log(\ell_n+1)])$ bits.
- $L_nN_n(d+dp)$ increment-coefficient entries, requiring $O(N_n\log(n+1))$ bits at fixed dimensions and bounds.
- $O(\log(n+1))$ variable clock/index bits, plus the fixed rational encoding of $T$.
- Online workspace $O(\ell_n+\log(n+1)+\log(\ell_n+1))$ bits apart from tables and output. This includes all $p$ random words, state/step labels, addresses and rational intermediates. Products have denominator $2^{2a_n}$; adding the state uses $n^22^{2a_n}$. Numerators add only $O(\log(\ell_n+1))$ bits, so exact floor and reduction modulo $n^2$ fit these widths.
- A complete node record of $(K_n+1)\lceil\log_2N_n\rceil$ packed bits, with a one-bit convention for $N_n=1$, or $O(K_nd\lceil\log_2(n^2+1)\rceil)$ coordinatewise. It is $O(n\log n)$ and, with the rational clock and fixed geodesic convention, specifies the exact output path.
- Exactly $p\ell_n$ fresh fair bits per step, or $pK_n\ell_n$ per path, without rejection or random stopping.

For logarithmic depth, quantile storage is $O(n\log n)$, total persistent storage is $O(n^{2d}\log n+n\log n)$ and online workspace is $O(\log n)$. For double-logarithmic depth, $2^{\ell_n}=O(\log n)$, so the corresponding quantities are $O((\log n)^2)$, $O(n^{2d}\log n+(\log n)^2)$ and $O(\log n)$.

Alternatively store the deterministic destination for every $(\Delta,x,v)$. Its literal table occupies at most
$$
L_nN_n2^{p\ell_n}\lceil\log_2N_n\rceil
\tag{Q.0.1ab.18}
$$
bits, with the same $N_n=1$ convention. It needs no stored irrational quantity or Gaussian probability integration. The arithmetic tables are usually smaller; a dense stochastic count table is unnecessary because (Q.0.1ab.3) already defines the exact kernel.

Per step, arithmetic uses a fixed-dimensional number of additions, multiplications, exact integer divisions/floors and table accesses at the stated finite widths. Physical access circuitry, bit-operation complexity of the chosen lookup, and compiler time are separate resources. Arbitrarily slow computable coefficient evaluators exclude any uniform polynomial preprocessing bound from these assumptions. This is a family of finite machines, not one fixed register size. The compiler terminates at each fixed $n$, but no effective LDP convergence rate or decision of a rate threshold follows, especially for arbitrarily slow $\ell_n$ divergence. $\square$

The midpoint inverse-normal random-bit quantizer and random-bit Euler simulation are established methods (Giles et al. 2019, §3.2). The result here is the supplied speed-$n$ superexponential transfer for the actual rational, rounded, state-dependent path source. It assigns no fixed-endpoint exponent or arbitrary closed-event lower bound, and it identifies no register count, randomness count or rate action with physical reset heat, a free bath, mechanical action or $\hbar$. Physical preparation, memory, clock, transport, lookup, erasure and bath services require their own declared source and resource laws.

## Q.0.7 Selected Update-Count Character and Its $U(1)$ Closure

This section studies the cyclic character generated by the chosen phase increment $\ln2$. Since $\ln2/(2\pi)$ is irrational, its image is dense in $U(1)$. Density is an arithmetic and topological statement; the physical phase assignment enters through the calibration of Theorem Q.0.2e, and the local gauge and Noether conclusions through Theorem Q.0.7d2 and Corollary Q.0.7d3 on their registered branches.

---

### Q.0.7.1 The Landauer Angle

Define the *Landauer angle* and its reciprocal by:
$$\alpha_L := \frac{\ln 2}{2\pi} \approx 0.110317800$$
$$\beta_L := \frac{2\pi}{\ln 2} = \frac{1}{\alpha_L} \approx 9.064720284$$

The number $\alpha_L$ is the registered ratio $\ln2/(2\pi)$. Interpreting it as a physical phase per event requires the action--entropy and quantum-phase calibrations; Theorem 31 does not supply that identification.

---

### Q.0.7.2 Transcendence of the Landauer Angle

<a id="lemma-q07b-transcendence-of-the-landauer-phase-ratio"></a>**Lemma Q.0.7b (Transcendence of the Landauer Phase Ratio).** *The ratio*
$$
\alpha_L = \frac{\ln 2}{2\pi}
$$
*is transcendental over $\mathbb{Q}$. In particular, it is irrational.*

*Proof.* Suppose for contradiction that $\alpha_L$ is algebraic. Define
$$
b := -2i\alpha_L.
$$
Then $b$ is algebraic. Since $\alpha_L>0$, $b$ is non-real and therefore $b\notin\mathbb{Q}$. By the Gelfond–Schneider theorem (Gelfond 1934; Schneider 1935), if $a\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\{0,1\}$ and $b\in\overline{\mathbb Q}\setminus\mathbb Q$, then every value of $a^b$ is transcendental. Taking $a=-1$ and using the branch $\log(-1)=i\pi$ gives one value
$$
(-1)^b
=
\exp(b\,i\pi)
=
\exp(2\pi\alpha_L)
=
\exp(\ln 2)
=
2.
$$
This value is algebraic, contradicting Gelfond–Schneider. Hence $\alpha_L$ is not algebraic, so it is transcendental and therefore irrational. $\square$

<a id="remark-q07b1-scope-of-the-transcendence-statement"></a>**Remark Q.0.7b.1: Scope of the Transcendence Statement.** The proof of Lemma Q.0.7b does not require algebraic independence of $\pi$ and $\ln 2$. It uses only the Gelfond–Schneider theorem and the identity $\exp(2\pi\alpha_L)=2$. The subsequent equidistribution and three-gap results require only irrationality, but the stronger transcendence statement rules out every rational or algebraic phase-locking replacement of $\alpha_L$.

---

### Q.0.7.3 Exact Matching for a Registered Irrational Phase Step

<a id="corollary-q07c-exact-matching-for-the-registered-irrational-phase-step"></a>**Corollary Q.0.7c (Exact Matching for the Registered Irrational Phase Step).** *Assume that each event in the declared history family is independently assigned the phase increment $\ln2$, and assume Lemma Q.0.7b. Then the exact selected-character phase-matching condition*
$$(N[\phi_1] - N[\phi_2]) \cdot \ln 2 = 2\pi k \qquad (k \in \mathbb{Z})$$

*implies:*
$$N[\phi_1] = N[\phi_2] \quad \text{and} \quad k = 0$$

*Proof.* Dividing by $2\pi$:
$$(N[\phi_1] - N[\phi_2]) \alpha_L = k$$

If $N[\phi_1] - N[\phi_2] \neq 0$, then $\alpha_L = k/(N[\phi_1] - N[\phi_2]) \in \mathbb{Q}$, contradicting Lemma Q.0.7b. Hence $N[\phi_1] = N[\phi_2]$, and then $k = 0$. $\square$

**Interpretation.** On this registered phase-assignment branch, two paths with different integer event counts cannot have exactly equal phase modulo $2\pi$. Theorem Q.0.2e supplies that phase assignment once the PU and reference coherent channels are identified.

---

### Q.0.7.4 Dense Cyclic Subgroup of $U(1)$

<a id="theorem-q07d-density-of-the-registered-phase-generator"></a>**Theorem Q.0.7d (Density of the Registered Phase Generator).** *On the branch that assigns phase $N\ln2$ to an integer registered event count $N$, define the generator*
$$g_L := e^{i\ln 2} \in U(1)$$

*The subgroup generated by integer powers of $g_L$:*
$$G_L := \{e^{iN\ln 2} : N \in \mathbb{Z}\} = \{g_L^N : N \in \mathbb{Z}\}$$

*is dense in $U(1)$. Equivalently, the sequence $\{N\alpha_L \bmod 1\}_{N \in \mathbb{Z}}$ is dense (and equidistributed) in $[0,1)$.*

*Proof.* By Lemma Q.0.7b, $\alpha_L$ is irrational. The one-dimensional case of Kronecker's approximation theorem (Kronecker 1884) states that for irrational $\alpha$, the set $\{N\alpha \bmod 1 : N \in \mathbb{Z}\}$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z}$.

Applying this to $\alpha = \alpha_L$ implies $\{e^{2\pi i N\alpha_L}\}_{N \in \mathbb{Z}} = \{e^{iN\ln 2}\}_{N \in \mathbb{Z}}$ is dense in $U(1)$.

Moreover, Weyl's equidistribution theorem (Weyl 1916) strengthens this: for irrational $\alpha$, the sequence $\{N\alpha \bmod 1\}_{N=1}^{M}$ becomes uniformly distributed as $M \to \infty$:
$$\lim_{M \to \infty} \frac{1}{M} \#\{1 \leq N \leq M : N\alpha \bmod 1 \in [a,b)\} = b - a$$

for any $0 \leq a < b \leq 1$. $\square$

<a id="corollary-q07d-closure-of-the-registered-dense-cyclic-subgroup"></a>**Corollary Q.0.7d′ (Closure of the Registered Dense Cyclic Subgroup).** *The topological closure of the registered phase subgroup is the full circle group:*
$$\overline{G_L} = U(1)$$

*Equivalently, for every target phase $e^{i\theta} \in U(1)$ and every tolerance $\nu > 0$, there exists $N \in \mathbb{Z}$ such that:*
$$|e^{iN\ln 2} - e^{i\theta}| < \nu$$

*Proof.* The closure of a dense subset equals the ambient space. Apply Theorem Q.0.7d. $\square$

<a id="theorem-q07d2-registered-phase-action-and-holonomy-completion"></a>**Theorem Q.0.7d2 (Registered Phase-Action and Holonomy Completion).** Let
$$
G_L=\{e^{iN\ln2}:N\in\mathbb Z\}\subset U(1),
$$
which is dense by Theorem Q.0.7d, and let $(Y,d)$ be a complete metric space of finite-resolution response configurations. Suppose there is an isometric action
$$
\rho_L:G_L\longrightarrow\operatorname{Isom}(Y)
$$
such that every orbit map is uniformly continuous when $G_L$ carries the inherited circle metric. Then there is a unique continuous isometric action
$$
\overline\rho:U(1)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Isom}(Y)
$$
extending $\rho_L$. Every continuous $G_L$-invariant response functional is $\overline\rho(U(1))$-invariant. The same statement holds cellwise for a finite product cover. If a continuous $U(1)$ action is registered from the outset, the invariance conclusion follows directly from density and continuity, with no metric or isometry hypothesis.

If, in addition, $Y$ is a smooth manifold, $Z_1(Y)$ denotes its group of smooth singular integral $1$-cycles, $h:Z_1(Y)\to U(1)$ is a homomorphism, and a closed real two-form $\Omega$ satisfies, for every smooth singular integral $2$-chain $C$,
$$
\left[\frac{\Omega}{2\pi}\right]
\in
\operatorname{im}\!\left(H^2(Y;\mathbb Z)\to H^2_{\mathrm{dR}}(Y;\mathbb R)\right),
\qquad
h(\partial C)=\exp\!\left(i\int_C\Omega\right),
\tag{Q.0.7d2.1}
$$
then $(h,\Omega)$ is a degree-two differential character. It determines, up to connection-preserving isomorphism, a principal $U(1)$ bundle with connection of curvature $\Omega$ and holonomy $h$. The physical charge convention is $\Omega=qF$.

*Proof.* For $z\in U(1)$ choose $g_n\in G_L$ with $g_n\to z$. Uniform continuity makes $\rho_L(g_n)y$ Cauchy; completeness supplies a limit independent of the approximating sequence. Define $\overline\rho(z)y$ by that limit. Passing to limits proves the isometry and group laws, while
$$
d(\overline\rho(z_n)y_n,\overline\rho(z)y)
\le d(y_n,y)+d(\overline\rho(z_n)y,\overline\rho(z)y)
$$
gives joint continuity. Density gives uniqueness and extends invariance. If the $U(1)$ action is registered and continuous, then for continuous $G_L$-invariant $Z$ and $g_m\to z$ in $G_L$, continuity of the action and of $Z$ give $Z(z\cdot y)=\lim_mZ(g_m\cdot y)=Z(y)$. The final assertion is the differential-character classification of principal $U(1)$ bundles with connection under the integral-period and boundary identities (Q.0.7d2.1). ∎

<a id="corollary-q07d3-local-gauge-and-noether-completion-on-the-registered-branch"></a>**Corollary Q.0.7d3 (Local Gauge and Noether Completion on the Registered Branch).** Assume the cellwise completed actions and differential characters are compatible under refinement and descent, and the continuum branch has the differentiable minimally coupled action and boundary hypotheses of Theorem G.6b. Then
$$
\phi\mapsto e^{iq\alpha(x)}\phi,
\qquad
A_\mu\mapsto A_\mu-\partial_\mu\alpha,
$$
and on shell
$$
\nabla_\mu J^\mu=0,
\qquad
J^\mu=-iq\bigl(\phi^*D^\mu\phi-(D^\mu\phi)^*\phi\bigr),
$$
in the sign convention of Theorem G.6b.

*Proof.* Refinement compatibility and differential-character descent produce one local $U(1)$ bundle with connection. Varying the differentiable invariant action by compactly supported $\alpha$ and integrating by parts gives the result. ∎

<a id="theorem-q07d4-explicit-refining-event-character-gauge-and-ward-model"></a>**Theorem Q.0.7d4 (Explicit Refining Event-Character Gauge and Ward Model).** Let $K$ be a finite oriented cell complex. Assign $U_e\in U(1)$ to every oriented edge with $U_{\bar e}=U_e^{-1}$ and $\phi_v\in\mathbb C$ to every vertex. For $z_v=e^{i\alpha_v}$ define
$$
\phi_v\longmapsto z_v\phi_v,
\qquad
U_e\longmapsto z_{t(e)}U_ez_{s(e)}^{-1}.
\tag{Q.0.7d4.1}
$$
For positive weights $w_e,\beta_f$ and any real $C^1$ function $V$ on $[0,\infty)$, the finite action
$$
S_K
=\sum_e w_e|\phi_{t(e)}-U_e\phi_{s(e)}|^2
+\sum_f\beta_f\bigl(1-\operatorname{Re}\operatorname{Hol}_{\partial f}(U)\bigr)
+\sum_vV(|\phi_v|^2)
\tag{Q.0.7d4.2}
$$
is invariant under (Q.0.7d4.1). If a refinement replaces $e$ by the oriented path $e_1\cdots e_r$, impose
$$
U_e=U_{e_r}\cdots U_{e_1}.
\tag{Q.0.7d4.3}
$$
Then every coarse-loop holonomy equals its refined-loop holonomy, and the rule is compatible with successive refinements.

Suppose the admitted oriented event loops carry an additive homological count
$$
N:H_1(K;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z.
$$
By the universal-coefficient isomorphism, choose an integral cellular cocycle $n\in Z^1(K;\mathbb Z)$ representing $N$. The background assignment
$$
U_e^{(N)}:=e^{i n(e)\ln2}
$$
then gives, simultaneously for every admitted loop $\gamma$,
$$
\operatorname{Hol}_\gamma(U^{(N)})=e^{iN([\gamma])\ln2}.
\tag{Q.0.7d4.4}
$$
Give every edge a unit parameter interval. On any subdivision, assign to a child interval $I$ the phase $\exp(i n(e)|I|\ln2)$, with the inherited orientation. Products over partitions recover $U_e^{(N)}$, and partition refinement is associative, so the whole event character has an explicit refinement-compatible connection representative.

Variation of the vertex phase gives the oriented edge current
$$
J_e:=2w_e\operatorname{Im}
\bigl(\overline{\phi_{t(e)}}U_e\phi_{s(e)}\bigr)
$$
and define $(\operatorname{div}J)_v:=\sum_{t(e)=v}J_e-\sum_{s(e)=v}J_e$. The matter Euler--Lagrange equation then gives the on-shell interior identity
$$
(\operatorname{div}J)_v=0.
\tag{Q.0.7d4.5}
$$
Summing over a vertex region $R$ gives the exact boundary Ward balance
$$
\sum_{v\in R}(\operatorname{div}J)_v
=\sum_{e\in\partial R}\operatorname{sgn}_R(e)J_e.
\tag{Q.0.7d4.6}
$$
The finite-dimensional reference measure $\prod_vd^2\phi_v\prod_edU_e$, with normalized Haar measure $dU_e$, is invariant under (Q.0.7d4.1); hence this bosonic finite realization has unit Jacobian and zero gauge anomaly. Fermionic determinant phases require a separate anomaly calculation.

*Proof.* Each covariant edge difference in (Q.0.7d4.2) is multiplied by $z_{t(e)}$, face holonomies are conjugated trivially in $U(1)$, and the potential depends only on $|\phi_v|$, proving invariance. Associativity of group multiplication proves refinement functoriality and holonomy preservation. Evaluation of the cocycle on a cycle is $N([\gamma])$, proving (Q.0.7d4.4) for all admitted loops at once; additivity of interval lengths proves the subdivision statement. Differentiating the $C^1$ action with respect to $\alpha_v$ gives (Q.0.7d4.5); cancellation of oppositely oriented interior edges gives (Q.0.7d4.6). Lebesgue rotations and Haar translations preserve the finite measure, so its change-of-variables Jacobian is one. ∎

<a id="theorem-q07d5-lattice-holonomy-classification-of-event-ledgers"></a>**Theorem Q.0.7d5 (Lattice-Holonomy Classification of Event Ledgers).** Keep the finite oriented cell complex $K$ and the edge variables of Theorem Q.0.7d4. Fix one orientation of each edge, let $C_1(K)$ be the free abelian group of integral $1$-chains and $Z_1(K)=\ker\partial_1$ its cycle group, and for an edge assignment $U$ and a cycle $z=\sum_ez_ee$ put $\operatorname{Hol}_z(U):=\prod_eU_e^{z_e}$. This is a homomorphism $Z_1(K)\to U(1)$ that agrees with the loop holonomy of Theorem Q.0.7d4 on closed edge paths. Let $\Gamma$ be a set of admitted oriented closed edge paths with cycles $[\gamma]\in Z_1(K)$, and let $N:\Gamma\to\mathbb Z$ be an event ledger. Then:

1. Some edge assignment satisfies
   $$
   \operatorname{Hol}_\gamma(U)=e^{iN(\gamma)\ln2}
   \qquad(\gamma\in\Gamma)
   \tag{Q.0.7d5.1}
   $$
   if and only if $N$ is additive on cycle relations: whenever $\sum_jc_j[\gamma_j]=0$ in $Z_1(K)$ with $c_j\in\mathbb Z$ and $\gamma_j\in\Gamma$, also $\sum_jc_jN(\gamma_j)=0$.
2. Two edge assignments with equal holonomy on all of $Z_1(K)$ differ by a gauge transformation (Q.0.7d4.1). Hence, when the admitted cycles generate $Z_1(K)$, an additive ledger fixes its realizing connection up to gauge.
3. Let $S$ be the subgroup generated by the admitted cycles and $\tilde N$ the additive extension of $N$ to $S$. For every face $f$ with $\partial f\in S$, every realizing connection has $\operatorname{Hol}_{\partial f}(U)=e^{i\tilde N(\partial f)\ln2}$, which equals $1$ exactly when $\tilde N(\partial f)=0$. When all face boundaries lie in $S$, the realizing connections are flat exactly for ledgers with $\tilde N(\partial f)=0$ on every face, the homological situation of Theorem Q.0.7d4. A nonhomological additive ledger, one with $\tilde N(\partial f)\ne0$ for some face with $\partial f\in S$, is realized only by curved connections, and their plaquette term in (Q.0.7d4.2) is $\beta_f\bigl(1-\cos(\tilde N(\partial f)\ln2)\bigr)>0$ on every such face.
4. No lattice $U(1)$ connection represents a ledger with $N(\gamma)+N(\bar\gamma)\ne0$ for an admitted loop and its reversal, in particular a forward event count with $N(\gamma)\ge1$ and $N(\bar\gamma)\ge1$, or with $N(\gamma^k)\ne kN(\gamma)$ for an admitted power.

Gauge invariance, the refinement rule (Q.0.7d4.3), the Ward identities (Q.0.7d4.5)--(Q.0.7d4.6) and the unit Jacobian of Theorem Q.0.7d4 hold for every realizing connection.

*Proof.* $\operatorname{Hol}$ is a homomorphism on $Z_1(K)$ because it is a product of integer powers of commuting unit numbers, and orientation reversal and concatenation of closed edge paths correspond to negation and addition of cycles. If $U$ satisfies (Q.0.7d5.1) and $\sum_jc_j[\gamma_j]=0$, then $\exp(i\ln2\sum_jc_jN(\gamma_j))=\operatorname{Hol}_0(U)=1$, so $\ln2\sum_jc_jN(\gamma_j)\in2\pi\mathbb Z$, and irrationality of $\ln2/(2\pi)$ (Lemma Q.0.7b) forces $\sum_jc_jN(\gamma_j)=0$. Conversely, additivity makes $\chi(\sum_jc_j[\gamma_j]):=\exp(i\ln2\sum_jc_jN(\gamma_j))$ a well-defined homomorphism $S\to U(1)$. By the elementary-divisor theorem there are a basis $e_1,\ldots,e_r$ of the free group $C_1(K)$ and integers $d_1,\ldots,d_s\ge1$ such that $d_1e_1,\ldots,d_se_s$ is a basis of $S$; choosing $\chi(e_i)$ as a $d_i$-th root of $\chi(d_ie_i)$ for $i\le s$ and $\chi(e_i)=1$ for $i>s$ extends $\chi$ to $C_1(K)$, and $U_e:=\chi(e)$, $U_{\bar e}:=U_e^{-1}$ satisfies (Q.0.7d5.1). This proves item 1.

If $U$ and $U'$ have equal holonomy on $Z_1(K)$, the edge ratios $V_e:=U'_eU_e^{-1}$ define a homomorphism $C_1(K)\to U(1)$ that is trivial on $Z_1(K)=\ker\partial_1$, so $V=\psi\circ\partial_1$ for a homomorphism $\psi$ on the subgroup $\partial_1C_1(K)$ of the free group $C_0(K)$. The same elementary-divisor extension extends $\psi$ to $C_0(K)$, and with $z_v:=\psi(v)$ one gets $V_e=\psi(t(e)-s(e))=z_{t(e)}z_{s(e)}^{-1}$, which is (Q.0.7d4.1). This proves item 2.

For item 3, $\operatorname{Hol}_{\partial f}(U)=\chi(\partial f)=e^{i\tilde N(\partial f)\ln2}$ for every realizing $U$, which equals $1$ exactly when $\tilde N(\partial f)=0$ by Lemma Q.0.7b, and $\operatorname{Re}e^{i\theta}=\cos\theta$ gives the plaquette value. Item 4 is item 1 applied to the relations $[\gamma]+[\bar\gamma]=0$ and $[\gamma^k]-k[\gamma]=0$. The proofs of gauge invariance, holonomy refinement, current variation, boundary cancellation and measure invariance in Theorem Q.0.7d4 use only the edge variables and group multiplication, and never flatness. ∎

<a id="theorem-q07d6-finite-vector-like-fermionic-matter-on-the-event-character-lattice"></a>**Theorem Q.0.7d6 (Finite Vector-Like Fermionic Matter on the Event-Character Lattice).** On $K$ attach to each vertex $v$ Grassmann generators $\psi_{v,\alpha},\bar\psi_{v,\alpha}$, $\alpha=1,\ldots,r$, and fix complex $r\times r$ matrices $M_v$, $A_e$ and $B_e$. With one fixed orientation per edge, define for every edge assignment $U$ the finite Dirac-type matrix on $\mathbb C^{K_0}\otimes\mathbb C^r$ and the fermionic action
$$
D(U):=\sum_vE_{vv}\otimes M_v
+\sum_e\bigl(U_eE_{t(e)s(e)}\otimes A_e+U_e^{-1}E_{s(e)t(e)}\otimes B_e\bigr),
\qquad
S_F(U):=\bar\psi D(U)\psi,
\tag{Q.0.7d6.1}
$$
and extend (Q.0.7d4.1) by $\psi_v\mapsto z_v\psi_v$ and $\bar\psi_v\mapsto z_v^{-1}\bar\psi_v$. Then:

1. $D(U^z)=(Z\otimes I_r)D(U)(Z\otimes I_r)^{-1}$ with $Z=\operatorname{diag}(z_v)$, so $S_F$ is gauge invariant and the fermionic partition function
   $$
   Z_F(U):=\int\prod_{v,\alpha}d\bar\psi_{v,\alpha}d\psi_{v,\alpha}\,e^{-S_F(U)}=\det D(U)
   $$
   satisfies $Z_F(U^z)=Z_F(U)$.
2. The Berezin integral is invariant under the vertex phase rotations, which multiply the top Grassmann monomial by $\prod_v(z_v^{-1}z_v)^r=1$. This vector-like realization therefore has unit Jacobian and zero gauge anomaly, jointly with the bosonic sector of Theorem Q.0.7d4.
3. With the edge current
   $$
   J_e^F:=i\bigl(\bar\psi_{s(e)}U_e^{-1}B_e\psi_{t(e)}-\bar\psi_{t(e)}U_eA_e\psi_{s(e)}\bigr)
   \tag{Q.0.7d6.2}
   $$
   and $(\operatorname{div}J^F)_v$ formed as in Theorem Q.0.7d4, every element $\mathcal O$ of the Grassmann algebra satisfies the Schwinger--Dyson Ward identity
   $$
   \int\prod_{u,\alpha}d\bar\psi_{u,\alpha}d\psi_{u,\alpha}\;e^{-S_F(U)}\Bigl[(\operatorname{div}J^F)_v\,\mathcal O-\delta_v\mathcal O\Bigr]=0,
   \tag{Q.0.7d6.3}
   $$
   where $\delta_v\mathcal O$ is the derivative at $\alpha=0$ of $\mathcal O$ under $\psi_v\mapsto e^{i\alpha}\psi_v$, $\bar\psi_v\mapsto e^{-i\alpha}\bar\psi_v$. In particular $\langle(\operatorname{div}J^F)_v\rangle_U=0$ whenever $\det D(U)\ne0$, and the cancellation identity (Q.0.7d4.6) turns this into vanishing expected fermionic flux through the boundary of every vertex region.

## Lemma Q.0.7d8.1: genuinely chiral integer representation

Let $q=(-9,-5,-1,7,8)$, and take two identical copies, $Q=q\oplus q$. All ten candidate Weyl flavours are left-handed. Then

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum q &= -9-5-1+7+8 = 0, \\
\sum q^3 &= -729-125-1+343+512 = 0.
\end{aligned}
$$

No $q_{i}$ is zero and no $q_i+q_j$ is zero, including $i=j$. The representation $R(z)=\operatorname{diag}(z^{Q_a})$ has no conjugate-charge pairs, is not isomorphic to its conjugate, and admits no gauge-invariant bare Weyl mass bilinear: an entry $m_{ab}$ must obey $z^{Q_a+Q_b}m_{ab}=m_{ab}$ for every $z$ and thus vanishes. Doubling identical chirality and charges does not make the representation vector-like. It ensures that each odd absolute charge occurs twice. The representation is faithful because charge $-1$ occurs.

For the conventional four-dimensional spin Weyl anomaly polynomial, the degree-six part of $(\sum\exp(Q_a c_1))(1-p_1/24+\dots)$ is

$$
I_6=(\sum Q_a^3)c_1^3/6-(\sum Q_a)c_1 p_1/24=0.
$$

This explicit formal expansion checks the cubic and mixed linear coefficients. It is not a global-anomaly, determinant-line trivialization, or physical regulator proof by itself. No Standard Model selection is asserted.

For every accepted edge and path define $R(U_e)$ and $R(\operatorname{Hol}_w)$. Matrix multiplication, orientation reversal and subdivision commute exactly with $R$. Hence the flavour-$a$ holonomy is $\exp(iQ_aN(w)\ln 2)$. Charge multiplication does not change the actual motor ledger $N(w)\ln 2$ or create $Q_{a}$ physical events. It specifies a candidate matter representation of the connection $U_{e}$ defined above. Realizing the charged coupling by paid physical ports remains a new source requirement.

## Lemma Q.0.7d8.3: explicit gapped overlap operator at the matched flat background

Fix Hermitian Euclidean Clifford matrices $\gamma_\mu$ and $\gamma_5$. In the uniform gauge, charge $Q$ has momentum

$$
p_0=(2\pi k_0-Q L)/M,\quad p_j=2\pi k_j/M\ (j=1,2,3),\quad k_\mu\in \{0,\dots,M-1\}.
$$

Define the Wilson symbol with Wilson parameter 1 and negative mass -1,

$$
\begin{aligned}
A_Q(p)&=i \sum_\mu \gamma_\mu \sin p_\mu + [\sum_\mu(1-\cos p_\mu)-1] I, \\
D_Q(p)&=I+A_Q(p)/\sqrt{A_Q(p)^{\dagger}A_Q(p)}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Writing $t_\mu=1-\cos p_\mu\ge 0$ gives the exact scalar identity

$$
A_Q^{\dagger}A_Q = [1+2 \sum_{\mu<\nu} t_\mu t_\nu] I \ge I.
$$

Thus no denominator singularity occurs, uniformly in $M$, $Q$ or toron phase. This is an analytic gap proof, not a numerical sample. Let $V=A(A^\dagger A)^{-1/2}$. Then $V^\dagger V=I$ and $\gamma_5V\gamma_5=V^\dagger$. Direct expansion gives

$$
\begin{gathered}
\gamma_5D+D\gamma_5=D\gamma_5D, \\
D^\dagger=\gamma_5D\gamma_5, \\
\hat{\gamma}_5=\gamma_5(1-D),\quad (\hat{\gamma}_5)^\dagger=\hat{\gamma}_5,\quad (\hat{\gamma}_5)^2=I.
\end{gathered}
$$

Therefore $\hat{P}_-=(1-\hat{\gamma}_5)/2$ and $P_+=(1+\gamma_5)/2$ are exact projectors and $D\hat{P}_-=P_+D$. Impose $\hat{P}_-\psi=\psi$ and $\bar{\psi}P_+=\bar{\psi}$ separately on every flavour. This is a genuine Weyl projection rather than the unconstrained vector-like Grassmann model of Q.0.7d6. As a finite matrix it is fully specified by the Fourier symbols above; transforms to the slab gauge by conjugation.

For this specific toron no $D_{Q}$ zero mode occurs. $D=0$ requires $A$ negative scalar, hence every $\sin p_\mu=0$ and $\sum(1-\cos p_\mu)<1$; this forces all $p_\mu=0$ modulo $2\pi$. But $p_0=0$ would imply $Q\ln 2\in 2\pi\mathbb{Z}$, excluded for nonzero integer $Q$ by the original irrationality lemma. Each Weyl matrix between its projected spaces is therefore invertible. Choosing orthonormal bases at this one background defines a finite Berezin integral, up to its basis phase. This does NOT fix a smooth gauge-covariant measure across the full background space, nor prove a native physical realization of that integral.

## 2. Explicit uniform regulator and chart radius

On each charge block let $T_{\mu}(u)\psi(x)=u(x,\mu)^Q\psi(x+\mu)$. With the Hermitian $\gamma$ matrices fixed in the matrix and phase convention above, set

$$
\begin{aligned}
A(u) &= 3 I - (1/2) \sum_\mu [(I-\gamma_\mu)T_\mu +(I+\gamma_\mu)T_\mu^\dagger], \\
H(u) &= \gamma_5 A(u),\quad D(u)=I+\gamma_5 \operatorname{sign} H(u),\quad P(u)=(I+\operatorname{sign} H(u))/2,\quad P_+=(I+\gamma_5)/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

Then $H$ is Hermitian. At $u^*$, $(H^*)^2=A^{*\dagger}A^*\ge I$ by the already proved Fourier identity. Since $\lVert(I\pm\gamma_{\mu})/2\rVert=1$ and $|\exp(iQ\alpha)-1|\le|Q\alpha|$,

$$
\lVert H(u_{\alpha})-H^*\rVert\le 8\lvert Q\rvert\delta\le 72\delta=:\eta.
$$

Let $s_{M}$ be the minimum of the positive singular values of all $D_Q(u^*)$; it is positive by the interface's finite momentum proof. It is an explicitly defined finite minimum, not an unknown continuum gap. Choose

$$
\delta=\min(10^{-4}, s_M/288),\quad g_0=1-\eta.
$$

Then $\eta\le 0.0072$, $H(u_{\alpha})$ has spectral gap at least $g_0$, and all matrix functions above are smooth throughout the chart. No admissibility theorem is needed for this bound. The elementary plaquette angles have magnitude $\le 4\delta$, so $9(4\delta)\le 0.0036<1/30$ as an additional check, but that alone is not used as a chiral-measure theorem.

For completeness, the sign bound is elementary. Subtract the imaginary-axis resolvent representations for two $g_0$-gapped Hermitian matrices. The difference is absolutely integrable; the resolvent identity bounds its norm by $\eta/(g_0^2+t^2)$. Integration with factor $1/\pi$ gives

$$
\begin{gathered}
\lVert\operatorname{sign}H-\operatorname{sign}H^*\rVert\le\eta/g_0, \\
\lVert P-P^*\rVert\le\eta/(2g_0)<1, \\
\lVert D-D^*\rVert\le\eta/g_0<s_M/2.
\end{gathered}
$$

Thus $D$ is invertible on this entire family. Its chiral restriction has equal input/output rank $n_Q=2V$ (constant along the chart), and is invertible because $DP=P_+D$. These statements remain true on every gauge orbit by conjugation. The bound $s_{M}$ is dimensionless; it is not a physical energy gap.

## 5. Exact obstruction to identifying S with the old coarse overlap matrix

At $t=0$, low/high momentum blocks decouple, so $S$ is exactly the fine Weyl operator restricted to the selected low momenta. Compare its physical-unit version $S/a_f$ with the earlier coarse $D_c/a_c$ restricted to their Weyl spaces, where $a_c=\ell/M$, $a_f=\ell/(2M)$. Singular values are invariant under all admissible orthonormal input/output frame choices, so a mismatch cannot be cured by a phase convention.

Take charge $Q=-1$ and a momentum with only its 0-component nonzero. Write $p=(2\pi k+\ln 2)/M$ in $(-\pi,\pi)$. The Wilson symbol is $A=-\cos p+i\gamma_{0}\sin p$, so $A^\dagger A=I$ and $D=1-\cos p+i\gamma_{0}\sin p$. Therefore both Weyl singular values are $2|\sin(p/2)|$. The corresponding selected fine momentum is $p/2$ and has singular values $2|\sin(p/4)|$. In physical units the fine/coarse singular-value ratio is exactly

$$
[(2M/\ell)2|\sin(p/4)|]/[(M/\ell)2|\sin(p/2)|]=1/\cos(p/4).
$$

At $M=3$, $k=0$ and $k=1$ both satisfy $0<p<\pi$ and have distinct $p$. Their ratios are unequal because cosine is strictly decreasing on $(0,\pi/4)$. Thus:

1. Under the nominated momentum-preserving identification, $S/a_f$ is not unitarily frame-equivalent to the nominated coarse $C_c/a_c$.
2. No one scalar field-strength factor, even charge dependent, repairs both momenta of this one charge.
3. A background phase/counterphase multiplying the determinant cannot fix this action/singular-value defect.

One can algebraically introduce a momentum-dependent field redefinition or simply adopt $S$ as the coarse action. Either changes the nominated coarse source/operator and must carry its Jacobian, determinant normalization, locality analysis and supplier map. It is not already supplied by the original chart construction. The defect is $O(p^2)$ for these individual fixed smooth modes as $M$ grows, but that elementary statement is not an all-mode determinant, local-current or continuum convergence estimate; ultraviolet modes and growing multiplicities remain uncontrolled.

Its period on $C$ alone would not imply flatness or fix the other periods, both of which the Fourier calculations that follow require.

## Precise two-mode obstruction

The two singular-value ratios in section 5 compare CORRESPONDING selected momentum blocks under the nominated integer-momentum identification. They prove failure of that momentum-preserving identification, even after arbitrary unitary input/output frame changes within those blocks and one scalar field-strength factor for the charge. They also exclude determinant phase changes as a repair of that blockwise action mismatch.

They do not, by themselves, rule out an arbitrary unitary transformation mixing different momentum blocks, or such a transformation combined with an arbitrary scalar. Item 1 of section 5, and every statement that frame changes are excluded, carries this momentum-preserving qualification. An unrestricted unitary-equivalence claim requires a comparison of the complete singular-value multisets, not two corresponding labels. No unrestricted obstruction is claimed.

The exact Schur-complement transition, high-factor retention, source responses and finite associativity are unaffected. The claim that the resulting effective matrix is not equal to the nominated coarse matrix in the specified momentum-compatible refinement map remains proved.

## 2. Uniform stability derived from the explicit toron spectrum

Let $d_*=\min_Q\operatorname{dist}(QL,2\pi\mathbb{Z})>0$. This is a finite positive constant fixed by the accepted character and charges. For every flat momentum $p$ in principal coordinates, its temporal component has $|p_0|\ge d_*/M$. Write $W=\sum_{\mu}(1-\cos p_{\mu})-1$, $R=\sqrt{W^2+\sum\sin^2 p_{\mu}}$. The overlap singular value is $s(p)=\sqrt{2+2W/R}$.

If $W\ge 0$ then $s\ge\sqrt{2}$. If $W<0$ then $\sum(1-\cos p)<1$, hence every $|p_{\mu}|<\pi/2$. The identity

$$
s^2=2 \sum \sin^2 p/[R(R-W)] \ge \sum \sin^2 p/R^2
$$

and $R<8$, $|\sin p_{\mu}|\ge 2|p_{\mu}|/\pi$ imply $s\ge|p|/(4\pi)\ge d_*/(4\pi M)$. The same lower bound is harmless in the $W\ge 0$ case. Thus the previously defined flat minimum obeys $s_M\ge d_*/(4\pi M)$, with no numerical extrapolation.

Choose a fixed positive t0 satisfying

$$
t_0 F < \min(3\cdot 10^{-4}, d_{*}/(1152\pi)).
$$

\end{gathered}
$$

These are uniform over $M$ and $|t|<t_0$ and transfer exactly to each Weyl restriction. They are dimensionful Euclidean inverse estimates, not a physical Hamiltonian energy-gap claim.

## 3. Continuum operator and smooth inverse, constructed without a continuum measure premise

For each charge define the continuum first-order operator on periodic smooth spinors

$$

K_Q(t) &= (1/\ell) \sum_\mu \gamma_\mu[\partial_{y_\mu}-iQ A_\mu(t)], \\

$$

constructs a bounded inverse with norm $\le 2\ell/d_*$ throughout the same family. It is not assumed as a primitive continuum propagator.

## 4. A uniform O(a) consistency and inverse-error proof

Use the sampling map $(J_M\psi)(j)=a^2\psi(aj)$, so Euclidean lattice $\ell^2$ approximates continuum $L^2$ on the side-$\ell$ torus. All lattice $\gamma$ matrices and links are expressed in the uniform gauge in this proof; the previously retained slab/tree maps give unitary-equivalent statements.

Let $A_{M}$ be the Wilson matrix and $B_M=A_M^\dagger A_M$. For each fixed smooth $\psi$, covariant Taylor expansion of the exact link integral and nearest-neighbor shift gives

\end{gathered}

The constants are uniform in $M$ and $|t|\le t_0$. Here the first-order expansion is $A_M=-I+aK+O(a^2)$; its adjoint has first-order term $-aK$ because $K$ is anti-Hermitian. Thus the first-order terms in $B_M-I$ cancel. The second estimate can equivalently be checked by expanding the finite width-two stencil directly. Finite derivatives of $f$ and $\psi$ bound all pointwise remainders; the $a^{2}$ sampling weight turns the sum over $M^4$ sites into a bounded volume factor. These are estimates on smooth vectors, not a false operator-norm claim that $B_{M}$ tends to $I$ on ultraviolet modes.

Since $B_M\ge g_M^2I$ with $g_{M}>0.99$, the scalar identity

and spectral calculus give

C=c_1+11c_2/[0.99(1+0.99)].
\end{gathered}
$$

For a fixed smooth source $h$ put $\psi=K_Q(t)^{-1}h$. The smooth-inverse construction supplies a uniform bound on $C(\psi)$. The resolvent identity on this vector, together with section 2 stability, proves

This is actual controlled convergence on the common nonflat family. It neither uses nor implies convergence uniformly over cutoff-dependent rough tests.

and converges to $S_K^{\mathrm{cont}}=B_K(t)^{-1}$, with error bounded by the inverse-product identity and the preceding $O(a)$ estimate. ## 4. Ward and region-flux content, with limits

Sampling a fixed smooth $\lambda$ and using the normalized fixed-test convergence yields its continuum version. ## 1. An explicit chiral, relative continuum construction

## 2. Controlled finite approximation of this target, distinct from overlap cutoffs

## 1. Exact operator identity and orientation

One may express F0 in the standard Pplus Fourier coordinates by a fixed unitary change of basis, which preserves all trace powers and the relative determinant. No moving input frame or new determinant phase is introduced by this representation.

Let $H_+$ be the continuum right-handed Hilbert space and $B=K(0)^{-1}P_+$. Let $V=\partial_zK(z)=-(iQ/\ell)\gamma_1f(y_2)$ on each charge, with the fixed ten-flavour direct sum. The target operator on $H_+$ is

This is the RIGHT-space orientation. The preceding target note used $T_-=K(0)^{-1}V$ on $H_-$.
