The abstract census for all continuous representations in Theorem Q.0.7t.4 remains mathematical: a representation given in a basis without finite description has no finite controller programme.

*Proof.* **One admitted compiler and positive physical pulse.** Every input word has finitely many finite-dimensional supports and a finite tree. Its matrix operations, Pauli expansion, norm-bound checks, slot emission and occurrence accounting are finite. A Hermitian matrix has real coefficients in the orthogonal Pauli basis, which proves (Q.0.7t.5.3) and gives an explicit finite list of supplied spin couplings. For $\|L\|\le B$ and $2\pi m\ge B$, $K_L\ge0$, so the total pulse Hamiltonian is nonnegative. Moreover
$$
\|H_L(s)\|\le\frac\hbar{\tau_*}(B+2\pi m),\qquad
\int_0^{\tau_*}\|H_L(s)\|\,ds
\le\hbar(B+2\pi m).
\tag{Q.0.7t.6.1}
$$
The constant pulse has propagator
$$
U_L(s)=e^{-iK_Ls/\hbar}.
$$
At the endpoint $e^{-2\pi im}=1$, so
$$
U_L(\tau_*)=e^{-iL}
\tag{Q.0.7t.6.2}
$$
on the entire carrier, with no data-dependent phase. Identity padding has zero Hamiltonian and endpoint $I$, while retaining its time, idle stock and clock charge. The same calculation with block-diagonal $L$ proves the coherent-control assertion: no measurement of its control and no control-conditioned supplier record occurs.

The waveform's finite work bookkeeping is explicit. There is no continuous variation inside a pulse. Switching on contributes $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho K_L)$ and switching off contributes $-\operatorname{Tr}(U_L\rho U_L^*K_L)$. Since $[U_L,K_L]=0$, they cancel for every input, including inputs entangled with a spectator. The signed work of this ideal complete pulse is zero, and its total absolute mean switching-work throughput is bounded by
$$
2\|K_L\|\le\frac{2\hbar}{\tau_*}(B+2\pi m).
\tag{Q.0.7t.6.3}
$$
This is an isolated zero-idle driven pulse with no bath. Prepared stock, controller, holding, peak reserve and later record services retain their positive source charges, and the tariff is separate from net work. The actual peak is $\|K_L\|$ and its pulse action is $\tau_*\|K_L\|$, with (Q.0.7t.6.1) as their certified bounds. Thus no drift cancellation, negative total Hamiltonian or unrecorded phase is needed.

The local service alphabet already admits a finitely described unitary with its complete supported generator and normalization certificate, fresh finite registers, finite classical controls and projective records. Equations (Q.0.7t.5.1)--(Q.0.7t.6.3) supply those data explicitly. All active factors are at the named port, so the source's inter-port rule is satisfied without an uncharged link. The two three-register port carriers and every auxiliary, including unused support, have allocated owners. The new control-word decoder specified here accepts exactly the emitted finite typed expansions and rejects an additional access port, unowned initial resource, missing spectator extension or unlisted command. It uses the inherited primitive contracts without changing the separate heat-source decoder. Conversely every descriptor satisfying the listed finite tests has the displayed expansion. This is admission and exhaustion of one prescribed source class on Definition 27's finite Hilbert/instrument branch.

**Group generators on the same carrier.** Choose a faithful finite unitary representation $\rho:G\to U(d)$ and use the reference-augmented $R=1\oplus\rho$ on $r=d+1$ dimensions. For the two Lie-algebra elements $Z_{j,q}$ in (Q.0.7t.4.5), set
$$
L_{j,q}=i\,dR(Z_{j,q}),\qquad
e^{-iL_{j,q}}=R(g_{j,q}).
\tag{Q.0.7t.6.4}
$$
These matrices are Hermitian, their zero reference block is explicit, and their norms have finite certified upper bounds, for example their Frobenius norms enlarged to positive rationals. Inverse controls use $-L_{j,q}$. The coherent command uses
$$
L_{{\rm ctrl},q}=|x\rangle\!\langle x|\otimes L_{1,q}
+|z\rangle\!\langle z|\otimes L_{2,q}
\tag{Q.0.7t.6.5}
$$
on the actual two-level interface. Use the same $m$ for its full matrix. By (Q.0.7t.6.2) the supplied pulse is exactly the controlled $R(g_{j,q})$, with the reference component retained in each block. In the one-generator case retain just its block; the trivial group needs no generating pulse. Multiplying the exact endpoint unitaries realizes every finite word and every inverse word. The constant connection and its ordered transports in Theorem Q.0.7t.4 are realized by these endpoint matrices on the same reference and representation; the connection's unit path parameter is not substituted for the pulse duration $\tau_*$.

Every group isomorphism class has a finite exact description. The semisimple simply connected cover is specified by its finite Cartan data. Its integral dominant weights give finite-dimensional representations whose matrix entries are obtained by the finite root-string construction; an admissible lattice gives integer matrices for the Chevalley generators (Humphreys 1972, Section 27). Tensoring and taking finite direct sums supplies representations with the prescribed central characters; finite central descent and a faithful finite sum recover the chosen compact quotient. Torus characters are integral weights. These are the usual finite root/weight constructions behind the faithful-representation and compact-group structure results used in Theorem Q.0.7t.4. Their generators are algebraic after a compact orthonormal basis choice; the displayed $q$ and $\alpha_L$ add only explicitly described constants. A chosen presentation and its verified representation matrices enter the source descriptor, while all subsequent pulse and record compilation is the single rule above.

**Preparations and complete measurements.** The Hadamard reflection satisfies $V_j^2=I$, so its spectral generator gives $e^{-iL_j^{\rm prep}}=V_j$. It sends the fresh data vector $|0\rangle$ to the required $|\psi_j\rangle$ without borrowing an undeclared coherent state. The supplied phase/drive reference is already in the inventory. For $A=X_{0a}$ or $Y_{0a}$, extend $A$ by zero on padding. Its spectrum lies in $\{-1,0,1\}$, so both effects are positive and normalized on the entire data carrier. Their square roots commute, $\|\Theta\|\le\pi/2$, and multiplication of (Q.0.7t.5.4) by its adjoint gives $I$. Applied to $|0\rangle_{\rm det}$ it has the two components $\sqrt{E_+}$ and $\sqrt{E_-}$. The retained computational record consequently gives exactly the selective maps stated in the definition, including their zero-probability leaves and their detector output states. Summing the maps preserves trace. The separate record slot has the same zero-idle convention; its ideal elementary computational record service is the same registered primitive as in Definition C.6c.4a, not an inferred measurement postulate for the spin Hamiltonian.

Theorem Q.0.7t.4 now gives (Q.0.7t.4.6) as the actual source probabilities. Recovering every entry of the faithful $\rho(g)$ proves payload response-faithfulness, including scalar central phases that unreferenced conjugation would erase. For example, $R(g)=\operatorname{diag}(1,zI)$ with $z\ne1$ changes at least one of these real or imaginary interference responses. No claimed central distinction rests on an unobservable common phase of the entire carrier.

**Full retained intertwiner.** Build the reference experiment with exactly the encoded data and interface carrier, the fresh detector factors, and every prepared supplier and record factor specified by the compiler. Its record label includes command, protocol-tree node, physical entrance and exit times, source/phase identities, outcome, success or failure flag, coefficient-certificate identity and the complete resource counters. The physical encoding is the computational-basis isometry on the data code, tensored with the identity identification on all other retained factors; invalid data-code states use their explicitly defined complementary reference sector. It therefore defines a unitary identification of the full physical carrier with the complete encoded reference carrier, rather than a partial trace over unobserved supplier stock.

For each full selective label $a$ at history $h$, the equality of the unitary or detector Kraus matrices gives
$$
\widetilde{\mathcal I}_{a|h}\bigl(E_h\rho E_h^*\bigr)
=E_{ha}\mathcal I_{a|h}(\rho)E_{ha}^*.
\tag{Q.0.7t.6.6}
$$
Every fresh source factor is inserted with the same specified state on the two sides; if a supplied state is mixed, that same density operator and its retained supplier factor are part of both reference carriers, rather than represented as a pure-state isometry. Equation (Q.0.7t.6.6) holds for all matrix units and after every spectator identity extension. Composition proves equality of every unnormalized finite history state. Taking traces gives all probabilities; conditioning is used only at positive trace, and null leaves remain zero operators. Adaptive commands are functions of the same previous retained records, so induction over the finite protocol tree proves the same equality for every admitted policy. Summing outcomes, retaining subsets of records and adjoining spectators commute with this equality. The identical emitted schedule and owner assignment preserve every clock and resource entry, including unused stock and the idle second port and lane.

This full statement is stronger than equality of the matrix-response array but has the correct quotient. A longer word representing the identity still has its executed pulses, clock duration and invoice. The full reference carries that decoration. Projecting both sides to the final data operation forgets only the explicitly selected source records and gives the homomorphism $w\mapsto R(g_w)$; equality of this payload action is exactly equality of $g_w$, by the reference-augmented separating experiment.

**Finite accuracy and resource completion.** In exact mode all source identities above are exact mathematical laws. For an implemented pulse $\widetilde H$ with the same duration,
$$
\|\widetilde U-U\|\le\hbar^{-1}\int\|\widetilde H(s)-H(s)\|\,ds
\tag{Q.0.7t.6.7}
$$
follows by differentiating the interaction-picture relative propagator and integrating. Its unitary channels differ in full diamond norm by at most twice this quantity. For comparison with an approximate implementation, retain the same actual descriptor, certificate labels, schedules and resource records in the exact-reference experiment and replace only its quantum primitive maps by their specified ideal maps. Different physical descriptor strings are not called trace-distance-close. Assign each full primitive instrument with that common record convention, including preparation and complete outcome flags, a half-diamond error $\varepsilon_j$. A hybrid argument on the history-extended state bounds the half trace distance of the entire retained output, and hence its total-variation record error, by the largest root-to-leaf sum $\sum_j\varepsilon_j$. Thus no conditional rare outcome is assigned an unproved error bound after division by its probability. Classical calibration and missing-record failures are explicit output flags; they are not deleted to improve the estimate.

For a requested finite matrix-response test, fresh independent trials under the same fixed calibrated descriptor estimate each binary probability. If $K$ probabilities are requested, $N\ge\lceil\log(2K/\alpha)/(2\delta^2)\rceil$ trials per setting give simultaneous sampling error at most $\delta$ with probability at least $1-\alpha$. Systematic complete-instrument errors add to this bound, and all $KN$ trial stocks and their retention intervals are reserved beforehand. Exact group separation is independent of this sampling estimate.

All counts and durations are finite for every finite descriptor and protocol. The Pauli list, setup computation, prepared support, detector and source records, phase/clock services, reserves and holding intervals have explicit disjoint owners. The fixed positive tariff prices their union; each resource occurs once, and shared services retain a single owner across trials. Restriction to a shorter protocol retains its already reserved stocks and invoices rather than making them free. No cyclic erasure, global minimality, autonomous control or uniform resource bound as dimension or word length grows is a premise of this finite source realization. This completes the source, response, clock, composition, resource and error predicates. $\square$

### Q.0.7.18 Summary

This section shows that repeatedly adding the registered binary phase step fills the circle densely. Physical gauge symmetry and interference still require the separately stated dynamics and calibration records.

#### Technical binary-phase results ledger

This section has established:

1. **Landauer Irrationality:** $\alpha_L = \ln 2/(2\pi) \notin \mathbb{Q}$ (Lemma Q.0.7b), proven via Gelfond–Schneider transcendence

2. **Dense U(1) Emergence:** $\overline{G_L} = U(1)$ where $G_L = \{e^{iN\ln 2}\}$ (Theorem Q.0.7d)

3. **Exact Phase Separation:** On the registered action-calibrated branch, distinct update counts have distinct baseline phases; an interference claim additionally requires realized coherent histories and their amplitudes (Corollary Q.0.7c)

4. **Exact-Closure Overhead:** On the registered calibrated branch, every nonzero exact-closure lift has $\Delta>0$; a topological interpretation additionally requires the differential-character identification (Corollary Q.0.7g)

5. **Continued-Fraction Spectrum and Arithmetic Index:** Convergent pairs $(k,N)$ of $\alpha_L$ satisfy the stated first- and second-kind best-approximation bounds; reduced pairs meeting the strict Legendre threshold are convergents. Physical loop realization remains a separate certificate (Theorem Q.0.7k, Theorem Q.0.7k.1, Corollary Q.0.7l)

6. **Three-Gap Arithmetic:** Finite arithmetic phase sets partition the circle into at most three arc lengths; accessibility requires realized phase-calibrated histories (Proposition Q.0.7n)

7. **Conditional Dephasing:** On the calibrated coherent-ensemble branch, overhead fluctuations suppress the averaged phase by $|\Phi_\Delta(1)|$ (Proposition Q.0.7p)

8. **Conditional Gauge-Holonomy Interface:** The discrete $G_L$ action extends to $U(1)$ under the continuity hypotheses; connection holonomy additionally requires the differential-character compatibility certificate (Remark Q.0.7r)

9. **Landauer-Noether Closure:** Continuous finite-resolution response functionals invariant under $G_L$ are invariant under $U(1)$, and, on the separate local-coupling closure branch, the Noether current of Appendix G follows (Theorem Q.0.7d2; Corollary Q.0.7d3)

<a id="proposition-q07d8a-necessary-face-budget-for-a-filled-event-holonomy-loop"></a>**Proposition Q.0.7d8a (Necessary Face Budget for a Filled Event-Holonomy Loop).** Retain the event-character holonomy $e^{iL}$, $L=\log2$, of Theorem Q.0.7d8. Suppose a proposed filling is an actual oriented disk made of $R$ elementary faces, with their $U(1)$ link variables agreeing on shared edges and with the prescribed loop as its boundary. Let the principal plaquette angles satisfy $|\theta_f|<\epsilon$ for a specified $0<\epsilon<1/270$. Then
$$
R\epsilon>L,\qquad R>270\log2>187,\qquad R\ge188.
\tag{Q.0.7d8a.1}
$$
In particular one elementary face with angle $L$ violates this specified small-field bound. Subdividing only the boundary cannot change its parent holonomy or create the required interior faces.

*Proof.* In the product of the oriented face holonomies, every internal edge cancels with its oppositely oriented occurrence. Thus
$$
\prod_{f=1}^R e^{i\theta_f}=e^{iL},\qquad
\sum_{f=1}^R\theta_f=L+2\pi k\quad\text{for some }k\in\mathbb Z.
\tag{Q.0.7d8a.2}
$$
Since $0<L<1<\pi$, every integer $k$ gives $|L+2\pi k|\ge L$. The triangle inequality and strict face bounds therefore give $R\epsilon>\sum_f|\theta_f|\ge L$. To certify the integer endpoint without a decimal logarithm, integrate the positive geometric series for $1/(1-x^2)$ between zero and $1/3$:
$$
\log2=2\operatorname{artanh}(1/3)
=2\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}\frac{(1/3)^{2j+1}}{2j+1} >2\left(\frac13+\frac1{81}+\frac1{1215}\right)
=\frac{842}{1215}
=\frac{187}{270}+\frac1{2430}.
\tag{Q.0.7d8a.3}
$$
This proves (Q.0.7d8a.1). The single-face and boundary-only statements follow because the boundary product remains $e^{iL}$. ∎

The bound is necessary for this filled-disk and prescribed face-angle contract. It supplies neither a sufficient filling nor an admitted physical subdivision, and it does not assert a singular overlap operator, an all-regulator obstruction or a four-dimensional extension. #### Q.0.8.1 The Cycle Number

<a id="definition-q02-cycle-number"></a>**Definition Q.0.2 (Cycle Number).** For a registered finite history $\phi$, define
$$
N[\phi]:=\#\{\text{registered update events along }\phi\}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}.
$$
If the branch assigns the structural ledger value $\ln2$ to every counted event, then $\mathcal L_{\mathrm{disc}}=N[\phi]\ln2$. If it also supplies $\mathcal S=\kappa_A\mathcal L$ and $\kappa_A=\hbar$, then $\mathcal S=N[\phi]\hbar\ln2$. Each implication is conditional on its own ledger.

<a id="proposition-q03-discrete-integrality"></a>**Proposition Q.0.3 (Discrete Integrality).** The count $N[\phi]$ is a nonnegative integer. This is immediate from the cardinality definition and supplies no quantization of an independently defined mechanical action. ∎

#### Q.0.8.2 Topological Quantization for Closed Paths

For a closed-path branch on which the total transported amplitude is required to have trivial holonomy, the following conditional quantization identity holds.

<a id="theorem-q04-conditional-phase-holonomy-quantization"></a>**Theorem Q.0.4 (Conditional Phase-Holonomy Quantization).** Let $\vartheta$ be a locally defined action one-form on a closed path $\gamma$, and suppose parallel transport multiplies the amplitude by
$$
\exp\!\left(\frac{i}{\hbar}\oint_\gamma\vartheta\right).
$$
Requiring the transported amplitude to return to the same value gives
$$
\frac1\hbar\oint_\gamma\vartheta=2\pi k,
\qquad k\in\mathbb Z.
$$
If a separately calibrated phase ledger identifies $\hbar^{-1}\oint_\gamma\vartheta$ with $\sum_iq_i$, then $\sum_iq_i=2\pi k$. A globally single-valued scalar action instead satisfies $\oint_\gamma d\mathcal S=0$. ∎

<a id="corollary-q04a-selected-character-closed-sector-obstruction"></a>**Corollary Q.0.4a (Selected-Character Closed-Sector Obstruction).** On the selected character branch $N\mapsto e^{iN\ln2}$, exact trivial holonomy requires
$$
N\ln2=2\pi k,
\qquad N,k\in\mathbb Z.
$$
Since $\ln2/(2\pi)$ is irrational, the only solution is $N=k=0$. This is a statement about the selected character, not a universal obstruction on physical cycles. ∎

<a id="remark-q04b-non-integer-period-and-resolution"></a>**Remark Q.0.4b: Non-Integer Period and Resolution.** The formal real-valued period $\Delta N_0=2\pi/\ln2\approx9.0647$ is not an admissible integer count period. On the selected-character branch,
$$
e^{iN\ln2}=1
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
N\ln2=2\pi k.
$$
Irrationality of $\ln2/(2\pi)$ implies $N=k=0$, so the character has no nonzero integer period. This is an arithmetic obstruction, not a physical tension requiring a dynamical resolution.

For consecutive integer labels, the orbit $\{e^{iN\ln2}\}$ is equidistributed in $U(1)$. A physical ensemble is uniform only if realized histories sample those labels with the required weights. At finite budget, convergent denominators give record-small arithmetic mismatches. Approximate interference additionally requires separately realized coherent histories, amplitudes, and an operational phase tolerance.

<a id="theorem-q05a4-calibrated-marked-leech-particle-realization"></a>**Theorem Q.0.5a.4 (Calibrated Marked Leech Particle Realization).** On the canonical four-dimensional complex-scalar source with marked internal configuration torus, isotropic metric, common gradient law and independently specified positive calibrator inputs below, every finite marked Leech-vector set has a positive physical particle mass operator, a singleton positive calibration fiber and finite normalized label/preparation/response instruments. ### 2. Marked lattice, configuration torus and exact mode map

### 3. The four-dimensional action and particle pole

Physical spacetime is $M=\mathbb{R}^{1,3}$, $x^0=ct$, with signature $(+---)$. The source field $\Phi(x,y)$ is complex and takes values in $L^2(Y)$. Its dimension is inverse length in the canonical action

and the same relation for $b$, all other elementary commutators zero. The positive one-particle Hilbert space is the direct sum over $v$ of $L^2(\mathbb{R}^3,d^3k/[(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_v])$, for each particle/antiparticle charge sector. Physical translations act with

### 7. Observable particle pole and certified finite-time source response

The particle pole can be checked by an independent driven response of the same action. Finite box normalization is owned in the spatial source/readout mode; it changes no mass term. Infinite-volume particle poles are the exact free distributional limit of the same dispersion law. At $\omega=0$ use the continuous value $\sin(\omega s)/\omega=s$. The infinite-window response is

Indeed $|\sin(\omega s)/\omega|\le s$ and the remaining exponential integral is exact. Thus any desired absolute susceptibility accuracy is attained by an explicitly finite window chosen from (7.2). No unbounded-time pole observation is assumed to be an executed experiment.

A classical source term linear in a free quantum field creates a coherent displacement whose mean satisfies this same retarded equation exactly. ### <a id="q09-the-conditional-rindler-landauer-timescale"></a>Q.0.9 The Conditional Rindler--Landauer Timescale

#### Q.0.9.1 Independent Ingredients

The Unruh temperature is
$$
T_U(a)=\frac{\hbar a}{2\pi k_Bc}.

On a registered uniformly accelerated reset branch with constant acceleration magnitude $a>0$ and a reservoir at the displayed Unruh temperature, impose the complete Definition 28 contract at $T_U(a)$. A conditionally uniform binary record then satisfies the ensemble-mean Landauer bound $\langle Q_{\mathrm{bath}}\rangle\ge k_BT_U\ln2$. $$
E\tau=\kappa_A\ln2.

#### Q.0.9.2 The Conditional Timescale

<a id="theorem-q010-conditional-rindler-landauer-timescale"></a>**Theorem Q.0.10 (Conditional Rindler--Landauer Timescale).** Assume the complete registered reset branch just stated, exact ensemble-mean Landauer heat saturation, a separately certified cyclic mean-energy balance $E=\langle Q_{\mathrm{bath}}\rangle$, and the independent action-duration equality $E\tau=\kappa_A\ln2$. Then
$$
\tau_U(a)=\frac{\kappa_A}{\hbar}\frac{2\pi c}{a}.
$$
