The horizon closed-loop transfer branch is accepted only after the additional finite entries of $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{hor}}$ are supplied and verified.

<a id="lemma-q07v-thermal-phase-identity"></a>**Lemma Q.0.7v (Thermal Phase Identity).** For any horizon with Hawking temperature $k_B T_H=\hbar\kappa/(2\pi c)$ and Rindler-Landauer cycle time $\tau_H=2\pi c/\kappa$,
$$
\frac{\hbar\omega}{k_B T_H}=\omega\tau_H.
$$

*Proof.* Multiplying $k_B T_H=\hbar\kappa/(2\pi c)$ by $\tau_H=2\pi c/\kappa$ gives $k_B T_H\tau_H=\hbar$. Dividing $\hbar\omega$ by $k_B T_H$ gives $\omega\tau_H$. $\square$

<a id="proposition-q07v1-explicit-finite-lossless-same-loop-transfer-map"></a>**Proposition Q.0.7v.1 (Explicit Finite Lossless Same-Loop Transfer Map).** Fix an accepted retained horizon channel $\mathfrak H_n^{\mathrm{ret}}$, a finite mode set $\Omega$, and the Rindler--Hawking entries $(T_H,\tau_H)$ of Definition Q.0.7u. On a one-dimensional retained scattering-mode fiber, define
$$
\mathcal S_\omega=e^{i\omega\tau_H},
\qquad
\mathcal M_{\mathrm{scat}}(\mathcal S_\omega)
:=[\omega\tau_H]_{2\pi}
=\left[\frac{\hbar\omega}{k_BT_H}\right]_{2\pi}.
\tag{Q.0.7v.1.1}
$$
For an independently registered structural label $N\ge1$, let the same loop fiber subsequently acquire the controlled phase $e^{-iN\ln2}$. The complete loop multiplier is therefore
$$
U_{\omega,N}
=e^{i(\omega\tau_H-N\ln2)},
\tag{Q.0.7v.1.2}
$$
so the complete loop multiplier equals one exactly when
$$
\omega\tau_H-N\ln2\in2\pi\mathbb Z.
\tag{Q.0.7v.1.3}
$$
Choose $\mathcal D_{\mathrm{loop}}=\Omega\times\{1,\ldots,N_{\max}\}$, and register the phase-acceptance predicate $\operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}(\omega\tau_H,N\ln2)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}$ on that domain before spectral comparison. This supplies a finite lossless abstract phase map and a tolerance predicate. On the one-dimensional fiber, $U_{\omega,N}\rho U_{\omega,N}^{\dagger}=\rho$ for every phase, so trivial loop holonomy alone is not an observable constructive-interference or resonance-peak condition. An operational $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{peak}}$ additionally requires a registered coherent reference and interference/readout certificate relating its measured response to that predicate, with the stated resolution and uncertainty. The retained horizon channel and its KMS/metric descent are also imported premises.

*Proof.* The scattering multiplier is unitary and its argument is the first expression in (Q.0.7v.1.1); Lemma Q.0.7v gives the thermal-coordinate equality. Serial phases on the same one-dimensional fiber multiply, proving (Q.0.7v.1.2). A unit complex number equals one exactly when its phase is in $2\pi\mathbb Z$, proving (Q.0.7v.1.3). Scalar phases cancel in the density-matrix channel, which proves the stated readout limitation. The displayed finite domain and predicate are specified independently of spectral data; they do not construct the additional interference instrument. ∎

<a id="proposition-q07v2-greybody-interferometric-readout-of-the-same-loop-predicate"></a>**Proposition Q.0.7v.2 (Greybody Interferometric Readout of the Same-Loop Predicate).** Keep the data of Proposition Q.0.7v.1 and replace the lossless multiplier $\mathcal S_\omega=e^{i\omega\tau_H}$ by a registered unitary two-port on the loop mode $|l\rangle$ and a loss mode $|\ell\rangle$ whose loop-to-loop amplitude is $\mathcal T_\omega e^{i\omega\tau_H}$, with greybody transmission $\mathcal T_\omega=|\mathcal T_\omega|e^{i\varphi_\omega}$, and whose loop-to-loss amplitude is $\mathcal R_\omega$, where $|\mathcal T_\omega|^2+|\mathcal R_\omega|^2=1$; the case $\mathcal T_\omega=1$ is (Q.0.7v.1.1). Add a reference mode $|r\rangle$, prepare the single excitation $(|r\rangle+|l\rangle)/\sqrt2$, send $|l\rangle$ through the two-port and then through the controlled phase $e^{-iN\ln2}$, recombine $|r\rangle$ and $|l\rangle$ on the balanced splitter $|r\rangle\mapsto(|+\rangle+|-\rangle)/\sqrt2$, $|l\rangle\mapsto(|+\rangle-|-\rangle)/\sqrt2$, and read out the projective measurement $\{|+\rangle,|-\rangle,|\ell\rangle\}$. With $\Phi_{\omega,N}:=\omega\tau_H-N\ln2$ the outcome probabilities are
$$
P_\pm=\frac14\Bigl(1+|\mathcal T_\omega|^2\pm2|\mathcal T_\omega|\cos(\Phi_{\omega,N}+\varphi_\omega)\Bigr),
\qquad
P_\ell=\frac12|\mathcal R_\omega|^2,
\tag{Q.0.7v.2.1}
$$
and the contrast is $\mathcal K:=P_+-P_-=|\mathcal T_\omega|\cos(\Phi_{\omega,N}+\varphi_\omega)$. Then:

1. If $|\mathcal T_\omega|>0$ and $\varphi_\omega$ is registered, then for every $\varepsilon\in[0,\pi]$
   $$
   \operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}(\omega\tau_H+\varphi_\omega,N\ln2)\le\varepsilon
   \iff
   \mathcal K\ge|\mathcal T_\omega|\cos\varepsilon.
   \tag{Q.0.7v.2.2}
   $$
   At $\mathcal T_\omega=1$ this is the tolerance predicate of Proposition Q.0.7v.1 as an observable threshold.
2. Two greybody records with equal $|\mathcal T_\omega|$ and phases differing by an element of $\mathbb R\setminus2\pi\mathbb Z$ have the same loss probability and the same fringe visibility $2|\mathcal T_\omega|/(1+|\mathcal T_\omega|^2)$, while at fixed $\omega$, hence fixed $\mathcal T_\omega$, $P_+$ as a function of the loop phase $\Phi_{\omega,N}$ is maximal exactly on $\Phi_{\omega,N}+\varphi_\omega\in2\pi\mathbb Z$. In a frequency scan, where $|\mathcal T_\omega|$ and $\varphi_\omega$ vary with $\omega$, the normalized contrast $\mathcal K/|\mathcal T_\omega|=\cos(\Phi_{\omega,N}+\varphi_\omega)$, with $|\mathcal T_\omega|^2=1-2P_\ell$ read from the loss outcome, attains its maximum $1$ exactly on that set; the raw probability $P_+$ has $\omega$-derivative $\frac12(1+|\mathcal T_\omega|)\,\partial_\omega|\mathcal T_\omega|$ there, so its frequency peaks are displaced from that set wherever $\partial_\omega|\mathcal T_\omega|\ne0$. Maxima of the normalized contrast therefore locate the Landauer grid of Proposition Q.0.19 only after the greybody phase is registered, and the grid appears displaced by $-\varphi_\omega$ in the thermal coordinate $x=\omega\tau_H$. If $\mathcal T_\omega=0$, then $P_\pm=1/4$ for every $\Phi_{\omega,N}$.
3. For $n$ independent repetitions with outcome counts $n_\pm$, the estimator $\hat{\mathcal K}:=(n_+-n_-)/n$ satisfies $\Pr(\hat{\mathcal K}-\mathcal K\ge s)\le e^{-ns^2/2}$ and $\Pr(\hat{\mathcal K}-\mathcal K\le-s)\le e^{-ns^2/2}$ for $s>0$. For $0<\vartheta\le\min\{\varepsilon,\pi-\varepsilon\}$ put $s_\vartheta:=|\mathcal T_\omega|\min\{\cos(\varepsilon-\vartheta)-\cos\varepsilon,\ \cos\varepsilon-\cos(\varepsilon+\vartheta)\}$. The rule that accepts exactly when $\hat{\mathcal K}\ge|\mathcal T_\omega|\cos\varepsilon$ rejects a pair at phase distance at most $\varepsilon-\vartheta$, and accepts a pair at phase distance at least $\varepsilon+\vartheta$, each with probability at most $e^{-ns_\vartheta^2/2}$.

*Proof.* After the two-port and the controlled phase the state is $\frac1{\sqrt2}\bigl(|r\rangle+\mathcal T_\omega e^{i\Phi_{\omega,N}}|l\rangle+\mathcal R_\omega|\ell\rangle\bigr)$, and balanced recombination gives the amplitudes $\frac12(1\pm\mathcal T_\omega e^{i\Phi_{\omega,N}})$ at $|\pm\rangle$ and $\mathcal R_\omega/\sqrt2$ at $|\ell\rangle$. Squaring gives (Q.0.7v.2.1), and the three probabilities sum to one because $|\mathcal T_\omega|^2+|\mathcal R_\omega|^2=1$. For item 1, $\cos(\Phi_{\omega,N}+\varphi_\omega)=\cos\operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}(\omega\tau_H+\varphi_\omega,N\ln2)$, the distance lies in $[0,\pi]$, and cosine is strictly decreasing there; division by $|\mathcal T_\omega|>0$ gives (Q.0.7v.2.2). Item 2 follows from (Q.0.7v.2.1), since $P_\ell$ and the visibility depend only on $|\mathcal T_\omega|$; differentiating $P_+$ along a frequency scan at $\Phi_{\omega,N}+\varphi_\omega\in2\pi\mathbb Z$, where the cosine is stationary, leaves the term $\frac12(1+|\mathcal T_\omega|)\,\partial_\omega|\mathcal T_\omega|$. For item 3, each repetition contributes an independent variable in $\{1,-1,0\}\subset[-1,1]$ with mean $\mathcal K$, so Hoeffding's inequality (Hoeffding 1963) gives both tails; on the two stated distance ranges, monotonicity of cosine places $\mathcal K$ at least $s_\vartheta$ above or below the threshold. ∎

<a id="proposition-q07v3-sharp-characteristic-return-bound"></a>**Proposition Q.0.7v.3 (Sharp Characteristic Return Bound).** The characteristic translation of Construction E.9.5f.29 has the following sharp one-time return bound, including its finite physical-source comparison. The retained longitudinal support and real elapsed time determine the bound independently of the KMS period. For any Hilbert space $\mathcal K$, $a>0$, and norm-one $f\in L^2(\mathbb R;\mathcal K)$ supported in an interval of length $W>0$, put $n=\lceil W/a\rceil$ and $T_af(y)=f(y-a)$. Then

$$
|\langle f,T_af\rangle|\le\cos\frac{\pi}{n+1}.
$$

The bound is sharp, and the return-error, leakage and finite-source estimates below hold on their specified classes.

*Proof.*

Let $a>0$, let $T_af(y)=f(y-a)$ on $L^2(\mathbb R;\mathcal K)$, and suppose $f$ has norm one and is supported in an interval of length $W>0$. Put $n=\lceil W/a\rceil$. Translation of the interval does not change the overlap. Decompose the interval into residues modulo $a$. Almost every residue has a chain of at most $n$ occupied sites. On a chain of length $m$, the relevant compressed translation is the truncated shift $J_m$.

For every real $\theta$, the Hermitian matrix

$$
\frac{e^{i\theta}J_m+e^{-i\theta}J_m^*}{2}
$$

is diagonally unitarily equivalent to the path adjacency matrix with off-diagonal entries $1/2$. Its eigenvectors have components $\sin(jk\pi/(m+1))$, $1\le j\le m$, and its eigenvalues are $\cos(k\pi/(m+1))$. Therefore

$$
\operatorname{Re}(e^{i\theta}\langle v,J_mv\rangle)
\le \cos\frac{\pi}{m+1}\,\|v\|^2
\le \cos\frac{\pi}{n+1}\,\|v\|^2.
$$

Integrate over residues, then maximize over $\theta$. This gives

$$
|\langle f,T_af\rangle|\le\cos\frac{\pi}{n+1}.
$$

The bound is attained by a common smooth bump supported inside a residue interval of width less than $W-(n-1)a$, copied to the $n$ consecutive translated cells with coefficients

$$
c_j=\sqrt{\frac{2}{n+1}}\sin\frac{j\pi}{n+1},\qquad 1\le j\le n.
$$

This construction is smooth and compactly supported. The endpoint case $W/a\in\mathbb N$ causes no correction: interval endpoints have measure zero. For $W\le a$, the overlap is zero.

Consequently the minimum vector return error after a freely optimized scalar phase and the leakage from the initial one-dimensional fibre obey

$$
\min_\theta\|T_af-e^{i\theta}f\|^2
\ge 2\left(1-\cos\frac{\pi}{n+1}\right),
\qquad
1-|\langle f,T_af\rangle|^2\ge\sin^2\frac{\pi}{n+1}.
$$

Even without compact support, a nonzero normalizable vector cannot have unit return overlap at $a\ne0$. Equality in Cauchy–Schwarz would imply $T_af=e^{i\theta}f$; its squared modulus would be periodic with positive integral over some period, contradicting square integrability. This is a single-time statement, stronger on its particular operand than an all-time invariant-subspace argument, but its source class remains unchanged translation.

**Finite physical-source comparison.**

Use the actual massless Dirac call of Construction E.9.5f.50 with fixed boost duration $a>0$, normalized initial mode

$$
J_{S,0}(y,z)=f(y+S)g(z)v_+,
\qquad \alpha^1v_+=v_+,
$$

where $v_+$ is a unit vector, $\|f\|=\|g\|=1$, $g\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^2)$, $f$ is smooth and supported in a longitudinal interval of width $W$, and $b$ bounds $e^y$ on that unshifted interval. (E.9.5f.50.N2) proves, for the actual geometric Dirac generator $K$ and chiral generator $K_0$,

$$
\|e^{-iaK}J_{S,0}-e^{-iaK_0}J_{S,0}\|
\le d_S,
\qquad d_S=be^{-S}(e^a-1)\|\nabla g\|_2.
$$

Proposition Q.0.7v.3 therefore gives, with $n=\lceil W/a\rceil$,

$$
\left|\left\langle J_{S,0},e^{-iaK}J_{S,0}\right\rangle\right|
\le \min\left\{1,\cos\frac{\pi}{n+1}+d_S\right\}.
$$

For a finite unitary $U_{\mathrm{fin}}$, normalized source input $j$ and isometric common realization $I$, suppose

$$
\|Ij-J_{S,0}\|\le\epsilon,\qquad
\|IU_{\mathrm{fin}}j-e^{-iaK}J_{S,0}\|\le\delta.
$$

Then its actual same-fibre return amplitude $A_{\mathrm{fin}}=\langle j,U_{\mathrm{fin}}j\rangle$ obeys

$$
|A_{\mathrm{fin}}|
\le \min\left\{1,\cos\frac{\pi}{n+1}+d_S+\epsilon+\delta\right\}.
$$

The difference between the physical Dirac overlap and the chiral overlap is at most $d_S$ by Cauchy–Schwarz. The chiral overlap is exactly $\langle f,T_af\rangle$ because the normalized transverse/spin factors are unchanged. For the finite source, subtract the two overlaps after using the isometry $I$. The error from the first vector is at most $\epsilon$ and the error from the second is at most $\delta$. Both finite vectors have unit norm. Apply the triangle inequality and the universal unitary-overlap bound one. This proves the finite-source estimate. The leakage from the retained input fibre is exactly $1-|A_{\mathrm{fin}}|^2$, so it has the corresponding squared lower bound.

At the actual thermal-period time $a=2\pi$, a longitudinal packet of width $W\le2\pi$ has zero ideal return overlap and finite-source overlap at most $d_S+\epsilon+\delta$. This bound concerns the unchanged one-pass source; the return of Theorem Q.0.7v.4 comes from its added loop boundary.

For $f_\lambda(y)=e^{i\lambda y}\chi(y)$ with real $\chi$, the unmodified chiral return amplitude is

$$
\langle f_\lambda,T_af_\lambda\rangle
=e^{-i\lambda a}\int\chi(y)\chi(y-a)\,dy.
$$

It is derived from the source packet and is generally attenuated. Its temporal Schrödinger sign is distinct from the positive spatial propagation phase $e^{i\lambda L}$ used in the stationary graph scattering calculation. Those two conventions must be related explicitly by a port dictionary rather than identified by symbol alone.

$\square$

<a id="theorem-q07v4-explicit-horizon-lead-loop-scattering-model"></a>**Theorem Q.0.7v.4 (Explicit Horizon-Lead Loop Scattering Model).** Take one invariant characteristic horizon channel of Constructions E.9.5f.29 and E.9.5f.50, with incoming one-particle space $L^2(\mathbb R)$, generator $h_0=-i\partial$ and its actual covariance $C_0=(1+e^{2\pi h_0})^{-1}$. Attach the oriented lead–loop quantum graph specified below, with loop length $L>0$, $0<r<1$, $t=\sqrt{1-r^2}$ and independently registered $\sigma\in\mathbb C$, $|\sigma|=1$. Then the explicit incoming wave operator is unitary onto the complete graph space; the graph dynamics and inherited quasifree reference have the same $2\pi$ KMS normalization; and its per-pass complex scattering amplitudes, eventual reflection, internal resonances and finite echo errors are the expressions below. A smooth bounded finite-width chiral coupling profile derives $r,t$ and its additional phase and delay. The real Rindler travel time is determined by the independently specified return geometry.

This is a continuum quantum-graph source with its complete incoming field and loop sector. Its realization by the finite Dirac/material source and the joint Definition-E.9.5d/F.10.12a comparison remain the finite-source interface described after the proof.

*Proof.*

**Stationary source and amplitudes.**

Let $0<r<1$, $t=\sqrt{1-r^2}$ and $|\sigma|=1$. Use an external oriented line, cut at zero, and an internal oriented loop $s\in(0,L)$. The unitary vertex rule is

$$
\begin{pmatrix}g(0+)\\a(0+)\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}r&t\\-t&r\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\sigma\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}f(0-)\\a(L-)\end{pmatrix}.
$$

On a stationary solution of $-i\partial_s$ with frequency $\lambda$, normalize the incoming amplitude to one and write $a(s)=Ae^{i\lambda s}$. With $z=e^{i\lambda L}$,

$$
A=-t+r\sigma zA,
\qquad
S=r+t\sigma zA.
$$

Since $|r\sigma z|<1$, this gives

$$
A=-\frac{t}{1-r\sigma z},
\qquad
S=\frac{r-\sigma z}{1-r\sigma z},
\qquad |S|=1.
$$

The internal same-pass retention amplitude is $r\sigma z$ and its escape amplitude is $t\sigma z$. The complete stationary one-lead reflection is all-pass; its modulus is not a greybody attenuation. Its internal intensity is

$$
|A|^2=\frac{1-r^2}{1+r^2-2r\operatorname{Re}(\sigma z)}.
$$

For $r>0$ it is maximal exactly at $\sigma z=1$. If $\sigma=e^{-iN\ln2}$, this is the registered structural-phase condition $\lambda L-N\ln2\in2\pi\mathbb Z$. This calculation distinguishes the per-pass two-port amplitude from the eventual one-lead all-pass reflection.

**Onto incoming wave operator and physical graph generator.**

For almost every $s\in(0,L)$ let $f_j(s)=F(s+jL)$, $j\ge0$, for the positive half of an incoming $F\in L^2(\mathbb R)$. Define

$$
a_j=-t\sum_{k\ge0}(r\sigma)^k f_{j+k},
\qquad
g_j=rf_j+t\sigma a_{j+1}.
$$

The sums converge by Cauchy–Schwarz. They obey

$$
\begin{pmatrix}g_j\\a_j\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}r&t\sigma\\-t&r\sigma\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}f_j\\a_{j+1}\end{pmatrix}.
$$

The matrix is unitary, so

$$
\sum_{j=0}^M|g_j|^2+|a_0|^2
=\sum_{j=0}^M|f_j|^2+|a_{M+1}|^2.
$$

The bound $|a_{M+1}|\le(\sum_{j\ge M+1}|f_j|^2)^{1/2}$ makes the last term tend to zero. Thus the map from $(f_j)_{j\ge0}$ to $(a_0,(g_j)_{j\ge0})$ is isometric.

For arbitrary square-summable $(g_j)$ and arbitrary $a_0$, invert recursively:

$$
f_j=rg_j-ta_j,
\qquad
a_{j+1}=\bar\sigma(tg_j+ra_j).
$$

The resulting sequence $a_j$ is the sum of the square-summable sequence $(r\bar\sigma)^ja_0$ and a convolution of $g_j$ with an $\ell^1$ geometric sequence. Thus $a\in\ell^2$, $a_j\to0$, and $f\in\ell^2$. Backward iteration recovers the displayed infinite series. This proves onto-ness. Integrating over $s$ and retaining the unchanged negative external half-line proves that $\Omega$ is unitary from the incoming line onto the full graph Hilbert space.

The inverse relation also checks every boundary sign. If $F\in H^1(\mathbb R)$, then $a_0(L-)=a_1(0+)$ and the vertex equations hold. The positive-line interval endpoints glue continuously. Differentiation commutes with the bounded geometric series. Therefore $h=\Omega(-i\partial)\Omega^*$ acts as $-i\partial$ on each edge with precisely the stated boundary condition and is self-adjoint. Conversely the inverse gluing formulas give the corresponding domain.

This $\Omega$ is the incoming wave operator. A compact incoming profile translated sufficiently far into the negative lead has no positive-half-line components. Its loop component and positive outgoing component under $\Omega$ vanish exactly. Hence $\Omega$ agrees with the natural embedding before that profile reaches the vertex. Density and unitary boundedness give the usual incoming asymptotic identity. Its onto-ness excludes omitted dark or bound modes for $0<r<1$.

**Inherited KMS reference and physical-time convention.**

If the incoming horizon field has the actual covariance

$$
C_0=(1+e^{2\pi h_0})^{-1},\qquad h_0=-i\partial,
$$

then the graph state obtained by the incoming field realization has

$$
C=\Omega C_0\Omega^*=(1+e^{2\pi h})^{-1}.
$$

Use the CAR convention

$$
\alpha_t(a^\dagger(f))=a^\dagger(e^{\mathrm{ith}}f),\qquad
\alpha_t(a(f))=\alpha_t(a^\dagger(f))^*,\qquad
\omega(a^\dagger(f)a(g))=\langle g,Cf\rangle.
$$

Then $C$ defines the gauge-invariant quasifree $2\pi$-KMS state for this physical boost flow. Indeed $Ce^{2\pi h}=I-C$ on bounded spectral supports supplies the upper-strip two-point KMS boundary identity; the CAR and Wick expansion extend that identity to every finite analytic monomial. Bounded spectral test vectors are dense, so the identity extends to the CAR algebra. The state is inherited through the incoming scattering transform. No Fock-normal density matrix or trace-class Gibbs partition function on the infinite graph is required.

The input covariance must remain the full correlated horizon covariance. Temporal wavepacket bins generally have nonzero correlations. Replacing them by independent local thermal ancillas changes the source and does not follow from this construction. Likewise the Gibbs formula at this stage is a continuum graph statement. A finite matrix compression is not automatically invariant under the graph flow and its compressed covariance need not equal the Gibbs function of the compressed physical generator.

**Finite echo errors and retained boundary defect.**

Truncating the internal sum after $k=M-1$ gives

$$
\|a_0-a_0^{(M)}\|_{L^2(0,L)}\le r^M\|F\|_{L^2(0,\infty)}.
$$

For the positive outgoing field,

$$
g(x)=rF(x)-t^2\sum_{k\ge0}(r\sigma)^k\sigma F(x+(k+1)L),\qquad x>0.
$$

Each positive translation is a contraction on the half-line, hence

$$
\|g-g^{(M)}\|\le t^2\sum_{k\ge M}r^k\|F\|
=(1+r)r^M\|F\|.
$$

The combined graph error is at most $\sqrt{1+(1+r)^2}\,r^M\|F\|$. For $F\in H^1$, the same estimates apply to $F'$ on the separate edges. They give an edgewise $H^1$ estimate. The truncated fields generally fail the vertex boundary condition: direct cancellation in the finite sum gives

$$
a_0^{(M)}(0+)+tF(0-)-r\sigma a_0^{(M)}(L-)
=t(r\sigma)^M F(ML).
$$

Thus the truncated field need not belong to $\operatorname{Dom}(h)$, and the edgewise derivative estimate is not an operator graph-norm estimate for $h$. For an $H^1$ representative, the retained trace defect is bounded by

$$
t r^M |F(ML)|\le t r^M\|F\|_{H^1(\mathbb R)}.
$$

The last bound follows from $|F(x)|^2\le2\|F\|_2\|F'\|_2\le\|F\|_{H^1}^2$, obtained by integrating the derivative of $|F|^2$ from a sequence tending to $-\infty$ on which $F$ tends to zero. An exact finite experiment instead retains the final loop memory and every emitted lead sector; deleting the tail is an approximation, not an exact unitary source.

**Source-derived finite-width coupling and complete phase.**

A two-component co-propagating chiral segment with source Hamiltonian

$$
h_c=-i\partial_s I-v(s)\sigma_y,
\qquad v\in C_c^\infty((0,d);\mathbb R),
$$

has stationary propagation

$$
\psi(d)=e^{i\lambda d}\exp\left(i\sigma_y\int_0^d v(s)\,ds\right)\psi(0).
$$

Extend $v$ by zero outside the segment and set $M(s)=\exp(i\sigma_y\int_{-\infty}^sv(q)\,dq)$. Multiplication by $M$ is unitary, preserves $H^1(\mathbb R;\mathbb C^2)$, and direct differentiation gives $h_c=M(-i\partial_s I)M^*$. This proves self-adjointness on that domain. The stationary formula follows by integrating the first-order equation; the matrices commute along this segment. For $\theta=\int v\in(0,\pi/2)$ the stripped scattering matrix is $B$ with $r=\cos\theta$, $t=\sin\theta$. The amplitudes are thus derived from a retained source coupling profile.

Let $L_{\mathrm{free}}$ be the return-path optical length excluding this common coupling segment. Its real delay $d$ enters the total loop length $L_{\mathrm{tot}}=L_{\mathrm{free}}+d$. Solving the same two boundary equations with the full segment matrix $e^{i\lambda d}B$ gives

$$
A_d(\lambda)=-\frac{t e^{i\lambda d}}{1-r\sigma e^{i\lambda L_{\mathrm{tot}}}},\qquad
S_d(\lambda)=e^{i\lambda d}\frac{r-\sigma e^{i\lambda L_{\mathrm{tot}}}}{1-r\sigma e^{i\lambda L_{\mathrm{tot}}}}.
$$

The loop resonance uses $L_{\mathrm{tot}}$, and the external common phase $e^{i\lambda d}$ remains in its comparison with a coherent reference unless that reference traverses the same owned delay. Stripping this factor is a coordinate convention, not permission to omit its measured phase. Taking a point-contact limit with fixed $\theta$ forces $\|v\|_\infty\ge\theta/d$, since $|\int_0^d v|\le d\|v\|_\infty$. The strength, real delay and source work/control ledger remain charged. This chiral matrix Hamiltonian requires its own realization in the original Dirac/material source for the finite transfer record of Definition Q.0.7u.

**Real return geometry.**

In a Rindler radial section, null propagation satisfies $|d\eta|=|d\rho|/\rho$. A reflection between boost-static radii $\rho_a<\rho_b$ therefore has round-trip boost time

$$
L=2\log(\rho_b/\rho_a).
$$

The equality $L=2\pi$ is an independently fixed geometric condition $\rho_b/\rho_a=e^\pi$ (modified by any separately present coupler delay). KMS periodicity supplies no equation selecting that radius ratio. Once the geometry is specified, the real travel time is derived rather than inserted as a nominal gate period.

For reference-clock radius $\rho_*=c^2/\kappa$, physical time is $s=(c/\kappa)\eta$, where $\eta$ is boost time. Hence a loop with total optical length $L_{\mathrm{tot}}$ has

$$
\tau_{\mathrm{loop}}=\frac{c}{\kappa}L_{\mathrm{tot}},\qquad
k_BT_H=\frac{\hbar\kappa}{2\pi c},\qquad
\frac{\hbar\omega}{k_BT_H}=\frac{2\pi c\omega}{\kappa}.
$$

Definition Q.0.7u's required duration $\tau_H=2\pi c/\kappa$ therefore holds exactly when $L_{\mathrm{tot}}=2\pi$; on that branch the real-time thermal-coordinate identity follows for every $\omega$. If the radial free path has $L_{\mathrm{free}}=2\log(\rho_b/\rho_a)$ and a separate coupler adds $d>0$, that condition is $2\log(\rho_b/\rho_a)+d=2\pi$, with no double counting of a coupling segment already included in the radial length. The frequency relation is $\lambda=c\omega/\kappa$. On the independently registered structural-phase branch $\sigma=e^{-iN\ln2}$, the internal resonance condition becomes $\omega\tau_{\mathrm{loop}}-N\ln2\in2\pi\mathbb Z$. The first-pass instrument of Proposition Q.0.7v.2 must use its actual complex per-pass amplitude and owned reference delay, and retain or separately resolve later echoes. The eventual reflection coefficient has unit modulus and is a different observable.

$\square$

**Finite-source comparison.** Constructions E.9.5f.50, E.9.5f.51 and E.9.5f.53, Proposition E.9.5f.52 and Theorem E.9.5f.53a supply the selected finite one-pass horizon/KMS/common-code source. Theorem Q.0.7v.5 below extends that source by finite smooth material barriers and a static phase plate, with its actual clock, supports, retained controllers and output sectors, interaction/energy/work bounds and common field comparison. It supplies the actual changed generator/reference, overlaps and local flux/capacity record consumed by Definition E.9.5d and Definition F.10.12a on the asserted cover. The exact graph KMS statement of Theorem Q.0.7v.4 does not supply these finite comparisons, as the following compression constraint shows.

A two-mode calculation identifies a specific finite-compression constraint.

Fix $\beta=2\pi$, $E>0$ and

$$
h=\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&E\end{pmatrix},\qquad
F(x)=\frac1{1+e^{\beta x}},\qquad
v=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\end{pmatrix}.
$$

The physical generator compressed to the $v$ mode is the scalar $h_v=E/2$, whereas the restriction of its faithful quasifree reference has covariance

$$
c_v=\langle v,F(h)v\rangle
=\frac14+\frac1{2(1+e^{\beta E})}.
$$

Set $q=e^{\beta E/2}>1$. Direct subtraction gives

$$
c_v-F(E/2)
=\frac{(q-1)^3}{4(1+q^2)(1+q)}>0.
$$

*Proof.* Substitute $e^{\beta E}=q^2$. The common numerator of
$(q^2+3)/(4(1+q^2))-1/(1+q)$ is

$$
q^3-3q^2+3q-1=(q-1)^3.
$$

Positivity follows from $q>1$. The full covariance is the physical Gibbs covariance by its defining functional calculus; restriction to the one-mode CAR algebra gives the displayed scalar covariance. Its compressed physical Hamiltonian is $\langle v,hv\rangle=E/2$. Thus the two quantities are explicitly unequal. $\square$

The one-mode modular generator can instead be defined by

$$
h_{\mathrm{mod}}=\beta^{-1}\log\frac{1-c_v}{c_v},
$$

but the strict inequality proves $h_{\mathrm{mod}}\ne E/2$. That choice changes the finite physical-time evolution. A legitimate finite source must provide the actual state/dynamics error comparison or an invariant finite realization; neither is supplied by writing a Gibbs formula after compression. The actual finite state/dynamics comparison therefore belongs to the new return-boundary source; the established selected source of Constructions E.9.5f.50, E.9.5f.51 and E.9.5f.53, Proposition E.9.5f.52 and Theorem E.9.5f.53a remains available.

Theorem Q.0.7v.4 establishes the stated graph-level return, derived scattering and inherited KMS construction. Theorem Q.0.7v.5 supplies the finite-source realization and its separate state/dynamics comparison on the stated operational domain. The structural $N\ln2$ phase retains its independent registration.

<a id="theorem-q-0-7v-5-finite-horizon-loop-source"></a>

<a id="theorem-q07v5-finite-material-horizon-loop-kms-reference-and-readout"></a>**Theorem Q.0.7v.5 (Finite Material Horizon Loop, KMS Reference and Readout).** In the prescribed-background, driven-material source class of Constructions E.9.5f.37, E.9.5f.48–51 and E.9.5f.53, Proposition E.9.5f.52 and Theorem E.9.5f.53a, the selected characteristic operational cover admits a finite-source horizon closed-loop transfer record of Definition Q.0.7u. Fix a finite spectral band, finitely many nominated mode centers, a finite structural-label range $1\le N\le N_{\max}$, strictly positive comparison and phase tolerances, and a confidence level before spectral comparison. The construction has the following properties.

1. Two smooth finite-width real mass barriers and a smooth static vector phase plate act on four identical Dirac information species. Their continuum scattering amplitudes follow from their specified differential operator. The actual finite pulsed source supplies its own matrix elements, with a certified comparison error to those amplitudes. Both leads, cavity occupation, spectator spin sectors, source controls, archives and all other carrier factors remain retained.
2. The inner-face distance is $\ell=\pi$ and the phase-plate integral is $(N\ln2+\pi)/2$. At the registered Rindler clock radius $\rho=c^2/\kappa_H$, the geometrical round-trip time is $\tau_H=2\pi c/\kappa_H$ and $\hbar\omega/(k_BT_H)=\omega\tau_H$. The exact finite-width continuum multiplier is $q(E)=G(E)e^{i(2\pi E-N\ln2)}$, with the source-derived complex greybody factor $G(E)=-r'_1(E)r_2(E)$. Its additional phase and dwell delay are retained; the geometrical round-trip time is not asserted to equal the full Wigner delay.
3. The true static KMS reference, actual finite geometric Gibbs covariance, installed active/ambient reference and driven scattering preparation have distinct specified roles. Exact incoming active compressions preserve the characteristic regional maps. Explicit covariance-column, local regularity, finite-code, graph and cell estimates supply their required comparisons. The local Hilbert heat/capacity identity is tested before the incoming packet reaches a potential; a later no-return receiver retains the entire scattered ququart, reflected and transmitted branches together.
4. Two reference quadratures measure the full complex reflection and recover the loop multiplier by a controlled rational inversion. Finite preparation, capture and observation tails, finite physical-source errors and registered confidence bounds enter the phase tolerance. The selected diagnostic clears the entire finite regulated field and reference-path field in their native basis, with full displacement archives. It requires no exact-rank decision on a backward-image span and does not assume time-isolated narrow-band echoes.
5. The common source-first schedule is terminating at every fixed strictly positive tolerance. It includes the complete covariant action, source and current payers, finite reference installation, full-carrier response gap, and actual preparation, control, timing, storage and readout costs. Old retained outputs and their geometric tests are preserved by the full-carrier hold/swap construction and actual support exclusion.

The theorem establishes existence in the prescribed-background finite operational source class on the selected characteristic cover. The structural phase is an independent physical registration. ##### Q.0.7v.5.2. Finite radial barriers and loop phase

All phases below are physical complex amplitudes at explicitly stated barrier faces. The claims concern specified finite-band incoming scattering packets, not convergence of entire ultraviolet unit balls.

###### 1. General mass phase and the registered structural factor

On the two-component radial block let

$$
h=-i\sigma_3\partial_x+M(x)(\cos\phi\,\sigma_1+\sin\phi\,\sigma_2).
$$

For a thin smooth barrier of integrated mass $\theta>0$ and width $d$, the zero-energy transfer matrix is

$$
P_0=\exp[\theta(\cos\phi\,\sigma_2-\sin\phi\,\sigma_1)]
=\begin{pmatrix}\cosh\theta&-ie^{-i\phi}\sinh\theta\\ie^{i\phi}\sinh\theta&\cosh\theta\end{pmatrix}.
$$

Thus, with reference planes at its two faces,

$$
t=t'=\operatorname{sech}\theta,
\quad r_L=-ie^{i\phi}\tanh\theta,
\quad r_R=-ie^{-i\phi}\tanh\theta.
$$

For every $|E|\le B$, variation of constants gives

$$
\|P_d(E)-P_0\|\le Bd\,e^{\theta+Bd}=:\delta(\theta,d,B).
$$

Let the first barrier have phase zero and strength $\theta=\operatorname{artanh}r$, $0<r<1$. The second has phase $\phi_N=\pi-N\ln2$ and strength $\Lambda$. Let the distance between their adjacent faces be $\ell=\pi$. In the thin-barrier, perfectly reflecting outer-wall limit,

$$
r_{1,R}r_{2,L}=(-ir)(-ie^{i\phi_N})=r e^{-iN\ln2}.
$$

The exact multiple-reflection denominator tends to

$$
1-r e^{i(2\pi E-N\ln2)}.
$$

This derives the same-loop structural multiplier from an explicitly registered material phase. It does not infer that phase from heat or KMS. The scalar/pseudoscalar source coefficients needed to implement this phase remain physical source entries. All other complex amplitudes, including the common $-i$ reflection phase and free reference-path phase, remain in the interference instrument.

The finite barriers do not have zero dwell time. Their complete energy-dependent matrices are used at every finite stage. The displayed denominator is the comparison limit, with a uniform finite-band error; it is not an exact formula for every finite source.

###### 2. Contractive scattering bound, retaining the outer lead

Write $\epsilon_j$ for a common bound on the four scattering-amplitude errors of barrier $j$ relative to its zero-width counterpart. The transfer estimate implies the conservative bound

$$
\epsilon_1\le(1+\sinh\theta)\delta(\theta,d_1,B).
$$

For the outer barrier compared directly with a perfect reflector,

$$
\epsilon_{2,r}\le(1+\sinh\Lambda)\delta(\Lambda,d_2,B)+1-\tanh\Lambda,
$$

$$
\epsilon_{2,t}\le\delta(\Lambda,d_2,B)+\operatorname{sech}\Lambda.
$$

All exact scattering amplitudes are bounded in modulus by one, by the conserved Dirac current. Choose $\epsilon_1\le(1-r)/2$, and set $g=(1-r)/2$. Then on the whole band,

$$
|1-r'_{1,d}(E)r_{2,d}(E)e^{2iE\ell}|\ge g.
$$

This is a uniform nonzero denominator. No resonance is dropped; the fixed nonperfect entrance coupler prevents a real-axis pole.

For incidence from the left, the total reflection and transmission are

$$
R_d=r_{1,d}+\frac{t'_{1,d}r_{2,d}e^{2iE\ell}t_{1,d}}
{1-r'_{1,d}r_{2,d}e^{2iE\ell}},
$$

$$
T_d=\frac{t_{2,d}e^{iE\ell}t_{1,d}}
{1-r'_{1,d}r_{2,d}e^{2iE\ell}}.
$$

Their comparison with the perfect-reflector loop obeys

$$
|R_d-R_0|\le \epsilon_1+
\frac{2\epsilon_1+\epsilon_{2,r}}g+
\frac{\epsilon_1+\epsilon_{2,r}}{g^2},
$$

$$
|T_d|\le\epsilon_{2,t}/g.
$$

For the right-moving internal cavity coefficient $A_d=t_{1,d}/(1-r'_{1,d}r_{2,d}e^{2iE\ell})$,

$$
|A_d-A_0|\le\epsilon_1/g+(\epsilon_1+\epsilon_{2,r})/g^2.
$$

The left-moving coefficient has the additional reflected multiplier, so its difference is bounded by $|A_d-A_0|+\epsilon_{2,r}/g$. These follow by the elementary reciprocal difference identity and the modulus-one bounds. They retain both finite leads. In particular the nonzero outer transmission is not silently traced away when comparing complete states.

The constants are deliberately loose. An explicit convergent choice is $\Lambda=n$, $d_1=e^{-n}$, $d_2=e^{-5n}$, with fixed $B,r$, starting after the entrance-error condition holds. Then every displayed scattering error tends to zero. Every finite width, strength, gradient and source norm is finite, but grows with $n$ and must remain in the cost and physical regulator schedule.

###### 3. Wavepacket and barrier-occupation comparison

###### 5. Selected four-component implementation: real masses and a static phase plate

##### Q.0.7v.5.3. Spectral completeness and normalization

Let $h=-i\sigma_3\partial_x+M(x)\sigma_1+v(x)I$ on $H^1(\mathbb R;\mathbb C^2)$, with real smooth compactly supported $M,v$. Bounded symmetric perturbation gives self-adjointness. This calculation supplies the spectral normalization for the finite-band packet estimates.

###### Jost Green kernel

Choose the left edge of the support to be positive for notational convenience. For $\operatorname{Im}z>0$, let $u_+(x,z)$ be the solution equal to $e^{izx}e_+$ on the right free lead, and $u_-(x,z)$ the solution equal to $e^{-izx}e_-$ on the left free lead. Both are obtained uniquely inside the compact interaction by the first-order Volterra equation. Let $Y_z(x)=(u_+(x,z),u_-(x,z))$.

The resolvent kernel is

$$
G_z(x,y)=\begin{cases}
i u_+(x,z)e_1^T Y_z(y)^{-1}\sigma_3,&x>y,\\
-i u_-(x,z)e_2^T Y_z(y)^{-1}\sigma_3,&x<y.
\end{cases}
$$

Indeed it solves the homogeneous equation away from $x=y$, decays at the required infinity, and its jump is $i\sigma_3$, so $-i\sigma_3[G_z(y+,y)-G_z(y-,y)]=I$. No nonzero square-integrable homogeneous solution exists at nonreal $z$ by self-adjointness, so the Green kernel is the resolvent kernel.

On the real axis the current $\psi^*\sigma_3\psi$ is conserved. The finite transfer matrix is in $SU(1,1)$: its form is $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}a&b\\\bar b&\bar a\end{smallmatrix}\right)$ and $|a|^2-|b|^2=1$. In particular the transmission denominator never vanishes on the real axis. The Volterra solution is analytic in $z$; on every compact real energy interval the upper/lower Green boundary kernels therefore exist and are continuous, uniformly on compact $x,y$ sets. There is no special zero-energy threshold for these massless first-order leads.

###### Exact spectral jump

Let $\psi_L(x,E)$ and $\psi_R(x,E)$ have unit incoming amplitude from the left and right respectively. On the left lead they have the forms

$$
\psi_L(x,E)=\binom{e^{\mathrm{iEx}}}{r_L(E)e^{-iEx}},\qquad
\psi_R(x,E)=\binom{0}{t_R(E)e^{-iEx}}.
$$

Current conservation and the same transfer matrix give $|r_L|^2+|t_R|^2=1$.

For $x,y$ on this left lead the upper Green kernel has diagonal entries

$$
i e^{iE(x-y)}1_{x>y},\qquad i e^{-iE(x-y)}1_{x<y},
$$

its $(2,1)$ entry is $i r_L(E)e^{-iE(x+y)}$, and its $(1,2)$ entry is zero. The lower boundary kernel is $G_{E-i0}(x,y)=G_{E+i0}(y,x)^*$. Subtracting proves on this open region

$$
G_{E+i0}(x,y)-G_{E-i0}(x,y)
=i\sum_{a=L,R}\psi_a(x,E)\psi_a(y,E)^*.
$$

The diagonal jumps of the two Green functions cancel in their difference. Consequently both sides solve the same homogeneous first-order equation in $x$, and the adjoint equation in $y$, everywhere. Uniqueness propagates the equality from the left-lead open set to all $x,y$.

Stone's formula now gives, first for compactly supported smooth test functions,

$$
dP_h(E)(x,y)=\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{a=L,R}\psi_a(x,E)\psi_a(y,E)^*\,dE.
$$

There is no omitted singular spectral part: the resolvent kernels are locally bounded up to every compact real energy interval on compact spatial test supports, as just proved. Their scalar spectral measures are therefore locally absolutely continuous by the resolvent/Stieltjes boundary formula. Compact smooth test vectors are dense. There is also no bound state: every real-energy exterior solution is a sum of constant-modulus plane waves; square integrability forces both coefficients to vanish on each exterior lead, and ODE uniqueness then forces the whole solution to vanish.

Thus the transform

$$
(\mathcal{F}_h f)_a(E)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int\psi_a(x,E)^*f(x)\,dx
$$

is an isometry from the physical Hilbert space into $L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C^2)$ and intertwines $h$ with multiplication by $E$. It is onto: its range projection commutes with every bounded function of $E$, so is fiberwise. At every real energy the two scattering solutions are independent, since the finite transmission amplitude $1/\bar a(E)$ is nonzero. Compactly supported test vectors hence span both fiber directions; the fiberwise range projection is the identity almost everywhere. This proves the unitary scattering transform and the inverse packet formula used in the barrier bounds.

The gauge-invariant quasifree static reference is therefore exactly

$$
C_V=\mathcal{F}_h^*\frac1{1+e^{2\pi E}}\mathcal{F}_h.
$$

It is not the free covariance on the entire physical line. Its full thermal incoming channels have the same energy-dependent occupation, and its reflected/transmitted correlations remain present. Any finite compression or local replacement must retain the separate error/provenance record.

###### Exact incoming active marginal, despite the changed full reference

Let $h_{\mathrm{free}}=-i\sigma_3\partial_x$, and let $J$ be any finite frame of compact smooth right-moving vectors whose supports lie strictly to the left of the potential. Define the incoming wave operator with the convention

$$
W_-=\operatorname*{s-lim}_{t\to-\infty}e^{\mathrm{ith}}e^{-ith_{\mathrm{free}}}.
$$

For every frame column $f$, backward free propagation moves its support still farther left. It never reaches the potential. The same characteristic uniqueness argument as in the causal-port lemma proves $e^{-ith}f=e^{-ith_{\mathrm{free}}}f$ for all $t\le0$. Hence every product in the limit equals $f$, and $W_-J=J$. Completeness gives $W_-^*J=J$ as well. Intertwining then yields

$$
J^*F(h)J=J^*W_-F(h_{\mathrm{free}})W_-^*J
=J^*F(h_{\mathrm{free}})J.
$$

Thus the active incoming finite covariance is exactly the old free characteristic covariance. Its tensor extensions over identical species and transverse catalogue labels have the same property in the ideal radial model. Nested all-right-moving incoming catalogues therefore retain the exact covariance restriction maps of E50.N27, provided each current source's potential lies strictly to the right of the full catalogue and its stated comparison window.

The identity is one of compressions; the full covariance columns differ. In general

$$
F(h)J=W_-F(h_{\mathrm{free}})J\ne F(h_{\mathrm{free}})J,
$$

because the Fermi function creates tails outside the compact incoming subspace. The separated-potential column bound, physical transverse approximation and actual regulator/ambient comparison must still be retained. No identity is asserted on arbitrary left-supported spinors, on the minus component, or on field observables that already straddle the barriers.

For precision in the onto argument above, choose a countable dense family of compact smooth test vectors. Their fiber spanning property holds on one common full-measure energy set. Independence of the two generalized eigenfunctions then forces the range projection to have rank two almost everywhere.

##### Q.0.7v.5.4. Causal whole-port and heat comparison

The whole-port calculation uses neither even greybody probabilities, a shifted energy convention, nor a transmitted-branch capacity proxy.

###### A. Exact one-dimensional statement

Let

$$
h_V=-i\sigma_3\partial_x+V(x)
$$

on $L^2(\mathbb R;\mathbb C^2)$ with domain $H^1$, where $V$ is a smooth bounded Hermitian matrix, zero for $x<D$, and compactly supported. The profile is static in boost time. Its strengths and derivatives are finite but are not required to be bounded uniformly over a source refinement.

Take real $\chi\in C_c^\infty((a,b))$, $a<b<0$, with norm one, and a real carrier $\nu>0$. Set $f(x)=e^{i\nu x}\chi(x)e_+$, where $\sigma_3e_+=e_+$. Choose

$$
-a<T<2D-b.
$$

The exact evolved state $f_T=e^{-iTh_V}f$ is supported in $x>0$. This holds irrespective of barrier reflection probability or phase.

Proof. The free right-moving part initially follows $x=x_0+t$. Before a path encounters the potential at $x=D$, its minus component is zero. The first such interaction can occur no earlier than $D-b$. From there finite propagation speed one implies that the leftmost affected point at time $t$ is no smaller than $D-[t-(D-b)]=2D-b-t$. The unaffected free right-moving part has support in $[a+t,b+t]$. Thus for $t=T$ both lower bounds are positive. This can be proved directly from the two Volterra characteristic equations, by iteration: every term containing a potential insertion has its first insertion at $x\ge D$ and time at least $D-b$, and subsequent characteristic segments have speed at most one. Bounded $V$ gives convergence of the Volterra series on every finite interval. It also proves finite propagation without a spectral or group-velocity approximation.

The same statement holds for every member of a finite frame supported in the same interval, and for the full frame with additional independent internal species or transverse labels.

The incident energy is

$$
\langle f,h_Vf\rangle=\nu,
$$

because $V=0$ on the initial support and the real envelope derivative integrates to zero. Since $V$ is time independent, the total energy remains $\nu$. No scalar potential, chemical-potential shift or even-scattering-probability argument enters this identity.

###### B. Exact tube flux before any return

Put a smooth cut $w(x)$ between zero and one, whose transition lies in $[0,c]$ with $0<c<D$. Choose a separate fixed tube-test endpoint $\Delta$ after the entire incoming packet passes the transition, with $\Delta<D-b$, so no part has yet reached the potential. The later final receiver cut may have $T>\Delta$, with the strengthened no-return inequality $T<2D-b-c$. The potential vanishes on the cut. The local Dirac energy flux there is therefore the free flux. There is no ideal reflected contribution at the cut before $T$. Integration over the fixed early window $[0,\Delta]$ gives $\nu$ in boost-energy units, exactly as the free E50 computation. On this early window the entire logical causal support, and not only the cut, is in the free region.

A sharp cut follows by a smooth-cut limit on the finite smooth solution. Alternatively free local energy conservation gives the same result from the initially empty and fully crossed exterior cap at the early time $\Delta$, before any potential interaction. A post-scattering $\langle h_V\rangle$ cap is not automatically a Hilbert-energy cap for a vector potential. The symmetric Dirac energy density may be signed pointwise, but neither proof assumes pointwise positivity.

Static prescribed scalar mass profiles can exchange radial momentum with their supports. A static vector potential can also do electric work $F_{\eta i}j^i$ on the matter even though $\partial_\eta A=0$. The conserved generator $h_V$ is the static canonical/Noether energy including its potential term, not automatically the matter Hilbert energy. All actual electric, medium, source-support, switching and Euler work/cap terms remain in the complete E48.L19 identity. The present heat proof avoids that substitution by using the early free tube window. It does not erase medium stress or claim bare commutator-current convergence.

###### C. Whole spatial receiver and capacity

Use four identical independent information species. At every stage include the entire finite incoming frame in a fixture, displace its old state and correlations to inaccessible archives, and prepare that fixture empty in both success/failure branches. Success with probability $p$ places one ququart into the four species of $f$; failure leaves the input in an inaccessible held store. Apply the identical field propagator in all species.

By part A the entire evolved fixture is in the exterior at the final cut. The exterior spatial projection therefore reduces that fixture. The actual full exterior output, including its input-independent side state, contains the species ququart on success and its orthogonal vacuum flag on failure. It is receiver-locally equivalent to the erasure channel $\mathcal E_p^{(4)}$.

For transverse catalogue columns in separated cells, use the ideal tensor product source $h_V\otimes I$ and one real transverse packet $g_v$. For a union $R$ of complete cells put $a_R=\|P_Rg_v\|^2$. Its entire spatial output is $\mathcal E_{pa_R}^{(4)}$. The capacity per fresh independent call is

$$
C_R(p)=pa_R\ln4.
$$

The source calculation in B gives

$$
\partial_pQ_R=E_*\nu a_R.
$$

Choosing the phase gradient $\nu=\ln4/(2\pi)$ before varying $p$ gives $\partial_pQ_R=T_*\partial_p(k_BC_R)$ at $T_*=E_*/(2\pi k_B)$. The old constant-capacity Page bypass, if retained in the receiver, is added unchanged and cancels in the difference.

This argument includes both scattered leads, all residual cavity occupation and every exterior fixture mode. A receiver that keeps only transmitted modes has a different capacity and heat record. No statement here substitutes its transmission probability for $a_R$.

The thermal occupation of the displaced old fixture does not change the success-minus-failure flux. Its complete prior state and correlations were archived identically in both branches. The finite prepared difference is exactly the one-particle code covariance. Unoccupied modes and archives remain part of the complete carrier and budget, not an informal vacuum replacement.

###### D. Finite observation of many cavity echoes

Let the first barrier begin at $D$, with fixed cavity round-trip scale $L$. Choose a finite echo count $M$ and let $T_{\mathrm{scat}}$ be a proved finite duration sufficient for that packet's scattering/echo observation, including pulse width and finite barrier corrections. The first arrival occurs near $D$. Choose $D$ large enough that a final time of the form $T=D+T_{\mathrm{scat}}$ satisfies the inequalities in A and B. For example, with fixed $a,b,c$, any $D>T_{\mathrm{scat}}+b+c$ satisfies the upper bound. The inward return cannot reach the horizon tube before the final cut.

The extra flight distance $D$ is an owned preparation/readout latency, not the loop time. The round-trip phase record must still derive its own $L=2\pi$ relation, with the finite-barrier tolerance. Moving the horizon cut farther away does not change the internal cavity free distance or discard its greybody phase.

The observation time is finite, and the return remains in the retained carrier.

###### E. Physical four-dimensional norm comparison

The intended actual boost-frame source is

$$
K_S=-i\alpha^1\partial_y+V_4(y+S)-ie^y\alpha^\perp\cdot\nabla_z,
$$

where $V_4=M\beta+v_NI$ is the specified smooth bounded Hermitian radial scalar-mass and vector-potential matrix supported in a finite interval to the right of the incoming tube. Its material mass coefficient carries the compensating $e^{-y}$ factor. Fix the entire finite longitudinal catalogue and all transverse derivatives before $S$.

For the ideal source $K_{S,0}=-i\alpha^1\partial_y+V_4(y+S)$, finite propagation confines the occupied radial support to $y+S\le b+T$. Duhamel then gives the explicit norm estimate

$$
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|(e^{-itK_S}-e^{-itK_{S,0}})J\|
\le e^{-S+b}(e^T-1)\|\nabla_z g\|.
$$

Here the ideal longitudinal evolution is unitary and commutes with transverse derivatives. The estimate applies columnwise and hence by column-square-sum to the full fixture. Mass terms do not alter the maximum propagation speed. A separate graph/energy estimate must include the actual finite $V_4,V_4'$ constants; norm convergence alone is not the Hilbert-flux estimate.

Part F supplies the graph-energy bound; §§Q.0.7v.5.5–7 give the reference, regulator and complete source current/work comparison. The norm estimate alone is not a heat or reference certificate.

###### F. Explicit boost-energy graph bound

The separate graph bound in E can be obtained without differentiating an asymptotic scattering matrix. Put $V_{\max}=\|V_4\|_\infty$, $F_1=\|\partial_y f\|$, $G_1=\|\nabla g\|$, and $G_2=\|\Delta_zg\|$. Use a real transverse envelope $g$. The initial longitudinal support lies to the left of the potential, so $\|K_{S,0}J\|=F_1$. If $\phi_s=e^{-isK_{S,0}}J$, conservation of the ideal generator norm gives

$$
\|\partial_y\phi_s\|\le F_1+V_{\max}.
$$

Let $W=-ie^y\alpha^\perp\cdot\nabla_z$. On the radial support $y\le b-S+s$,

$$
\|K_{S,0}W\phi_s\|
\le e^{b-S+s}(F_1+1+2V_{\max})G_1,
$$

$$
\|W^2\phi_s\|\le e^{2(b-S+s)}G_2.
$$

The first inequality follows by differentiating the factor $e^y$ and the longitudinal spinor in the kinetic term, then adding the bounded mass multiplication. The real transverse envelope makes the Clifford cross term vanish in the squared transverse derivative norm. The second uses $W^2=-e^{2y}\Delta_z$.

The actual generator $K_S=K_{S,0}+W$ commutes with its own propagator. Applying it to the Duhamel integral, justified first on the smooth compact core, therefore gives

$$
\sup_{0\le t\le T}\|K_S(e^{-itK_S}-e^{-itK_{S,0}})J\|
\le e_S,
$$

$$
e_S=e^{b-S}(e^T-1)(F_1+1+2V_{\max})G_1
+\frac{e^{2(b-S)}}2(e^{2T}-1)G_2.
$$

Together with $d_S=e^{b-S}(e^T-1)G_1$, this is an actual norm-and-energy comparison. For a finite frame use the respective column-square-sum bounds and retain its actual occupation trace bound.

The ideal initial generator norm remains $F_1$, since its initial support is outside the mass. The actual ideal-orbit bound needed in the quadratic cap estimate is

$$
\sup_{t\le T}\|K_S\phi_t\|\le F_1+e^{b-S+T}G_1.
$$

Thus the endpoint **generator-energy** quadratic-form discrepancy is bounded by the same algebraic expansion as E50.N22,

$$
E_*\operatorname{Tr}|A|[d_S(M_S+e_S)+e_S],
$$

with $M_S=F_1+e^{b-S+T}G_1$. For the physical Hilbert heat use this cap bound at the early $\Delta<D-b$ window, where the whole logical support has not reached the vector/mass source and its generator-energy cap is the free Hilbert cap. Do not use a later post-scattering $K_V$ cap as Hilbert heat without the actual potential/current-work corrections. The final receiver support statement at $T$ remains a separate channel fact. For transverse cell-union tests, choose $S$ after their smallest positive gap collar, so physical finite propagation cannot reach the transverse test gradients during the call. The lateral logical flux and spin-boundary term then vanish there, as in E50.N22. For smooth non-cell-union tests the explicit E50 spin-boundary term must instead remain in the bound.

This is the finite transverse energy estimate for the specified static radial potential. The ordinary regulator, reference preparation and matching/clock first variations are established separately in §§Q.0.7v.5.5–7.

###### G. Actual four-dimensional covariance comparison with finite transverse source support

The physically installed radial mass and phase plate have a smooth compact transverse multiplier $\zeta(z)$ equal to one on a neighborhood of every catalogue support. \|[F(K_S)-F(K_{S,0})]J\|

##### Q.0.7v.5.5. Local reference, spectral buffer and modular comparison

The following estimates concern the protected operational cover and the finite tested mode frames.

Let $h_0$ and $h_V=h_0+V$ be self-adjoint first-order Dirac generators on the same line or complete collar, with propagation speed at most one and bounded self-adjoint multiplication potential $V$. Let $P$ be multiplication by an observation region separated from $\operatorname{supp}V$ by distance $D>0$ in the propagation metric. Assume the free and perturbed dynamics both have that speed and share the same domain. Then

$$
\|P[(1+e^{2\pi h_V})^{-1}-(1+e^{2\pi h_0})^{-1}]P\|
\le \frac{2}{\pi}\log\coth(D/2).
$$

For $|t|<2D$, the local propagators agree. For $t>0$, the Duhamel integrand of $P(e^{ith_V}-e^{ith_0})P$ is

$$
iP e^{i(t-s)h_V}V e^{ish_0}P.
$$

Its right factor vanishes if $s<D$ and its left factor vanishes if $t-s<D$. Thus it vanishes for every $0\le s\le t<2D$. Negative times follow by adjunction.

For a real scalar $\lambda$,

$$
\frac{1}{1+e^{2\pi\lambda}}
=\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^\infty \frac{\sin(t\lambda)}{\sinh(t/2)}\,dt.
$$

Use truncated functional calculus and the local cancellation before $2D$; the difference integral on $[2D,\infty)$ converges in operator norm. Since the norm of each compressed sine is at most one,

$$
\|P(f(h_V)-f(h_0))P\|
\le \frac{1}{\pi}\int_{2D}^\infty \frac{dt}{\sinh(t/2)}
=\frac{2}{\pi}\log\coth(D/2).
$$

One can justify the scalar identity by expanding $1/\sinh(t/2)$ into its positive exponential series and integrating, or by the elementary Fourier transform of $\tanh$. For the unbounded functional calculus, the truncated scalar integrals are uniformly bounded (Dirichlet estimate); convergence is strong, sufficient to identify the norm-convergent difference after cancellation.

For a finite isometry $W$ with range inside $P$, the same estimate bounds $W^*f(h_V)W-W^*f(h_0)W$. If both finite covariances have spectra in $[\eta,1-\eta]$, $\eta>0$, the logarithm integral representation yields

$$
\|\log(C_V(I-C_V)^{-1})-\log(C_0(I-C_0)^{-1})\|
\le \frac{2}{\eta}\|C_V-C_0\|.
$$

The eigenvalue buffer must be established for the actual chosen finite modes; it is not dimension-independent by default. The full-column and finite CAR estimates below supply the additional reference comparisons; §Q.0.7v.5.4 supplies the local heat/capacity calculation, and §Q.0.7v.5.7 supplies the source and preparation costs. The actual perturbed covariance remains $f(h_V)$, not $f(h_0)$ or $f(W^*h_VW)$.

###### Explicit finite-code spectral buffer

Let $W$ be a finite isometry into $\operatorname{Dom}h$ with $\|hW\|\le H$. For any $E>H$, spectral Markov gives

The Hadamard property on the protected cover, where $V$ vanishes, is proved by a separate smoothing argument, since norm-small covariance columns carry no regularity information.

Let $\mu$ be a smooth compact spatial cutoff with support separated from $\operatorname{supp}V$ by $D>0$. Local finite propagation gives $\mu(e^{ith_V}-e^{ith_0})\mu=0$ for $|t|<2D$. The actual changed reference consequently inherits the accepted free reference's local Hadamard singularity on precisely this operational cover. ##### Q.0.7v.5.6. Geometry-first regulator for the actual source

The construction uses the cell averaging, zero-boundary stencil, norm and proper-time conventions of Theorem 48a.10.

###### Actual finite source and consistency

Let $K$ be the geometric Dirac generator in (48a.10-L2), and let $V(y,z)$ be a smooth compactly supported Hermitian spin/species matrix multiplication operator, fixed before choosing the regulator. Put $v=\|V\|_\infty$ and $K_V=K+V$. Bounded perturbation preserves self-adjointness on $\operatorname{Dom}K$ and the compact-smooth core. The principal hyperbolic part is unchanged, so finite propagation is unchanged; every compact-smooth orbit over a fixed finite time interval remains compact smooth. All derivative bounds below are those of this actual perturbed orbit.

Use the original $I_n,E_n=I_n^*,P_n=I_nE_n$ and geometric $K_n$. Define the **actual onsite cell matrix**

$$
V_n=E_n V I_n,\qquad K_{V,n}=K_n+V_n.
$$

Disjoint cell supports make $V_n$ block diagonal in the cell index; each block is the normalized cell average of the Hermitian matrix $V$. It is Hermitian and $\|V_n\|\le v$. No spectral projection or state-dependent fitting is involved. Every original lattice mode, including high-frequency branches, remains in the source. The finite Fock Hamiltonian is $E_*d\Gamma(K_{V,n})$, and its actual Gibbs covariance is

$$
C_{V,n}=(I+e^{2\pi K_{V,n}})^{-1}.
$$

It is faithful and exactly KMS at the original physical temperature. $V_n$ is an additional onsite coefficient in the already admitted ordinary-source construction; its physical action and first variations are the separate covariant scalar/vector source dictionary, not frozen matrix derivatives.

For compact smooth $g$ with the required box/stencil collar, (F.10.4b.8b-L5) and cell Poincaré give the explicit new residual

$$
\begin{aligned}
\|K_{V,n}E_ng-E_nK_Vg\|
&\le r_n(g)+\|E_nV(P_ng-g)\|\\
&\le r_n(g)+\frac{v a_n}{\pi}\|\nabla g\|
=:r_n^V(g).
\end{aligned}
$$

The identity in the first line uses exact cell averages $V_n$, rather than sampling $V$ at cell centers. It does not omit a potential-gradient error: the projection discrepancy is bounded before averaging. Potential gradients still enter the actual orbit's derivative seminorms and the physical source/variation ledger.

###### Finite-time and generator-graph errors

For a fixed $f$ and $T$, define

$$
R_n^V(f,T)=\sup_{|s|\le T}r_n^V(e^{isK_V}f),\qquad
G_V(f,T)=\sup_{|s|\le T}\|\nabla e^{isK_V}f\|.
$$

Duhamel in the averaged finite space, followed by cell Poincaré, gives

$$
\sup_{|s|\le T}
\|I_ne^{isK_{V,n}}E_nf-e^{isK_V}f\|
\le T R_n^V(f,T)+\frac{a_n}{\pi}G_V(f,T)
=:\epsilon_n^V(f,T).
$$

The finite source is unitary, so its large cutoff norm does not multiply the Duhamel residual. Every term tends to zero after $V,f,T$ and their support collar are fixed.

For the actual generator graph, use $K_Vf$ as an additional compact-smooth test vector. Commutation of each generator with its own unitary group then gives

$$
\sup_{|s|\le T}
\|I_nK_{V,n}e^{isK_{V,n}}E_nf
 -K_Ve^{isK_V}f\|
\le r_n^V(f)+\epsilon_n^V(K_Vf,T).
$$

This gives the finite-code graph-energy comparison used with the separately specified finite variation tests.

The required orbit seminorms are finite with computable conservative bounds. In the finite causal support collar, write $K_V=-i\sum_j A_j(x)\partial_j+B(x)$ with its actual smooth coefficients. For each multi-index $\alpha$ of order $\le3$, differentiate the evolution equation. The principal $K_V$ term is norm preserving; commutators contain

$$
\sum_{0<\beta\le\alpha}\binom{\alpha}{\beta}
[(\partial^\beta A_j)\partial_j\partial^{\alpha-\beta}g
 +(\partial^\beta B)\partial^{\alpha-\beta}g],
$$

with irrelevant unit factors in the norm. Every derivative of $g$ on the right has order $\le3$. Sum the corresponding coefficient suprema, binomial factors and finite multiplicities to obtain $C_3$; for the sum of the derivative $L^2$ norms this gives the conservative Gronwall bound

$$
\sum_{|\alpha|\le3}\|\partial^\alpha e^{isK_V}f\|
\le e^{C_3|s|}\sum_{|\alpha|\le3}\|\partial^\alpha f\|.
$$

Use coefficients on a known finite propagation collar, or a bounded smooth continuation agreeing there. For $K_Vf$ repeat the bound with its actual derivative norms (one extra initial derivative may be required). All thin-wall, radial and phase-plate derivatives are included in $C_3$. This is deliberately a finite, potentially very expensive bound, not a uniform thin-wall estimate.

###### True covariance columns

Let $C_V=F(K_V)$. The same scalar sine identity as (F.10.4b.8b-L9), the averaged Duhamel estimate before $T_0$, and the unitary tail after $T_0$ yield

$$
\|C_{V,n}E_nf-E_nC_Vf\|
\le \frac{\pi}{2}R_n^V(f,T_0)
 +\frac{2\|f\|}{\pi}\log\coth(T_0/4)
=:b_n^V(f,T_0).
$$

This is a full covariance-column estimate for the actual changed field and actual changed finite matrix, not $F(E_nK_VI_n)$ substituted for $E_nF(K_V)I_n$. Choose $T_0$ first to control the exponential tail, then the box/mesh to control the actual perturbed orbit on that window. The potential remains fixed during these choices.

For a finite smooth frame $J$, Gram normalize $E_nJ$ exactly as in Theorem 48a.10. Its Gram defect, column normalization error, finite CAR state lift and all dimension factors are included before evaluating the target error. Noncompact columns such as $C_0J$ are first approximated by their actual norm tails on the fixed finite list, as in E46.R27; they are not treated as compact by assertion.

Combine this bound with the separate radial incoming-reference theorem: the exact installed characteristic covariance has the unchanged E50.N27 active compression, while true radial columns differ by the actual longitudinal projection tail plus the one-way thermal distance bound. The actual four-dimensional/radial comparison adds its proved transverse and finite support terms. For each fixed tested frame, the physical-versus-installed covariance column therefore has the explicit triangle bound of E46.R27 with these new values substituted. The reference's purification, full logit matrix, gap-dependent derivative and counterterm work remain charged.

The finite-code positive covariance buffer proved in §Q.0.7v.5.5 can be applied before taking logarithms. Alternatively use the actual finite matrix gap with a certified enclosure. No uniform gap independent of frame or regulator is assumed.

###### Terminating order and scope

Freeze the mode/time/cover/variation list, finite source profiles and all comparison scales. Fix the required probability and covariance tolerances, then $T_0$, the physical support collar, the actual derivative bounds and a sufficiently fine geometry-first mesh. Evaluate $r_n^V$, $b_n^V$ and Gram errors on the finite expanded frame; all displayed bounds tend to zero at this stage. Choose the ordinary pair-local schedule only afterwards from the enlarged source's actual coefficients and first-variation constants. A change of source width, profile, code dimension or test list requires recomputing this schedule.

The estimates prove smooth finite-response and reference transfer for the prescribed bounded smooth scalar/vector profiles. The finite geometric Gibbs covariance and installed active marginal retain their separately specified dynamics and physical current/work/boundary accounts.

##### Q.0.7v.5.7. Ordinary source, covariant action and costs

The following action extends E37/E48's prescribed, externally maintained material subclass.

###### 1. Added covariant source terms

Use the four identical Dirac species, the same material cells, proper clock and regulated mode/Gram/Berry construction. The matter action adds the standard scalar bilinear and vector-current coupling,

$$
S_{\mathrm{add}}=-\sum_{a=1}^4\int\sqrt{|g|}\,[m\bar\psi_a\psi_a+q A_\mu\bar\psi_a\gamma^\mu\psi_a]\,d^4x.
$$

The signs of $A$ are fixed so that its static boost-frame Hamiltonian term is $+qA_\eta I$. They are tested against the stationary Dirac equation rather than inferred from a desired phase. Choose $qA_\eta=v_N(x)$ on the protocol plateau. The scalar mass supplies the two real barriers. Both vanish on the horizon crossing tube and its support collar. Their transverse plateau contains every logical fixture column and its finite causal expansion; smooth outer cutoffs are retained in the source.

The fields and sources are static under the registered boost clock during the entire comparison interval. Their installation, removal and switching occur at owned boundaries and have actual work/precision charges. Maintaining prescribed profiles can require momentum-force and current-source payers depending on the field state. Such terms are retained, as E37.B12/B14a requires.

If a Maxwell background is included, its field tensor, prescribed background-source current and positive finite field energy are calculated from the same compact smooth potential. The background-source current is an external maintaining payer in the specified source class.

The heat statement is local to the original tube where $m=A=0$: the logical pulse crosses it before the support can send a return. The complete fixture success-minus-failure subtraction removes identical background source stress there. It does not erase the actual profile, apparatus and switching cost elsewhere.

###### 2. Finite field matrices and full-carrier support

At a fixed physical regulator the added multiplication operators have matrix elements in the already specified normalized cell basis. Their supports are within each cell, so they add onsite Hermitian blocks to the one-particle matrix $K[g,q]$. The off-reference expression is obtained from the covariant action above, with the existing material Gram/Berry map, proper lapse, tetrad, field/charge normalization, transported scalar profile and one-form pullback. It is not defined by freezing its reference matrix and declaring its derivative zero.

The derivative includes the actual mass and potential gradients times support displacements, tetrad and lapse changes, changes of $A_\mu\gamma^\mu$, the cell measure, both normalized mode columns and their Gram derivative, and the stated controller/clock pullbacks. Every coefficient is a smooth finite function on the fixed finite material chart. Thus its operator norm and every registered finite first-variation norm can be computed or conservatively bounded before choosing a matching time step. Large radial and thin-wall gradients enter those constants without omission.

E48.L4 applies to a general Hermitian one-particle coefficient matrix. These additional onsite spin/species terms are complete single-pack operators. The original edge hopping terms remain neighboring-pair operators. The exact algebraic intertwining and its derivative in E48.L5 therefore hold for the enlarged matrix with the same fixed representation. No new nonlocal or three-pack term is introduced by the prescribed multiplication potentials.

Use the selected prescribed-profile, fixed-enable, decoupled-spectator subclass in part 2 of E48. The unsplit source is the actual Dirac-plus-profile finite regulator, not the old free regulator. Its channel and flux comparison must use the new physical estimates. Hold the entire new generator, including its potentials and every off-code sector, during the old Page interval by the actual full negative cancellation; retain that cancellation's boundary action/work. Release the source only in its appended scattering/calibration interval. This preserves the old Page law without retrospectively changing its input or timing.

###### 3. No free implementation or stress transfer

After the regulator and all finite tests are fixed, compute the actual $A,D,B$ and first-variation constants of E48.L12–L19 for the enlarged source. The same matching construction then supplies a full-carrier pair/free-layer history. Its explicit E48.L23 switching-work and E48.L24 timing bounds include the new onsite norms, mass gradients, vector-potential derivatives and full source clock. The finite comparison error is the actual E48.L15/L19 bound for this source; the current/work/boundary comparison uses it, not endpoint channel agreement alone.

The complete inventory includes four fields and spectator spin sectors, radial/transverse regulators, scalar/vector profile supports, source charge/field or externally maintained potential payers, both barriers and their finite strength/width precision, clocks/enable modules, doubled endpoint and gauge factors, all fixture displacement archives and failed-input stores, reference purification, penalty preparation/cancellation, both lead outputs, cavity memory, physical capture/readout and any renewal service.

For fixed barrier parameters all these matrices and bounds are finite. Choose the ordinary regulator before the matching step, and the matching precision after its actual norms. As the barrier parameters refine, redo that finite computation; do not exchange the thin-wall limit with a fixed ultraviolet or clock bound.

###### 4. Reference remains a separate proved comparison

The true static field reference is the quasifree state with covariance $F(h_V)$ at the registered boost inverse temperature. The finite matrix source may use either the actual-regulator Gibbs covariance or a correctly installed actual-marginal covariance under E48.L7/L8, but its choice must be explicit. The Definition F.10.12a certificate uses the finite-code field/unitary/covariance comparison, actual spectral buffer and logit/CAR lift in §§Q.0.7v.5.4–6, together with the regional maps, reference preparation and joint error schedule in §Q.0.7v.5.1.

The separated-support Fermi and causal-port estimates supply their stated comparison terms; they are used together with the exact incoming reference maps, regulator bounds and full source action, not as substitutes for those additional entries.

###### Identical charge and absence of an unrecorded species-message side channel

The four information species have identical masses, charge, spatial input profile and source couplings. Every physical source current or stress in the prescribed quadratic matter model is the sum of the same diagonal species bilinear. Restricted to the one-particle internal ququart with its common spatial wavefunction, such a bilinear compresses to its scalar spatial value times $I_4$. Off-diagonal species matrix elements vanish because the action does not convert species; diagonal values agree. This remains true for arbitrary ququart states entangled with an external reference.

Thus the external profile/support response within this specified model cannot reveal which internal-species message was sent. Its common dependence on success probability, occupation, spatial motion and source parameters is retained in the work and source-state record. The selected source contains no species-sensitive coupling.

##### Q.0.7v.5.8. Coherent reflection readout and finite diagnostic preparation

This component uses the actual finite two-barrier source and a registered coherent reference. It avoids assigning a narrow-frequency, long wavepacket to an exactly time-isolated single lap of a finite cavity.

Fix $r=1/2$, $\ell=\pi$, the real-barrier/phase-plate source, and the reference planes of §Q.0.7v.5.2. The ideal one-lead reflection coefficient is

$$
R_0(E)=i\frac{w(E)-r}{1-rw(E)},\qquad w(E)=e^{i(2\pi E-N\ln2)}.
$$

The factor $i$ is part of the actual port dictionary. It is not dropped from the interferometer. Solving this equation gives the source-derived extraction map

$$
w=\frac{r-iR_0}{1-irR_0}=:\mathcal{M}(R_0).
$$

For $|z|,|z'|\le1$,

$$
|\mathcal{M}(z)-\mathcal{M}(z')|
\le\frac{1+r}{1-r}|z-z'|=3|z-z'|.
$$

This follows by subtracting the fractions; the numerator is $(1-r^2)(-i)(z-z')$ and each denominator has modulus at least $1-r$. The ideal reflection derivative obeys

$$
|R_0'(E)|\le2\pi\frac{1+r}{1-r}=6\pi.
$$

###### Actual finite-band experiment

Choose a normalized smooth spectral packet $A$ supported within $[E_0-h,E_0+h]$ and the globally certified band. Prepare one excitation coherently split between the incoming physical lead and an owned reference path with the registered matching output packet. All propagation phases and delays of that reference are measured/derived source entries. They are not fixed after observing a resonance.

Let $R_d(E)$ and $T_d(E)$ be the complete finite-source amplitudes. The reflected component is $R_d A$, and the outer-lead component and all unmatched reflected modes are retained in the zero-score outcome. Select the normalized matched reflected output mode specified by the same packet dictionary. Recombine that mode with the reference by a balanced splitter and a reference phase $\vartheta$. With

$$
\bar R_d=\int |A(E)|^2R_d(E)\,dE,
$$

the exact ideal-apparatus probabilities are

$$
P_\pm(\vartheta)=\frac{1+|\bar R_d|^2\pm2\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\vartheta}\bar R_d)}4,
\qquad P_0=\frac{1-|\bar R_d|^2}2.
$$

Thus the outcome variable $Z\in\{-1,0,+1\}$ has mean $\operatorname{Re}(e^{-i\vartheta}\bar R_d)$. Separate $\vartheta=0$ and $\pi/2$ trials estimate the real and imaginary parts. No division by a small raw reflection probability occurs.

With $n$ independent fresh trials on each axis, Hoeffding gives simultaneous error at most $\eta$ on both components, except with probability $4e^{-n\eta^2/2}$. The complex statistical error is at most $\sqrt2\eta$. Fresh preparation or an explicitly verified renewal channel, all copies of the reference, clocks, splitter, detector, archives and output sectors are charged.

If $\Delta_R$ is the uniform finite-barrier bound on $|R_d-R_0|$ from §Q.0.7v.5.2, then

$$
|\bar R_d-R_0(E_0)|\le\Delta_R+6\pi h.
$$

Add the actual physical preparation/capture/readout error in this complex expectation, denoted $\epsilon_{\mathrm{phys}}$. A half-trace error $\delta$ per setting contributes at most $2\delta$ to its bounded $Z$ mean and hence at most $2\sqrt2\delta$ to the complex estimate. The already retained norm/energy and field/ordinary-source comparisons must supply this $\delta$.

Project the noisy complex estimate onto the closed unit disk. Euclidean projection cannot increase its distance to the true $\bar R_d$, which lies in that disk. The resulting $\widetilde R$ obeys, with the stated confidence,

$$
|\widetilde R-R_0(E_0)|\le
\Delta_R+6\pi h+\epsilon_{\mathrm{phys}}+\sqrt2\eta=:\epsilon_R.
$$

Compute $\widehat w=\mathcal{M}(\widetilde R)$. Then $|\widehat w-w(E_0)|\le3\epsilon_R$. If $3\epsilon_R<1/2$, $\widehat w$ is nonzero. Its normalized phase satisfies

$$
\operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}(\arg\widehat w,2\pi E_0-N\ln2)
\le2\arcsin(3\epsilon_R).
$$

Indeed normalization changes a complex number within $\epsilon<1$ of a unit number by at most another $\epsilon$, giving chord distance at most $2\epsilon$. The corresponding angular distance is at most $2\arcsin\epsilon$.

This is an explicit confidence-aware phase acceptance protocol: register the mode centers, widths, $N$ range, all source/refinement parameters, statistical confidence and phase margin before data. Accept a phase-grid position only when its confidence interval lies within the registered tolerance. Reject only when the interval is disjoint; otherwise report unresolved. The protocol reconstructs the loop phase from derived complete complex scattering; raw intensity maxima are not used as grid positions.

In physical units $E_0=c\omega/\kappa_H$, so $2\pi E_0=\omega\tau_H=\hbar\omega/(k_BT_H)$ for $\tau_H=2\pi c/\kappa_H$. The material plate supplies the independently registered $N\ln2$ phase. The finite barrier dwell phases are retained in $\Delta_R$ (or can be used through the exact finite transfer matrix); they are not treated as absent.

###### Finite spatial and temporal realizations

A smooth compact spectral packet has Schwartz free spatial tails. Choose finite preparation and capture windows using its actual norm and energy-weighted tail integrals and the finite-source scattering coefficients. Physically truncate, smooth and renormalize the initial/readout modes, and retain the resulting norm/graph errors in $\epsilon_{\mathrm{phys}}$ and the energy ledger. The two-channel scattering transform is unitary by the separate Jost/Stone proof. The exact field experiment is never claimed to start from an infinitely extended monochromatic mode or to have completed infinitely many laps at finite time.
