All such tails can be bounded from the registered smooth compact spectral packet and the nonzero-denominator bound before the trial.

###### Exact finite greybody variant: no perfect-mirror requirement

The original transfer record permits greybody attenuation. Thus a fully finite source can avoid the thin-wall/perfect-reflector limit entirely. Fix two finite smooth real mass barriers. Choose their strengths and widths from the transfer bounds so that on the entire admitted band

$$
|r'_1(E)|\ge\rho_1>0,\quad |r_2(E)|\ge\rho_2>0,
\quad |t_1(E)|,|t'_1(E)|\ge\tau>0,\quad |r'_1(E)|\le r_*<1.
$$

For example choose zero-width target moduli $1/2$ and $3/4$, and widths sufficiently small that each amplitude error is at most $1/20$. All four positive constants then follow before measuring a spectrum. Both finite leads and barrier interiors are retained. There is no claim of zero outer transmission.

Keep the inner reference faces separated by exactly $\ell=\pi$, including the phase plate. Set

$$
z(E)=r_2(E)e^{2iE\ell-2i\alpha_N},\quad
q(E)=r'_1(E)z(E),\quad G(E)=-r'_1(E)r_2(E).
$$

Then the **exact finite source** has

$$
q(E)=G(E)e^{i(2\pi E-N\ln2)}.
$$

Its complex greybody factor $G(E)$, including both barrier phases and their dispersive delay, is derived by the actual finite Volterra transfer matrices. It is not fitted after spectral comparison. The free-cavity loop time and the greybody phase are distinct entries, exactly as in the original greybody-inclusive record.

Let $Y(E)=R(E)-r_1(E)$ and $a(E)=t'_1(E)t_1(E)$. The exact reflection formula gives

$$
Y=\frac{az}{1-r'_1z},\qquad
z=\frac{Y}{a+r'_1Y},\qquad
q=\frac{r'_1Y}{a+r'_1Y}.
$$

At the true value, $a+r'_1Y=a/(1-q)$, so its modulus is at least $\tau^2/2$. If the complex reflection estimate has error $\epsilon<\tau^2/4$, the estimated denominator has modulus at least $\tau^2/4$, since $|r'_1|\le1$. Subtracting the two rational expressions gives the conservative bound

$$
|\widehat q-q|\le 8\epsilon/\tau^4.
$$

Indeed the numerator of that difference is $r'_1a\,\Delta Y$, of modulus at most $\epsilon$, and the product of denominator lower bounds is at least $\tau^4/8$.

Dividing by the **derived** nonzero $G$ gives an estimate of the intrinsic loop unit phase with error at most $8\epsilon/(\tau^4\rho_1\rho_2)$. Alternatively retain $\arg G$ and report the greybody-inclusive phase predicate directly. Neither operation removes an unmeasured phase by convention; it consumes source-derived complex amplitudes at the fixed physical reference planes.

For a finite-width packet centered at $E_0$, replace the ideal $6\pi h$ bound by $L_Rh$, where $L_R=\sup_{|E|\le B}|R'(E)|$ is bounded from the exact smooth transfer ODE and the positive scattering denominator. All profile coefficients and their finite energy derivatives are fixed first; the packet width is chosen afterward. The finite $L_R$ is computable without any experimental fit. The same two-quadrature/Hoeffding and physical-tail argument supplies $\epsilon$. The source amplitude tables can be evaluated with certified interval errors, which are added to numerator and denominator bounds before inversion.

The exact finite greybody source has the required geometrical loop phase, source-derived nontrivial greybody amplitudes, full retained losses and a certified interference/readout extraction. The actual finite horizon/KMS/material and Definition F.10.12a conjunction is supplied by §§Q.0.7v.5.1–7, with the finite diagnostic preparation and tails below; it does not require another ideal-wall limit.

At the finite physical stage let $U$ be the actual one-particle propagation, including its owned reference-path map, and let $D$ be the finite orthonormal frame of the matched reflected and reference detection modes. ##### Q.0.7v.5.9. Explicit finite-duration and capture tails

For any smooth compact spectral vector $B(E)$, let

$$
\widehat B(x)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int e^{\mathrm{iEx}}B(E)\,dE.
$$

Integration by parts $k$ times, $k\ge1$, gives

$$
\|\widehat B(x)\|\le\frac{\|B^{(k)}\|_1}{\sqrt{2\pi}|x|^k},\qquad
 \int_{|x|\ge L}\|\widehat B(x)\|^2dx
 \le\frac{\|B^{(k)}\|_1^2}{\pi(2k-1)}L^{1-2k}.
$$

Apply this to the finitely many free-lead incoming and outgoing coefficients $A,AR,AT$, including their actual reference-plane shifts. At large negative time, unwanted outgoing portions lie in such tails; at large positive time, the remaining incoming portion does. On the finite interaction interval use the same integration by parts in $E$ on $A(E)\psi(x,E)e^{-iEt}$, with the supremum of its $L^1$ derivative over that finite interval. This bounds the cavity/barrier remainder by a finite constant times $|t|^{-k}$. The Jost/Volterra solutions and their energy derivatives give the constants without dropping resonances.

Energy/graph tails are obtained by the same calculation with $EA(E)$ in place of $A(E)$. To prepare a genuinely compact initial state, multiply the large-negative-time scattering packet by a registered smooth cutoff and normalize. Its generator error additionally includes the exact commutator $-i\sigma_3\chi'\psi$; its cutoff derivative and normalization defect are charged. Unitary evolution then propagates the initial norm/graph errors. Physical finite-cell and matching-source errors are added afterward on this actual finite catalogue.

Consequently all readout time windows and spatial capture supports are finite at any strictly positive tolerance. Their costs can be large. Choose horizon-to-barrier separation $D$ only after the required finite duration is fixed, so that all these observations occur before a return reaches the original horizon tube. This flight distance is not inserted into the internal loop clock.

The common schedule in §Q.0.7v.5.1 now combines the finite source, its actual reference and physical comparisons, and the confidence-aware instrument. <a id="theorem-q07v6-common-horizon-recovery-page-and-transfer-realization"></a>**Theorem Q.0.7v.6 (Common Horizon Recovery, Page and Transfer Realization).** The prescribed-background finite material source of Theorem Q.0.7v.5 carries the original common-code exterior-recovery, design, trace-coupled Page and closed-loop transfer records on one complete finite horizon dynamics.  d=4^{22},\qquad K=4,\qquad \eta=\pi2^{-42},\qquad

$$
 \epsilon_j\le32\sqrt{2(\mu+\eta)}<\frac15

with the original complete success/failure record and $p_{\mathrm{fail}}<1/100$. Its moment and PageTV entries at all original completed cuts are
$$
 \begin{gathered}

<a id="proposition-q019-conditional-landauer-phase-grid-signature"></a>**Proposition Q.0.19 (Conditional Landauer Phase-Grid Signature).** On an accepted horizon closed-loop transfer record $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{hor}}$, every peak accepted by its certified interference/readout protocol at an admitted pair $(\omega,N)\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{loop}}$ obeys
$$
\operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}(x,N\ln2)
:=
\min_{k\in\mathbb Z}|x-N\ln2-2\pi k|
\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}},
\qquad x=\frac{\hbar\omega}{k_BT_H},\quad N\ge1.
\tag{Q.0.19.1}
$$
Exact congruence is the subbranch $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}=0$. Independently of which labels and modes are realized, the nominal arithmetic grid obtained by extending the label to all positive integers is
$$
\{N\alpha_L\bmod1:N\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\},
\qquad
\alpha_L=\frac{\ln2}{2\pi}.
\tag{Q.0.19.2}
$$
This nominal infinite orbit is dense and equidistributed in $[0,1)$, and its first $N_{\max}$ labels have at most three adjacent circular gap lengths. A finite transfer record claims physical peaks only on its admitted domain; it does not realize the entire infinite orbit or every finite initial label block. At nonzero tolerance, accepted measured phases lie near their nominal labels and need not retain exact gap equalities. Even at zero tolerance, an arbitrary admitted subset is not necessarily an initial label block. Amplitudes, widths, greybody factors and nonresonant envelopes remain separate outputs.

*Proof.* The accepted transfer record and its interference/readout certificate give (Q.0.19.1) on the admitted domain. The nominal label phases divided by $2\pi$ form the displayed irrational rotation orbit. Lemma Q.0.7b gives irrationality, so Weyl equidistribution supplies the infinite-orbit statement. Proposition Q.0.7n gives the gap bound for the first $N_{\max}$ nominal labels. Neither theorem enlarges the physical transfer domain or removes its nonzero phase tolerance. $\square$

<a id="corollary-q019a-beatty-staircase-of-lower-phase-approximants"></a>**Corollary Q.0.19a (Beatty Staircase of Lower Phase Approximants).** For each $k\ge1$, define
$$
N_k^+:=\lfloor\beta_Lk\rfloor,
\qquad
\beta_L=\frac{2\pi}{\ln2},
$$
and
$$
\Delta_k^+:=2\pi k-N_k^+\ln2.
$$
Then
$$
0<\Delta_k^+<\ln2,
$$
and $N_{k+1}^+-N_k^+\in\{9,10\}$ with limiting $10$-step frequency $\beta_L-9$. These are arithmetic phase approximants. They are structural horizon-loop phase overheads only when an admitted loop satisfies Definition Q.0.7e and Proposition Q.0.7f for the same pair; physical entropy production additionally requires the eventwise reset calibration (Q.0.7e.0).

*Proof.* Proposition Q.0.7j gives the Beatty staircase. Irrationality of $\beta_L$ makes the lower mismatch strictly positive. The physical-status statement follows from Definition Q.0.7h. ∎

<a id="corollary-q019b-convergent-hierarchy-of-smallest-phase-defects"></a>**Corollary Q.0.19b (Convergent Hierarchy of Smallest Phase Defects).** *Let $(k_n,N_n)=(p_n,q_n)$ be the continued-fraction convergents of $\alpha_L=\ln2/(2\pi)$. Then*
$$
\delta_{N_n}:=\min_{k\in\mathbb Z}|N_n\ln2-2\pi k|<\frac{2\pi}{N_n}.
$$
*The first low-defect pairs are*
$$
(k,N)\in\{(1,9),\ (15,136),\ (31,281),\ (139,1260),\ (170,1541),\ldots\}.
$$

*Proof.* This is Corollary Q.0.7l translated from $|N\alpha_L-k|$ to $|N\ln2-2\pi k|$ by multiplication by $2\pi$. $\square$

<a id="proposition-q020-conditional-phase-scales-on-the-transfer-branch"></a>**Proposition Q.0.20 (Conditional Phase Scales on the Transfer Branch).** On an accepted horizon closed-loop transfer record $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{hor}}$ that independently registers the phase step $\ln2$, the grid scales are $(2\pi,\ln2)$. Hence the grid in $x=\hbar\omega/(k_BT_H)$ is independent of horizon mass, charge, spin, and matter content at the level of phase positions, up to the certified tolerance $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}$. Amplitudes, widths, greybody factors, peak heights, and the nonresonant envelope remain separate outputs of $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{scat}}$.

*Proof.* The period $2\pi$ is the single-valuedness period, and $\ln2$ is an explicit phase-step entry of $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{hor}}$. Neither varies with horizon parameters by the definition of that transfer branch. The phase step is not derived from SPAP or Theorem 31. $\square$

<a id="corollary-q020a-temperature-normalized-cross-horizon-collapse"></a>**Corollary Q.0.20a (Temperature-Normalized Cross-Horizon Collapse).** *Let $H_1$ and $H_2$ be two horizons satisfying the same closed-loop transfer branch of Definition Q.0.7u with peak tolerance $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}$, with Hawking temperatures $T_{H,1}$ and $T_{H,2}$. Define the reduced thermal phase map*
$$
\Pi(\omega,H)
:=
\left[
\frac{\hbar\omega}{k_B T_H}
\right]_{2\pi}
\in\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z).
$$
*If two resonant transfer peaks carry the same cycle label $N$, then*
$$
\operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}\!\left(\Pi(\omega_N^{(1)},H_1),\,\Pi(\omega_N^{(2)},H_2)\right)\le2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}},
$$
*and on the exact-closure subbranch $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}=0$ both reduced phases equal $[N\ln2]_{2\pi}$. For an unwrapped frequency comparison, additionally require a common lift $m\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ for the two actual registered frequencies such that*
$$
x_{N,m}:=N\ln2+2\pi m,\qquad
\left|\frac{\hbar\omega_{N,m}^{(r)}}{k_BT_{H,r}}-x_{N,m}\right|
\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}\quad(r=1,2).
$$
*If $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}<x_{N,m}$, then these frequencies obey*
$$
\left|\frac{\omega_{N,m}^{(1)}}{\omega_{N,m}^{(2)}}-\frac{T_{H,1}}{T_{H,2}}\right|
\le
\frac{T_{H,1}}{T_{H,2}}\,
\frac{2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}}{x_{N,m}-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}},
$$
*with the exact ratio $\omega_{N,m}^{(1)}/\omega_{N,m}^{(2)}=T_{H,1}/T_{H,2}$ on the exact-closure subbranch. Thus the branch predicts a universal temperature-normalized phase ruler at tolerance $2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}$, while raw frequencies scale with horizon temperature.*

*Proof.* Proposition Q.0.19 gives
$$
\operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}\!\left(\frac{\hbar\omega_N^{(r)}}{k_B T_{H,r}},\,N\ln2\right)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}
$$
for each horizon $H_r$, and the triangle inequality in $\mathbb R/(2\pi\mathbb Z)$ gives the reduced-phase bound; at $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}=0$ both phases equal $[N\ln2]_{2\pi}$. For the lifted form write $\hbar\omega_{N,m}^{(r)}/(k_B T_{H,r})=x_{N,m}+e_r$ with $|e_r|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}$. Then
$$
\frac{\omega_{N,m}^{(1)}}{\omega_{N,m}^{(2)}}
=
\frac{T_{H,1}}{T_{H,2}}\cdot\frac{x_{N,m}+e_1}{x_{N,m}+e_2},
\qquad
\left|\frac{x_{N,m}+e_1}{x_{N,m}+e_2}-1\right|
\le
\frac{|e_1-e_2|}{x_{N,m}-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}}
\le
\frac{2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}}{x_{N,m}-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}},
$$
and at $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}=0$ the ratio is exactly $T_{H,1}/T_{H,2}$. $\square$

<a id="corollary-q020b-three-gap-spectral-fingerprint"></a>**Corollary Q.0.20b (Three-Gap Spectral Fingerprint).** *For a finite Landauer-spectroscopy truncation*
$$
\mathcal P_{N_{\max}}
:=
\{[N\ln2]_{2\pi}:1\le N\le N_{\max}\},
$$
*sort the points cyclically in $[0,2\pi)$ and let $\mathcal G_{N_{\max}}$ be the set of adjacent circular gap lengths. Then*
$$
|\mathcal G_{N_{\max}}|\le3.
$$
*Consequently, on the exact phase-matching subbranch $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}=0$, a peak set realizing the first $N_{\max}$ Landauer labels has at most three adjacent circular gap lengths after transforming frequencies to $x=\hbar\omega/(k_B T_H)$. At nonzero tolerance, the exact three-gap statement concerns the nominal grid $\mathcal P_{N_{\max}}$; measured phases satisfy the circular-distance bound of Proposition Q.0.19.*

*Proof.* Divide the nominal phase points by $2\pi$. The set becomes
$$
\{N\alpha_L\bmod1:1\le N\le N_{\max}\},
\qquad
\alpha_L=\frac{\ln2}{2\pi}.
$$
By Lemma Q.0.7b, $\alpha_L$ is irrational. The index range $1,\ldots,N_{\max}$ is a common circle translation of the range $0,\ldots,N_{\max}-1$ in Proposition Q.0.7n, so it has the same gap lengths. Multiplication by $2\pi$ preserves their number. Proposition Q.0.19 identifies measured phases with the nominal grid on the zero-tolerance subbranch; at nonzero tolerance it supplies a proximity bound and does not preserve exact equality of gaps. $\square$

*Proof.* The certificate enclosures for the two transcendental inputs can be checked using convergent series. The identity
$$
\ln2=2\sum_{m=0}^{\infty}\frac1{(2m+1)3^{2m+1}}
$$
has, after the terms $m=0,\ldots,M-1$, a positive remainder bounded by
$$
\frac{2}{2M+1}\frac{3^{-(2M+1)}}{1-3^{-2}}.
$$
Machin's identity
$$
\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)
$$
is verified by the tangent addition formula and the fact that both sides lie in $(3,4)$; each arctangent is enclosed by its alternating series, whose error is smaller than the first omitted term. Rational interval division then encloses $\alpha_L=\ln2/(2\pi)$ and verifies the printed prefix in item 1 by containment in its decimal-prefix interval.

For item 2, begin with the certified interval for $y_0=\alpha_L$. At stage $j$, the certificate verifies that $y_j$ lies strictly inside one unit interval $(a_j,a_j+1)$ and forms an outward enclosure for
$$
y_{j+1}=\frac1{y_j-a_j}.
$$
Induction therefore proves every recorded partial quotient. The exact recurrences
$$
p_j=a_jp_{j-1}+p_{j-2},
\qquad
q_j=a_jq_{j-1}+q_{j-2},
$$
with $(p_{-1},p_0)=(1,0)$ and $(q_{-1},q_0)=(0,1)$ prove all integer entries in item 3. The certificate evaluates
$$
e_j=\left|\alpha_L-\frac{p_j}{q_j}\right|,
\qquad
q_j\lVert q_j\alpha_L\rVert=q_j|q_j\alpha_L-p_j|,
\qquad
|q_j\ln2-2\pi p_j|=2\pi|q_j\alpha_L-p_j|
$$
by outward interval arithmetic. Each resulting interval lies inside the rounding cell of the printed entry. Theorem Q.0.7k proves the record-minimum interpretation.

For item 4, the continued-fraction discrepancy theorem for an irrational rotation (Kuipers and Niederreiter 1974) applies because Lemma Q.0.7b proves irrationality and the exact recurrence verifies $q_k\le N<q_{k+1}$. It yields
$$
ND_N^*\le3+\sum_{i=1}^{k+1}a_i.
$$
The certified quotients give $\sum_{i=1}^{10}a_i=38$, hence $D_N^*\le41/N$ on the displayed range. If $0\le y_1\le\cdots\le y_N<1$ are the certified sorted residues, then
$$
D_N^*
=\max_{1\le i\le N}
\max\left\{\frac iN-y_i,\ y_i-\frac{i-1}{N}\right\}.
$$
The supplied permutations and interval comparisons prove the three displayed finite values by this formula. An arbitrary circular arc is a difference of at most two anchored intervals, so its counting error is at most $2ND_N^*$.

For item 5, the three-gap theorem for irrational rotations (Sós 1958; Świerczkowski 1958) applies to $\alpha_L$. At $N=q_k$, the Farey-neighbor gap-count formula (Taha 2018, Theorem 2), applied to the adjacent convergents $p_{k-1}/q_{k-1}$ and $p_k/q_k$, gives the two lengths
$$
\lVert q_{k-1}\alpha_L\rVert,
\qquad
\lVert q_{k-1}\alpha_L\rVert+\lVert q_k\alpha_L\rVert
$$
with multiplicities $q_k-q_{k-1}$ and $q_{k-1}$; these sum to $q_k$. For every other displayed row, the certificate permutation places the intervals for $\{j\alpha_L\}$ in strict cyclic order. Subtracting successive intervals, including the wraparound gap, proves the listed lengths, multiplicities, and their sum-to-one check. Finally, $0<\alpha_L<1$ implies
$$
\lfloor(N+1)\alpha_L\rfloor-\lfloor N\alpha_L\rfloor\in\{0,1\},
$$
which proves the binary winding-increment formula. No statement about amplitudes, widths, greybody factors, or nonresonant envelopes enters the certificate. $\square$

<a id="remark-q020b2-status-split-for-the-horizon-transfer-branch"></a>**Remark Q.0.20b.2 (Status Split for the Horizon Transfer Branch).** Proposition Q.0.20b.1 closes only the phase-grid arithmetic after an accepted transfer record $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{hor}}$ is present. It fixes the positions, recurrence hierarchy, finite gap statistics, and window-counting bounds of the Landauer grid. It does not by itself derive the transfer map from retained horizon channel data, and it does not fix amplitudes, widths, greybody factors, nonresonant envelopes, or peak-identification tolerances.

<a id="theorem-q020b3-conditional-transfer-map-separation"></a>**Theorem Q.0.20b.3 (Conditional Transfer-Map Separation).** Fix the retained horizon channel $\mathfrak H_n^{\mathrm{ret}}$, deterministic exterior recovery certificate $\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{hor},n}$, and Page/design scrambling certificates. Assume two finite scattering completions satisfy every prior constraint and agree on these records but give inequivalent retained phase-position outputs. Then those records do not determine the phase-position output. If one such completion violates
$$
\operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}(x,N\ln2)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}
$$
on the same registered domain and tolerance, the records do not imply that transfer law. An accepted horizon transfer record $\mathfrak T_{\mathrm{hor}}$ supplies the additional scattering map, loop time, MPU-cycle phase, domain, and phase tolerance of Definition Q.0.7u.

*Proof.* The assumed completions have the same prior datum and inequivalent retained outputs, so they satisfy the non-identifiability criterion of Theorem P.14.1f. If an admissible completion violates the displayed inequality, that inequality cannot be a consequence of the shared prior constraints. The existence and admissibility of the two completions are separate hypotheses; they do not follow solely from the absence of an explicit scattering-map entry. Definition Q.0.7u specifies the additional record on which the phase-grid conclusions are conditional. ∎
<a id="corollary-q020c-landauer-horizon-spectroscopy-null-conditions"></a>**Corollary Q.0.20c (Landauer Horizon Spectroscopy Null Conditions).** *Within an independently validated Definition Q.0.7u transfer branch, fix the admitted label domain, peak tolerance, and measurement-uncertainty protocol before comparison. The following statistically resolved observations falsify the Landauer phase-grid component of that branch:*

\operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}(\Pi(\omega_N,H),N\ln2)\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}
$$
*after accounting for the registered instrumental and greybody-model phase uncertainty;*

2. *a cross-horizon comparison of the same registered labels whose reduced phases violate*
$$
\operatorname{dist}_{2\pi}(\Pi(\omega_N^{(1)},H_1),\Pi(\omega_N^{(2)},H_2))\le2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}};
$$

3. *on the exact phase-matching subbranch $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{peak}}=0$, a resolved block of the first $N_{\max}$ labels whose adjacent reduced-phase gaps are incompatible with the three-gap bound after measurement uncertainty is included.*

*Proof.* Item 1 contradicts Proposition Q.0.19 on its registered domain and tolerance. Item 2 contradicts the circular-distance inequality of Corollary Q.0.20a. Item 3 contradicts the zero-tolerance observed-grid consequence of Corollary Q.0.20b. Nonzero phase tolerance does not preserve the exact number of distinct measured gap lengths. Each contradiction is conditional on prior validation of Definition Q.0.7u; absent that branch, the null result rejects the transfer bridge rather than the SPAP/Landauer cost theorem itself. $\square$

## Q.1 Foundational Relation and the Optimization Goal

This appendix relates the emergent Planck length $L_P$ to the MPU spacing $\delta$ on the capacity-achieving, entropy-saturating, additive-ledger branch of Theorem E.6 and then evaluates the relation on a specified intersection of channel branches. Adopt the same-family saturation $C(\mathcal E_N)=C_{\max}$ and the independent calibration $G_{\mathrm{op}}=G$, so that $L_P^2=G\hbar/c^3$. Under these identifications, Equation E.9 gives
$$
G=\frac{\eta\delta^2c^3}{4\hbar\chi C_{\max}}.
\tag{Q.1}
$$
Using $L_P^2=G\hbar/c^3$ yields
$$
L_P^2=\frac{\eta\delta^2}{4\chi C_{\max}},
\tag{Q.2}
$$
and hence
$$
\frac{\delta^2}{L_P^2}=\frac{4\chi C_{\max}}{\eta}.
\tag{Q.3}
$$

## Q.2 Conditional Boundary-Parameter Assignments

Equation Q.3 is evaluated below using three independent entries: the residual-budget capacity assignment, the throughput-saturated channel-independence selection with the other variables held constant, and the ideal-packing selection with the other variables held constant. Their simultaneous use defines the combined branch.

### <a id="q21-channel-capacity-c_max-2ln-2-on-the-residual-budget-branch"></a>Q.2.1 Channel Capacity: $C_{\max}^* = 2\ln 2$ on the Residual-Budget Branch

On the separately assumed residual-budget branch of Appendix E, Equation E.14 assigns
$$
C_{\max}^*=\ln d_0-\varepsilon_0.
$$
Combining the Theorem-Z.2 comparator value $d_0=8$ with the registered binary structural value $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$ from Definition 28, Definition J.1, and Theorem J.1 gives
$$
\boxed{C_{\max}^*=\ln8-\ln2=2\ln2=2\varepsilon_0}. \tag{Q.10}
$$
This is a conditional allocation identity, not a consequence of SPAP or of physical reset heat. Alternative resource-partition rules give different $C_{\max}^*$ and therefore different values of $\delta/L_P$ in Sections Q.2.4 and Q.5.

<a id="remark-q101-bit-budget-characterization"></a>**Remark Q.10.1 (Bit-Budget Characterization).** Since $N_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\min}=2^{K_0}=8$ and the minimal complex Hilbert carrier saturates $d_0=N_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\min}$ on the minimal branch, while the PCE reference uses structural $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$, the capacity-cost ratio, evaluated at $\varepsilon=\varepsilon_0$, has the structural form
$$
\frac{C_{\max}^*}{\varepsilon} = \frac{\ln(d_0)-\varepsilon}{\varepsilon} = K_0 - 1.
$$
At $K_0=3$ this gives $C_{\max}^*/\varepsilon=2$: under the residual-budget rule, one structural bit is reserved and $K_0-1=2$ structural bits remain as residual channel capacity. This counting identity does not imply a physical Landauer cost without the independent reset hypotheses stated above.

### <a id="q22-correlation-factor-chi-1"></a>Q.2.2 Correlation Factor: $\chi^* = 1$

<a id="lemma-q22-channel-independence-on-the-throughput-saturated-branch"></a>**Lemma Q.2.2 (Channel Independence on the Throughput-Saturated Branch).** Hold $(\delta,\eta,C_{\max})$ constant, assume the accepted optimization maximizes a utility strictly increasing in the saturated ND-RID throughput, and assume $\chi=1$ is feasible. Then
$$
\boxed{\chi^*=1.}
\tag{Q.11}
$$

*Proof.* The effective link count is $N_{\mathrm{eff}}=\chi N_{\mathrm{geom}}$ with $0<\chi\le1$. With the remaining variables constant, the throughput is strictly increasing in $\chi$, so its feasible maximum is attained at $\chi=1$. ∎

### <a id="q23-packing-factor-eta-1"></a>Q.2.3 Packing Factor: $\eta^* = 1$

<a id="lemma-q23-ideal-packing-on-the-throughput-saturated-branch"></a>**Lemma Q.2.3 (Ideal Packing on the Throughput-Saturated Branch).** Hold $(\delta,\chi,C_{\max})$ constant, assume the accepted optimization maximizes a utility strictly increasing in the saturated ND-RID throughput, and assume $\eta=1$ is feasible. Then
$$
\boxed{\eta^*=1.}
\tag{Q.12}
$$

*Proof.* Since $\sigma_{\mathrm{geom}}=1/(\eta\delta^2)$ with $\eta\ge1$, the throughput is strictly decreasing in $\eta$ while the remaining variables are constant. Its feasible maximum is therefore attained at $\eta=1$. ∎

### Q.2.4 Final Result

Substituting the three independently selected branch values $C_{\max}^*=2\ln2$, $\chi^*=1$, and $\eta^*=1$ into Equation (Q.3) yields the closed-form ratio reported in Equation (Q.18):
$$
\frac{\delta^2}{L_P^2}=8\ln 2,\qquad \frac{\delta}{L_P}=\sqrt{8\ln 2}\approx 2.355.
$$

<a id="theorem-q24a-scale-surface-and-coupled-objective-nonentailment"></a>**Theorem Q.2.4a (Scale-Surface and Coupled-Objective Nonentailment).** Fix any $r>0$. On the declared parameter domain $C_{\max}>0$, $0<\chi\le1$, and $\eta\ge1$, Equation Q.3 with $\delta^2/L_P^2=r$ has the two-parameter solution surface
$$
\mathcal F_r
=\left\{
\left(\frac{r\eta}{4\chi},\chi,\eta\right):
0<\chi\le1,\ \eta\ge1
\right\}.
\tag{Q.2.4a.1}
$$
In particular, at $r=8\ln2$, both
$$
z_0=(2\ln2,1,1),
\qquad
z_1=(4\ln2,1,2)
\tag{Q.2.4a.2}
$$
give the same spacing ratio. For $j\in\{0,1\}$ the smooth objective completion on the ambient parameter domain
$$
J_j(z)=\|z-z_j\|_2^2
\tag{Q.2.4a.3}
$$
is strongly convex, has Hessian $2I$, and has the unique stable minimizer $z_j$. Thus Equation Q.3 and its spacing value do not select a coupled objective, a unique optimizer, or its stochastic dynamics. Hard-imposing the three separate branch assignments selects $z_0$ by premise, not by a coupled optimization theorem.

*Proof.* Solving $4\chi C_{\max}/\eta=r$ for $C_{\max}$ gives (Q.2.4a.1); substitution gives (Q.2.4a.2). The gradient and Hessian of (Q.2.4a.3) are $2(z-z_j)$ and $2I$, so $z_j$ is its unique global minimizer and is Lyapunov stable under the gradient flow $\dot z=-\nabla J_j(z)$. Since the two admissible completions share $r$ but select different minimizers, the scale relation cannot entail the missing coupled objective or optimizer. ∎

<a id="proposition-q24b-monotone-product-box-optimizer-classification"></a>**Proposition Q.2.4b (Monotone Product-Box Optimizer Classification).** Fix $C^*>0$ and the compact product box
$$
B:=[C_-,C^*]\times[\chi_-,1]\times[1,\eta_+],
\qquad
0<C_-<C^*,\quad0<\chi_-<1<\eta_+,
\tag{Q.2.4b.1}
$$
in the coordinates $z=(C_{\max},\chi,\eta)$, and let $\mathcal U$ be the class of continuous utilities on $B$ that are strictly increasing in $C_{\max}$, strictly increasing in $\chi$ and strictly decreasing in $\eta$. Then:

1. Every $U\in\mathcal U$ has the unique maximizer $z_*:=(C^*,1,1)$ on $B$. The Gibbs laws $\pi_\beta(dz)\propto e^{\beta U(z)}dz$ on $B$ converge weakly to $\delta_{z_*}$ as $\beta\to\infty$; for every neighborhood $O$ of $z_*$ there are constants $c_O,s_O>0$ with $\pi_\beta(B\setminus O)\le c_Oe^{-s_O\beta}$. At $C^*=2\ln2$, $z_*$ is the point $z_0$ of (Q.2.4a.2) and the spacing response $4\chi C_{\max}/\eta$ equals $8\ln2$.
2. A coupling constraint can remove this selection. Assume $C_-<\frac34C^*$ and $\chi_-<\frac12$, and let $B_\flat:=\{z\in B:2C_{\max}/C^*+\chi\le5/2\}$. Then $z_*\notin B_\flat$, and the members $U_1:=C_{\max}/C^*+\chi-\eta$ and $U_2:=3C_{\max}/C^*+\chi-\eta$ of $\mathcal U$ have on $B_\flat$ the distinct unique maximizers $(\frac34C^*,1,1)$ and $(C^*,\frac12,1)$, with spacing responses $3C^*$ and $2C^*$.

*Proof.* Item 1. For $z=(C_{\max},\chi,\eta)\in B$, coordinatewise monotonicity gives $U(z)\le U(C^*,\chi,\eta)\le U(C^*,1,\eta)\le U(C^*,1,1)$, with equality throughout only at $z_*$. Let $O$ be a neighborhood of $z_*$. Compactness and uniqueness give $m_O:=\max_{B\setminus O}U<U(z_*)$; put $s_O:=\frac12(U(z_*)-m_O)$ and $O'_O:=\{z\in B:U(z)>U(z_*)-s_O\}$, a nonempty relatively open subset of $B$ with positive volume $|O'_O|$. Then
$$
\pi_\beta(B\setminus O)
\le\frac{|B|\,e^{\beta m_O}}{|O'_O|\,e^{\beta(U(z_*)-s_O)}}
=\frac{|B|}{|O'_O|}e^{-\beta s_O},
$$
which proves the tail bound and weak convergence. Substitution gives the spacing value. Item 2. Since $2+1>5/2$, $z_*\notin B_\flat$. Both utilities decrease strictly in $\eta$ and the coupling constraint does not involve $\eta$, so every maximizer has $\eta=1$. In $(s,\chi):=(C_{\max}/C^*,\chi)$ the remaining feasible set is the polygon with vertices $(s_-,\chi_-)$, $(1,\chi_-)$, $(1,\frac12)$, $(\frac34,1)$ and $(s_-,1)$, where $s_-:=C_-/C^*<\frac34$. The linear function $s+\chi$ takes the values $s_-+\chi_-$, $1+\chi_-$, $\frac32$, $\frac74$, $s_-+1$ at these vertices, and $3s+\chi$ takes $3s_-+\chi_-$, $3+\chi_-$, $\frac72$, $\frac{13}4$, $3s_-+1$. The strict vertex maxima $\frac74$ at $(\frac34,1)$ and $\frac72$ at $(1,\frac12)$ are the unique maximizers of the two linear programs, because the maximizing set of a linear function on a polygon is a face spanned by maximizing vertices. The spacing responses are $4\cdot1\cdot\frac34C^*=3C^*$ and $4\cdot\frac12\cdot C^*=2C^*$. ∎

<a id="definition-q24c-finite-reset-link-source-and-complete-invoice"></a>**Definition Q.2.4c (Finite Reset-Link Source and Complete Invoice).** Fix the ideal externally driven source Q10-RESET-LINK-PERIODIC-v1 with the following exact preparation, intervention, ownership, physical-clock and positive-tariff contract.

### 1. Frozen source and scope

The manufacturing grammar has exactly eight configurations $x=(q,k,g)$, $q,k,g\in\{1,2\}$. These choices precede every output, cost comparison and proposed spacing prediction. $q$ is a data-factor width, $k$ a geometric row spacing, and $g$ a wired duplication multiplicity. They are not themselves declared to be Q10's coordinates: those are derived below. The source includes a complete finite eight-position controller; arbitrary extra couplings or channels are outside this named architecture. No all-hardware optimality is claimed. Configuration controls are classical and fixed during each communication episode. Coherent superposition of manufacturing settings and sender-controlled switching are not source operations. The nominated physical initial state is $X_{0}=000$, indexing $(q,k,g)=(1,1,1)$, and the specified adaptation law reaches every setting with positive probability. Other initial probability laws are analyzed mathematically; their physical preparation is not claimed without a separate invoice. Distributions over these eight actual settings do not add input ports. Their expected frame potential is the affine average of the conditional frame potentials, so no mixture can improve below the pure minimum, and a mixture attains it exactly when supported on the minimizing states. Physical $C_{\max}$, $\chi$ and $\eta$ are reported conditional on the actual setting, not manufactured by averaging incompatible channel geometries.

For every positive integer $L$ use spatial geometry $T^2_{2L\delta}\times\mathbb{R}$, with BOTH tangential coordinates periodic and the normal coordinate nonperiodic. The registered cut is $H=T^2\times\{0\}$, the compact boundary of the source-side region $T^2\times(-\infty,0)$. There is no second normal-periodic cut. The source and receiver layers are at normal coordinates $-\delta/2$ and $+\delta/2$, respectively. The boundary has side lengths $2L\delta$. The fixed resolution $\delta>0$, clock period $\tau>0$ and service prices are independent dimensional source parameters. The two layers lie on opposite sides of the boundary. There are $A=4L^2$ base surface cells. Positions $(i\delta,j\delta)$, $i,j\in\{0,\dots,2L-1\}$, fix the geometry. A configuration $k$ has one boundary-crossing link at each site with $j$ divisible by $k$. Its geometric link count is $N=A/k$. Pair adjacent $i$ positions when $g=2$; singleton groups when $g=1$. There are $M=A/(kg)$ groups. All links are finite-range, vertex degree is uniformly bounded, and the source-side pair wire has length $\delta$. Inactive components are still priced stocks, but have no crossing interaction, signal port or edge in the active network. The geometric count concerns actual nonzero crossing edges, not the number of purchased spare components.

Every base cell contains a source-side pair of persistent fair classical bits $Z_i=(Z_{i1},Z_{i2})$, independent over $i$. This same environment and prediction task is used for every configuration. The next-time target is $Z$ itself. Every episode uses fresh independent source labels, prepared by $|+\rangle$ states and source-side computational-basis measurement. Persistence means from the observation instant to the prediction instant WITHIN that episode, not reuse of an old hidden label in later adaptive frames. Past receiver transcripts therefore contain no information about a new episode’s unrevealed target bits. The complete preparation hardware and records are owned. All these bits, including ignored bits, remain on the source side and inaccessible to the predictor except through the specified boundary channel.

Each group has exactly one admitted independently addressable 8-level input cell (three qubits); the remaining would-be inputs are not independent intervention ports. The group anchor is the least i site. Preparation loads the first q bits of its actual Z into the q data factors; the other factors are nuisance registers, not extra message ports. For channel capacity proofs arbitrary quantum inputs and reference systems on the one group input are admitted. No secret restriction to the fair encoding is used in the capacity upper bound.

### 2. Source primitives and boundary

The finite driven source supplies the following independently declared primitives:

1. The finite square-lattice source/receiver apparatus, three-qubit input, courier and receiver cells; finite mode menu; static unused stocks; nearest-neighbor configuration paths and source pair wires.
2. The degenerate ready cells, their finite protection/retention service, and the fresh source-side reset and pinching auxiliaries. Their zero idle Hamiltonian does not make their purchase or protection free.
3. The finite-duration Hadamard, CNOT, SWAP, reversible finite lookup, and receipt-writing ports; their exact matrices and supplied external waveforms specified in Section 5.
4. The exact finite lazy/proposal/acceptance preparation menu and 56 acceptance angles specified in Section 6. These are calibrated native coefficients, not exact real numbers represented by an unpriced finite bit string.
5. The local mode, forecast and proper-score lookup services, all their physical ROM cells, and their complete truth-table rules in Section 4.
6. The finite externally driven timing schedule, fresh phase flags, execution receipts, and complete positive stock/service/retention tariff of Sections 7–8.
7. The input/output intervention cut, source-only grading and baths, the complete receiver output algebra, and the independent-episode environment law below.

The source is an **open, externally driven finite native instrument**. It does not purport to compile all these ports into a particular Boolean gate library, derive their apparatus from a finite isolated Hamiltonian clock, or establish empirical manufacturability. The delivered coupling, not an inert ROM string alone, is part of each priced native work port. An additional microscopic supplier, driver response port, command, or bath access would require a new inventory and channel audit.

All source bath/reset/pinching registers, source copies of labels, the grader, and adaptation randomness are physically on the source side. There is no wire, optical output, receiver command, or receiver-accessible storage path from them to the receiver except the explicitly listed local crossing gates. They are not excluded by an accounting convention. Source-side local wires never cross the boundary.

The sole always-present configuration crossing is at lattice site (0,0), which belongs to every mode's active set. Before the unknown input boundary, its existing link sends the three classical mode bits to the receiver seed. This adds no geometric edge and is not a label-dependent channel output for fixed x. The mode is fixed before the admitted input. Admitting a sender's message as an extra mode-selection command would define a different channel and is not claimed here.

The rest of the lattice receives the mode via two nearest-neighbor snake paths, one in each layer. They have A−1 edges each; the three mode bits are copied along each path. Source and receiver tables then determine active and anchor masks locally from that mode and the station's fixed lattice address. There is no additional crossing edge at an inactive site. All data couplings are switched off outside their prescribed slots. A lattice site has only its path neighbors, its optional source pair neighbor, its local crossing neighbor, and a fixed finite number of internal ports. The intercell degree and edge range are uniformly bounded. Every native local lookup has bounded arity independent of L; a giant all-lattice scoring gate is not used.

### 3. Literal cells, active routing and full receiver output

Each period has a fresh package. The following are distinct physical two-level cells; readiness is included in their positive stock price. Source input and courier cells are grouped in threes. ROM and actuator stocks are separately counted in Section 8, not charged as these cells again.

| Cells per package | Count | Side and purpose |
|---|---:|---|
| Z, persistent target bits | 2A | Source; same full task for every mode |
| T, fair-preparation shadow | 2A | Source; retained purifier/record |
| I, potential three-bit inputs | 3A | Source; independent intervention only at active anchors |
| B, reset auxiliaries | 3A | Source; fresh ready SWAP destinations |
| P, pinching pointers | 3A | Source |
| Q, pinching dephasing shadows | 3A | Source |
| E, potential couriers | 3A | Source; one cell at every possible crossing site |
| Y, potential receiver cells | 3A | Receiver |
| Local mode banks | 6A | Three bits per site per layer |
| Local mask banks | 8A | Four fresh bits per site per layer |
| Enabled-latch banks | 2A | One per site per layer |
| Local forecast banks | 8A | Four bits per site per layer |
| Local score banks | 2A | Source only |
| Ready/completion flags | 2A | Receiver; fixed given successful schedule |
| Dummy-loading bank | 2A | Source; fresh destinations only for arbitrary-input test mode |
| Adaptation registers | 16 | Source; $X_{\mathrm{old}}$(3), $X_{\mathrm{new}}$(3), $J$(3), $J_{\mathrm{shadow}}$(3), lazy(1), lazy_shadow(1), accept(1), accept_shadow(1) |
| One-use operation receipts | $P_{\mathrm{op}}=32A+12$ | One fresh cell for each dedicated possible operation port |
| Phase flags | 2S | S fresh source and S fresh receiver flags |

Thus the exact non-ROM physical-cell count is

$$
\begin{aligned}
B_{\mathrm{cell}} &= 52A+16+(32A+12)+2S = 84A+28+2S, \\
S&=32A+32.
\end{aligned}
$$

There are additionally three initial source-side configuration cells shared by the finite $H$-period run, supplied ready in $X_{0}=000$, which denotes $(q,k,g)=(1,1,1)$. This is the physical initial law nominated here. Arbitrary alternative initial distributions are mathematical starting laws for the same kernel; supplying one physically would require its own preparation/record invoice. Every period receives the previous period's $X_{\mathrm{new}}$ through three charged source-side copies into fresh $X_{\mathrm{old}}$; previous states remain retained.

All A potential input/courier/receiver positions, every unused bit factor, disabled actuator, spare auxiliary and unused ROM row remain purchased and retained. Buying a spare does not turn its disabled crossing coupling into an active network edge.

For an active anchor $a$, data factors are $I_{a,1}$ through $I_{a,q}$. In task mode load $Z_{a,\ell}$ into $I_{a,\ell}$ by a CNOT, $q$ calls per anchor. For each nuisance factor $\ell=q+1,\dots,3$, apply $\mathrm{SWAP}(I_{a,\ell},B_{a,\ell})$, exactly $(3-q)M$ calls. This is an actual reset to a supplied ready state and retains the removed input in $B$. It is not an erasure with an unpriced bath.

For each data factor apply $\mathrm{CNOT}(I_{a,\ell},P_{a,\ell})$ and $\mathrm{CNOT}(P_{a,\ell},Q_{a,\ell})$. Then move to y if accepted and otherwise remain x. To guarantee an explicit self loop at every state even when all proposals are accepted, perform this proposal only with probability 1/2; otherwise idle. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_{xy} &= (1/14)\, a_{xy} \quad \text{for } y\ne x, \\
P_{xx} &= 1-\sum_{y\ne x}P_{xy}\ge 1/2.
\end{aligned}
$$

The complete discrete kernel is stochastic and irreducible because all $a_{xy}>0$. Define $\pi_x=\exp(-\beta V(x))/\sum_z\exp(-\beta V(z))$. Then $\pi_xP_{xy}=(1/14)\min(\pi_x,\pi_y)=\pi_yP_{yx}$. Therefore $\pi$ is invariant and unique. An elementary uniform convergence bound follows: let $R=\max V-\min V$ and $\varepsilon=e^{-\beta R}/14$. Every entry of $P$ is at least $\varepsilon$, so $P=8\varepsilon U+(1-8\varepsilon)Q$ for the uniform-row matrix $U$ and a stochastic $Q$. Consequently total-variation distances contract by at most $1-8\varepsilon$ per step. This proves convergence from every initial state and stability of the unique invariant law. At positive $\beta$ no claim of permanent convergence to a particular configuration is made.

Let $m=|S|$ and gap $\Delta V>0$. Then

$$
\pi(E\setminus S) \le ((8-m)/m) \exp(-\beta\Delta V).
$$

Within S the stationary weights are exactly equal. Thus the low-noise limiting law is uniform on the complete minimizing set. The bound includes every tie identified above. These statements concern the adopted paid stochastic update source, not a universal law of physical adaptation.

∎

On the intersection of the residual-capacity, throughput-saturated, channel-independence, and ideal-packing branches, the registered values are:

<a id="proposition-q61c-deterministic-retained-link-clock-from-common-hard-rod-microdynamics"></a>**Proposition Q.6.1c (Deterministic Retained-Link Clock from Common Hard-Rod Microdynamics).**

## Complete finite-N deterministic mechanical link theorem

### 1. Statement, including its quantifiers and declared data

For every integer $N\ge 1$ and every independently specified $m,p_0,g,\delta>0$ and $a\ge 0$, there is an autonomous classical hard-core two-rail source with $2(N+2)$ rods, a binary input $b\in\{0,1\}$, and counted vertices $0,\dots,N$. Its source and receiver phase variables, collision flow, passive local observation, retained record and edge resource prices are specified below. For either input, and therefore for every probability mixture of the two inputs, the first source-sensitive complete local record at vertex $i$ is attained at

$$
T_i=i\tau,\qquad \tau=mg/p_0>0.
$$

Before $T_i$, every allowed observation of the full downstream local phase history has a source-independent distribution. At and after $T_i$ the actual receiving rod pair retains $b$ with zero error. Each of the $N$ counted edges takes exactly $\tau$; their serialized contact events generate the clock. The construction has no separately supplied tick schedule or release timer. For the explicitly chosen receiver-material per delivered protocol nat representative, normalized weights are $w_e=1$ and

$$
d(i,j)=\delta|i-j|,\qquad c_{\mathrm{link}}=\delta/\tau=\delta p_0/(mg).
$$

This is a first-arrival and attained-distance/time result within the declared source and response grammar. It is neither a universally fastest-device bound nor a claim that graph structure determines a dimensionful constant. The source phase space is continuous, its interactions singular, and its preparation exact. The claimed capacity ln 2 is that of the registered binary protocol, never unrestricted analog phase space.

### 2. Complete source and autonomous flow

Use two parallel, noninteracting one-dimensional rails $r=0,1$. Each has labeled equal-mass rods $i=0,\dots,N+1$; the last pair is an uncounted guard. Each rod has mass $m$ and length $a$. Let $x_i=i(a+g)$. Both source preparations have

$$
q_{i,r}(0)=x_i,\qquad p_{i,r}(0)=0,
$$

except $p_{0,b}(0)=p_0$. The independent inputs fix all lengths, masses, momenta and the source label before propagation. Timing is not modulated to convey another symbol. The all-zero-momentum null preparation is a separate diagnostic and is not a third admitted channel input.

On each rail impose $q_{i+1,r}-q_{i,r}\ge a$. Between contacts,

$$
dq_{i,r}/dt=p_{i,r}/m,\qquad dp_{i,r}/dt=0.
$$

At an isolated approaching contact the adjacent momenta exchange. The autonomous Hamiltonian billiard has free Hamiltonian $H=\sum_{i,r}p_{i,r}^{2}/(2m)$ in the nonoverlap chamber, with elastic reflection on its boundary. Its contact boundary is part of the source specification; no finite smooth contact potential is asserted.

For completeness, equal masses plus momentum and energy conservation imply $p+q=p'+q'$ and $p^{2}+q^{2}=p'^{2}+q'^{2}$. Therefore the two outgoing roots are the same unordered pair $\{p,q\}$. Of the identity and exchange alternatives, the approaching collision requires the exchange branch to produce nonapproaching relative motion. Here the incoming pair is $(p_0,0)$, so it becomes $(0,p_0)$. This physical update, not an assigned clock reading, defines each event.

At each contact use the outgoing, right-continuous momentum as the event state. Positions remain continuous. This convention is essential to attainment at the endpoint; a preimpact read would not give the same minimum for the displayed decoder. Only finitely many forward contacts occur, and their explicit solution below establishes existence and uniqueness for these source preparations without assuming a general many-body billiard theorem.

### 3. Exact all-time solution and induction proof

Put $v=p_0/m$ and $\tau=g/v$. For each counted rod $0\le i\le N$, on rail $b$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
q_{i,b}(t)&=x_i+\min\{g,\max\{0,v(t-i\tau)\}\}, \\
p_{i,b}(t)&=p_0 \quad \text{if } i\tau\le t<(i+1)\tau, \text{ and } 0 \text{ otherwise}.
\end{aligned}
$$

The guard obeys

$$
\begin{aligned}
q_{n+1,b}(t)&=x_{n+1}+\max\{0,v(t-(N+1)\tau)\}, \\
p_{n+1,b}(t)&=p_0 \quad \text{if } t\ge(N+1)\tau, \text{ and } 0 \text{ otherwise}.
\end{aligned}
$$

Every inactive-rail rod remains at (xᵢ,0). All formulas are for $t\ge 0$ and use the postimpact convention at equality.

Proof. At time 0 only rod 0 on rail $b$ moves, at velocity $v$. Its right end is separated by $g$ from rod 1's left end. For $0\le t<g/v$ it encounters nothing; all other rods remain stationary. At $t=g/v$, $q_{0,b}=x_0+g=x_1-a$, so the two rods contact, and the elastic exchange transfers $p_{0}$ to rod 1. Rod 0 stops at $x_0+g$. Now rod 1 is at $x_{1}$ and faces exactly the same free gap $g$ to rod 2. Inductively, when rod $j$ receives momentum at $j\tau$, it is the only moving rod, with the next receiver at $x_{j+1}$, and traverses $g$ before the next collision. Previous stopped rods cannot overtake it. Every other adjacent pair has no approaching relative velocity. At $(j+1)\tau$ it stops at $x_j+g$ and transfers $p_{0}$ to $j+1$. Induction through $j=N$ establishes every counted and guard arrival. The guard thereafter has no obstacle and moves freely forever. No unlisted event or accumulating collision sequence is possible. ∎

Exactly one rod carries $p_{0}$ at every time. Thus the conserved total momentum is $p_{0}$ and the finite kinetic energy is $p_0^{2}/(2m)$. The source is still singular: finite kinetic energy says nothing about a finite force or finite stiffness bound.

### 4. Full spatial support and what “local” means

For every counted vertex i fix the one-sided cell

$$
C_i=[x_i-a/2,x_{i+1}-a/2].
$$

The complete physical support of either owned rod is $[q_{i,r}-a/2,q_{i,r}+a/2]$. Since $0\le q_{i,r}-x_i\le g$, that support lies in $C_i$ for all $t\ge 0$. The upper bound is exact: $x_i+g+a/2=x_{i+1}-a/2$. A shared endpoint causes no earlier source dependence. Before $T_i$, the incoming rod $i-1$ has its right endpoint strictly below $x_i-a/2$; at $T_i$ it first touches that boundary.

The owned local phase variables are $z_i=(q_{i,0},p_{i,0},q_{i,1},p_{i,1})$. Passive classical observations may read arbitrary functions of those variables, or any time history/joint collection of downstream variables, with independent private randomness. They may not reach outside the declared downstream cells, launch extra carriers, alter momenta or gaps, or change the dynamics. This is a locality and operation registration, not a scheduled-read restriction. Observations at every time are permitted.

The locality restriction has content. An instrument observing an upstream collar of width $0<r<g$ encounters the incoming rod at $T_i-r/v$. A centered Voronoi assignment can likewise see an incoming rod before its contact. The theorem does not assert the same first-arrival time for those different support choices.

The guard is necessary for permanent records in fixed terminal cells. Without it, the last counted rod eventually exits any bounded terminal cell. Here counted rod $N$ transfers momentum to guard $N+1$ at $(N+1)\tau$ and remains stopped inside $C_N$ forever. The outgoing guard travels on an explicitly unbounded free output ray. Therefore the all-time construction is finite-particle and finite-kinetic-energy, not a claim of bounded total spatial extent. At any specified finite observation horizon $H$ one may allocate only the finite output length required up to $H$, without asserting behavior after that horizon or installing an uncharged absorbing wall.

### 5. Persistent decoder, no-early theorem and actual minimum

Define, for each counted pair and rail,

$$
A_{i,r}=1\{p_{i,r}\ge p_0/2 \text{ or } q_{i,r}-x_i\ge g/2\}.
$$

The record Rᵢ is ready (⊥) when both indicators vanish, and r when exactly Aᵢ,r is one. The double-active case is outside the admitted source histories and is not silently assigned a valid transmitted bit.

For $t<T_i$ both rods at node $i$ remain at their identical initial phase points. Indeed every rod $j\ge i$, including the guard, is identical in the $b=0$ and $b=1$ histories for all such $t$. Consequently every deterministic passive response to these histories is identical, and adding independent randomness yields identical conditional outcome laws. Adaptivity cannot help: until $T_i$, identical prior observations give identical adaptive choices and equal subsequent local data. No phase observable, threshold crossing, random success tail, or downstream joint read can distinguish the input earlier.

At $t=T_i$, rail $b$ has momentum $p_{0}$ and the other has momentum zero, so $R_i=b$. For $T_i<t<T_{i+1}$ the same momentum term maintains the record. At $T_{i+1}$ the momentum leaves but the displacement is already $g$, so the displacement term keeps $R_i=b$ forever. The guard makes this also true at the terminal counted node. Therefore

$$
\inf\{t\ge 0:R_i(t)\ne\bot\}=\min\{t\ge 0:R_i(t)\ne\bot\}=T_i.
$$

The infimum is genuinely attained in the registered postimpact grammar. This is a source-sensitive physical phase record, not a separately postulated latch or external archive. Its storage is paid for by retaining the displaced rods. The indicator has finite static readout margins on the exact states: independent momentum errors of magnitude strictly less than $p_0/2$ and displacement errors strictly less than $g/2$ preserve the decoded values. This does not preserve exact event times under dynamical preparation errors.

A normalized passive classical instrument is explicit. If $\mu$ is a probability measure supported on the admitted phase histories at a fixed time, set $I_r(\mu)(B)=\mu(B\cap\{R_i=r\})$ for $r\in\{\perp,0,1\}$. These submeasures sum to $\mu$ and yield the same result on repeated passive reads. The source-preparation/flow/record diagram is exactly the ready channel before $T_i$ and the identity binary channel from $T_i$ onward. Mixtures commute with this map. Exchanging source rails exchanges outputs. The null preparation gives no records. This formal instrument does not supply a free external digitizer, communication interface or detector with nonzero physical latency.

### 6. Derived deterministic clock and finite-prefix compatibility

The event time comes from free flight $g$ at velocity $p_0/m$, not from another period. Thus, for every admitted history and every counted edge,

$$
D_i=T_i-T_{i-1}=mg/p_0=\tau>0.
$$

The event count is $\min\{N,\lfloor t/\tau\rfloor\}$. The variables $D_i$ have point-mass law $\delta_\tau$ under every input prior and are trivially independent. Every completed edge attains the lower duration $\tau$; a larger proposed bound is violated by the first edge. Each active carrier comes from the same collision that establishes the preceding event and faces precisely the next untouched gap. Edge serialization is therefore a property of the solved flow.

The full continuous flight phase remains in the owned source. Coarse ready/completed symbols alone are not asserted to form an autonomous continuous-time Markov state; omitting phase while retaining timing would conceal the clock.

If the chain is extended with extra prepared rods, all old counted rods have exactly the same displayed phase histories for every $t\ge 0$. After the old terminal transfers momentum, later collisions cannot catch it or send a reverse disturbance. Thus this is a compatible family of finite-$N$ statements with $O(N)$ material/archive inventory. It is not a finite device capable of infinitely many new updates. The binary bit is copied into distinct owned records rather than erased and renewed for free.

### 7. Binary protocol capacity and the declared positive weighted path

The input alphabet contains precisely the two fixed phase preparations. For $t<T_i$ both transition columns of the receiver channel equal the ready output, so channel capacity is zero. For $t\ge T_i$ the transition matrix is the identity on $\{0,1\}$. For any prior, $I(b;R_i)=H(b)\le\ln 2$, with equality for the fair prior. Thus completed one-use protocol capacity $C_e$ is exactly $\ln 2$ nats. This is not an analog phase-space bound: allowing continuously variable momentum, launch timing, position, or other encodings changes the source class and may increase capacity without bound. A third distinguishable preparation already invalidates an unrestricted $\ln 2$ claim.

Before cost comparison, choose owned receiving material per completed protocol nat as the resource representative. Allocate to directed edge $i-1\to i$ its two previously ready receiving rods once; their mass is $M_e=2m$. They remain in its archive. The source pair and guard pair are separate overhead, and rails, isolation, exact preparation, geometry, calibration, passive-response convention and singular constraints remain declared resources. The functional below prices receiver material; it is not a complete monetary, manufacturing, entropy or total-apparatus cost.

$$
\kappa_e=M_e/C_e=2m/(\ln 2),\qquad \kappa^{*}=2m/(\ln 2),\qquad w_e=\kappa_e/\kappa^{*}=1.
$$

A separately prepared reflected experiment uses the same two-rod local allocation and scalar in the reverse direction, giving a symmetric representative. It is not the same already-spent chain magically reusable in both directions. On the path graph, a path from $i$ to $j$ has at least $|i-j|$ edges; the direct path has exactly that many. Every forward subpath of the actual cascade takes $|i-j|\tau$ and attains $d/(\text{elapsed time})=\delta/\tau$; a new reverse or arbitrary-source experiment requires its own preparation.

The positive scalar is a chosen resource representative extracted from actual owned rods and the proved finite binary transfer budget. The choice of this functional is declared branch data, not a derivation that it is uniquely required. Uniform numbers alone do not identify it with a different preselected representative. The reset-specific entropy/capacity/refresh formula is never applied: there is no reset heat ledger, positive entropy-export derivation, refresh contraction, invented $d_{0}$, or Landauer saturation. ### 8. Calibration, physical interpretation and exact limitations

There are three lengths: free gap $g$, initial physical center spacing $a+g$, and propagation-cost edge length $\delta$. They coincide only if separately chosen/calibrated. If $\delta=a+g$, then $c_{\mathrm{link}}=v(a+g)/g$; the rigid-rod ideal can propagate this front faster than the rod's translational velocity. If $a=0$ and $\delta=g$, then $c_{\mathrm{link}}=v$. Neither is a relativistic identification.

Hamilton's time coordinate is common to every degree of freedom. Independent $m,g,p_0$ calibration yields $\tau=mg/p_0$ in that coordinate. Rescaling $p_{0}$ by $\lambda$ rescales $\tau$ by $1/\lambda$ while preserving adjacency, $\delta$ and normalized weights. Therefore the original clock-modulus nonentailment is preserved. For positive independent calibration intervals the enclosing duration interval is $[m_-g_-/p_+,m_+g_+/p_-]$. Exact theorem preparation is not exact laboratory calibration.

The theorem assumes equal masses, identical gaps, isolated rails, perfectly elastic singular collisions, exact initial rest/momentum, fixed local support and passive zero-latency phase extraction. Random momenta, thermal motion, unequal gaps or masses, nonelasticity or a real external readout can change the duration law. Finite static decoder margins are not dynamical timing robustness. No quantum-only or bounded finite-Hilbert realization is claimed. No universal material substrate, physical c, Planck identification, continuum characteristic symbol, Lorentzian cone equality, empirical hardware validation, or historical campaign acceptance is established.

### 9. Why a soft contact does not inherit the attained full-phase front

For an isolated approaching pair, replace the hard boundary by $V_\kappa(d)=\kappa(a-d)_+^{2}/2$ and put $\omega=\sqrt{2\kappa/m}$, $t_c=\pi/\omega$. The center of mass moves at $v/2$, while relative compression $y$ obeys $y''+\omega^{2}y=0$, $y(0)=0$, $y'(0)=v$. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
y(s)&=(v/\omega)\sin(\omega s), \\
p_{\mathrm{receiver}}(s)&=(p_0/2)(1-\cos(\omega s)),\quad 0\le s\le t_c.
\end{aligned}
$$

At $s=t_c$ momentum exchanges and each rod advances $vt_c/2$. Under $vt_c/2<g$, the next receiver is still untouched when a collision completes. The first onset is $A_1=g/v$; after each full collision the remaining free gap is $g-vt_c/2$, giving $A_{n+1}-A_n=t_c+(g-vt_c/2)/v=\tau+t_c/2$. Therefore

$$
A_n=n\tau+(n-1)t_c/2,\qquad B_n=A_n+t_c=n\tau+(n+1)t_c/2.
$$

Both converge to $n\tau$ at each fixed finite $n$ as $\kappa\to\infty$. For finite $\kappa$ the receiver is unchanged at onset but $p_{\mathrm{receiver}}(s)>0$ for every $0<s<t_c$, so an exact full-phase observer has source sensitivity arbitrarily soon afterward and no attained first sensitive time at $A_n$. A finite threshold gives a later crossing, but it changes which responses count and cannot erase an already allowed earlier analog response. Continuous momenta also cannot converge uniformly to the hard-core jump. This is a scoped falsifier of transferring the hard theorem to that soft family, not an impossibility theorem for every finite-force design.

### 10. Exact finite-dimensional coherent-checkpoint obstruction

For any fixed finite-dimensional self-adjoint $H$, fixed initial state $\rho$ and effect $0\le F\le I$,

$$
p_F(t)=\operatorname{Tr}[F \exp(-itH/\hbar)\rho \exp(itH/\hbar)]
$$

is a finite linear combination of exponentials $\exp[-it(E_a-E_b)/\hbar]$, by spectral decomposition. It is real analytic. If it vanishes on an open interval $(0,\tau)$, its analytic continuation is identically zero, so it cannot first become positive exactly at $\tau$. Each matrix element of a fixed downstream reduced-state difference between two source states has the same property: equality on a nonempty open time interval implies equality for all times.

Consequently an autonomous finite coherent checkpoint alone cannot provide this hard no-early-response step under a fixed unrestricted downstream response grammar. For example, $\sin^{2}(Jt/\hbar)>0$ at sufficiently small positive times despite perfect transfer at $\pi\hbar/(2J)$. This does not outlaw interventions, nonautonomous controls with owned dynamics, hybrid flow, field limits, or distinct admissible response grammars. It does not assert that relativistic quantum fields signal outside their causal cones.

### Q.6.2 Temporal Scale on the Calibrated Branch

<a id="theorem-q61-temporal-scale-on-the-serialized-frontier-branch"></a>**Theorem Q.6.1 (Temporal Scale on the Serialized-Frontier Branch).** On the full branch of Proposition Q.6.1 and the spatial branch of Equation Q.18,
$$
\boxed{
\tau_{\min}=\sqrt{8\ln2}\,t_P\approx2.355\,t_P.
}
$$

*Proof.* Substitute $\delta/L_P=\sqrt{8\ln2}$ into the conditional ratio of Proposition Q.6.1. ∎

<a id="corollary-q61-conditional-unified-discretization-formula"></a>**Corollary Q.6.1 (Conditional Unified Discretization Formula).** On the same joint branch,
$$
\boxed{
\frac{\delta}{L_P}
=
\frac{\tau_{\min}}{t_P}
=
\sqrt{8\ln2}\approx2.355.
}
$$

### Q.6.3 Information-Theoretic Interpretation

<a id="remark-q61-decomposition-of-the-discretization-scale"></a>**Remark Q.6.1: Decomposition of the Discretization Scale.** The unified discretization factor $\sqrt{d_0 \cdot \varepsilon}$ admits a transparent information-theoretic decomposition:

- **Factor $d_0 = 8$:** Theorem 15 gives the finite operational-context floor $N_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\min}=2^{K_0}=8$; Theorem 23 gives the Hilbert-carrier lower bound $d_0\ge N_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\min}$; and the minimal PCE branch used in the Appendix Z backbone selects $d_0 = 8$ (Theorem Z.2). This encodes the logical structure required for self-referential prediction.

- **Factor $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$:** Definition 28 and Definition J.1 register the binary quotient, and Theorem J.1 supplies its structural log-cardinality. Lemma J.1 separately proves reset noninjectivity when its constant-ready-state architecture has a reachable pre-reset domain $A$ with $|A|>2$. Theorem 31 governs physical reset heat and is not used to define this factor.

The dimensionless value $\sqrt{d_0\varepsilon_0}=\sqrt{8\ln2}$ combines the selected carrier dimension with the structural binary reference on the stated saturation branch; it is not a universal thermodynamic cost of self-reference.

<a id="remark-q62-complete-dependency-ledger"></a>**Remark Q.6.2 (Complete Dependency Ledger).** The discretization formula uses two independently registered structural inputs:
$$
\left.
\begin{aligned}
(\mathrm{O1})\text{--}(\mathrm{O3})+(\mathrm{FC})
&\xrightarrow{\text{Thm 15}}K_0=3,\ N_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\min}=8
\xrightarrow{\text{Thm 23 + Hilbert distinguishability}}d_0\ge8
\xrightarrow{\text{Thm Z.2 comparator}}d_0=8,\\
\text{registered binary quotient}
&\xrightarrow{\text{Def 28; Def J.1; Thm J.1}}\varepsilon_0=\ln2
\end{aligned}
\right\}
\Longrightarrow
\frac{\delta}{L_P}
=
\sqrt{d_0\varepsilon_0}
=
\sqrt{8\ln2}
\quad\text{on Equation Q.18's branch.}
$$

The two inputs are recorded separately below; neither is derived from the other.

1. **The Hilbert space dimension** satisfies $d_0 \ge N_{\mathrm{vis}}^{\min}=8$ by Theorem 23, with equality $d_0=8$ on the minimal PCE branch (Theorem Z.2).

2. **The registered physical reset ledger** satisfies $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}\ge H_q(P\mid R)$ by Theorem 31, with a positive uniform floor only if $H_q(P\mid R)\ge h_{\min}>0$. The structural reference $\varepsilon_0=\ln2$ instead comes from Definition 28, Definition J.1, and Theorem J.1; equality $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{reset}}=H_q(P\mid R)$ requires the overhead-free implementation branch.
