## Q.7 The Time-Quantum-to-Hubble Ratio

On the serialized-frontier calibration branch of Section Q.6, the registered edge-update duration satisfies $\tau_{\min}=\sqrt{8\ln2}\,t_P$. Adjoining the de Sitter definition of $t_H$ then gives the following conditional time-scale ratio.

### Q.7.1 The Hubble Time on the de Sitter Branch

<a id="definition-q71-de-sitter-hubble-time"></a>**Definition Q.7.1 (de Sitter Hubble Time).** On the cosmological branch with cosmological constant $\Lambda>0$, the de Sitter Hubble time is
$$
t_H\;:=\;\frac{1}{H_\Lambda}\;=\;\frac{1}{c}\sqrt{\frac{3}{\Lambda}},
$$
where $H_\Lambda=c\sqrt{\Lambda/3}$ is the de Sitter Hubble rate (Appendix E, Theorem E.9.3; Appendix H, Equation H.2).

### Q.7.2 The Closed-Form Ratio

<a id="theorem-q71-time-quantum-to-hubble-identity"></a>**Theorem Q.7.1 (Time-Quantum-to-Hubble Identity).** On the full joint branch of Equation Q.18, Proposition Q.6.1, Theorem Q.6.1, and Definition Q.7.1, the ratio of the serialized-frontier update time to the de Sitter Hubble time is
$$
\boxed{\;\frac{\tau_{\min}}{t_H}\;=\;\sqrt{8\ln 2}\,\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda L_P^2}{3}}\;.}
$$

*Proof.* By Theorem Q.6.1, $\tau_{\min}=\sqrt{8\ln 2}\,t_P$. By the Planck unit identity $L_P/t_P=c$,
$$
\tau_{\min}\;=\;\sqrt{8\ln 2}\cdot\frac{L_P}{c}.
$$
By Definition Q.7.1, $t_H=\sqrt{3/\Lambda}/c$. Therefore
$$
\frac{\tau_{\min}}{t_H}\;=\;\sqrt{8\ln 2}\cdot\frac{L_P/c}{\sqrt{3/\Lambda}/c}\;=\;\sqrt{8\ln 2}\cdot L_P\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda}{3}}\;=\;\sqrt{8\ln 2}\,\sqrt{\frac{\Lambda L_P^2}{3}}.
$$
∎

<a id="corollary-q72-conditional-reciprocal-hubble-to-update-timescale-ratio"></a>**Corollary Q.7.2 (Conditional Reciprocal Hubble-to-Update Timescale Ratio).** On the same joint branch, the reciprocal timescale ratio is
$$
\frac{t_H}{\tau_{\min}}\;=\;\frac{1}{\sqrt{8\ln 2}}\,\sqrt{\frac{3}{\Lambda L_P^2}}.
$$

*Proof.* Taking the reciprocal of Theorem Q.7.1 gives the formula. Interpreting it as an executed cycle count additionally requires continuous attained-rate operation for the entire Hubble interval. ∎

<a id="proposition-q72a-executed-count-schedule-nonentailment"></a>**Proposition Q.7.2a (Executed-Count Schedule Nonentailment).** Fix a de Sitter interval of duration $t_H\ge\tau>0$ and an attained cycle duration $\tau$, and put $m=\lfloor t_H/\tau\rfloor\ge1$. The $m$ nonoverlapping slots
$$
[j\tau,(j+1)\tau),
\qquad j=0,\ldots,m-1,
\tag{Q.7.2a.1}
$$
all share the same cosmology and clock. For every integer $n\in\{0,\ldots,m\}$, executing the cycle on any $n$ of these slots gives actual count $N_{\mathrm{exec}}=n$. Therefore $(\Lambda,t_H,\tau)$ and the ratio $t_H/\tau$ do not determine an executed count. A continuous-duty schedule fixed in advance selects $m$ completed cycles; even then the real ratio $t_H/\tau$ is itself an integer count only when the endpoint divides exactly.

*Proof.* Every subset of $n$ slots in (Q.7.2a.1) is a valid nonoverlapping schedule, so all integers from $0$ through $m$ occur while the three registered scale entries remain fixed. The continuous-duty assertion follows from the definition of the floor. ∎

<a id="corollary-q72b-continuous-duty-count-map-for-renewal-clocks"></a>**Corollary Q.7.2b (Continuous-Duty Count Map for Renewal Clocks).** Run a renewal link clock of Proposition Q.6.1b with $\tau_\mu>0$ on continuous duty from time $0$, so that $N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t):=\max\{n\ge0:T_n\le t\}$, and let $t\ge\tau_\mu$. Put $m:=\lfloor t/\tau_\mu\rfloor$ and $\tau^+:=\operatorname{ess\,sup}D_1\in(0,\infty]$. Then $N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t)\le m$ almost surely, and
$$
N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t)=m\ \text{almost surely}
\iff
m\,\tau^+\le t.
\tag{Q.7.2b.1}
$$
The deterministic clock $\mu_\tau$ gives $N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t)=\lfloor t/\tau\rfloor$ for every $t$, and a clock with relative spread $(\tau^+-\tau_\mu)/\tau_\mu\ge1/m$ executes fewer than $m$ cycles with positive probability. If $\mathbb ED_1<\infty$, then $N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t)/t\to1/\mathbb ED_1$ almost surely as $t\to\infty$. At the conditional ratio $t_H/\tau_{\min}\approx4.345\times10^{60}$ of Section Q.7.3, almost-sure equality of the executed count with $\lfloor t_H/\tau_{\min}\rfloor$ therefore requires a relative clock spread below $1/m\approx2.30\times10^{-61}$. A clock with larger spread whose duration law has an atom at $\tau_\mu$ still attains the count with positive probability, on the event that the first $m$ durations equal $\tau_\mu$, since then $T_m=m\tau_\mu\le t$.

*Proof.* Proposition Q.6.1b item 1 gives $T_{m+1}\ge(m+1)\tau_\mu>t$ almost surely, so $N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t)\le m$, and $N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t)=m$ exactly when $T_m\le t$. If $m\tau^+\le t$, then $T_m\le m\tau^+\le t$ almost surely. If $m\tau^+>t$, choose a finite $\tau'<\tau^+$ with $m\tau'>t$; each $D_j$ exceeds $\tau'$ with positive probability, and independence gives $\Pr(T_m>t)>0$. A relative spread at least $1/m$ gives $m\tau^+\ge(m+1)\tau_\mu>t$. The renewal strong law follows from $T_{N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t)}\le t<T_{N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t)+1}$ and $T_n/n\to\mathbb ED_1$. The numerical tolerance is $1/m$ at the displayed ratio. ∎

<a id="theorem-q72c-attained-observable-one-hubble-count"></a>

<a id="theorem-q72c-attained-observable-one-hubble-count-on-a-kinetic-de-sitter-source"></a>**Theorem Q.7.2c (Attained, Observable One-Hubble Count on a Kinetic de Sitter Source).** Let $c,\hbar,\delta,R>0$ with $x=\delta/R\le1/100$, put $\tau=\delta/c$, $t_H=R/c$ and $m=\lfloor R/\delta\rfloor$, given with a certified comparison at the floor boundary, and let $k\ge4$ be an integer with $r_{\mathrm{cal}}=k\delta\sqrt{3/(2\pi)}<R/20$ and $N=6k^2$. The source consists of positive-energy null rays carrying two-dimensional internal factors (three bundled into an eight-dimensional carrier), stationary memories with degenerate internal registers, the boundary permutations named below at their registered intersections, the identity at every other intersection, and reflected radial support beams, on the prescribed metric
$$
g=-c^2dt^2+\bigl\lvert d\mathbf r-(c/R)\,\mathbf r\,dt\bigr\rvert^2 .
\tag{Q.7.2c.1}
$$

1. *Cosmological branch.* (Q.7.2c.1) is de Sitter space with $\mathrm{Ric}=3g/R^2$ and $\Lambda=3/R^2$. The central line $\mathbf r=0$ is a geodesic with proper time $t$, and its Hubble interval is $[0,t_H]$, fixed by the geometry before any count.

2. *Attained clock.* Put $A_*=R^2-\delta^2/(4\sinh^2(x/2))$ and $r_j^2=A_*+e^{jx}(R^2/4-A_*)$ for $j=0,\dots,m+1$, and place stations $\mathbf a_j$ with $\lvert\mathbf a_j\rvert=r_j$, $\lvert\mathbf a_{j+1}-\mathbf a_j\rvert=\delta$ and no three collinear. Then $R/2\le r_j<0.84R$, and a null ray leaving $\mathbf a_j$ at time $t_0$ in the direction of $\mathbf a_{j+1}$ reaches it exactly at $t_0+\tau$. The first response of station $j+1$ to a change of the label sent from station $j$ occurs exactly at delay $\tau$.

3. *Forward-locked duty and event records.* Bundles $W_j$, $j=1,\dots,m+1$, on the null chords from $E_{j-1}$ to $E_j=(j\tau,\mathbf a_j)$ are fixed before the run. At $E_j$ the station loads $W_j$ into its core $(a,d,b)$ and applies, with the fresh outgoing bundle $(u,v,w)$, a private bit $e$ and a hit bit $h$,
$$
F:\bigl((a,d,b),(u,v,w),e,h\bigr)\longmapsto\bigl((u,v,e),(a,d,w),b,h\oplus a\bigr).
\tag{Q.7.2c.2}
$$
$F$ is a permutation of the $256$ basis states and preserves every four-momentum; on fresh stocks it sends $(a,d)$ onward, archives $b$ and writes $h=a$. With the label $(1,0,0)$ launched at $E_0$, every station $j\le m+1$ records $h_j=1$, and a missing transfer leaves its hit $0$. Station $m+1$ receives after $t_H$.

4. *Observable count.* Inward null readers meet the stations at $t_{\mathrm{read}}=t_H+2\tau$ and deliver the hits to a central bank before $t_{\mathrm{read}}+1.84\,t_H$. A reversible circuit of $m(5B+2)$ gates, $B=\lceil\log_2(m+2)\rceil$, adds $h_1,\dots,h_m$ into a $B$-bit register and returns its carries to zero, and the computational-basis measurement of the register gives
$$
N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t_H)=\sum_{j\tau\le t_H}h_j=\lfloor t_H/\tau\rfloor .
\tag{Q.7.2c.3}
$$

5. *Capacity-area calibration on the same source.* The sphere of radius $r_{\mathrm{cal}}$ has area $N\delta^2$. An equal-area cubed-sphere partition divides it into $N$ cells of area $\delta^2$ and uniformly bounded shape, and each cell is crossed by one channel (Q.7.2c.2) from a sender at radius $r_-$ inside to a receiver at radius $r_+$ outside, with $r_-^2=[2r_{\mathrm{cal}}^2+(e^x-1)A_*]/(1+e^x)$, $r_+^2=2r_{\mathrm{cal}}^2-r_-^2$, chord length $\delta$ and flight time $\tau$. The message-dependent output across the sphere is the tensor product of the $N$ channels, each of classical capacity $\ln4$, so the capacity is $N\ln4$ and the capacity per area is $\ln4/\delta^2$. With $G_{\mathrm{op}}=\delta^2c^3/(4\hbar\ln4)$ and, on the capacity-achieving, entropy-saturating, additive-ledger branch of Section Q.1, the independent calibration $G_{\mathrm{op}}=G$,
$$
\delta^2=8\ln2\,L_P^2,\qquad \tau=\sqrt{8\ln2}\,t_P,\qquad
N_{\mathrm{exec}}(t_H)=\Bigl\lfloor\frac{1}{\sqrt{8\ln2}}\sqrt{\frac{3}{\Lambda L_P^2}}\Bigr\rfloor .
\tag{Q.7.2c.4}
$$

6. *Stress account.* A station of mass $M_j$ at radius $r_j$ needs the inward proper force $f_j=M_jc^2r_j/(R^2N_j)$, $N_j=\sqrt{1-r_j^2/R^2}$, and an incident radial beam reflected at the station with power $J_j=cf_j/2$ supplies it. With $T^{\mu\nu}_{\mathrm{ray}}=c\int p^\mu p^\nu\delta_g\,d\lambda$ and $T^{\mu\nu}_B=c\int Mu^\mu u^\nu\delta_g\,d\sigma$, the total stress obeys $\nabla_\nu(T_B+T_{\mathrm{rad}})^{\mu\nu}=j_S^\mu$, where $j_S$ is the current of ray endpoints at the initial and final slices.

*Proof.* Item 1. With $\mathbf q=e^{-ct/R}\mathbf r$, $g=-c^2dt^2+e^{2ct/R}\lvert d\mathbf q\rvert^2$, the flat Friedmann metric with $\dot a/a=c/R$; its Ricci tensor is $3g/R^2$, so $\Lambda=3/R^2$. The central line is a geodesic with proper time $t$.

Item 2. The ray Hamiltonian $c\lvert\mathbf p\rvert+(c/R)\,\mathbf r\cdot\mathbf p$ gives $\dot{\mathbf r}=c\mathbf n+(c/R)\mathbf r$ and $\dot{\mathbf p}=-(c/R)\mathbf p$, so $\mathbf r(t)=e^{c(t-t_0)/R}(\mathbf a+R\mathbf n)-R\mathbf n$ with $\lvert\mathbf n\rvert=1$. It reaches $\mathbf b$ at $t_0+\tau$ exactly when $\lvert e^{-x}\mathbf b-\mathbf a\rvert=R(1-e^{-x})$; with $\lvert\mathbf b-\mathbf a\rvert=\delta$ this is equivalent to $\lvert\mathbf b\rvert^2-A_*=e^x(\lvert\mathbf a\rvert^2-A_*)$, the recurrence for $r_j$. Since $0\le A_*\le x^2R^2$ and $jx\le1+x$, $r_j^2\le e^{1.01}R^2/4<0.687R^2$; moreover $r_{j+1}-r_j\le(e^x-1)r_j/2<0.425\,\delta$ and $r_j+r_{j+1}\ge R>\delta$, so each intersection circle of the two spheres is nondegenerate and a point avoiding the finitely many earlier lines exists. The squared increment is at least $xR^2(1/4-x^2)>\delta^2$, so $\mathbf a_j\cdot(\mathbf a_{j+1}-\mathbf a_j)>0$ and consecutive chords lie in disjoint open radial annuli. Before $E_{j+1}$ the only route carrying the label to station $j+1$ is the bundle $W_{j+1}$, which has not met it; every other input of that station is fixed independently of the label; at $E_{j+1}$, (Q.7.2c.2) gives distinct hits for $a=0$ and $a=1$.

Item 3. The inverse of $F$ reads $(a,d,w)$ from the second output, $(u,v,e)$ from the first, $b$ from the archive and $h$ as the last output plus $a$; internal registers are degenerate, so momenta are unchanged. Induction along the chain gives the hits.

Item 4. An inward radial reader obeys $\dot r=(c/R)r-c$, so from $r_j$ it reaches the centre after $(R/c)\log(R/(R-r_j))<(R/c)\log(1/0.16)<1.84\,t_H$. In each increment step the carries $c_{k+1}=c_k\wedge z_k$ are computed, $z_k\mapsto z_k\oplus c_k$ adds the hit, and the flipped Toffoli layer recomputes and erases the same carries because $c_{k+1}=c_k\wedge\neg z_k^{\mathrm{new}}$; hence $z\mapsto z+h_j \bmod 2^B$ with $5B+2$ gates, and $m<2^B$ excludes overflow. The register value is $\sum_{j\le m}h_j=m=\lfloor t_H/\tau\rfloor$.

Item 5. $4\pi r_{\mathrm{cal}}^2=6k^2\delta^2$ by the choice of $r_{\mathrm{cal}}$. On a cube face the radial projection has area density $r_{\mathrm{cal}}^2(1+u^2+v^2)^{-3/2}$ and face area $2\pi r_{\mathrm{cal}}^2/3$; an explicit equal-area chart of the face onto $[0,1]^2$ with bounded derivatives and inverse derivatives, divided into $k^2$ equal squares, gives cells of area $\delta^2$ and diameter bounded by a fixed multiple of $\delta$. The radii $r_\pm$ satisfy $r_+^2-A_*=e^x(r_-^2-A_*)$ and $\lvert r_+-r_-\rvert<\delta<r_++r_-$, so a chord of length $\delta$ from radius $r_-$ to $r_+$ crosses the sphere once and has flight time $\tau$ by item 2; a rotation places the crossing in the assigned cell. The channels act on disjoint factors, so the message-dependent output is their tensor product with an input-independent state; each factors through the four-dimensional input $(a,d)$, so by the Holevo bound its capacity is at most $\ln4$, attained by the four orthogonal codes. Finally $G_{\mathrm{op}}=G$ gives $\delta^2=4\hbar\ln4\,G/c^3=8\ln2\,L_P^2$, and $t_H/\tau=R/\delta$ with $R=\sqrt{3/\Lambda}$ gives (Q.7.2c.4).

Item 6. A static site at radius $r$ has proper acceleration $c^2r/(R^2N_r)$ toward the centre. Reflection reverses the radial momentum flux $J/c$ of the beam, transferring $2J_j/c=f_j$. The divergence of a ray stress consists of its endpoint momenta; every boundary map preserves the momentum of each channel, so interior endpoint terms cancel, the support forces cancel between bodies and beams, and the initial and final endpoints form $j_S$. ∎

### Q.7.3 Numerical Evaluation

Using the observed central value $\Lambda L_P^2=2.86599\times 10^{-122}$ from Equation V.5 (Appendix V), Theorem Q.7.1 gives
$$
\frac{\tau_{\min}}{t_H}\;=\;\sqrt{8\ln 2}\,\sqrt{\frac{2.86599\times 10^{-122}}{3}}\;\approx\;2.302\times 10^{-61}.
$$
The reciprocal conditional timescale ratio is
$$
\frac{t_H}{\tau_{\min}}\;\approx\;4.345\times 10^{60}.
$$

### Q.7.4 Status of the Identity

<a id="remark-q71-status-of-theorem-q71"></a>**Remark Q.7.1 (Status of Theorem Q.7.1).** Theorem Q.7.1 is algebraic only after three independent branch packages are accepted: the spatial ratio of Equation Q.18, the serialized-frontier clock calibration of Proposition Q.6.1, and the de Sitter definition of $t_H$. It is not a consequence of $K_0$, $\varepsilon_0$, $d_0$, and $\Lambda L_P^2$ alone, and it does not independently close either the temporal or cosmological branch.

<a id="remark-q72-cosmological-microscopic-bridge-scope"></a>**Remark Q.7.2 (Cosmological--Microscopic Bridge Scope).** Theorem Q.7.1 packages the conditional serialized-frontier update scale and de Sitter Hubble scale. Its numerical ratio also depends on the residual-budget, ideal-packing, channel-independence, and clock/frontier calibration premises.
